articles.title: Save up to 36% on a some of the best PC speakers we've reviewed — deals starting at just $26 from AudioEngine, Creative, Edifier, and more
articles.text:
Save up to 36% on a some of the best PC speakers we've reviewed — deals starting at just $26 from AudioEngine, Creative, Edifier, and more
Upgrade your audio setup with a bit of savings.
If you want to upgrade your PC setup without paying high prices for new components, the best PC speakers, provide a tangible upgrade that isn't running at triple the typical price. Many of the sets we've reviewed are on sale for Black Friday, and we've tracked down five of the best deals on speakers we've tested, some of which are among the best we've tested on the market.
We're focused on typical 2.0 stereo speakers here, though some of the options include a subwoofer output so you can configure a 2.1 setup in the future. Although surround sound sets and soundbars are available as PC speakers, we weren't impressed with the deals available.
One of the best desktop speakers we've tested, now updated with USB-C and aptX Adaptive, aptX HD, aptX, AAC, and SBC for stellar wireless connectivity up to 100 feet, these are an excellent audio upgrade for any desk.
Read moreRead less▼
We've recommended the AudioEngine A2+ speakers for years, and the newer A2 GEN3 speakers only make them better. As usual, these speakers feature a 2.75-inch woofer and 0.75-inch tweeter, and they're among the best-sounding speakers in this class. They're expensive at $300, and even during shopping events, they don't always go on sale. That's what makes the 25% discount during Black Friday so attractive.
Although the cabinet and speakers remain unchanged, there are some updates under the hood. The GEN3 speakers support Bluetooth 5.3, adding support for various aptX codecs, and it uses a Class D amplifier, which should help the speakers run cooler. AudioEngine also swapped out the micro-USB port on the original speakers for a USB-C port.
The Creative Labs Pebble V2 is a set of stereo speakers that connect to your PC via USB and feature a minimalist design.
Read moreRead less▼
The Creative Labs Pebble V2 speakers are a go-to recommendation for cheap PC speakers here at Tom's Hardware, and for good reason. As you can read about in our review of the larger Creative Pebble Pro speakers, this range offers plenty of headroom, providing clean sound at higher volumes despite the tiny woofer size (just two inches). Like many Bluetooth speakers, the Pebble V2 set features passive radiators, capturing low-end frequencies to give the impression of a subwoofer. Of course, it's not the same as a subwoofer, but passive bass chambers help a lot with these smaller speakers.
You connect the speakers over a 3.5mm cable for audio, and power them with USB-C (the speakers call for a 10W port). Sustained RMS power is just 8W for the speakers, but they can peak a bit higher at 16W. They run lower by default, but a high-gain switch on the back will kick the power amp into full gear if you need the speakers louder.
The G2000 speakers from Edifier come with a peak power raing of 32W and a frequency response of 98 Hz up to 22 kHz, along with analog and Bluetooth connections.
Read moreRead less▼
The Edifer G2000 speakers double the power output of the Pebble V2's, and they feature larger 2.75-inch drivers (though no tweeter). At $80 on sale, they're much more expensive, but Edifier justifies the extra price with USB and Bluetooth output, alongside a standard 3.5mm connection, as well as a dedicated power adapter to avoid unwanted noise over USB power. If you want to expand your setup, there's also a subwoofer output.
RMS power here is 16W, giving you significantly more headroom at higher volumes to avoid any distortion. The 2.75-inch full range drivers offers decent low-end, though the frequency response cuts off just below 100 Hz, leaving precious sub-region frequencies out of the sonic picture. That gives you a good cutoff point to add a subwoofer, however.
The Edifier M60 speakers feature a 3-inch woofer and 1-inch tweeter, as well as 66W of total output across the four drivers.
Read moreRead less▼
Edifer's M60 speakers are larger, and they take some obvious notes from Audioengine. They're not quite the same as the A2+ speakers, however. The M60s feature a 3-inch woofer and 1-inch tweeter, with an average RMS of 66W across all four drivers (18W each for the woofers, and 15W for the tweeters).
The speakers come with a Hi-Res audio certification, extending the frequency response up from the typical 20 kHz to 40 kHz. Although the human ear typically can't hear about 20 kHz, extra harmonic information down in the audible range of frequencies can add richness to the sound. The speakers can output via USB-C, Bluetooth 5.3, or a 3.5mm, and they come with included stands, which is something even AudioEngine lacks.
These 6.81 x 4.68 x 5.51-inch speakers have attractive removable cloth fronts, 10-degree angled stands to aim them up at your ears, and they performed well in our testing. They also have ample connectivity, with Bluetooth 5.3 LE, USB-C, RCA (with a built-in Phono stage for vinyl record players), optical, and a subwoofer connector.
Read moreRead less▼
For slightly more than the M60s, we have a pair of the GX-10DB speakers from the Japanese brand Onkyo. They come with 3-inch woofers, as well, though slightly smaller 0.75-inch tweets, as well as a Class D amp that can drive RMS of 30W through the speakers. Onkyo gives you a ton of ways to connect to the speakers, including USB-C, optical, Bluetooth, and RCA. The RCA inputs feature a phono stage for use with a turntable, as well.
Although these are relatively inexpensive speakers, Onkyo still makes them feel premium with removable speaker grilles and built-in, wood-finished stands that angle the speakers up toward your ears.
This desktop speaker includes dual four-inch drivers, as well as an integrated EQ and wireless remote.
Read moreRead less▼
If bookshelf speakers aren't your speed, you can save 44% on the Edifier D12 all-in-one desktop speaker. It's a 70-watt speaker with Bluetooth, RCA, and 3.5mm inputs with an attractive wood-grain finish and sleek removeable front grille that sports the Edifier logo.
The speaker is equipped with dual 4-inch drivers along with two 19mm silk down tweeters. Two bass radiator ports provide low-end support. At the top of the speaker, you'll find bass, middle, and treble controls, and the speaker includes a remote so you can control it wirelessly.
Read moreRead less▼
If you're looking for maximum power, you get 120W of goodness with Edifier's S1000MKII speakers, which are on sale for $100 off right now. These are large speakers with 5.5-inch aluminum alloy drivers and 1-inch titanium dome tweeters.
It features Bluetooth, optical, coaxial, and RCA inputs, and there's a universal bass and treble control. These are large bookshelf speakers meant for listening to music, so make sure you have a large-enough desk to fit them byside your monitor.

articles.title: “Debemos estar preparados para los próximos meses”: presidente de Microsoft advierte de más interrupciones tecnológicas masivas
articles.text:
El riesgo de que se repitan interrupciones tecnológicas masivas podría mantenerse elevado durante los próximos meses, mientras las organizaciones aceleran la actualización de software vulnerable y la modernización de infraestructura obsoleta, advirtió el presidente de Microsoft, Brad Smith.
“Creo que tenemos que estar preparados, francamente, para los próximos meses, porque esto no es el tipo de cosa que se resuelve en un par de semanas”, afirmó Smith en el programa Face the Nation, de CBS News, el domingo. “Toda la infraestructura de información del mundo está, en efecto, siendo actualizada en este momento”.
Una cadena de fallas técnicas sin relación entre sí
La advertencia llega luego de un período turbulento marcado por fallas técnicas independientes que afectaron a grandes bancos, aerolíneas, el control de tráfico aéreo y los propios servicios de nube global de Microsoft. Aunque las autoridades descartaron ataques cibernéticos coordinados, la sucesión de interrupciones expuso la dependencia de empresas, agencias gubernamentales y viajeros respecto de sistemas digitales interconectados.
La seguidilla de incidentes comenzó el 12 de noviembre y se extendió hasta el 13, cuando una falla global de Microsoft interrumpió los servicios de Microsoft 365, Exchange Online y Outlook para empresas y organismos gubernamentales en todo el mundo.
Smith explicó que esa falla no estuvo vinculada ni a un error de inteligencia artificial ni a un ciberataque, sino que fue producto de una “tormenta perfecta” generada por la interacción entre una actualización de software de cuatro meses atrás, una actualización más reciente y un cambio en el tráfico de red. Según precisó, Microsoft publicó dos informes sobre el episodio y ya completó nueve medidas correctivas, con 13 adicionales planificadas.
Ese mismo 13 de noviembre, la Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA) ordenó una infrecuente detención total de vuelos a escala nacional después de que una falla de telecomunicaciones interrumpiera durante unas cuatro horas su red de control de tráfico aéreo, lo que provocó demoras y cancelaciones generalizadas.
De acuerdo con la FAA, su red heredada se volvió inestable al recibir alrededor de 1.000 intentos de conexión cada cuatro o cinco segundos, lo que afectó las comunicaciones y las señales de radar en 17 de los 22 centros de control de tráfico aéreo de la agencia. Los investigadores señalaron dos posibles orígenes de ese pico de conexiones, entre ellos un sitio de comunicaciones en Arkansas donde el contratista de defensa L3Harris instalaba un enrutador.
El secretario de Transporte, Sean Duffy, atribuyó la interrupción a la antigüedad de la tecnología de control de tráfico aéreo del país y señaló que conmutadores y enrutadores sobrecargados comenzaron a generar datos inconsistentes.
Días después, United Airlines sufrió una falla tecnológica independiente que alteró las salidas de vuelos en toda su red en Estados Unidos. En paralelo, un problema técnico en JPMorgan Chase retrasó transacciones en distintos puntos del sistema bancario estadounidense, mientras miles de clientes reportaron dificultades para acceder a sus cuentas en línea en Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank y Capital One.
El secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, afirmó que no existe “ninguna prueba” que vincule los distintos episodios ni que sugiera la existencia de ciberataques coordinados.
La inteligencia artificial, motor de una carrera de parches sin precedentes
Smith sostuvo que la inteligencia artificial aceleró la detección de debilidades en el código informático. Si bien esto permite a los equipos de defensa corregir fallas con mayor rapidez, los actores maliciosos pueden emplear las mismas herramientas para atacar sistemas, lo que obliga a las organizaciones a desplegar actualizaciones a un ritmo acelerado que deja menos tiempo para las pruebas.
“Lo que hizo la inteligencia artificial a comienzos de este año fue básicamente facilitar mucho que la gente encuentre vulnerabilidades en el código, y entonces se puede usar ese conocimiento para parchear el código o, si uno es un actor malicioso, usar ese mismo conocimiento para intentar vulnerar sistemas”, explicó.
Debido a que las organizaciones corrigen vulnerabilidades “a un ritmo que nunca habíamos visto antes”, esa misma urgencia genera inestabilidad, en particular en los sistemas heredados, señaló Smith. “Especialmente cuando se tiene infraestructura más antigua, especialmente cuando se intenta parchear a ese ritmo, especialmente cuando hay que ir tan rápido que no se puede dedicar tanto tiempo a probar lo que se cambia en el código, se incrementa el riesgo de que algo salga mal”, agregó.
El directivo instó a los consumidores a instalar con prontitud las actualizaciones de seguridad y pidió a las empresas modernizar la infraestructura antigua y mejorar la coordinación con el gobierno. “Si reciben una actualización en su teléfono o su computadora con un parche, aplíquenlo, porque creo que eso va a mantener su tecnología mucho más segura”, dijo.
Smith remarcó que, si bien la falla de Microsoft tuvo causas propias, buena parte de las interrupciones registradas puede entenderse como un “efecto dominó de la inteligencia artificial” derivado de la carrera global por asegurar código vulnerable.

articles.title: Drupal Fail2Install Exploit Details Emerge as Critical RCE Flaw Faces Active Exploitation
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday added a critical flaw impacting Drupal to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring federal agencies to apply the fixes by November 27, 2026.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-132165 aka Fail2Install (CVSS score: 9.8), is a case of remote code execution (RCE) impacting Drupal core.
"Drupal Core contains a not failing securely vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to take over an existing site or execute arbitrary code via the Drupal installer," CISA said. "Under specific conditions, the attacker can use install.php to attempt to reinstall Drupal on the site."
As previously reported by The Hacker News, an attacker can use the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal, resulting in site takeover or remote code execution under certain circumstances.
According to an independent analysis by Searchlight Cyber, it has emerged that ordinary server resource limits can be abused to trick Drupal into mistakenly believing that an existing website was not installed, enter its installation process via "install.php," create an administrator-controlled account, and execute arbitrary PHP code.
While Drupal has checks in place to determine whether the website is already installed before allowing installation to proceed, the research found that it's possible to bypass these checks by exhausting server resources.
As a result, a failed database connection to the configured database and a failed database check for an existing installation are interpreted as evidence that the website has not been installed, and Drupal allows the installation to proceed after winning a race condition that allows a second database connectivity check to pass.
To achieve this, the three resource exhaustion techniques have been put to use -
- EMFILE, which refers to a limit on how many files a Linux process can open
- Database connection exhaustion
- TCP source-port exhaustion
"We started with EMFILE, then explored database and TCP limits to determine whether availability failures could become security primitives," the cybersecurity company said.
"Applying this methodology to Drupal uncovered a pre-authentication RCE affecting Drupal 8.9, 9, 10, and 11 across four common deployment combinations: Apache with PostgreSQL, Apache with MySQL, PHP-FPM with PostgreSQL, and PHP-FPM with MySQL."
This behavior can be turned into a pathway for code execution by taking advantage of the fact that Drupal's installer supports SQLite database files and allows the database path to be selected during installation. This is made possible because the installer doesn't restrict the file name extension.
"By selecting a path ending in .php under the document root, the installer creates an SQLite database with a PHP extension," Searchlight Cyber said. "Once the installation reaches the site configuration form, Drupal stores the submitted website name inside the SQLite database. By using PHP code as the website name, the payload bytes are written into the .php database file."
While direct access to the generated PHP file is blocked by Drupal's stock .htaccess on a stock Apache deployment, a path-handling weakness in the Apache RewriteRule could be exploited to achieve arbitrary PHP execution.
"Starting from three system-wide limits, we showed how errors that appear to affect only availability can become primitives for crossing a security boundary," Searchlight Cyber researchers Kevin Gervot and Adam Kues said.
"In Drupal, temporary database failures can produce a FAIL, FAIL, and then SUCCESS sequence that reopens the installer on an existing website and ultimately leads to pre-authentication RCE through an SQLite database containing PHP code."
The issue has been addressed in the following versions -
- Drupal 11.4.x - Update to Drupal 11.4.13
- Drupal 11.3.x - Update to Drupal 11.3.22
- Drupal 10.6.x - Update to Drupal 10.6.22
The addition of CVE-2026-132165 to the KEV catalog follows a report received by the Drupal Security Team that it "was exploited on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC."
It's worth noting that CVE-2026-132165 is the third Drupal flaw to come under active exploitation this year following CVE-2026-9082 (CVSS score: 6.5) and CVE-2026-118539 (CVSS score: 6.5).

articles.text:
Un temps pionnier sur le mini-PC, Shuttle veut revenir dans la course et profite pour cela de la génération Wildcat Lake d'Intel.
Shuttle est une marque emblématique du phénomène du mini-PC et si la firme est moins en vogue depuis déjà quelques années, elle cherche toujours à proposer des produits innovants. Semi-durci et conçu autour de la génération Wildcat Lake d'Intel, le NW10U est de ceux-là.
Shuttle mise sur Wildcat Lake
Juillet 2002. Voilà qui ne nous rajeunit pas. À l'époque déjà, je testais des composants pour Clubic et j'avais été l'un des premiers Européens à mettre la main sur le SS50, un PC pas tout à fait comme les autres.
Venue d'Asie, la vague des mini-PC commençait à peine à arriver en Europe et le shuttle SS50 était l'un des premiers modèles à être disponible sur le Vieux Continent. Des sacrifices, il fallait en faire – notamment au niveau de la carte graphique – mais l'idée était déjà de proposer des PC aussi complets que possible tout en réduisant fortement leur encombrement.
Vous vous en doutez, en près de 25 ans, de l'eau a coulé sous les ponts et, paradoxalement, l'une des marques pionnières en la matière a presque disparu des radars, en tout cas en Europe. Shuttle existe toujours, mais sa présence en France est bien moins notable et des marques de mini-PC comme Beelink, Geekom ou NiPoGi l'ont largement éclipsé.
Éclipsé certes, mais Shuttle n'a pas dit son dernier mot et la firme taïwanaise dispose encore d'une belle réputation, notamment dans son pays d'origine où elle cherche encore et toujours à innover là où les marques de mini-PC se copient très souvent les unes les autres.
Un mini-PC d'à peine 0,4 litre de volume
Le NW10U s'inscrit dans cette ambition d'apporter quelque chose de neuf au monde du mini-PC et, pour ce faire, il se repose sur la nouvelle architecture Wildcat Lake d'Intel.
Si vous connaissez cette gamme de puces, vous savez déjà que l'objectif n'est pas la quête de la puissance extrême, mais plutôt celle du compromis entre puissance effective et empreinte énergétique afin de limiter à la fois le bruit, la consommation et la chauffe. Signe qui ne trompe pas, le NW10U est d'ailleurs un produit que Shuttle présente comme « semi-durci ».
Derrière ce terme se cache un PC conçu pour fonctionner même dans des environnements relativement hostiles : Shuttle parle d'une machine capable de tourner 24 heures sur 24, 7 jours sur 7, et ce, avec une température ambiante comprise entre 0°C et 50°C. Mieux, le NW10U reste redoutablement compact, avec un volume de 0,4 litre (103 x 97 x 36,5 mm).
À l'intérieur de la bête, on retrouve au choix Intel Core 3 304, Core 5 320, Core 7 350 de la gamme Wildcat Lake, soit 5 ou 6 cœurs avec un TDP de 15 watts et un maximum de 64 Go de mémoire vive DDR5-6400. Il est prévu un maximum de deux SSD M.2 NVMe 2280 PCIe 4.0 avec option RAID 0/1 et un troisième M.2 au format 2230 est prévu pour un module sans fil optionnel.
Shuttle met en avant la riche connectique – compte tenu de la taille du PC – avec un port HDMI 2.1, deux USB-C compatibles DisplayPort 2.1 ainsi que deux USB-A 3.2 et deux USB-A 2.0. Un port Ethernet RJ45 à la norme 1 GbE vient compléter l'ensemble alors que Shuttle souligne la présence d'une fixation VESA compatible 75 x 75 mm et 100 x 100 mm. Bien vu.
Pour l'heure, nous ne savons pas si ce mini-PC ultra compact sera disponible en Europe, à fortiori en France. Il est toutefois question d'un prix de 1 259 dollars pour la version Core 3 304 avec 8 Go de RAM et un SSD de 512 Go, tandis que le modèle « haut de gamme » est facturé 3 034 dollars avec un Core 7 350, 32 Go de RAM et un SSD de 1 To. Tout cela, hors taxes : oui, ça pique quand même pas mal.
Source : Shuttle

articles.title: Dell's RTX 5050 Alienware 16 Aurora drops by $900 for Black Friday
articles.text:
Dell slashes $900 off the Alienware 16 Aurora — bringing this 16-inch RTX 5050 creator laptop down to $1,100 for Black Friday
Alienware 16 Aurora now available with $900 saving, free year's Elite Care and more
For an RTX 50-series laptop, the Alienware 16 Aurora is already relatively affordable. This particular specification packs a punch with its Intel Core 7 240H processor, Nvidia GeForce RTX 5050 graphics card, and 16GB of DDR5 memory that make it ideal for general content creators, streamers, and marketers.
But the biggest news is that Dell is selling it at nearly half price – this $2,000 laptop is now available for $1,100, and other configurations are also available with equally massive savings.
Dell is also giving buyers one free year of Alienware Elite Care on two-, three- and four-year packages, plus 25 free Xbox games (worth up to $500) and other discounts on McAfee, Microsoft 365 and more.
Save $900 on the Alienware 16 Aurora gaming laptop, packing an Intel Core 7 processor, Nvidia GeForce RTX 5050 graphics and Wi-Fi 7. Plus, Dell will give you more discounts and deals on top.
Why we recommend it
This portable gaming PC offers powerful graphics and a sharp 16-inch display. It's already good for price vs. performance, but this $900 discount makes it far better value.
With color accuracy of 100% sRGB, it's ideal for creators working on digital content - think social media posts or marketing assets. The RTX 5050 graphics helps here, too. It might not be as meaty as the 5090 cards (but it's also less expensive), and it'll handle clips and YouTube content with total ease.
Price Context & Historical Value
Admittedly, it launched for $1,149 back in May 2025, but we all know prices have risen sharply since then. Today, you'll need to fork out $2,000 for the cheapest model with RTX 5050 graphics, but this super saving brings it below even its cheapest launch price.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Alienware 16 Aurora if... a dedicated creator laptop with premium styling and cooling technology is what you need, but you don't want to fork out even more for Alienware's Area-51 models
❌ Skip the Alienware 16 Aurora if... faster refresh rates and a 4K display are important to your workflow.

articles.title: Lanzamiento de GTA 6 afectó a Call of Duty: perdió más de 3 millones de jugadores diarios
articles.text:
El lanzamiento de Grand Theft Auto 6 provocó una caída de más de 3 millones de jugadores diarios en Call of Duty HQ, la aplicación que reúne entregas como Modern Warfare 4, Black Ops 7 y Warzone. La baja coincidió con los primeros días de disponibilidad del juego de Rockstar Games en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S.
Los usuarios no abandonaron necesariamente Call of Duty de forma definitiva, pero el descenso refleja que parte de su tiempo de juego se trasladó a Leonida, el escenario de GTA 6.
Call of Duty perdió el 42% de sus usuarios diarios
Las estimaciones de Alinea Analytics indican que Call of Duty HQ pasó de un promedio de 7,5 millones de jugadores diarios a 4,4 millones durante el fin de semana del lanzamiento de GTA 6. La diferencia representa una reducción cercana al 42% entre PlayStation, Xbox y Steam.
Los datos fueron compartidos por Rhys Elliott, responsable de análisis de mercado de la firma. Cuatro días después del estreno, la plataforma de Activision continuaba un 41% por debajo de su ritmo habitual, lo que sugiere que la recuperación inicial fue limitada.
La mayor caída ocurrió en PlayStation, una de las plataformas históricamente más importantes para Call of Duty. Allí, la disminución alcanzó el 44%, según las estimaciones. El dato resulta relevante porque GTA 6 solo llegó inicialmente a consolas de nueva generación, mientras que el cálculo de Call of Duty incluye también a Steam.
Las cifras no proceden de Activision ni de Rockstar Games, por lo que deben interpretarse como una medición de terceros sobre la actividad de los jugadores. Aun así, el comportamiento permite observar el alcance que puede tener un lanzamiento esperado durante años sobre otros títulos con comunidades estables.
Fortnite y EA Sports FC 27 también registraron descensos
Call of Duty no fue el único juego afectado. Fortnite redujo su número de jugadores diarios en PlayStation y Xbox durante el mismo período, con una caída estimada del 28%. Su comunidad pasó de 17,8 millones de usuarios diarios a 12,8 millones, aunque recuperó parte de la actividad antes de terminar el fin de semana.
El caso de EA Sports FC 27 fue similar. El simulador de fútbol habría perdido cerca del 27% de sus usuarios diarios, al pasar de 5,9 millones a 4,3 millones. Sin embargo, el título redujo posteriormente parte de esa distancia frente a su promedio, apoyado por una promoción que rebajó su precio.
La diferencia entre estos juegos apunta a que no todas las comunidades reaccionan del mismo modo a un lanzamiento masivo. Fortnite y EA Sports FC conservan modelos basados en temporadas, actualizaciones frecuentes, eventos y competiciones que pueden acelerar el regreso de los usuarios.
Call of Duty también cuenta con contenido periódico y una base consolidada, pero su descenso fue más prolongado. La explicación puede estar en el tiempo que exige un juego de mundo abierto como GTA 6, donde la campaña, la exploración y las actividades secundarias compiten de forma directa con las partidas multijugador nocturnas.
El cruce de jugadores no explica por sí solo la caída
Alinea Analytics señaló que el 29% de quienes jugaron GTA 6 también habían dedicado tiempo a Fortnite durante el mes. En Call of Duty HQ, esa coincidencia fue menor, cercana al 16%.
El dato sugiere que GTA 6 atrajo a jugadores más allá de la comunidad que comparte habitualmente con Call of Duty. La pérdida de actividad no se explicaría únicamente por una migración entre públicos similares, sino por la capacidad del título de Rockstar para ocupar el tiempo disponible de jugadores con intereses distintos.
Esta situación contradice la expectativa que Activision había planteado semanas antes. Tyler Bahl, director de marketing de la compañía, consideraba que el estreno de GTA 6 podía reactivar consolas que permanecían sin uso y abrir una oportunidad para que parte de esos usuarios probara la nueva entrega de Call of Duty.
La caída de jugadores en otros títulos confirma que el efecto de GTA 6 trasciende su propio rendimiento comercial. El juego no solo compite por ventas: disputa horas de atención frente a servicios que dependen de usuarios activos, compras dentro de las plataformas y temporadas de contenido.
Para otras editoras, el lanzamiento obliga a revisar calendarios, promociones y actualizaciones. La llegada futura del componente en línea de GTA 6 podría intensificar esa competencia por el tiempo de los jugadores.

articles.title: Ex-OpenAI Employee Accused of Bugging Company Offices Granted $1 Million Bail
articles.text:
A former OpenAI employee accused of concealing a covert recording device at the company's San Francisco offices will be allowed to be released from jail on a $1 million bond, a San Francisco federal court judge ruled Tuesday.
Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national, was arrested on October 9, 2026, for allegedly bugging the artificial intelligence (AI) company's offices with the aim of recording sensitive conversations.
Subsequent court filings have pointed out that Alfozan was in touch on WhatsApp with a member of the Saudi royal family, as well as expressed interest in moving back to Saudi Arabia following OpenAI's initial public offering (IPO).
He has been charged with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. If convicted, Alfozan faces a maximum penalty of 5 years in prison and a $250,000 fine, followed by 3 years of supervised release.
"At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," the ChatGPT-maker said at the time.
Alfozan pleaded not guilty to the charges during his appearance in San Francisco federal court earlier this month.
According to CNBC, the decision comes after prosecutors told the court last week that they had "found no new evidence to support the theory that Mr. Alfozan was stealing trade secrets, or to support the speculation that he was acting as an unregistered foreign agent for Saudi Arabia."
However, they said investigators have found hundreds of audio files on the defendant's personal devices, including dozens of recordings of meetings or conversations that took place at OpenAI throughout September 2026.
Some of these involved meetings with OpenAI customers and contained material protected by attorney-client privilege, prosecutors said, adding he possessed a photograph of what's believed to be a term sheet for a "strategic partnership" between OpenAI and another company.
"What the defendant did or intended to do with those audio files remains under investigation," they said.
Under the bail conditions, Alfozan will be required to wear a GPS ankle monitor, observe a curfew from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m., stay within the Northern District of California, and avoid airports and train and bus stations. He is expected to be released on Wednesday morning.
"There is no spy story that we're talking about right now," U.S. Magistrate Judge Alex G. Tse said, per The Wall Street Journal. "The government doesn't have that."

articles.title: Building a workstation PC? These 3 high-airflow cases are up to 60% off
articles.text:
Building a workstation or studio PC? Here are 3 Black Friday high-airflow case deals from Fractal, Cooler Master, and Phanteks
Need a cool, quiet PC case for your workstation or office build? Here's my top high-airflow Black Friday deals
If you're assembling an office desktop, high-end AI workstation, or a 3D rendering rig, choosing the right case determines how cool, and quiet, your PC runs under sustained use. So, I went looking for the best cases in the Black Friday sales (and no prizes for guessing that Newegg wins for price cuts).
For budget builders, Cooler Master TD500 Mesh ATX mid-tower case is now $60 (was $150) at Newegg. That $90 saving nets you a case with a polygonal mesh front for airflow, four pre-installed ARGB fans, a tempered glass side panel, and room for GPUs up to 410mm long.
For a studio or streamer show-stopper build, the Phanteks XT View Matrix mid-tower ATX case is $70 (was $100) with customizable 600-LED matrix display, near-seamless glass front and side panels, and support for back-connector motherboards. And for a workstation built for multi-core CPU and GPU workloads, the Fractal Design Torrent is a E-ATX mid-tower case priced at $188 (was $250).
An ATX mid-tower case that supports E-ATX, ATX, micro ATX, and mini-ITX motherboards. It comes with four CF120 ARGB fans (three in front, one at the rear), a polygonal mesh front panel, and a tempered glass side panel. It fits graphics cards up to 410mm long and CPU coolers up to 180mm tall, and it has two USB 3.2 Gen 1 ports on the front.
A mid-tower case that supports E-ATX, ATX, micro ATX, and mini-ITX motherboards, including back-connector boards like ASUS BTF and MSI Project Zero. It has a 600-LED matrix display behind a fabric panel, tempered glass front and side panels, three pre-installed D-RGB fans, a USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 front port, room for GPUs up to 415mm and CPU coolers up to 184mm, and a top mount for a 360mm radiator.
A mid-tower case that supports E-ATX and smaller motherboards. It comes with two 180mm front fans and three 140mm bottom fans, all with addressable RGB, plus tempered glass panels. It fits graphics cards up to 461mm long (423mm with a front fan installed) and CPU coolers up to 188mm tall.
Why we recommend them
With the Cooler Master TD500, it's a rock-solid pick for a home office setup, where you can turn off or customize the lighting to a clean white for a more professional style. The four included ARGB fans would cost you $40 or more on their own, so getting them with a solid case for $60 is a great value. The mesh front panel lets those fans pull in plenty of cool air. It's a few years old, so you won't get front USB-C, but it does the basics very well.
Our sister site PC Gamer gave the Phanteks XT View Matrix a score of 92 in its review, calling it easy to build in, impressively cheap, and lovely to own. The matrix panel offers a good way to monitor your workstation at a glance using Phanteks' NexLinq app. Its look won't suit every office, but it's an excellent pick for a studio or streaming setup at this price.
With the Fractal Design Torrent, our sister site Tom's Hardware praised the excellent thermal performance in its review, and called it unlike most other ATX cases. If you're cooling a flagship workstation GPU, few cases move more air than this one. For heavy workloads, it's the one to choose.
Price Context & Historical Value
All three PC cases prove excellent value - particularly the Cool Master (thanks to the included ARGB fans) and the Phanteks models.
Which should you buy?
✅ Buy the Cooler Master TD500 Mesh if... you're building a budget work PC and need good airflow without buying extra fans.
✅ Buy the Phanteks XT View Matrix if... you want a statement case, a showpiece for your studio or streaming setup.
✅ Buy the Fractal Design Torrent RGB if... you're running a high-end GPU and CPU, you want great temperatures out of the box, or you like the bold look of the open front grille.

articles.title: Here are the best OLED gaming monitor deals you can snag for Black Friday — beautiful monitors up to 39% off
articles.text:
Here are the best OLED gaming monitor deals you can snag for Black Friday — beautiful monitors up to 39% off
OLED gaming monitors are hot right now, and Black Friday is an excellent time to be in the market.
OLED panels are quickly becoming a must-have item for desktop PCs. Most of us were introduced to the panel technology in smartphones, and it’s become increasingly popular on laptops. For desktop gamers seeking an immediate visual upgrade, OLED is the way to go, and fortunately, Prime Day is proving to be a great time to take the plunge. From massive DQHD panels on the Samsung Odyssey OLED G9 (G93SC) to more value-oriented offerings like the Acer Nitro VG277U Xbiip, we have you covered.
Here are the best OLED gaming monitors that we’ve seen so far:
Mega-Ultrawide OLED Gaming Monitors
Mega-ultrawide gaming monitors are not for the faint of heart. Not only can these monitors be quite expensive, but they can also occupy a substantial amount of desktop space. However, for those who have the need (and the space), there are options such as the Samsung 49" Odyssey OLED G9 (G91SD), which is currently on sale for just $799.99 at Amazon.
It features a gorgeous 49-inch QD-OLED panel with a 5120 x 1440 resolution, but instead of a maximum 240 Hz refresh rate, you'll top out at 144 Hz. Brightness tops out at 250 nits (typical), and you'll still get a fast 0.03 ms GtG response time. The monitor supports AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, and it's also Nvidia G-Sync compatible. As for ports, you'll find one DisplayPort 1.4, two HDMI 2.1, and two downstream USB-C ports.
The Samsung Odyssey OLED G9 (G91SD) is a slightly less ambitious 49-inch QD-OLED gaming monitor with a DQHD resolution. Instead of a 240 Hz top speed, the G91SD dials it back to a maximum of 144 Hz.
34-inch Ultrawide OLED Gaming Monitors
The AOC Agon Pro AG346UCD is a highly desirable QD-OLED monitor that strikes a sweet spot with its 34-inch WQHD panel and a 165 Hz refresh rate.
If you're looking for something more in a “mid-range” size class, the AOC Agon Pro AG346UCD should be on your shopping list. This is a 34-inch QD-OLED monitor with a 3440 x 1440 resolution and a 165 Hz refresh rate. While that figure may not be as high as the 240 Hz more commonly found with 34-inch panels, the Agon Pro AG346UCD is priced at just $599, taking $50 off its typical asking price. In our review, we praised the monitor for its well-saturated color, excellent contrast, and out-of-the-box accuracy.
27-inch OLED Gaming Monitors
All-time low price
The Samsung Odyssey OLED G50SF is a 27-inch 1440p QD-OLED gaming monitor that offers up to 180 Hz refresh rate, 99% coverage of DCI-P3, 0.03ms of response time, and a bunch of features to prevent OLED burn-in.
The Asus ROG Strix XG27ACDNG might be small in stature, but its 27-inch QHD panel delivers a sizzling 360 Hz maximum refresh rate.
One of the best things to happen to gaming monitors in recent years has been the emergence of OLED panel technology. OLED panels are fast, offer rich color and blacker blacks, but have come with a big price premium. But as the technology has matured, prices have come down. That fact is exemplified by the 27-inch Samsung Odyssey OLED G50SF, which is currently priced at $319.99.
The Odyssey OLED G50SF features a QD-OLED panel measuring 27 inches with a QHD resolution of 2560×1440, which is currently the sweet spot for PC gaming. It supports up to a 180 Hz refresh rate via DisplayPort and 144 Hz through HDMI. Samsung claims that the display offers a response time of 0.03ms (GTG), essentially offering smooth and responsive visuals during fast action. With G-Sync compatibility and support for AMD FreeSync, expect zero screen lag and image tearing.
Another option is the Asus ROG Strix XG27ACDNG, which also sports a 27-inch QHD QD-OLED panel. When the ROG Strix XG27ACDNG arrived in our testing lab, we noted its accuracy, fast response, and stunning image quality. The monitor also boasts a 360 Hz refresh rate for ultra-twitch gamers. Currently, the ROG Strix XG27ACDNG is on sale for $549, representing a 28% savings.

articles.title: Huawei reconnu coupable aux États-Unis de vol de secrets commerciaux et de trafic avec l'Iran
articles.text:
Le géant chinois arrive au bout d'une procédure judiciaire de huit ans aux États-Unis. Et elle le reconnaît coupable de plusieurs méfaits.
Cela peut sembler dater, mais il faut se souvenir que les actions des États-Unis contre Huawei ont commencé en janvier 2019. À l'époque, une instruction judiciaire était lancée par le département de la Justice des États-Unis contre le géant des télécommunications chinois. Le procès ne s'était finalement ouvert qu'au mois de septembre 2026, et après trois mois, ainsi que l'audition de près de 60 témoins pour l'accusation, le verdict est enfin tombé !
Huawei reconnu coupable de 10 des 12 chefs d'accusation
Huawei était poursuivi pour 12 chefs d'accusation devant un tribunal de New York. Il a finalement été reconnu coupable pour 10 d'entre eux, avec le plus grave - celui d'association de malfaiteurs en vue de détournement de propriété intellectuel - finalement écarté.
Le géant chinois est ainsi dorénavant officiellement coupable aux yeux de la justice américaine de vols de secrets industriels. Parmi les entreprises ciblées (américaines et internationales) sont citées T-Mobile, Cisco Systems, Quintel, CNEX et Fujitsu.
L'entreprise reconnue comme un vrai danger pour la sécurité nationale américaine
Les autres chefs d'accusation portent notamment sur des faits de fraude électronique, de fraude bancaire ainsi que de contournement des sanctions américaines contre l'Iran. Huawei est ainsi coupable d'avoir trompé les banques sur ses activités avec l'Iran. « Huawei a menti aux banques au sujet de ses activités en Iran afin d'obtenir des milliards de dollars américains et d'accéder à des services de compensation en dollars américains » note le département de la Justice.
Le groupe chinois aurait travaillé avec les renseignements iraniens, aidé à la censure du web local, et fourni des caméras de surveillance pour surveiller les protestations. Ses activités étaient regroupées dans une filiale du nom de « Skycom », présentée par Huawei comme un simple partenaire commercial - ce qui lui permettait d'affirmer à Washington avoir cessé officiellement de travailler avec l'Iran depuis 2011.
« Peu de crimes sont aussi graves que la pratique, mise en œuvre depuis des décennies par Huawei, qui consiste à mettre en danger la sécurité nationale des États-Unis, à porter atteinte à l'intégrité du commerce américain et à entraver l'application des lois américaines » a résumé le procureur fédéral Joseph Nocella. Du côté de Huawei, on parle déjà de faire appel, alors que Pékin accuse Washington de manoeuvre inéquitable pour faire mal à un fleuron chinois.
Source : US department of Justice

articles.title: Hackers Exploited CVSS 10.0 Hex.pm RCE Flaw to Compromise 6 Package Registry Servers
articles.text:
An attacker ran operating system commands on Monday on six production servers of Hex.pm, the package registry that Elixir and Erlang developers fetch their dependencies from.
The flaw used in the attack had been in the registry's code since February 2016, and the team that maintains the service had every server on a patched build within about 15 minutes of the first malicious request.
Checks since then found no sign that any package was changed. Whether the attacker read account data such as email addresses, password hashes, and two-factor authentication secrets could not be ruled out, the team said.
What Hex Users Should Do Now
Everyone with a hex.pm account has been logged out because the maintainers replaced the keys that sign sessions and access tokens. They advise account holders to take these steps:
- Change your hex.pm password.
- Reset two-factor authentication by setting up a new authenticator entry, and store the new recovery codes.
- Log back in to the client with mix hex.user auth or, for Erlang projects, rebar3 hex user auth.
- Update the Hex client when the next release ships, expected within days, with a new registry signing system.
- Watch for phishing. Exposed email addresses may be misused, so check that links in any email about Hex go to hex.pm.
API keys do not need to be replaced, according to the team: they are random 128-bit values stored only as HMAC-SHA256 hashes, which it says cannot realistically be brute-forced. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt, which slows guessing but does not stop it for weak passwords, so changing them still matters.
Developers who never created a hex.pm account and only fetch public packages have nothing to reset, Peter Ullrich, one of the report's authors, said in a maintainer clarification on the Elixir Forum. Those who signed up with GitHub should still log back in to their clients, and reset two-factor authentication if they enabled it.
Until the new client ships, the advice is to fetch packages only from repo.hex.pm and to avoid third-party mirrors. The registry signing key has not yet been replaced, and it was among the credentials the attacker could have read.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-129514 with the maximum CVSS score of 10.0, sat in the parser hex.pm used to read request bodies sent in an Erlang data format. That parser ran before routing and authentication, so an unauthenticated POST request to any address on the site could reach it.
The decoding function was meant to be safe, and it did block dangerous terms such as functions, but it accepted maps with a __struct__ key, which allowed a request body to pose as any Elixir struct the application had loaded.
The safety check that would have stopped this was removed from the code on February 23, 2016, which is where the flaw's age comes from. Exploitation before Monday has not been established.
A crafted struct ran nothing by itself. It caused an error, and the error reporting code then inspected the struct. That inspection, via the Ecto and DBConnection database libraries, led to a point where the server called a function of the attacker's choice, which then ran operating system commands with the permissions of the registry's service account.
The security advisory lists hex.pm as affected from February 23, 2016 until Monday. The fix commit makes the decoder reject any term containing a map with a __struct__ key, and every hex.pm server was running it by 18:31 UTC on Monday.
Load balancer logs recorded 69 exploit requests between 18:16 and 18:29 UTC on Monday, all from two addresses, the Hex.pm team said in its incident report yesterday. Files created by the exploit appeared on six web servers, in one case just 3 milliseconds after the request. Three of those servers joined mid-attack, when a restart brought up machines still on the vulnerable build.
To check the packages, the team compared every database table against a copy taken two minutes before the first exploit request and traced each difference to normal activity. The 23 releases published during the attack all match the audit log, no older release was changed, and the package and registry files written that evening match the database records.
Database reads, shell commands, environment variables and direct reads from file storage were not logged. For that reason, "we cannot rule out that the attacker accessed data stored in the database," the team wrote. That database holds email addresses, password hashes, API key hashes, two-factor authentication secrets and session data, and private packages could also have been read without leaving a trace.
The checks found no leftover shells and no new accounts or cloud keys in the audit logs. Who was behind the attack is unknown. Activity from the two addresses going back to late last week suggests the attacker built a local copy of hex.pm to test against, according to the team.
A separate security report describing the same flaw arrived by email at 19:07 UTC on Monday, after the attack had ended. By yesterday morning the team had replaced every credential the attacker could have read except the registry signing key. On Monday night it reported the breach to the Swedish data protection authority, to CISA in the United States and to ENISA in the European Union.
Related Library Fixes
Alongside the incident, maintainers of three widely used Elixir libraries disclosed flaws of their own involving structs built from untrusted data, and shipped fixed versions yesterday. These are separate disclosures, not further attacks on Hex.pm.
| Library | CVE | Affected versions | Fixed versions | 
|---|---|---|---|
| ash | CVE-2026-124283 | 3.31.3 up to, but not including, 3.38.0 | 3.38.0 | 
| db_connection | CVE-2026-133555 | 1.1.0 up to, but not including, 2.10.3 | 2.10.3 | 
| flop | CVE-2026-130411 | From 0.8.0, each branch before its fixed version | 0.26.7, 0.27.3, 0.28.1, 0.29.2 | 
Each needs its own conditions to be exploited. The Ash flaw requires keyset pagination with a client-supplied cursor, certain sort field types, and a signing secret left at its unset default, according to the Ash advisory.
The db_connection flaw "is not exploitable in db_connection alone," the DBConnection advisory says, because another component must first decode untrusted data into structs. The Flop flaw has similar conditions around its pagination cursors, according to the Flop advisory.
The exploited flaw sits in the hexpm server code, not in the Hex client, so organizations that run their own copy of the registry are affected until they deploy the patch.

articles.title: Save on a budget router with prices starting at just $39 — TP-Link Archer AX1450 and Netgear RAX5 Wi-Fi 6 routers go on low sale
articles.text:
Save on a budget router with prices starting at just $39 — TP-Link Archer AX1450 and Netgear RAX5 Wi-Fi 6 routers go on low sale
Walmart has some hot deals on budget Wi-Fi 6 routers
Suppose you don’t need the extra speed and capacity that Wi-Fi 7 offers, and you just want something cheap to give you decent coverage throughout your house? Well, that’s where something like the TP-Link Archer AX1450 comes into focus. Walmart has the router on sale this week for $39, a $10 discount off its regular asking price.
The Archer AX1450 is by no means a speed demon, delivering up to 250 Mbps over the 2.4 GHz band and up to 1,201 Mbps on the 5 GHz band. That should be more than sufficient if you have a 1 Gbps or lower broadband connection. You get one GbE WAN port and four GbE LAN ports for connecting your wired devices. The router features four antennas and four wireless streams.
You can manage the Archer AX1450 with the usual webGUI on a desktop/laptop or use the TP-Link Tether app to control the router from your smartphone or tablet.
There’s also the Netgear RAX5, which Walmart has on sale for $44.33 ($35 off its usual selling price). This is another Wi-Fi 6 router delivering up to 1.6 Gbps aggregate speeds. The router covers up to 1,500 square feet and includes a GbE WAN and four GbE LAN ports.
The TP-Link Archer AX1450 is a Wi-Fi 6 router with four GbE LAN ports and up to 1.45 Gbps aggregate wireless speeds across 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.
The Netgear RAX5 is a Wi-Fi 6 router with four GbE LAN ports and up to 1.6 Gbps aggregate wireless speeds across 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.
Keep in mind that the RAX5 isn’t meant for homes that have a ton of smartphones, computers, and smart home devices. It only reliably supports up to 20 wireless devices. So if you have a desktop, a laptop, a couple of TVs, and a couple of smartphones, the RAX5 should do perfectly fine handling the load. If you have more demanding needs, step up to one of the best Wi-Fi 7 routers.
As I previously mentioned, the TP-Link and Netgear routers are aimed at people who have less demanding wireless needs, and they’re priced to reflect this fact. They won’t win any throughput contests against their newer Wi-Fi 6E or Wi-Fi 7 competition, but those routers will also cost you around twice as much money.

articles.title: El iPhone 18e estrenaría un módulo de cámara cuadrado al estilo iPad Pro
articles.text:
Apple prepara una renovación estética para su gama económica de iPhone. Según imágenes de diseño asistido por computadora (CAD) vistas por Engadget, el iPhone 18e incorporaría un módulo de cámara cuadrado de inspiración similar al del iPad Pro M5, con una línea que se alejaría del diseño actual de lente al ras que caracteriza al iPhone 17e.
Las imágenes provienen de una fuente cercana a la cadena de suministro de Apple que ya había anticipado los colores del iPhone 17 y del iPhone 18 Pro antes de sus respectivos anuncios, lo que otorga cierto respaldo a la filtración.
Cómo sería el nuevo diseño de cámara del iPhone 18e
El cambio más llamativo de la filtración recae en el iPhone 18e. El teléfono económico de Apple dejaría atrás el sistema actual, en el que la lente sobresale levemente y queda casi a ras de la parte posterior, con el micrófono y el flash LED integrados en recortes directos sobre el cristal trasero.
En su lugar, las imágenes CAD muestran un módulo casi cuadrado de aproximadamente 28 milímetros (1,10 pulgadas) por 35 milímetros (1,37 pulgadas), que concentraría en una sola plataforma la cámara trasera, el flash LED y el micrófono posterior.
El diseño guarda semejanza con el módulo de cámara del iPad Pro M5, lo que sugiere un cambio de lenguaje visual más que una simple mejora funcional. De confirmarse, el iPhone 18e sería el único modelo de la próxima camada con esta plataforma de cámara, ya que los demás equipos filtrados mantendrían esquemas distintos.
Un módulo de cámara cuadrado es una estructura elevada y delimitada en la parte trasera del teléfono que agrupa lente, flash y micrófono en un mismo bloque, a diferencia de los recortes individuales que Apple usa en sus modelos de entrada. Este formato, ya presente en el iPad Pro M5, otorgaría al iPhone 18e una apariencia más cercana a la de los modelos Pro.
Qué otros cambios traerían el iPhone 18 y el iPhone Air 2
Los mismos archivos de diseño incluyen, además del iPhone 18e, los CAD del iPhone 18 básico y del iPhone Air 2, ambos con lanzamiento previsto para marzo de 2027. En el caso del iPhone 18 estándar, el diseño general se mantendría sin cambios, pero el módulo de cámara pasaría de un grosor de 3,45 milímetros (0,14 pulgadas) a 3,8 milímetros (0,15 pulgadas).
Apple ha utilizado el mismo sensor Sony IMX904 de 48 megapíxeles en sus modelos básicos desde el iPhone 15, por lo que un módulo más grueso podría anticipar la llegada de nuevos sensores o de cámaras con prestaciones mejoradas.
El iPhone Air 2, por su parte, confirmaría a través de estas imágenes CAD los rumores previos sobre la incorporación de una segunda cámara trasera, una demanda recurrente tras las críticas que recibió la primera generación del equipo por contar con una sola lente.
El teléfono ultrafino de Apple conservaría su grosor de 5,6 milímetros (0,22 pulgadas), aunque el módulo de cámara también crecería de 3,45 milímetros (0,14 pulgadas) a 3,8 milímetros (0,15 pulgadas), con las dos lentes dispuestas de forma horizontal.
Mark Gurman, de Bloomberg, el filtrador conocido como Digital Chat Station y el analista Jeff Pu habían adelantado que Apple sumaría una lente ultra gran angular a la segunda generación del Air, un dato que ahora las imágenes CAD respaldarían.
Qué pasará con la pantalla y el recorte frontal
Más allá de los cambios en la parte trasera, las filtraciones apuntan a que el iPhone 18 y el iPhone Air 2 mantendrán la pantalla con Dynamic Island que ya utilizan los modelos actuales, en lugar de adoptar el recorte más pequeño que incorporó el iPhone 18 Pro.
Esto marcaría una diferencia de diseño entre la gama Pro y los modelos estándar o económicos, que seguirían un camino propio en cuanto a la interfaz frontal, incluso cuando se acerquen a los modelos más caros en el diseño de sus cámaras traseras.
Apple todavía dispone de varios meses antes de que estos dispositivos lleguen a las tiendas el próximo año, por lo que los cambios reflejados en las imágenes CAD podrían modificarse o descartarse antes del lanzamiento final.

articles.title: Profitez du Black Friday pour passer à l’éclairage connecté : le pack Philips Hue Entertainment perd 130€ chez Boulanger
articles.text:
Le pack Philips Hue Entertainment permet d’équiper un téléviseur d’un système d’éclairage synchronisé, et associe à cela une lampe à poser Hue Play. Durant le Black Friday de Boulanger, l’ensemble passe de 299,99 € à 169,99 €.
Si le système Ambilight de Philips vous attire, mais que vous n’avez pas envie d’acheter un téléviseur de cette marque pour autant, alors cette alternative peut vous intéresser. Il s’agit du pack Philips Hue Entertainment, actuellement disponible pour 169,99 € chez Boulanger. Ce dernier permet d’installer un système similaire à Ambilight sur un téléviseur de 65 pouces au maximum, de n’importe quelle marque. En complément, une lampe à poser Hue Play est fournie, pour prolonger l’ambiance lumineuse.
Le pack Philips Hue Entertainment est disponible à 169,99 € chez Boulanger, contre un prix de référence de 299,99 €.
Pourquoi choisir le pack Philips Hue Entertainment ?
- Pour accompagner vos films et vos jeux : les éclairages reproduisent les couleurs présentes à l’écran afin de créer une ambiance autour du téléviseur.
- Pour son fonctionnement astucieux : la caméra analyse directement l’image, y compris lorsque vous regardez une plateforme de streaming depuis votre TV.
- Pour personnaliser votre installation : l’application Hue permet d’ajuster les effets et l’intensité lumineuse selon vos préférences.
Des éclairages synchronisés avec l’image à l’écran
La caméra Play Screen Sync s’installe au sommet du téléviseur. Grâce à son objectif fisheye, elle scrute l’écran puis adapte les éclairages au contenu. Pour profiter de cette immersion, il faut prendre le temps d’installer le ruban lumineux LED Play gradient de 2,5 mètres à l’arrière de votre téléviseur. Pour ce qui est de la lampe Hue Play, vous pouvez l’installer où vous voulez, à condition de disposer d’une prise secteur pour la brancher.
Un ruban qui fonctionne sans pont Hue
L’avantage de l’association entre la caméra Hue Play Screen Sync et le ruban LED Play gradient, c’est qu’elle gère la synchronisation toute seule et offre un grand choix de personnalisation via l’application Philips Hue. Néanmoins, si le ruban peut être synchronisé seul sans pont, un Hue Bridge vendu séparément est nécessaire pour synchroniser également la lampe à poser du pack.
✅ Les points forts
- Synchronisation avec tous les programmes présents à l’écran.
- Ruban lumineux et lampe à poser réunis dans le pack.
- Aucun changement nécessaire dans les branchements HDMI.
❌ Les limites
- Hue Bridge nécessaire pour synchroniser plusieurs éclairages.
- Caméra visible et sensible aux reflets sur l’écran.
Boulanger propose ce pack Philips Hue à 169,99 €, une offre intéressante pour bien démarrer dans l’éclairage connecté.
Pour renforcer l’immersion de vos séances de gaming et de cinéma, ce pack Philips Hue Entertainment peut représenter un bon investissement. Si vous disposez déjà d’un pont Hue à votre domicile, vous aurez accès à davantage d’options, dont la synchronisation de la lampe à poser. Sans pont, seul le ruban pourra suivre l’image.
Prenez cependant en compte que le ruban LED Play gradient compris dans ce pack est destiné à un téléviseur de 65 pouces au maximum. Il peut être découpé pour ajuster sa longueur, en suivant scrupuleusement le mode d'emploi de Philips.

articles.title: I’ve tested 7 gaming headsets while playing GTA 6 for 130 hours, from budget bangers to premium planars, and I'd recommend any one of them this Black Friday
articles.text:
I've now clocked up around 130 hours in Grand Theft Auto 6 and have been using a host of different gadgets since booting it up for the very first time for review last month.
One of the areas of gaming hardware I know most about is headsets, and I've been able to test a fair few while playing GTA 6. From premium planar sets to mid-range open-backers, to budget-friendly reliable wired headsets, I've really mixed it up with my Vice City audio experience.
And getting the most out of your sound and audio is something you'll want to consider with GTA 6: it's got some incredible audio design, sound effects, and use of music, which only pulls you further into the game if you've got some awesome gear to immerse you deeper.
This isn't an exhaustive list by any means, but a short list of the sets I've been able to test and why they might be good ones to look out for if you're after something to enhance your Vice City audio experience.
Audeze Maxwell 2 ANC and 'regular' Maxwell 2 — planar brilliance
My absolute favorite gaming headsets of the day for pure quality audio were always going to be one of my top picks for and best experiences in GTA 6.
The planar magnetic drivers of the Maxwell 2 and Maxwell2 ANC are a huge joy for listening to the world and soundscape of Leonida. The detail of the audio is extraordinary to begin with, but then being able to hear all of it so clearly through the Maxwell 2's drivers is truly excellent. And even when things get their most chaotic in car crashes and high-octane gunfights with gangs, you'll still be able to hear clearly.
The Maxwell 2 ANC then offers you the extra welcome functionality of just shutting off the outside world by enabling the noise cancellation — and it won't kill the bass, either.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Beyerdynamic MMX 130 wireless
If you're looking for a gaming headset that's in the 'slightly north of $100 / £100' price bracket, then the recently released Beyerdynamic MMX 130 Wireless is one of the easiest headsets to recommend. It's such a good headset, and at such a good price.
I have loved using this headset, and have probably used it the second most out of all the products listed here. It's an open-back beauty that channels all the audio brilliance and pedigree of Beyerdynamic to make for a fantastically expansive soundscape experience, which has been a joy.
It's simple to use and get going with, has no complicated parts, and is also fabulously comfortable, so you won't even remember you're wearing it in those long, long hours in Vice City.
SteelSeries Arctis Nova 1
If you really need to keep the budget down when thinking about a headset for GTA 6, then the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 1 is a belter of a headset that won't cost you much, and if you don't mind being tethered to your controller, it will offer you a cracking audio experience.
While it sits at the budget end of SteelSeries' headset range, it still shares a lot of the same pedigree, standards, and audio quality that the very top of the brand's line offers — see below for more on those.
At its core, it has the same 40-mm neodymium drivers as other more expensive headsets in the SteelSeries range, which offer excellent audio quality of all kinds, and while its build might not be quite as robust or premium-feeling or changeable through a companion app, it's comfortable to wear, has easy-to-handle controls, and is spectacular value for money — especially in sales periods when you can pick one up for a song.
Turtle Beach Stealth Pro 2 — Superb superhuman hearing
I knew the Turtle Beach Stealth Pro 2 headset would likely be a great fit for Leonida — we did give it a full five stars after all — but I have been really taken with this headset, particularly when it comes to gunfire, deep and rumbling noises, and, in particular, that Superhuman Hearing feature.
These are the kind of things that Turtle Beach headsets have always done well anyway: proper gaming audio that accentuates the big and bombastic noises such as gunfire, crashes, chaos, high-octane impacts, and more.
However, with a touch of that Superhuman Hearing button to engage the feature, the headset offers a whole new level of immersion; details become more detailed (somehow), everything becomes clearer, and as a result, the immersion is greater. A fabulous choice for GTA 6.
SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni
One of my favorite headset releases of the year: the Nova Pro Omni from SteelSeries is such a great Swiss Army Knife of a gaming headset and one that's perfect to deploy for GTA 6.
As well as offering that excellent default SteelSeries audio quality right out of the box, it's got a whole host of 2026-ifications that make it a world-beater of a multiplatform headset. It builds upon the Nova Pro Wireless beautifully with a host of comfort and design benefits such as plush earcups and a ratcheted volume wheel, excellent battery life for those long hours driving across Vice City, and brilliant, certified Hi-Res wireless audio.
I've found it a particularly excellent option for playing GTA 6 on my PS5 Pro as part of a PC-and-console setup — it's a single headset solution to a multiplatform setup and makes it perfect for playing and absorbing the game on one platform, while being able to enjoy media, look up guides, or devour albums of music from artists from the game all in the comfort of one seat.
SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite
But the only real problem I have with the above Nova Pro Omni is that the Nova Elite exists, and I could test that straight after.
Both are wonderful headsets that I'd encourage anyone to go for if they are considering; however, the Nova Elite really does just offer something extra on the audio quality front. It just sounds better. Those custom carbon fiber drivers and the brass ring surround do seem to offer a level of audio brilliance that's both of the SteelSeries style and quality, but simultaneously better than the other SteelSeries headsets.
So if you had narrowed it down to one or the other of SteelSeries' premium headsets, then it might just be the sheer audio quality and prowess of the Elite that wins you over — as it did with me in GTA 6, as everything just sounded sharper, clearer, and offered more depth and richness, be it sirens from afar, vocal tones from NPCs, or the chaotic barrages of music and gunfights at the same time.

articles.title: Hackers Compromise 24 Check Point Management Servers in Suspected AI-Driven Attack Campaign
articles.text:
An unknown threat actor has been using artificial intelligence (AI)-driven offensive tooling in a campaign targeting Check Point Security Management servers, impacting 22 distinct organizations across the world.
The intrusion activity, tracked by GreyNoise under the moniker GreyNoise Threat 13 (GT13), is assessed to have targeted organizations in the financial services, energy, government, transportation, mining, engineering, and manufacturing sectors across the U.K., Ireland, France, Netherlands, Greece, Germany, Austria, Bulgaria, Poland, India, Thailand, Vietnam, South Korea, Hong Kong, China, Australia, and the U.S.
Confirmed attack activity has been recorded between October 17 and November 2, 2026, with the threat actor using 99 IP addresses to conduct scanning, exploitation, and control. Most of these IP addresses are associated with disposable network infrastructure.
The campaign has not been attributed to any known threat actor or group. It's suspected that the attackers are relying on agentic harnesses and systems for vulnerability scanning, exploitation, and automatic interaction with compromised assets.
The threat actor has also been observed using tools like Nmap, Chisel, Impacket, Paramiko, and other Python scripts to carry out internal reconnaissance, privilege escalation, and lateral movement on victim environments.
"We witnessed the GT13 actor use 99 IP addresses, all of which were either egresses through ExpressVPN or compromised victim Check Point devices, including activity over 1400+ network sessions, 800+ command line artifacts, and 1200+ files downloaded, uploaded, or created," GreyNoise said.
In one case, the attackers have been found using an automated scanning and exploitation pipeline to compromise an HFS server using CVE-2026-61500, a critical flaw in Rejetto HFS, in early October 2026 to obtain control of the server and issue commands, including adding an SSH key to the "/root/.ssh/authorized_keys" file.
Subsequently, GT13 is said to have used the compromised server as a relay for follow-on operations centered around saving command results and exfiltrating data from 24 previously compromised Check Point Security Management servers. The attackers also unsuccessfully attempted to deploy a Linux implant named ZULT to the compromised Rejetto HFS server.
"The GT13 adversary had access to the victim Check Point Security Management Servers before they compromised the HFS server," the cybersecurity company said. "We could not determine when or how the attacker gained access to those Check Point assets."
The attackers also moved to burrow deeper into one of the victim networks, using a script for a now-patched Check Point flaw (CVE-2026-16232) to launch over 100 management tasks on multiple Check Point Management Servers to -
- Steal firewall databases and internal certificate authority files
- Mint a new certificate
- Unload security policies, effectively disabling firewall protections
- Conduct internal network reconnaissance and attempt lateral movement
The post-compromise activity also involved attempts to target other enterprise systems, such as Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2023-4966), Ivanti Connect Secure (CVE-2024-21893), VMware vCenter (CVE-2021-21972 and CVE-2023-34048), Microsoft Exchange (CVE-2021-26855 and CVE-2021-34473), and Microsoft Netlogon (CVE-2020-1472).
In tandem, the threat actor has attempted to exploit various other security flaws, including, but not limited to -
- CVE-2024-21893 (Ivanti Connect Secure)
- CVE-2025-5777 (Citrix NetScaler)
- CVE-2026-41089 (Windows Netlogon)
- CVE-2026-98432 (Linux IPv4 UAF)
GreyNoise has theorized that GT13 has in its possession a "mature AI-enabled offensive apparatus" that it uses to weaponize vulnerabilities, scan for susceptible assets, and exploit them to gain access to systems that can be later used as operational relays or true targets.
"The activity reported by the GreyNoise article involves CVE-2026-16232, a previously disclosed vulnerability with patches already available, and does not represent a new vulnerability or exploitation technique," Sergey Shykevich, Director, Threat Intelligence at Check Point Software Technologies, told The Hacker News.
"Our priority remains ensuring customers apply the available updates and follow Check Point’s published hardening guidance to restrict management access and identify suspicious activity."

articles.title: Las 5 preguntas que ponen a Nvidia bajo la lupa tras el regreso de Jensen Huang
articles.text:
La junta directiva de Nvidia aprobó la restitución de Jensen Huang al frente de la compañía tras su renuncia la semana pasada, una maniobra con fuerte impacto político en Estados Unidos. La vuelta del directivo a la firma líder en inteligencia artificial desató una fuerte controversia en el Capitolio, luego de que Donald Trump confirmara su intervención directa ante la junta directiva para facilitar el retorno.
El nuevo mandato de Huang coloca a la corporación bajo la lupa institucional por cinco interrogantes clave sobre seguridad nacional, presiones partidarias, litigios societarios, barreras comerciales y la viabilidad del negocio tecnológico. Estas dudas amenazan el equilibrio diplomático con China, comprometen la relación de la empresa con los reguladores en Washington y siembran incertidumbre entre los inversores acerca del modelo corporativo del fabricante.
Nigel Green, director ejecutivo de la firma de asesoría financiera deVere Group, advirtió a CBS News que tres pruebas definirán el futuro de la firma: su encaje con el poder político, la gestión del vínculo con el mercado asiático y el ritmo de inversión en el sector.
¿Comprometió Nvidia la seguridad nacional frente al nuevo escrutinio de Donald Trump?
El foco más sensible apunta a la relación entre la tecnológica y Megaspeed, una firma de centros de datos con sede en Singapur. Informes de los servicios de inteligencia de Estados Unidos sospechan que una empresaria china vinculada a esa compañía, quien mantuvo una relación personal con Jensen Huang, realizó labores de espionaje para China.
De acuerdo con las pesquisas en curso, existen acusaciones contra Megaspeed por la presunta introducción clandestina de chips avanzados en territorio chino y por la habilitación de accesos remotos a esa tecnología prohibida. Los presidentes republicanos de comités en la Cámara de Representantes señalaron que la breve investigación interna del directorio no borra las amenazas a la seguridad del país, por lo que estas sospechas todavía carecen de resolución judicial definitiva.
¿Qué papel tuvo Donald Trump en la sorpresiva restitución de Jensen Huang?
El propio Donald Trump confirmó en declaraciones públicas que intervino de manera directa e indirecta ante la junta directiva para asegurar el regreso del magnate. Esta admisión desató el reclamo de miembros del Congreso, quienes exigen indagatorias formales sobre el alcance de esas presiones políticas y buscan esclarecer si la cúpula de Nvidia eludió de forma deliberada las restricciones de exportación vigentes.
Este escrutinio político expone a la compañía a un desgaste institucional en el Capitolio, donde diversos sectores temen que los intereses de la industria de la inteligencia artificial queden subordinados a conveniencias políticas particulares o concesiones al gobierno.
¿Qué litigios y riesgos financieros encara Nvidia en el nuevo escenario de Washington?
La restitución del directivo abre la puerta a múltiples querellas colectivas por parte de accionistas descontentos. Charles Elson, director fundador del Centro John L. Weinberg de Gobierno Corporativo de la Universidad de Delaware, explicó que los inversores disponen de un amplio abanico de causales para iniciar acciones legales.
El principal motivo radica en la omisión de información sensible al público inversor, en particular sobre las acusaciones de espionaje y los nexos con Megaspeed. A este frente se suma un litigio presentado este mes contra el fabricante por ocultar presuntos vínculos personales de Huang con subordinadas y con una exejecutiva de la firma de centros de datos, conductas que quebrantan el código interno de ética empresarial.
¿Cómo afectará a Nvidia la intensificación de las trabas comerciales con China y Asia?
El cerco regulatorio sobre la venta de microprocesadores amenaza con reducir de modo drástico los ingresos internacionales de Nvidia. El Departamento de Comercio de Estados Unidos impuso este mes nuevas trabas a las transferencias tecnológicas hacia Singapur, Malasia, Indonesia, Tailandia y Brasil para evitar desvíos hacia China.
Cody Acree, analista de investigación patrimonial de StoneX, remarcó a CBS News que las operaciones directas con el mercado chino constituirán el foco central de supervisión estatal.
Por su parte, Gil Luria, especialista principal de la firma de inversiones D.A. Davidson, pronosticó que el endurecimiento de los controles aduaneros provocará la pérdida definitiva de ese negocio para el fabricante en Asia.
¿Podrá sostenerse el negocio de la inteligencia artificial ante las nuevas presiones políticas?
La estructura operativa de Nvidia exhibe una alta dependencia de su fundador, quien antes de su renuncia concentraba más de 60 reportes directos sin un esquema de sucesión formal. Este personalismo genera inquietud institucional, aunque los mercados celebraron su regreso debido a su capacidad para articular el financiamiento del sector.
La empresa opera como un banco informal de la industria al aportar capital a firmas emergentes, como OpenAI, que luego destinan esos fondos a comprar sus procesadores. Sin embargo, James Reilly, economista senior de Capital Economics, advirtió que existen dudas profundas sobre si las inversiones en inteligencia artificial generarán los ingresos suficientes a largo plazo para asegurar la rentabilidad del negocio.
El desenlace institucional comenzará a perfilarse el 1 y 2 de diciembre, cuando Jensen Huang y el asesor jurídico general Tim Teter comparezcan en sesiones a puertas cerradas ante comités del Congreso de Estados Unidos.
Al día siguiente, el 3 de diciembre, Huang asistirá a una audiencia pública convocada por el Comité Bancario del Senado para responder sobre normativas aduaneras, sospechas de espionaje y la rivalidad tecnológica global. Estas comparecencias marcarán el rumbo regulatorio y corporativo que determinará la estabilidad definitiva de la compañía.
