articles.title: Justiça condena oito pessoas por pirataria da Sky
articles.text:
Justiça condena oito pessoas por pirataria da Sky
Maior pena passou dos 15 anos de prisão. Grupo vendia receptores e chaves para liberar canais via satélite.
A Justiça Federal condenou oito pessoas envolvidas em um esquema que vendia receptores de TV via satélite e chaves para liberar canais pagos sem autorização. O grupo atuou entre 2013 e 2017, com fornecedores no Paraguai e revendedores em Porto Alegre. A Sky participou do processo como assistente de acusação.
A sentença foi assinada em 10 de novembro pelo juiz federal Lademiro Dors Filho, da 7ª Vara Federal de Porto Alegre. Todos os condenados poderão recorrer em liberdade. O chefe do núcleo fornecedor no Paraguai recebeu a maior pena: 15 anos, três meses e 20 dias de prisão, em regime inicial fechado.
O esquema utilizava o card sharing, ou compartilhamento de chaves. Segundo explicações da Sky anexadas ao processo, os decodificadores oficiais usam cartões criptográficos para liberar a programação transmitida via satélite. Na modalidade de pirataria, dados de cartões legítimos são copiados e distribuídos pela internet a vários usuários. Além dos aparelhos, o grupo oferecia suporte para renovar o acesso à programação.
As defesas sustentaram que os aparelhos eram receptores de canais abertos e questionaram sua capacidade de captar programação paga. O juiz considerou que o contrabando estava demonstrado pela entrada clandestina dos equipamentos sem homologação da Anatel. Já a venda de acesso aos canais foi comprovada por diálogos interceptados, códigos comercializados e depoimentos.
Os fornecedores mantinham uma empresa no Paraguai e abasteciam dois núcleos de revenda em Porto Alegre. Os receptores também entravam no Brasil sem documentação fiscal em remessas semanais ou quinzenais.
A sentença reconheceu 117 entradas clandestinas de mercadorias: 59 destinadas à Aztime e 58 à Azmegashop. Em um dos depósitos, a Polícia Federal apreendeu 446 receptores, além de planilhas de estoque, códigos de acesso e registros de vendas.
Os oito réus foram condenados por organização criminosa e contrabando. Os líderes dos núcleos também receberam penas por violação de direito autoral e estelionato. Três integrantes também foram punidos por lavagem de dinheiro: dois do núcleo fornecedor no Paraguai e o responsável pela Azmegashop.
As defesas negaram a existência de uma organização estruturada e sustentaram que os acusados mantinham relações comerciais ou profissionais. Os pedidos de absolvição dos oito condenados foram rejeitados e outros dois acusados foram absolvidos por falta de provas.
A decisão também determinou multas e a perda de bens e valores ligados aos crimes em favor da União. O juiz não fixou indenização mínima e os prejuízos das operadoras não foram estimados durante o processo. As empresas ainda poderão buscar compensação na Justiça cível.
A condenação ainda pode ser revista em segunda instância. A consulta ao processo registra apelações apresentadas em 23 de novembro. Esses recursos permitem pedir ao Tribunal Regional Federal da 4ª Região (TRF4) a revisão da sentença.
Em outro caso, divulgado em junho, dois irmãos receberam penas de nove anos e dois meses por operarem um serviço de IPTV pirata em Goiás.

articles.title: Black Friday : le n°1 des antivirus Mac tombe à 65€ pour 2 ans aujourd'hui
articles.text:
Intego affiche 50 % de remise sur sa suite de sécurité pour Mac pour le Black Friday, calculée sur un tarif qui sera aussi celui du renouvellement. Intego ONE Complete, premier de notre comparatif des antivirus pour Mac avec 9,6/10, est facturé 65 € les deux premières années, soit 12,99 € sous son plus bas des 30 derniers jours, mais notre test lui reproche un moteur gourmand en mémoire.
Intego est un nom ancien de la sécurité sur Mac : l’éditeur a été fondé en 1997 et a lancé Intego ONE début avril 2026 pour remplacer Intego X9. La suite réunit dans une seule application l’antivirus, le pare-feu, le nettoyage SmartClean et, dans la formule Complete, le VPN de l’éditeur.
L’offre Intego ONE Complete à 65 € pour deux ans couvre un Mac et un iPhone, avec 50 % de remise affichée par rapport à 129,99 €. Elle s’adresse à celles et ceux qui veulent un antivirus, un pare-feu et un VPN sous une seule facture, sans empiler les abonnements.
Intego ONE Complete pour 1 Mac et 1 iPhone, c’est 65 € pour les deux premières années au lieu de 129,99 €, soit 2,71 € par mois, directement chez Intego.
Pourquoi choisir Intego ONE Complete ?
- Une détection validée par un laboratoire : en mars 2026, AV-TEST a relevé 100 % de détection sur 405 échantillons de malwares macOS, sans faux positif, avec 6/6 en protection, en performance et en utilisation.
- Un VPN dans la même application : notre test salue ses excellentes performances, son kill switch et ses 51 pays, un atout que les formules inférieures d’Intego n’incluent pas.
- Un tarif sous le plus bas récent : à 65 € pour deux ans, soit 2,71 € par mois, l’offre passe 12,99 € sous le plus bas des 30 derniers jours affiché par Intego, 77,99 €.
Protéger un Mac, un iPhone et votre connexion au quotidien
Au quotidien, l’antivirus surveille votre Mac en temps réel, tandis que le pare-feu affiche les applications qui se connectent à Internet et vous laisse bloquer celles de votre choix. Le VPN préserve la confidentialité de votre navigation, avec 51 pays au choix. SmartClean surveille le processeur, la mémoire et le stockage, et nettoie caches, journaux et fichiers de corbeille. Côté iPhone, la page de l’offre annonce une vérification de ses risques de sécurité.
Dans notre test d’Intego ONE, nous avons salué une interface claire et un VPN convaincant, mais relevé un moteur anti-malware qui occupe environ 1,3 Go de mémoire hors analyse. Sur notre MacBook M1 de 8 Go, un scan complet a duré 26 minutes, avec une latence d’environ une seconde dans les actions courantes. Cette suite convient donc mieux à un Mac récent ou bien doté en mémoire, et moins à un modèle modeste que vous utilisez pendant les analyses.
Intego face aux suites multi-appareils de Bitdefender et Norton
Intego ONE Complete mise sur un Mac et un iPhone, quand Bitdefender Total Security, deuxième de notre comparatif des meilleurs antivirus pour Mac, couvre 3 à 10 appareils et ajoute anti-phishing, anti-ransomware et contrôle parental, trois protections absentes d’Intego ONE. Norton 360, troisième, vise les familles avec 10 appareils. Intego reste pourtant en tête chez nous grâce à sa conception pour macOS et à son VPN. Si vous protégez un seul Mac, c’est l’argument qui compte ; si toute la famille doit être couverte, regardez ailleurs.
✅ Les points forts
- Premier de notre comparatif des antivirus pour Mac, noté 9,6/10
- Note maximale chez AV-TEST en mars 2026
- VPN avec kill switch inclus dans la formule Complete
- Un Mac et un iPhone couverts pour 65 € pendant deux ans
- Garantie satisfait ou remboursé de 30 jours
❌ Les limites
- Renouvellement automatique à 129,99 € tous les deux ans
- Moteur anti-malware lourd en mémoire, scan complet de 26 minutes sur notre Mac de test
- Ni anti-phishing, ni anti-ransomware, ni contrôle parental
- Pare-feu très directif au premier lancement
Si le renouvellement à 129,99 € ne vous freine pas, la garantie de 30 jours satisfait ou remboursé permet d’essayer Intego ONE Complete sur votre propre Mac.
La remise de 50 % se mesure par rapport à 129,99 €, un prix qui est aussi celui du renouvellement. Le gain réel se lit plutôt face au plus bas des 30 derniers jours : 12,99 € de moins, soit près de 17 %. Pour un Mac et un iPhone couverts deux ans, avec antivirus, pare-feu et VPN, la facture de 2,71 € par mois reste mesurée.
Cette offre s’adresse au propriétaire d’un Mac récent qui veut une suite pensée pour macOS, VPN compris, et qui accepte de repasser à 129,99 € au renouvellement. Elle convaincra moins si vous devez protéger plusieurs appareils ou toute une famille, car Bitdefender et Norton en couvrent davantage et ajoutent des protections absentes ici. Avant de payer, notez dans votre agenda la date du renouvellement : c’est à ce moment que le tarif change vraiment.

articles.title: No GPS required: Ukrainian 11th-grader creates AI drone navigation system
articles.text:
No Starlink, no problem, part deux: Ukrainian student invents autopilot system for UAV that works without GPS, receives "The future of Ukraine" presidential award
Ukrainian teenager builds an AI-powered drone guidance system
- Ukrainian teenager develops drone autopilot capable of operating without GPS signals
- 11th-grade student Yaroslav Sheiko receives Ukraine's presidential award for drone innovations
- Artificial intelligence powers the student's GPS-independent drone navigation technology
A Ukrainian high school student has developed drone technology capable of guiding unmanned aircraft without depending on satellite navigation systems.
Yaroslav Sheiko, an 11th-grade pupil from Poltava, received the presidential distinction known as "The Future of Ukraine" for his engineering achievements.
His work includes an artificial intelligence-powered flight control system and optical-electronic stabilization technology designed for unmanned aerial vehicles.
Ukrainian student develops drone navigation technology without GPS
Sheiko's main innovation involves an autonomous guidance system that allows drones to reach designated destinations without relying on conventional satellite positioning signals.
The technology is designed to help unmanned aircraft maintain their intended flight paths when GPS and other global navigation services become unavailable.
According to information released by Poltava's municipal education department, the student has been developing engineering solutions for unmanned aerial vehicles.
His navigation system enables an aircraft to independently approach a location selected by its operator while flying relatively close to the ground.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
This capability addresses a major difficulty facing drone operators when electronic interference disrupts satellite navigation signals during flight.
GPS jamming and spoofing can interfere with conventional navigation equipment, potentially preventing aircraft from maintaining accurate positioning.
Sheiko's work also includes optical-electronic stabilization equipment incorporating artificial intelligence for improved drone control and navigation.
Such equipment can help maintain stable observations and support guidance when conventional satellite-based positioning becomes unreliable.
However, there is no information on the precise sensors, algorithms, or computational hardware powering his navigation system.
Details about its operational testing, navigation accuracy, maximum range, and performance under different environmental conditions have also not been disclosed.
Without further technical details, it remains difficult to determine how his invention compares with existing GPS-independent navigation systems.
Nevertheless, receiving national recognition while still attending secondary school is a major achievement for the young Ukrainian engineer.
Presidential award follows several international science competition victories
The "The Future of Ukraine" distinction adds another achievement to Sheiko's growing record of recognition in engineering and scientific competitions.
He has previously received presidential scholarships on two occasions, recognizing his performance and contributions to scientific research.
The student has also secured first place twice in nationwide competitions organized by Ukraine's Junior Academy of Sciences.
His entries competed within the aerospace and defense technology category, focusing on engineering developments relevant to unmanned systems.
International competitions have also featured his inventions, including the INOVA 2025 International Inventions Show, where he secured a gold medal.
He additionally received a silver medal in the 2025 Hackathon, adding another international achievement to his academic record.
His latest presidential award recognizes his contributions to drone engineering, particularly developments involving autonomous navigation and electronic stabilization.
Ukraine's continuing efforts to maintain drone operations despite electronic interference have also encouraged interest in alternative communication technologies.
The country has been exploring alternatives to Starlink for maintaining drone communications when satellite connectivity becomes unavailable during military operations.
It recently reportedly combined airborne relay systems with Israeli-Italian satellite communications technology to provide alternative links for unmanned aircraft.
While these systems maintain communication with operators, Sheiko's invention addresses another challenge by allowing drones to navigate without GPS signals.

articles.title: Com-Affiliated Hackers Hijack Cloud Accounts via Vishing for Data Theft and Extortion
articles.text:
Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 has disclosed that it's tracking and has responded to "numerous waves of vishing attacks" orchestrated by Com-affiliated threat actors since August 2026 that have led to data theft and extortion attempts.
The attacks have targeted financial services, healthcare, and legal services located in the U.S., the U.K., and Australia. Other targets include construction, high-technology, transportation, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, insurance, and real estate sectors.
"The victims share a common profile: they hold large volumes of high-impact corporate data where exposure carries severe regulatory, legal, or market consequences," Unit 42 said. "These attackers targeted financial services organizations about twice as often as healthcare organizations in August 2026, but healthcare overtook financial services in September."
The activity has been attributed to a number of threat clusters, including -
- Bling Libra (aka ShinyHunters)
- CL-CRI-1116 (aka Redact, formerly BlackFile), first observed in January 2026
- CL-CRI-1147 (aka Pink), first observed in May 2026
- CL-CRI-1182 (aka Falcon), first observed in mid-2026
- CL-CRI-1192 (aka Helix and UNC6671), first observed in June 2026
- CL-CRI-1264 (aka Vortex), first observed in September 2026
- CL-CRI-1274 (aka Cinder), first observed in September 2026
Intrusions typically commence with voice phishing, with the attackers posing as IT staff to resolve a purported authentication issue and direct the victim to a phishing page personalized to their organization.
Once the AiTM kit captures credentials and session tokens, the attackers quickly enroll their own multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices, abuse cloud utilities and, in a few instances, deploy malicious browser extensions to exfiltrate data and extort victims.
The harvested authentication data is used to authenticate to victim environments, typically by routing such requests through residential proxy networks and commercial VPNs. The adversaries then seek to establish multi-layered persistence by registering their MFA devices, generating cloud infrastructure temporary credentials, authorizing unapproved third-party OAuth applications; enumerate sensitive data; evade defenses by modifying mailbox rules and clearing security alert events; and harvest data from cloud platforms.
"Attackers associated with CL-CRI-1264 establish initial access through vishing, where they pose as internal IT support and direct employees to servers using subdomains tailored to each targeted organization," Unit 42 said.
"These servers act as adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) proxies that pass user credentials and multi-factor authentication (MFA) approvals to the attackers in real time. Attackers have targeted employees on both their corporate workstations and personal mobile devices."
CL-CRI-1264 has also been observed enrolling unauthorized MFA devices within minutes of authenticating to establish persistence, often reusing a single device named Pixel 10a across compromised accounts. The attack chains involve automated data exfiltration using Python scripts to harvest information from Microsoft 365 mailbox, OneDrive, and SharePoint.
Once data is exfiltrated, the threat actor sends Microsoft Teams messages directly to employees at victim organizations, claiming data theft and instructing them to visit a TOR-hosted ransom negotiation site.
The second new cluster to emerge around the same time is CL-CRI-1274, which has also leaned on vishing for initial access and leveraged the Microsoft Graph software development kit (SDK) to collect and exfiltrate data from the victim's SharePoint and OneDrive environments.
"Afterwards, the attackers used a compromised account to send extortion messages internally via email and Microsoft Teams, ultimately directing recipients to a Tor-hosted negotiation site," Unit 42 said.
The cybersecurity company said it also observed the CL-CRI-1192 attackers using a malicious browser extension named "Google Chrome" that's said to have been sideloaded onto the browser after enabling Developer Mode. The add-on performs a number of malicious actions, such as -
- Installing global keyloggers
- Stealing local/session storage and authentication cookies for Microsoft and Google accounts
- Scanning pages for QR codes to capture login/MFA tokens
- Streaming webcam feeds
- Implementing a command-and-control (C2) remote control module via Chrome DevTools Protocol to capture screenshots, dispatch input events, steal clipboard contents, and allow remote site navigation.
"We assess with moderate confidence that the attackers associated with CL-CRI-1192 developed this malicious browser extension as an alternative method to extract credentials from desktop and laptop devices running Chromium-based browsers such as Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge," Unit 42 said.
"The extension might also be shared with and used by other Com-affiliated attackers, although we currently have no evidence to suggest this."
One of the defining traits of the threat actors is their use of "apex" domains that impersonate single sign-on (SSO) portals, IT support pages, and passkey configuration services for each of the targeted organizations.
Also shared among the attackers is an AitM phishing kit called Doko's Panel that allows them to steal authenticated sessions and then abuse them to access connected software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms like SharePoint, Salesforce, DocuSign, and Slack to exfiltrate data of interest.
"The same persona behind Doko's Panel has been observed actively recruiting 'experienced callers' via Telegram, specifying requirements including fluent English with no accent, and advertising six-to-seven-figure weekly returns — evidence of the professionalized vishing-as-a-service model that complements the phishing kit ecosystem," Push Security noted in a report published earlier this May.
Microsoft has also revealed cloud-based intrusions in which threat actors have employed passkey and SSO lures to obtain unauthorized access and add their own authentication methods to set up persistence, as well as conduct high-volume Microsoft Graph activity, SharePoint and OneDrive downloads, and mailbox collection through REST APIs.
"Rather than employing custom tools, the threat actors primarily leveraged native cloud utilities and selectively limited executions and persistence deployments," Unit 42 said. "Cybercriminals like Bling Libra and other Com-affiliated threat actors are pivoting away from encryption, enabling them to move at greater speed across their intrusion lifecycle while still achieving their objectives."

articles.title: Tidal eliminará cerca de 29 millones de canciones creadas con IA
articles.text:
Tidal eliminará cerca de 29 millones de canciones creadas íntegramente con inteligencia artificial a partir del 9 de diciembre de 2026. La plataforma de streaming confirmó que, además, rechazará entre 80.000 y 85.000 pistas diarias generadas por IA una vez entre en vigor la prohibición.
El anuncio lo realizó Robert Andersen, responsable de música de Tidal, a través de una publicación en X. Según sus datos, la música generada por IA representó el 43% de las canciones distribuidas a la plataforma durante los últimos 90 días, una cifra que llevó a la empresa a endurecer su política.
Por qué Tidal decidió prohibir la música de inteligencia artificial
La decisión de Tidal responde a un crecimiento que la plataforma considera insostenible: casi la mitad de todo el contenido que recibía en los últimos tres meses provenía de generadores de IA. Ante ese volumen, la empresa optó por pasar de las medidas parciales a una prohibición total.
El servicio de música en streaming había comenzado meses atrás a etiquetar y desmonetizar las canciones identificadas como generadas íntegramente por inteligencia artificial. Sin embargo, Andersen explicó que esa estrategia resultó insuficiente frente al ritmo de crecimiento del fenómeno.
El ejecutivo también aportó un dato que, según él, respalda la medida desde la perspectiva del oyente: el 96% de las canciones generadas por IA no recibe ninguna reproducción.
“Creemos que esto tendrá repercusión tanto para los artistas como para los oyentes, dado que el 96% de las canciones generadas por IA no reciben ninguna reproducción”, afirmó Andersen.
En qué consiste la prohibición de música de inteligencia artificial en Tidal se resume en una medida concreta: a partir del 9 de diciembre, la plataforma bloqueará el ingreso de canciones creadas exclusivamente con IA y borrará de su catálogo las que ya identificó bajo esa categoría, afectando a unos 29 millones de temas.
Cómo funcionará el bloqueo a distribuidores y canciones generadas por IA
Tidal no se limitará a retirar canciones ya publicadas. La plataforma también prohibirá a los distribuidores de música enviar pistas creadas con inteligencia artificial, lo que implica un filtro previo a la llegada de ese contenido al catálogo.
Para sostener ese control, la plataforma utilizará la herramienta de detección de IA Ircam Amplify junto con comprobaciones de metadatos, mecanismos pensados para rechazar las canciones generadas exclusivamente con esta tecnología antes de que lleguen a los oyentes.
La empresa fue explícita respecto a los límites de su política: no prohibirá las canciones creadas con la ayuda de herramientas de IA, siempre y cuando la inteligencia artificial no sea el único resultado del proceso creativo.
La distinción busca proteger a artistas que incorporan estas herramientas como parte de un proceso con intervención humana, sin alcanzar a la producción íntegramente automatizada.
En una publicación aparte en X, Tidal detalló el problema que busca combatir con esta política. “La música generada íntegramente por IA, con la intención de engañar a los oyentes e imitar a los artistas, es otro problema grave que no ha hecho más que aumentar: desvía las reproducciones y los derechos de autor de los artistas y confunde a los fans”, señaló la plataforma.
Qué otras plataformas de streaming combaten la música generada por IA
Tidal no es la única plataforma que endurece su postura frente a la música generada por inteligencia artificial. Bandcamp prohibió este tipo de contenido a principios de este año, una medida previa a la que ahora adopta Tidal.
Otras plataformas de streaming musical optaron por enfoques distintos, basados en etiquetado y ajustes algorítmicos en lugar de prohibiciones totales. Spotify anunció recientemente que eliminó 50 millones de canciones basura y spam de IA de las recomendaciones durante el último año.
Spotify también lanzó nuevas insignias de “persona de IA” para los artistas que usan una identidad de inteligencia artificial, una forma de transparencia dirigida a que los oyentes identifiquen el origen del contenido sin necesariamente eliminarlo del catálogo.
Por su parte, YouTube implementó etiquetas de música de IA, sumándose a una tendencia de la industria que combina distintas estrategias: desde el etiquetado y la desmonetización hasta la eliminación directa, como ahora aplicará Tidal a partir de diciembre.

articles.title: AMD Ryzen™ 7 9800X3D à 399,99 € : Grosbill muscle son Black Friday
articles.text:
Vous envisagez de donner un coup de fouet à votre PC gaming ou de renouveler une configuration un peu vieillissante ? Chez Grosbill, durant le Black Friday, plusieurs processeurs AMD Ryzen™ profitent de remises allant jusqu’à 35 %. De quoi accéder à de belles performances, sans forcément faire un trou dans votre budget de Noël.
Changer de processeur reste l’une des pistes les plus intéressantes pour qui souhaite faire évoluer son ordinateur. Mais avec l’offre disponible, encore faut-il choisir une puce adaptée à ses usages et, surtout, au reste de sa configuration.
Que l’on vise le gaming, le streaming, le montage vidéo ou la création 3D, AMD dispose aujourd’hui d’une gamme AMD Ryzen™ particulièrement complète, capable de répondre à des besoins très variés. Et avec les offres Black Friday proposées par Grosbill, plusieurs références méritent que l’on s’y attarde.
AMD Ryzen™ 9000X3D : AMD met le paquet sur les performances gaming
Commençons par les modèles qui attirent particulièrement l’attention des joueurs : les AMD Ryzen™ X3D. Avec cette gamme, AMD mise sur une technologie qui a largement fait ses preuves, le 3D V-Cache. Sa deuxième génération permet d’empiler de la mémoire cache supplémentaire directement au sein du processeur, afin de réduire les temps d’accès aux données et la latence.
Un avantage qui se révèle particulièrement intéressant dans les jeux vidéo, où le processeur doit traiter une multitude d’informations en permanence.
L’AMD Ryzen™ 7 9800X3D illustre parfaitement cette approche. Basé sur l’architecture Zen 5, il embarque 8 cœurs et 16 threads, avec une fréquence pouvant atteindre 5,2 GHz (mode Turbo) et 96 Mo de cache L3.
Une autre évolution intéressante de cette génération concerne l’organisation du 3D V-Cache, avec une mémoire positionnée sous les cœurs du processeur. Une conception qui favorise leur refroidissement et laisse davantage de marge pour exploiter les fréquences élevées. L’AMD Ryzen™ 7 9800X3D est par ailleurs débloqué pour l’overclocking et compatible avec Precision Boost Overdrive et AMD Ryzen Master, afin d’ajuster ses paramètres selon ses préférences.
La mémoire n’est pas oubliée, avec la prise en charge d’AMD EXPO, qui facilite l’activation de profils optimisés pour la DDR5. Enfin, le socket AM5 et la compatibilité PCIe 5.0 assurent une connectivité moderne, avec de belles possibilités d’évolution pour les configurations compatibles.
Des AMD Ryzen™ 5 aux AMD Ryzen™ 9 : des promotions pour tous les profils
L’autre bonne nouvelle, c’est que les réductions Grosbill ne se limitent absolument pas aux références les plus musclées. L’AMD Ryzen™ 7 9800X3D Tray figure parmi les meilleures ventes de l’enseigne, en voyant son tarif passer de 484,99 € à 399,99 €, soit 85 € d’économie.
Mais les joueurs disposant d’un budget plus serré peuvent également regarder du côté de l’AMD Ryzen™ 7 7800X3D Tray, affiché à 304,99 € au lieu de 469,99 €. Malgré son architecture de génération précédente, il conserve de très sérieux arguments pour jouer dans de bonnes conditions.
D’autres références méritent également un coup d’œil. L’AMD Ryzen™ 5 9600X WOF passe ainsi de 274,99 € à 184,99 €, tandis que l’AMD Ryzen™ 7 9700X WOF descend à 289,99 € au lieu de 379,99 €. Deux modèles Zen 5 polyvalents, adaptés aussi bien au jeu qu’aux usages quotidiens plus exigeants.
Pour les configurations qui réclament davantage de ressources, Grosbill propose aussi des réductions sur les AMD Ryzen™ 9. L’AMD Ryzen™ 9 9900X WOF passe à 344,99 € (au lieu de 469,99 €) et l’AMD Ryzen™ 9 9950X3D WOF à 634,99 € (au lieu de 794,99 €).
Que vous souhaitiez simplement moderniser votre machine ou bâtir une configuration haut de gamme, plusieurs niveaux de performances sont représentés. L’ensemble des références concernées est à retrouver dans la sélection des processeurs AMD en promotion chez Grosbill.
Grosbill et AMD : la performance, sans oublier le prix
Derrière ces promotions, il y a aussi deux acteurs qui se connaissent très bien. Grosbill et AMD collaborent depuis plusieurs années autour des processeurs AMD Ryzen™ et des cartes graphiques Radeon. Les composants sont évidemment proposés à l’unité, mais ils sont également intégrés dans des machines assemblées, avec une ambition commune : « 100 % performance, 100 % prix malin ».
Acteur historique de l’informatique en France, né en octobre 1998, Grosbill s’est notamment construit autour d’un large choix de composants et de tarifs compétitifs. L’enseigne dispose également de magasins de proximité (à Paris, Lyon, Lille, Rouen…), où il est possible de bénéficier de conseils personnalisés et de retirer les produits disponibles en stock. Le SAV est quant à lui accessible en ligne comme en boutique.
Et pour ceux qui préfèrent éviter les joies du montage, Grosbill propose aussi l’assemblage de PC sur mesure. Gaming, bureautique, usage professionnel… Chacun est libre de construire une machine adaptée à ses besoins (et à son budget).
Vous préférez un PC Full AMD déjà assemblé ? C’est possible !
Si vous souhaitez repartir sur une configuration complète plutôt que de changer uniquement votre processeur, Grosbill propose également plusieurs PC fixes associant processeur AMD Ryzen™ et carte graphique Radeon.
Parmi les modèles disponibles, le BLACKEXPERT, équipé d’un AMD Ryzen™ 7 7800X3D et d’une Radeon RX 9070 XT avec 32 Go de RAM et un SSD de 1 To, passe de 2 399,99 € à 2 299,99 €.
Le BLACKMASTER, avec son AMD Ryzen™ 7 9800X3D, sa Radeon RX 9070 XT, ses 32 Go de mémoire et son SSD de 2 To, bénéficie lui aussi de 100 euros de remise, pour un tarif de 2 599,99 euros.
Deux configurations gaming ambitieuses, pensées pour profiter pleinement de l’écosystème AMD sans avoir à sélectionner et assembler chaque composant soi-même. Des offres à retrouver dans la sélection des PC fixes « Full AMD » chez Grosbill.
Avec des AMD Ryzen™ 5, AMD Ryzen™ 7 et AMD Ryzen™ 9 proposés à prix réduit, il serait forcément dommage de ne pas jeter un œil aux offres Grosbill avant de finaliser votre prochain PC.

Esquenta Black: Galaxy Tab S11 para jogos sai por menos de R$ 5.000
Galaxy Tab S11 Wi-Fi de 256 GB tem RAM de 12 GB, suporte a ray tracing, e tela de 120 Hz; tablet da Samsung baixa 42% em relação ao preço sugerido mais recente
O Galaxy Tab S11 Wi-Fi de 256 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 4.939 no Pix na Amazon. A oferta representa um desconto de 42% frente ao preço oficial mais recente sugerido pelo site da Samsung (R$ 8.499), e que ficou mais alto recentemente no site provavelmente devido à alta de preços geral da marca.
Mesmo assim, em oferta, o Galaxy Tab S11 ainda tem um preço bom, ainda mais se comparado aos da nova geração. E traz como destaques a GPU com suporte a ray tracing, RAM de 12 GB, e a tela AMOLED de 120 Hz.
O menor preço que já encontramos para o Galaxy Tab S11 Wi-Fi 256 GB foi R$ 4.701,64, na Semana do Consumidor de 2026 (Mercado Livre). Fora de datas promocionais, o melhor foi R$ 4.751,12 (Amazon, 9/7/2026), e esta oferta está R$ 187,93 acima.
Equipado com o processador Dimensity 9400+ de 3 nm e 12 GB de RAM, o tablet roda qualquer aplicativo sem engasgos, oferecendo alta performance para tarefas de produtividade e jogos. A tela Dynamic AMOLED 2X de 11 polegadas com 120 Hz garante imagens fluidas e cores vibrantes. Na prática, isso significa que você terá uma experiência visual rica e bastante confortável. Por fim, um último destaque do Galaxy Tab S11 é que o conjunto na caixa já inclui caneta S Pen e capa com teclado, garantindo uma experiência de uso completa para trabalho, estudos e criatividade. articles.title: SSD prices spiked all year — I'd buy these 5 1TB Black Friday deals
articles.text:
SSD prices are soaring, so I picked 5 Black Friday NVMe deals actually worth buying from Samsung, Lexar, and Kingston
It's time to beat the component cost crisis
Finding a good deal on high-speed internal storage has become increasingly difficult amid the ongoing NAND and DRAM shortages. But with Black Friday here, I've found five 1TB SSDs from Samsung, Kingston, Lexar, and WD that buck the trend of rising prices.
Now, my personal favorite is the Samsung 990, currently $180 (was $230). With read speeds up to 7,150 and write speeds of 6,450 MB/s, it offers a solid balance of performance and power efficiency. For a faster drive, the Samsung 990 Pro is the better pick, but more expensive at $248 (was $320).
Alternatively, the Lexar NM790 is 50 cents cheaper than the Samsung, but was originally $250. It boasts read/write speeds of up to 7,400MB/s reads and 6,500MB/s writes. The WD_Black SN7100, currently $195 (was $210) at Newegg, delivers impressive sequential read speeds of up to 7,250MB/s and write speeds of up to 6,900MB/s. And the Kingston NV3 is cheaper than all of them at $140 (was $216), but it's also the slowest, reaching up to 6,000MB/s read and 4,000MB/s write speeds.
Today's best 1TB SSD deals
The 1TB Samsung 990 PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD delivers sequential read/write speeds of up to 7,150/6,450 MB/s, improved power efficiency, hardware encryption, TRIM support, and dedicated SSD management software tools.
Read moreRead less▼
A PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe SSD in the M.2 2280 form factor with 1TB of storage and rated speeds up to 7,400MB/s read and 6,500MB/s write. It's rated for 1,000TB written and uses Host Memory Buffer 3.0 instead of onboard DRAM, which helps it use up to 40% less power than DRAM-equipped Gen 4 drives.
Read moreRead less▼
The 990 Pro is one of the fastest PCIe 4.0 SSDs around, with read/write speeds of up to 7,450/6,900 MB/s. But don't worry, there's no compromise on power consumption as the 990 Pro offers 50% better performance-per-Watt than the 980 PRO.
Read moreRead less▼
A PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe SSD in the M.2 2280 size with 1TB of storage and rated speeds of up to 6,000MB/s reads and 4,000MB/s writes. It's a DRAM-less design built for low power use, and it comes with Acronis True Image software for cloning your old drive.
Read moreRead less▼
Western Digital's popular drive is faster than the Samsung 990 - but not quite matching either the 990 Pro or Lexar. Still, it's impressive enough, with read/write speeds up to 7,250MB/s and 6,900MB/s.
Read moreRead less▼
Why we recommend them
The Samsung 990 delivers sequential read and write speeds of up to 7,150MB/s and 6,450MB/s. That's fast enough to handle most tasks without needing to upgrade to a PCIe 5.0 platform. Random read and write speeds reach up to 700,000 and 1.1 million IOPS, respectively.
Our sister site, Tom's Hardware, called the Lexar NM790 an all-around excellent SSD with little to lament in its review. We tested the heatsink version in our Lexar NM790 with Heatsink review, giving it a Great Value award and praising its PS5 benchmark score, though we noticed very occasional stutters while playing.
In our five-star Samsung 990 Pro review, we called it "an absolutely stellar M.2 SSD for both professional users and gamers alike. With solid capacities at a fair price and the fastest read/write performance of any PCIe 4.0 SSD we’ve tested, this SSD should definitely be at the top of your list if you’re looking to upgrade or do a new PC build."
The Kingston NV3 is a solid, affordable SSD - in Tom's Hardware's review, they noted that Kingston can change the components inside the NV3 over time, so the drive you buy may not perform exactly like the review unit. That's common for budget drives, and the NV3 is still much faster than any SATA SSD or hard drive.
The WD_Black SN7100 is a popular pick, particularly for gaming, where its read/write speeds favor fast loading and saving. The review from our sister site PC Gamer highlighted its strong read performance and low operating temperatures and concluding that it was “perfect for any gaming PC or console.” Personally, I'm not convinced the extra speed is worth the extra cost here, when the Lexar and 990 Pro are beating it. But others may disagree.
Price context & historical value
All five SSDs are set a fair price for today's market, but far from where they used to be before the component price sent every cost skyrocketing. Even last year, 1TB drives were around the $100 mark - and I'm not sure when we'll see prices fall back to that again. Fingers crossed for 2027.
One thing to note about the Samsung 990. The 1TB model currently offers better value per terabyte than its 2TB sibling, so there's little financial incentive in buying the larger drive unless you need the extra capacity.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Samsung 990 if... you're upgrading an older SSD or building a PC and want fast PCIe 4.0 storage for games, applications, and creative projects.
✅ Buy the Lexar NM790 if... you want near-flagship PCIe 4.0 speed for less than Samsung or WD charge, or you want high endurance for the money.
✅ Buy the Samsung 990 Pro if... you want blazing-fast speeds for heavy file transfers, video editing, and game saves.
✅ Buy the Kingston NV3 1TB if... you need an affordable boot drive or game drive, you're upgrading an older PC or laptop from a hard drive or SATA SSD, or you want the included cloning software.
✅ Buy the WD Black SN7100 if… you want a fast PCIe 4.0 SSD for a PC or laptop upgrade, and prefer it over the moderately pricier Samsung 990.

articles.title: WordPress Blocks Six Backdoored WP Connect Plugins Before Malicious Releases Go Live
articles.text:
WordPress has removed six WordPress plugins developed by WP Connect after they were backdoored on November 22, 2026, to enable arbitrary code execution on sites that have them installed, following a suspected compromise of the developer's account.
The WordPress plugins team has proactively detected and blocked the threat before it could be officially released. Visiting each plugin listing now serves the message: "This plugin has been closed as of November 22, 2026, and is not available for download. This closure is permanent."
The names of the affected plugins and the malicious versions are listed below -
- Air WP Sync – Airtable to WordPress (2.9.1 – 2.9.4)
- WP Sync for Notion – Notion to WordPress (1.7.4)
- Add-on Brevo for Gravity Forms (2.6.3)
- Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Airtable (2.5.4)
- Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Notion (1.6.4)
- Orders Sync to Airtable for WooCommerce (1.0.2)
These plugins have been collectively installed on more than 3,600 WordPress sites, according to WordPress security company Wordfence. The supply chain compromise is being tracked as CVE-2026-135202 (CVSS score: 9.8). It remains unpatched.
"Each release silently loaded the same remote-control module, which phones home to an attacker-controlled server, executes any PHP code it is sent, and exposes a full command set for running shell commands, stealing password hashes, and planting webshells," security researcher Chloe Chamberland said.
Specifically, the plugins come with a backdoor module ("includes/airwp-online.php") that runs on every request, sends site information (site URL, PHP, WordPress, and OS versions, and the server user) to a hard-coded command-and-control server ("tascredit-pay[.]com"), and runs PHP code returned by the server via eval().
It can also perform the following actions -
- Accept queued commands that run shell commands
- Read, write, and delete arbitrary files
- Query arbitrary database tables
- Dump the users table including login, email address, and password hashes
- Drop a web shell into the uploads directory or to a path of the attacker's choosing
- Register an hourly WP-Cron hook that runs attacker-supplied code
As a result, an unauthenticated attacker in control of the site can execute arbitrary code on the server and take complete control, facilitating credential theft and persistence through web shells and cron hooks that outlast the plugin removal.
Because the malicious versions were never released and blocked due to WordPress's new cooldown protections as part of its Protect The Shire initiative, sites running these plugins are unlikely to be affected. However, it's essential that site owners check their websites to make sure that they are not running one of the compromised versions and remove them as soon as possible.
"Unlike a typical vulnerability, this was not a coding mistake, and there is no patch: the malicious code was added deliberately and committed to each plugin's WordPress.org repository," Chamberland said. "Taken together, this strongly suggests that the developer's WordPress.org account was compromised and used to push the malicious releases, rather than that the vendor shipped this code intentionally."
The disclosure comes as URLscan.io revealed that an unspecified WordPress site had been infected by multiple cybercriminal campaigns, with attackers attempting to disable or remove scripts belonging to competing threat actors.
The site carried "thirteen separate ClickFix injections from three distinct kits [LOM, ErrTraffic, and Macfinger], alongside seven further malicious loaders," it said. "Several of the injections attempt to remove each other's code and overlays, and one injection disables another through a JavaScript naming collision. Five of the thirteen injections resolve their next-stage infrastructure from Polygon smart contracts, a technique known as EtherHiding."

articles.title: SpaceX de Elon Musk recibe autorización para lanzar un millón de satélites y crear centros de datos en el espacio
articles.text:
La Comisión Federal de Comunicaciones de Estados Unidos (FCC) autorizó a SpaceX, la compañía aeroespacial de Elon Musk, a desplegar un millón de satélites para crear una constelación de centros de datos en el espacio.
La autorización permitirá a SpaceX poner en órbita hasta un millón de módulos informáticos de la constelación Starmind, destinados a procesar grandes cantidades de datos que luego se utilizarían en la Tierra.
Según la FCC, se trata de la primera autorización de este tipo en la historia de Estados Unidos.
La agencia estadounidense señaló que el proyecto busca responder a la creciente demanda de capacidad de procesamiento para inteligencia artificial. Los módulos orbitales utilizarían energía solar y operarían de acuerdo con las normas de la FCC sobre desechos espaciales.
Qué autoriza la FCC a SpaceX
La decisión habilita a SpaceX a establecer una red de centros de datos orbitales a gran escala. La compañía había solicitado el permiso a principios de 2026 para desplegar los módulos informáticos y procesar datos desde el espacio.
Además, la FCC autorizó el uso de enlaces de radiofrecuencia para respaldo, telemetría de emergencia, seguimiento y control de los satélites. También aprobó comunicaciones adicionales para reforzar la red óptica de la empresa.
De acuerdo con los términos del permiso, SpaceX deberá iniciar el despliegue antes de noviembre de 2033. La empresa tendrá que poner en órbita 100.000 satélites antes de noviembre de 2035 y completar el 50% del proyecto antes de noviembre de 2038.
Respuesta de Elon Musk ante la autorización de la FCC
El presidente de la FCC, Brendan Carr, sostuvo que el traslado de la capacidad de procesamiento fuera de la Tierra permitirá responder a las necesidades de infraestructura para la inteligencia artificial.
“Al trasladar la capacidad de procesamiento más allá de la Tierra, SpaceX y los numerosos competidores que desarrollan sus propios centros de datos orbitales están respondiendo a las exigencias de este momento histórico”, expresó.
Carr afirmó que los centros de datos son esenciales para sostener el liderazgo de Estados Unidos en inteligencia artificial y que las constelaciones orbitales podrían aprovechar la energía solar de forma casi constante.
Por su parte, Elon Musk respondió al anuncio de la FCC en X: “Muy agradecido. Esto será un gran activo para América y el mundo”.
La FCC indicó que continúa evaluando otras propuestas de centros de datos orbitales y que emitirá resoluciones sobre cada una de ellas conforme a sus procedimientos habituales.
Elon Musk visita a Jensen Huang en sede de Nvidia
Elon Musk estuvo en las oficinas centrales de Nvidia, en Santa Clara, California, para mantener una reunión con Jensen Huang, máximo responsable de la empresa de chips e inteligencia artificial.
El fundador de Tesla y SpaceX asistió junto a dos de sus hijos y replicó en X una imagen del encuentro que había publicado la cuenta Tesla Owners Silicon Valley. Por su parte, Ben Pouladian, fundador de BEP Research y accionista de Nvidia, difundió otras fotografías de los dos empresarios.
La reunión se realizó después de que Nvidia anunciara, el 23 de noviembre, el retorno de Huang como director ejecutivo.
El directivo había dejado el cargo el 12 de noviembre, en medio de cuestionamientos vinculados con su conducta personal y eventuales implicaciones para la seguridad nacional. Musk celebró su vuelta con un mensaje en X: “El error ha sido corregido”.
El directorio de Nvidia señaló que avaló la reincorporación después de conversar con Huang y recopilar información de altos funcionarios estadounidenses.
La compañía afirmó que no considera que su regreso represente un riesgo para la seguridad nacional, aunque continuará con la investigación interna sobre las circunstancias de su salida.
Durante una reunión con empleados, Huang admitió fallas, ofreció disculpas y remarcó que debe cumplir las reglas de la empresa. Está previsto que responda preguntas de legisladores de Estados Unidos en diciembre de 2026.

articles.title: Disney+ : tous les abonnés mobiles Bouygues Telecom ont désormais droit à un prix cassé !
articles.text:
Voilà une offre qui va toucher tous les amoureux du streaming. Bouygues Telecom promet de réduire quasiment de moitié le prix d'une souscription chez Disney+ pour tous ses abonnés mobiles
C'est le Black Friday en fin de semaine, et les grandes entreprises commencent à dégainer des promos pour attirer le chaland. Les opérateurs des télécommunications n'échappent pas à la règle, et ils vont vous proposer tout un tas d'opportunités pour payer votre abonnement moins cher. Avec potentiellement, aussi d'autres offres intéressantes à saisir, comme aujourd'hui chez Bouygues Telecom.
Disney+ dorénavant à 3,99 € par mois pour tous les abonnés mobiles de Bouygues Telecom
Les opérateurs des télécommunications peuvent proposer des rabais sur autre chose que leur abonnement. On le voit avec Bouygues Telecom, qui vient d'annoncer une offre pour tous ses abonnés - y compris ceux qui sont chez B&You !
Ceux-ci peuvent ainsi dès aujourd'hui souscrire à l'abonnement standard avec publicités chez Disney+ (qui coûte normalement 6,99 € par mois), et bénéficier d'une remise mensuelle de 3 euros par mois. Accéder à Disney+ leur coûtera ainsi seulement 3,99 € par mois, soit une remise de 43%.
Une offre sans limite de durée
L'offre est d'autant plus intéressante qu'elle n'est - sur le papier - absolument pas limitée dans le temps par Bouygues Telecom. C'est ainsi sûrement l'opportunité pour ceux qui apprécient le catalogue du géant américain du streaming de bénéficier pour longtemps d'un prix extrêmement attractif.
Pour rappel, vous pouvez retrouver sur Disney+ les séries des grandes franchises comme Marvel ou Star Wars, mais aussi des séries toujours très populaires comme Grey's Anatomy ou bien Scrubs. Et l'offre standard avec publicités, lancée en 2023, n'a à ce jour vu son prix être augmenté qu'une seule fois, à la rentrée 2025 (d'1 euro). De quoi espérer ne pas trop voir les prix bouger à l'avenir.
Dernier petit point, si jamais vous êtes intéressé, sachez que l'opportunité offerte par Bouygues Telecom est disponible jusqu'au 24 janvier prochain.

articles.title: Urban VPN under legal scrutiny over claims it harvested users' private AI prompts
articles.text:
Urban VPN under legal scrutiny over claims it harvested users' private AI prompts
Attorneys are investigating whether three Urban VPN browser extensions allegedly captured and shared California users' AI chats without consent in 2025
- Urban VPN is under legal scrutiny over alleged data privacy violations
- California Chrome, Edge users of one of its VPN extensions may qualify
- Over 8M users may have had their AI prompts harvested by Urban VPN
Users who relied on Urban VPN's free browser tools for privacy may have had their AI chatbot prompts quietly recorded and sold instead. Attorneys are now investigating those claims for a potential class action lawsuit.
As reported by Top Class Actions, lawyers are examining whether Urban VPN's extensions broke California privacy law by collecting and sharing AI chats — a potential violation first revealed by researchers in December last year.
No court has ruled on the allegations, and no settlement exists yet. As of November 2026, the law firm is reviewing claims from eligible users before taking further legal steps.
TechRadar has contacted Urban VPN for comment on the investigation and will update this story if the company responds.
The probe, however, highlights why users should turn to the best VPN services instead of unvetted browser add-ons.
NordVPN Basic: New and improved Black Friday deal
Was: $3.49/month
Now: $2.99/month
NordVPN's improved Black Friday deal is perfect for streamers looking for a cheap way to boost their binge-watching. Having spent hundreds of hours with NordVPN, it's by far the best streaming VPN I've used in 2026. At $2.99 per month, it's at its lowest price in months, too. Unsure? Try it risk-free with its 30-day money-back guarantee.
Who qualifies for the Urban VPN lawsuit investigation?
The inquiry targets California residents who installed Urban VPN Proxy, 1ClickVPN Proxy, or Urban Browser Guard on Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge.
Eligible users must have had one of those extensions installed between July 9, 2025, and December 15, 2025, and used an AI chatbot in the same browser during that window.
Affected platforms include ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Grok, and Meta AI. As the Top Class Actions page states, "People who trusted Urban VPN to protect their online activity may instead have had their private AI chatbot conversations collected and sold without their knowledge."
Attorneys are assessing whether CIPA, which protects private communications from unauthorized recording or sharing, applies to these AI conversations. Readers outside California fall outside this specific inquiry, and submitting a form does not guarantee compensation.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance.
Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
How the AI snooping allegations emerged
This investigation follows December 2025 findings from cybersecurity firm Koi Security. As reported by TechRadar at the time, researchers discovered that version 5.5.0 of Urban VPN Proxy, pushed silently via browser auto-updates on July 9, 2025, added code that grabbed every prompt sent to supported AI chatbots.
That script compressed chats in real time and sent them to analytics.urban-vpn.com and stats.urban-vpn.com, where the data was aggregated before allegedly being passed to data broker BiScience. It kept running even when the VPN was off, or its "AI Protection" toggle was disabled, affecting over 8 million Chrome and Edge users.
Long before this incident, our Urban VPN review warned readers to avoid the service. It uses a peer-to-peer network, lacks any independent audit, and admitted in its own policy to logging IP addresses, search results, and visited pages
Does switching VPNs actually keep AI chats private?
Removing a compromised extension stops future interception, though it cannot claw back prompts already collected. Choosing a paid, audited virtual private network (VPN) also avoids the trap of free apps that monetize user traffic.
Top10VPN testing covered by TechRadar Pro found that 88% of 100 popular free Android VPNs leaked data and 71% shared it with third parties.
"The free VPN market is flooded with poor-quality apps whose only justification for their existence is to generate advertising revenue for their developers," Top10VPN Head of Research Simon Migliano told TechRadar.
Even a trusted VPN has limits, though. It encrypts traffic between your device and the VPN server, meaning the AI provider itself can still log whatever you type into your chat window.

articles.title: Cómo activar en Android los ajustes que bloquean el celular si un ladrón te lo arrebata
articles.text:
Google explica en su página de ayuda oficial de Android cómo activar la Protección contra robo, un conjunto de ajustes que bloquea la pantalla del celular si alguien lo arrebata, si el dispositivo queda sin internet o si el código se ingresa mal varias veces. Se activan desde Configuración, en pocos toques.
Las funciones forman parte del menú Protección contra robo, que Google ubica dentro de su sección de seguridad. Algunos pasos solo funcionan en Android 10 o versiones posteriores, y otros exigen Android 15. Tampoco están disponibles en dispositivos Android Go, tabletas ni relojes, y el soporte puede variar según el modelo.
Para empezar, el teléfono debe tener un bloqueo de pantalla configurado. Después: abrir Configuración, tocar Google, luego Todos los servicios y, en el apartado “Personal y seguridad del dispositivo”, entrar en Protección contra robo. Desde ahí se enciende cada función por separado. Google aclara que algunas ya vienen activadas de fábrica y remite a la guía de cada fabricante. Si una opción aparece en gris, el aparato no la admite.
Tres bloqueos automáticos de la pantalla
El primero es el Bloqueo por detección de robo. Según Google, usa inteligencia artificial, los sensores de movimiento del teléfono, el Wi-Fi y el Bluetooth para detectar que alguien se lo quitó de la mano y huye corriendo, en bicicleta o en un vehículo. En ese caso, la pantalla se bloquea sola. La función no actúa con la pantalla ya bloqueada y tampoco se dispara si el teléfono tiene una conexión estable de Wi-Fi o Bluetooth, o si hubo varios bloqueos seguidos en poco tiempo.
El segundo es el Bloqueo sin conexión. Si un ladrón apaga el internet para impedir que el dueño localice el aparato con Find Hub —la herramienta de Google para ubicar dispositivos—, la pantalla se bloquea tras un breve período de uso sin conexión. El teléfono debe estar desbloqueado cuando pierde la conectividad, y la pantalla puede bloquearse dos veces cada 24 horas.
El tercero, el Bloqueo por autenticación fallida, cierra la pantalla cuando se ingresa mal el código varias veces seguidas. Junto con la protección de ajustes sensibles, viene activado por defecto cuando hay un bloqueo de pantalla configurado.
Bloqueo remoto y verificación de identidad
El Bloqueo remoto permite trabar la pantalla de un teléfono perdido solo con un número de teléfono verificado. Requiere bloqueo de pantalla, una tarjeta SIM activa, Find Hub encendido y conexión a internet. Si el aparato está sin conexión, se bloquea cuando vuelva a conectarse. También puede usarse dos veces cada 24 horas.
Para activarlo, el camino es el mismo menú: Protección contra robo, Bloqueo remoto y activar la opción. Si el número no está verificado, hay que tocar Verificar número o activar la verificación automática. Con el teléfono ya perdido, se ingresa a android.com/lock desde otro dispositivo, se escribe el número, se resuelve un reCAPTCHA y se solicita el bloqueo.
Google ofrece además una pregunta de seguridad opcional, que se define en el mismo apartado tras verificar la identidad con PIN o datos biométricos. Quien la configura debe responderla en android.com/lock para que el bloqueo se concrete; una respuesta incorrecta lo hace fallar. Para borrar o asegurar el aparato a distancia hay que iniciar sesión en Find Hub.
La Verificación de identidad es la capa más estricta y solo aparece en ciertos dispositivos. Fuera de los lugares de confianza que el usuario define —como casa o trabajo—, exige huella o rostro y no admite PIN, patrón ni contraseña. Se activa en el mismo menú, con una cuenta de Google, bloqueo de pantalla, datos biométricos y lugares de confianza configurados.
Con esa verificación activa, hacen falta datos biométricos para ver contraseñas y llaves de acceso guardadas en el Administrador de contraseñas de Google, cambiar el bloqueo de pantalla, restablecer el teléfono de fábrica, apagar Find Hub o desactivar la propia función. También para cambiar la contraseña de la cuenta de Google o sus factores de recuperación.
Otros pasos que recomienda Google
La página aconseja un PIN de seis o más dígitos, aun si se usa huella o rostro, y activar la copia de seguridad para poder restablecer un teléfono robado sin perder datos. Find Hub debe estar encendido antes del robo: se activa solo al añadir una cuenta de Google. Desde allí se puede ubicar, bloquear o borrar el aparato.
Google recomienda también anotar el número IMEI —el código único del teléfono—, porque la operadora puede usarlo para ubicarlo o suspender el servicio, y las autoridades pueden pedirlo al denunciar el robo. En Configuración se consulta, según el modelo. Las instrucciones corresponden a la página de ayuda de Android consultada el 25 de noviembre de 2026.

Save $200 with surprising deals on new Nvidia RTX Spark-powered Asus ProArt P14 laptops — both 24GB and 32GB configurations are already on sale
A discount just a month after launch.
Nvidia's RTX Spark chip burst onto the laptop market just a month ago, and at least one model carrying Nvidia's first dedicated mobile SoC is already discounted for Black Friday. Both the 24GB and 32GB configurations of the Asus ProArt P14 are $200 off at Best Buy, which is a surprising discount to see so soon after the device launched.
The discount is partially explained by memory capacity, as we haven't seen any discounts on devices with 128GB of unified memory that fully unlock the capabilities of the GB10 chip. At either 32GB or 24GB of memory, you won't be able to run most of the larger AI models available, at least at any reasonable speed. You'll need to resort to smaller, heavily quantized models.
With 32GB of memory, this is not an AI powerhouse. However, what you are getting is a premium 14-inch laptop with Nvidia's latest consumer SoC, which is a potent chip among the standard laptop crowd.
The Asus ProArt P14 with RTX Spark is a 14-inch laptop with 512GB of storage. This model includes 24GB of unified memory, a 5,120-core Blackwell GPU, and an 18-core Grace CPU.
The Asus ProArt P14 with RTX Spark is a 14-inch laptop with 512GB of storage. This model includes 32GB of unified memory, a 6,144-core Blackwell GPU, and an 20-core Grace CPU.
Although the GPU available to the RTX Spark chip should be around a mobile RTX 5070, it currently performs around the level of a mobile RTX 5060, likely due to Arm-to-x86 translation in Windows. We haven't tested the P14 specifically, but you can see the results we gathered from the RTX Spark GB10 chip in the MSI EdgeMesa N AI+ below.

Of course, the performance level is dramatically influenced by the chassis, so don't take the numbers above as directly applicable to the ProArt P14. We're including them to show how the RTX Spark chip stacks up to the competition, and as you can see, it's a potent SoC across both CPU and GPU performance.
Outside of the chip itself, the ProArt P14 features a 14-inch 3K touch display with a 120Hz refresh rate. It uses an OLED panel and boasts up to 1,100 nits of peak brightness in HDR. Both the 24GB and 32GB configurations come with 512GB of storage. That's not much, but even the highest-end RTX Spark configurations seemingly top out at 2TB of storage.
The laptop is highly portable with an aluminum chassis, weighing in at just 3.26 pounds and measuring 0.63 inches thick. It may be a while before we see RTX Spark deals again, so don't miss $200 off the Asus ProArt P14 RTX Spark at Best Buy.

articles.title: Europol annonce une opération contre 57 services d’IPTV pirate
articles.text:
Europol a perturbé 57 services d'IPTV pirate en suivant les paiements en cryptomonnaies de leurs abonnés, avec l'aide de Binance, de Coinbase et de Chainalysis. Plus de 26 millions d'euros de transactions ont été tracés, et l'analyse continue.
L'empêcheur de tourner en rond. Des policiers de onze pays ont passé cinq jours à Séville, au siège de la police nationale espagnole, du 16 au 20 novembre, sous la coordination d'Europol. Ils ont enquêté sur l'argent de l'IPTV pirate, ces offres de télévision par Internet qui donnent accès à des milliers de chaînes, au sport en direct et aux films pour quelques euros par mois, sans l'accord des ayants droit. D'après le communiqué d'Europol, l'opération a perturbé 57 services et permis de repérer 321 sites de diffusion illégale, qui totalisent plus de 7,3 millions de visites par an. Les polices nationales doivent encore mettre un nom sur les personnes qui encaissent cet argent.
Europol suit l'argent des abonnés jusqu'aux portefeuilles des pirates
En février, Europol avait soutenu l'opération Switch Off, qui a fermé trois grandes plateformes pirates en Italie. Mais l'agence européenne s'attaque davantage aux paiements, car fermer un service n'arrête pas forcément les criminels qui le dirigent. Pour Europol, l'IPTV pirate est « un marché criminel pesant des milliards d'euros par an ». Les vendeurs encaissent souvent les abonnements en cryptomonnaies, et leurs portefeuilles numériques leur permettent aussi de faire passer l'argent d'un pays à l'autre et d'en cacher l'origine, selon BleepingComputer.
À Séville, les enquêteurs ont donc suivi ces transactions d'une blockchain à l'autre, pour relier chaque service à ses portefeuilles, puis aux personnes qui les contrôlent, rapporte The Block. Les plateformes d'échange Binance et Coinbase ont participé à ce travail, avec Chainalysis, une société spécialisée dans l'analyse des blockchains. Les informations recueillies à Séville serviront aux enquêtes nationales, pour identifier les suspects, couper les services et retrouver leurs avoirs.
L'an dernier, à Alicante, une première semaine d'enquête sur ces paiements avait permis de tracer 47 millions d'euros en cryptomonnaies et de signaler 25 services pirates aux plateformes d'échange, selon Finance Magnates. À l'époque, Europol et ses partenaires estimaient qu'un service d'IPTV pirate sur cinq acceptait les cryptomonnaies.
Environ 60 millions d'Européens regardent l'IPTV pirate
L'AAPA, l'association européenne de lutte contre le piratage audiovisuel, a aussi participé à l'opération, avec Interpol et l'Office de l'Union européenne pour la propriété intellectuelle. D'après ses estimations, relayées par Europol, environ 60 millions de personnes utilisent ces services en Europe. Les diffuseurs légaux perdent 4,83 milliards d'euros par an, et les États 1,08 milliard d'euros d'impôts.
Une trentaine de policiers ont fait le déplacement à Séville. Ils venaient de Belgique, de Bulgarie, de Croatie, d'Espagne, des États-Unis, de Grèce, d'Irlande, d'Italie, des Pays-Bas, du Portugal et de Roumanie, selon The Block. La police française manque à l'appel.
Les gendarmes français mènent leurs enquêtes de leur côté. En juin, ceux de l'Unité nationale cyber ont démantelé Noos+. Selon eux, cette plateforme pirate aurait encaissé plus de 12 millions d'euros en cinq ans.
Et si vous payez un abonnement à l'un de ces services, vous enfreignez la loi, rappelle l'Arcom.

articles.title: Hackers breach CIA system in possible ARTEX cyberattack and leak unclassified data
articles.text:
Hackers breach CIA system in possible ARTEX cyberattack and leak unclassified data
Three US spy agencies were broken into
- Attackers breached unclassified intelligence-analysis systems used by multiple US intelligence agencies and exfiltrated collected data
- Officials said classified information was not compromised, and the affected systems primarily contained open-source intelligence material
- Investigators are examining possible China-linked involvement, with reports highlighting use of the AI-powered ARTEX reconnaissance platform
The US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, were recently breached by what appear to be Chinese hackers, who got away with some data, but fortunately it appears to be nothing classified.
The New York Times, citing multiple US officials and other people familiar with the matter, reported that threat actors broke into an open source intelligence analysis system - essentially a network that harvests public, unclassified material, and turns it into actionable intelligence - and took the data found there.
In other words, these are all information available to anyone, these agencies just scraped them and likely built a narrative around them.
ARTEX is the talk of the town
We don’t know what the nature of the stolen files is. We don’t know if those are names or emails, but the publication stressed that classified material was not jeopardized. We also don’t know exactly how the incident played out, but we do know some of the tools that were used, ARTEX being one of them.
ARTEX has been making headlines for several weeks now - recently as news broke of cybercriminals using the tool to break into the European Commission, and even forcing the organization to pull a few apps offline, namely Sysper, the Commission’s human resources platform that employees use to access payroll information, leave requests, and work hour logs, and MyPMO, a medical reimbursement system.
A few weeks before that, security researchers Censys reported finding more than a thousand of ARTEX instances readily available for anyone who knew where to look. Many were also running other known hacking tools alongside it.
ARTEX started out as a legitimate penetration testing tool, only to later be hijacked for malicious purposes, similar to what happened to Cobalt Strike, for example. The tool was released in the summer of 2025 by a developer called Autumn-27. This author, who appears to be Chinese, first built ScopeSentry, a tool security researchers described as a “widely used Chinese asset-discovery and vulnerability-scanning platform.”
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
They then added an AI agent layer on top of that tool, and thus ARTEX was born. In other words - it is an LLM-powered version of Scope Sentry that syncs assets found by the tool’s domains, subdomains, IPs, ports, and endpoints.
Who is the world's biggest cyber-bully?
ARTEX was released in late July 2026 and quickly gained popularity. On October 7, security researchers CrowdStrike reported seeing it used in malicious attacks and a day later, the developer distanced themselves from the illicit activity and stressed the tool was built for testing within authorized asset scopes. They then turned it into a closed-source tool with no further releases.
However, despite the repository being taken down, Censys claims archived copies, translations, and different rebrands are still circulating.
At the time of publication, no one claimed responsibility for the attack on the CIA and other spy agencies. NYT says initial signs, including the use of ARTEX, suggests that China may be behind it. For this information it cited two of the people who are familiar with the breach.
For years, security researchers and law enforcement agencies have been pointing the finger at China, warning about malicious activities such as cyber-espionage or data theft, aimed at western enterprises and governments. In fact, this is one of the reasons why US President Donald Trump barred American companies from doing business with many Chinese tech firms such as Huawei or ZTE.
China, on the other hand, vehemently denies all such claims, describing them as baseless allegations, and instead saying it’s the US government that’s acting as the world’s biggest cyber-bully.
Via AP

articles.title: ChatGPT ahora analiza la actividad física y salud en Android con esta función
articles.text:
OpenAI habilitó ChatGPT Health en la aplicación de ChatGPT para Android, con soporte para Health Connect, el servicio de Google que reúne datos de salud y actividad física del teléfono. La función llega de forma gradual y, por ahora, solo para usuarios elegibles de Estados Unidos mayores de 18 años.
Según OpenAI, Health está disponible para cuentas de ChatGPT Free, Go, Plus y Pro con sesión iniciada en ese país. Funciona en la web, en iOS, en Android y en la aplicación de escritorio.
Si no aparece en el menú lateral, la empresa recomienda actualizar la aplicación. La página oficial aclara que algunas cuentas todavía pueden no tenerla.
Los usuarios pueden hacer preguntas de salud sin conectar nada. Para obtener respuestas basadas en sus propios datos, pueden vincular Health Connect en Android o Apple Health en iPhone, además de historiales médicos de ciertos sistemas hospitalarios de Estados Unidos, One Medical y Function Health.
Cómo funciona ChatGPT Health en Android
El proceso empieza en la sección Health del menú lateral o en el menú Explorar. Allí el usuario elige Health Connect y marca las categorías de datos que autoriza, como sueño, actividad o entrenamientos. Puede agregar o quitar cuentas cuando quiera desde la pestaña de cuentas.
Con esa información, ChatGPT puede comparar resultados de análisis con estudios anteriores, resumir cambios desde la última consulta o explorar cómo se relacionan el sueño, la actividad y los entrenamientos con la rutina de la persona, según OpenAI.
Health Connect funciona como intermediario. Dataconomy precisó que quienes usan relojes Garmin o el anillo Oura deben comprobar que las aplicaciones de esos dispositivos compartan datos con Health Connect.
OpenAI advierte que ChatGPT solo ve lo que esas aplicaciones comparten y que algunas métricas propias, como una puntuación de sueño, pueden no aparecer o calcularse de otro modo.
OpenAI indica que ChatGPT no puede modificar los historiales que guarda un proveedor médico ni escribir información de vuelta en Apple Health o Health Connect.
Los cambios en condiciones actuales, medicamentos o antecedentes familiares solo afectan el perfil de Health dentro de ChatGPT.
La empresa describe el servicio como un apoyo y no un reemplazo de la atención médica, y señala que no está pensado para diagnosticar ni tratar. Para síntomas urgentes recomienda buscar ayuda profesional inmediata.
El medio agrega que las mediciones de los dispositivos de consumo pueden ser incompletas o inexactas.
Qué promete OpenAI en cuanto a privacidad
Según OpenAI, los datos sincronizados en Health, incluidos los de Health Connect, no se usan para entrenar sus modelos base ni para dirigir publicidad. La empresa afirma que los chats se cifran por defecto y que la información conectada en Health recibe protecciones adicionales.
Hay una salvedad en la misma página: el ajuste “Mejorar el modelo para todos” determina si las conversaciones que mencionan datos de Health, y el contenido derivado de ellos, pueden usarse para mejorar los modelos. Quien no lo desee debe desactivarlo en los controles de datos de la configuración.
Si la memoria de ChatGPT está activada, las conversaciones que usan Health pueden crear recuerdos para personalizar chats futuros, por ejemplo la meta de mejorar el sueño. OpenAI aclara que los recuerdos no se crean directamente a partir de los datos sincronizados, y ofrece proyectos con memoria propia o chats temporales para separarlos.
Al desconectar una cuenta, los datos sincronizados desde esa fuente se eliminan de los sistemas de OpenAI en un plazo de 30 días.
Lo que ya quedó incluido en las conversaciones se conserva hasta que el usuario borre esos chats.
La compañía precisa que Health no es apto para uso clínico ni ofrece un contrato de asociado comercial, el requisito de la ley estadounidense de privacidad médica (HIPAA) para proveedores y aseguradoras. Los padres pueden desactivar Health en las cuentas vinculadas de adolescentes, lo que elimina los datos sincronizados.
OpenAI no indicó fechas para otros países. La página de ayuda limita la disponibilidad a Estados Unidos y no menciona una ampliación.

articles.title: Mozilla Launches Firefox 161.0 With Per-Site VPN, Classic Themes, and New Keyboard Shortcuts
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Mozilla Launches Firefox 161.0 With Per-Site VPN, Classic Themes, and New Keyboard Shortcuts
Mozilla has officially released Firefox 161.0 for download, and one of the headline features in the browser's third mainline update since the introduction of the new Nova UI is the addition of classic Firefox themes to the Add-ons Manager. The new themes include a variety of solid-color themes, a Firefox OLED theme, and the Proton theme from prior Firefox releases. 
Also in Firefox 161.0, Firefox has added the ability to enable its built-in VPN for select websites only, noting that this is specifically implemented in order to increase privacy on specific pages—like banking apps—or to access content that would otherwise be restricted in certain locations. The browser also gets a new keyboard shortcut to copy the URL of the current page, although this is intentionally undefined at release, so those who want the shortcut will need to set their own keyboard shortcut in settings.Firefox 161.0 obviously also includes the usual slew of bug fixes, including a fix for missing tabs when the browser session is restored, fixing the Windows taskbar obscuring part of full-screen Firefox windows in certain cases, improved performance when opening many bookmarks on macOS 26+, fixing low-resolution video streams when using WebRTC and H.264 encoding. Firefox will now also be able to detect how many times you've visited pages imported from Chrome history, so that sites you visit are ranked higher in the address suggestions and shortcuts.

articles.title: Lawsuit reveals Trump’s alleged strong-arming of Intel — troubled chipmaker allegedly forced to give White House 10% stake for release of CHIPS Act funds
articles.text:
Lawsuit alleges Trump strong-armed Intel — troubled chipmaker allegedly forced to give White House 10% stake for release of CHIPS Act funds
Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as the CEO of Nvidia wasn’t the first time that the president meddled in the business of private companies.
An Intel shareholder lawsuit against the company has revealed the extent to which President Donald Trump is allegedly willing to bend companies to his will. Richard Paisner sued the chipmaker earlier this year, saying that the White House’s 10% stake in exchange for the release of the previously granted CHIPS Act funds was unlawful. Now, Wired viewed unsealed documents from the case that allegedly showed how the president used his influence and position to strong-arm Intel’s board into accepting the deal.
Intel was already suffering from financial woes since July 2024, and its new CEO, Lip-Bu Tan, was facing scrutiny over his links to Chinese tech companies. Trump himself has called for Tan’s resignation in August 2025, calling him “highly conflicted.” The Intel chief eventually went to the White House and personally talked to the president, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. It was during this conversation that Trump said that he cooked up the 10% Intel deal. Intel was still waiting on $8.9 billion in funding from the U.S. government through the CHIPS and Science Act, but the White House allegedly wanted something in return. The president quoted himself to the Wall Street Journal telling Lip-Bu Tan, “You know what? I think the United States should be given 10% of Intel,” to which the Intel chief replied, “I would consider that.”
Court documents reveal how much pressure Intel’s leadership faced at that time. Internal notes show that a call between the company and Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro had the latter tell the former’s chief financial officer not to make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” and that “the president is expecting to announce a deal on Friday.” Furthermore, even though the government official said that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” it was also noted, “that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.”
Because of this, Paisner and his attorney said in the complaint [PDF], “In extraordinary and expedited fashion, the Board, operating under the shadow of the President’s threat, and advised by legal counsel that itself was conflicted due to its pro bono promises to the president, caved to the government’s extortion.” Other sources also pointed out that Intel’s external legal counsel provided up to $100 million in free legal services to the Trump administration so it could avoid an executive order that would have prevented it from working with the federal government — something that the White House did to Anthropic after it refused to allow the Pentagon to use Claude for mass domestic surveillance or to control weapons systems.
Earlier this week, the president called the Nvidia board to pressure them into reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. This wasn’t the first time that Trump made a deal with the company. The AI chipmaker has previously agreed to pay 15% on its H20 sales to China so that it could be allowed to export them again, followed by an even larger 25% slice on H200 chips in December 2025.
