articles.title: Black Friday LEGO : Star Wars, Harry Potter, Pokémon et One Piece jusqu'à -42 % sur Amazon
articles.text:
Le Black Friday tombe officiellement le vendredi 27 novembre, mais Amazon a lancé ses offres plusieurs jours en avance et les prolongera jusqu'au Cyber Monday, le lundi 30 novembre. Pour les fans de LEGO, c'est souvent le meilleur moment de l'année pour s'offrir un grand set d'exposition ou boucler les cadeaux de Noël sans payer le prix fort.
Nous avons retenu dix offres qui couvrent les licences les plus recherchées, de Star Wars à Harry Potter en passant par Disney Pixar, la Formule 1, DC, Fortnite, One Piece et Pokémon. Toutes sont vendues et expédiées par Amazon, les prix barrés correspondent aux prix publics conseillés par LEGO, et la plupart des sets bénéficient du retour prolongé jusqu'au 15 janvier 2027, pratique si le cadeau ne fait pas mouche.
Black Friday LEGO : les offres folles de ce jour
- LEGO Star Wars TIE Fighter de Dark Vador à 40,59 € au lieu de 69,99 €
- LEGO Star Wars U-Wing à 44,99 € au lieu de 69,99 €
- LEGO Disney Pixar Alien Pizza Planet à 52,99 € au lieu de 59,99 €
- LEGO Editions Casque de Charles Leclerc à 56,99 € au lieu de 89,99 €
- LEGO Harry Potter Book Poudlard Express à 61,99 € au lieu de 99,99 €
- LEGO DC Batmobile Batman Forever à 66,99 € au lieu de 99,99 €
- LEGO Harry Potter Château Poudlard à 107,99 € au lieu de 169,99 €
- LEGO Fortnite Chef de l'équipe Mécha à 142,49 € au lieu de 229,99 €
- LEGO One Piece Le Baratie à 182,39 € au lieu de 299,99 €
- LEGO Pokémonà 583,99 € au lieu de 649,99 €
LEGO Star Wars SMART Play : le TIE Fighter de Dark Vador qui s'anime passe à 40,59 €
C'est l'un des premiers sets de la gamme SMART Play, que LEGO présente comme sa plus grosse innovation depuis la création de la brique. La boîte embarque une SMART Brique et son chargeur, ainsi qu'un Tag qui déclenche sons et effets lumineux selon la façon dont l'enfant manipule le chasseur de Dark Vador. Avec ses 473 pièces, le vaisseau s'adresse aux enfants dès 8 ans, qui pourront rejouer les combats spatiaux de la saga avec la minifigurine du Seigneur Sith, et la brique électronique servira aussi avec les autres sets SMART Play. À 40,59 €, soit 29,40 € de moins que son prix conseillé, c'est la plus forte remise de notre sélection et une façon abordable de découvrir cette nouvelle génération de LEGO.
✅ Les points forts
- Un LEGO qui réagit au jeu : la SMART Brique et son Tag ajoutent sons et lumières pendant les parties
- Une porte d'entrée dans SMART Play : la brique et son chargeur sont inclus et resservent avec les autres sets de la gamme
- Un excellent accueil : 4,7/5 sur près de 300 avis, et plus de 700 exemplaires achetés récemment
LEGO Star Wars U-Wing : le vaisseau rebelle d'Andor descend à 44,99 €
Remis en lumière par la saison 2 d'Andor, le U-Wing est l'un des vaisseaux de l'Alliance rebelle les plus appréciés des fans. Le set de 594 pièces s'adresse aux constructeurs dès 8 ans et réunit trois minifigurines ainsi que le droïde K-2SO, compagnon indissociable de Cassian Andor, dans un modèle assez solide pour être manipulé et assez détaillé pour trôner sur une étagère. Il perd ici 25 € par rapport à son prix conseillé, un bon calcul pour un cadeau d'enfant comme pour un adulte qui complète sa flotte Star Wars. Ceux qui visent plus grand pourront jeter un œil au set XXL qui a bluffé les équipes de Star Wars.
✅ Les points forts
- Un vaisseau culte de la saga : le U-Wing de la série Andor, fidèle aux images de la saison 2
- K-2SO dans la boîte : le droïde accompagne trois minifigurines pour rejouer les missions rebelles
- Très bien noté : 4,7/5 sur près de 880 avis
LEGO Disney Pixar Alien et fusée Pizza Planet : l'exclusivité Amazon pour les fans de Toy Story
Les fans de Toy Story connaissent bien la fusée du Pizza Planet, et LEGO en a fait un set de 714 pièces vendu en exclusivité sur Amazon. La boîte reproduit le manège avec une manivelle à actionner et une grande figurine d'Alien articulée, dans un set conseillé à partir de 9 ans qui se prête aussi bien au jeu qu'à la décoration d'une chambre ou d'un bureau. La remise est plus modeste que sur le reste de la sélection, mais elle reste intéressante sur une référence qu'on ne trouve pas ailleurs.
✅ Les points forts
- Une exclusivité Amazon : un set Toy Story introuvable chez les autres revendeurs
- Une fusée animée : la manivelle actionne le manège, et la figurine d'Alien est articulée
- Une pièce déco réussie : 714 pièces pour un objet qui plaira aussi aux nostalgiques de Pixar
LEGO Editions Casque Charles Leclerc : la pièce d'exposition des tifosi tombe à 56,99 €
LEGO poursuit sa collection de casques de pilotes avec celui de Charles Leclerc aux couleurs de la Scuderia Ferrari HP. Conseillé dès 14 ans, ce modèle de 886 pièces ne se joue pas, il s'expose, et reproduit fidèlement les lignes et la livrée rouge du pilote monégasque, avec en prime une minifigurine collector. Avec 33 € de remise et plus de 1 000 exemplaires vendus récemment, c'est l'un des sets les plus demandés de la sélection, et une idée de cadeau toute trouvée pour un fan de Formule 1.
✅ Les points forts
- Un objet de collection : une réplique fidèle du casque de Charles Leclerc, pensée pour l'exposition
- Une minifigurine collector : un bonus qui fera plaisir aux fans de la Scuderia
- Un best-seller : 4,6/5 sur plus de 770 avis, et plus de 1 000 achats récents
LEGO Harry Potter Book Nook Poudlard Express : la voie 9¾ s'installe dans votre bibliothèque pour 61,99 €
Le principe du book nook consiste à glisser un petit décor entre deux livres sur une étagère, et LEGO l'a appliqué à l'une des scènes les plus célèbres de la saga Harry Potter. Les 832 pièces reproduisent le quai de la voie 9¾ et le Poudlard Express avec quatre personnages, dans un ensemble qui sert de serre-livres et apporte une touche de magie à n'importe quelle bibliothèque. Conseillé dès 10 ans, le set coûte 38 € de moins que son prix conseillé, ce qui en fait un cadeau original pour les lecteurs qui ont grandi avec les romans de J.K. Rowling.
✅ Les points forts
- Un concept original : un décor qui se glisse entre deux livres et fait office de serre-livres
- Une scène culte : le quai de la voie 9¾ et le Poudlard Express, avec quatre personnages
- Accessible dès 10 ans : un montage agréable pour les jeunes lecteurs comme pour les adultes
LEGO Batmobile Batman Forever : la voiture culte du film de 1995 passe à 66,99 €
Chaque film Batman a eu sa Batmobile, et celle de Batman Forever reste l'une des plus spectaculaires avec ses lignes effilées et ses ailerons sculptés. LEGO la reproduit en 909 pièces dans un modèle conseillé dès 12 ans, avec un cockpit qui s'ouvre comme dans le film de Joel Schumacher. Une belle pièce à exposer pour les fans de DC et de cinéma des années 1990, qui perd ici 33 € sur Amazon.
✅ Les points forts
- Une Batmobile iconique : le design très reconnaissable du film de 1995, fidèlement reproduit
- Un cockpit ouvrant : un détail qui donne du caractère au modèle exposé
- Un format adapté : 909 pièces, une construction de quelques soirées, accessible dès 12 ans
LEGO Harry Potter Château et domaine de Poudlard : le set plébiscité par près de 3 900 fans passe à 107,99 €
C'est l'un des sets Harry Potter pour adultes les plus appréciés, et ses notes en attestent. Il représente le château de Poudlard et son domaine dans une version miniature, assez compacte pour tenir sur un meuble mais suffisamment riche, avec ses 2 660 pièces, pour offrir une longue séance de construction. Réservé aux 18 ans et plus, il s'adresse aux fans qui veulent tout le château sur leur étagère sans y consacrer une pièce entière, et il coûte ici 62 € de moins que son prix conseillé, avec plus de 900 exemplaires vendus récemment.
✅ Les points forts
- Tout Poudlard en un seul set : le château et son domaine en version miniature, idéale à exposer
- Une construction généreuse : 2 660 pièces pour de longues heures de montage
- Le mieux noté de la sélection : 4,8/5 sur près de 3 900 avis
LEGO Fortnite Chef de l'équipe Mécha 77078 : un robot de plus de 45 cm à 142,49 €
LEGO et Epic Games continuent d'étendre leur partenariat, et le Chef de l'équipe Mécha en est l'un des sets les plus impressionnants. Une fois monté, ce robot de 2 503 pièces dépasse 45 cm de haut et reprend l'allure de l'un des skins les plus connus de Fortnite. Conseillé dès 18 ans, il s'adresse avant tout aux joueurs adultes qui veulent exposer leur personnage préféré, et ses 87,50 € de remise le ramènent à un prix bien plus raisonnable pour une construction de cette envergure.
✅ Les points forts
- Un format XXL : plus de 45 cm de haut, de quoi attirer les regards sur une étagère
- Un skin culte : un personnage que les joueurs de Fortnite reconnaîtront immédiatement
- Une construction exigeante : 2 503 pièces pensées pour les constructeurs adultes
LEGO One Piece Baratie 75640 : le restaurant flottant de Zeff et Sanji perd 117 € sur Amazon
Les lecteurs de One Piece connaissent le Baratie, ce restaurant flottant où Luffy croise la route de Sanji au début de l'aventure. LEGO en fait un set de 3 402 pièces conseillé dès 18 ans, avec dix minifigurines dont Luffy, de quoi reconstituer l'un des arcs les plus marquants du manga. C'est aussi l'une des plus belles remises de la sélection, puisqu'il passe de 299,99 € à 182,39 €. Attention toutefois : Amazon annonce une livraison entre le 24 décembre et le 6 janvier, il arrivera donc probablement après le réveillon s'il s'agit d'un cadeau de Noël.
✅ Les points forts
- Un lieu culte du manga : le restaurant flottant de l'arc du Baratie, fidèlement reproduit
- Dix minifigurines : Luffy et d'autres personnages pour une scène très vivante
- Une construction ambitieuse : 3 402 pièces pour les fans adultes de One Piece
LEGO Pokémon Florizarre, Dracaufeu et Tortank 72153 : le set géant de 6 838 pièces passe sous les 600 €
C'est la pièce maîtresse de la gamme Pokémon de LEGO, et nous vous avions déjà présenté ce set titanesque qui va vider votre compte en banque. Florizarre, Dracaufeu et Tortank, les évolutions finales des trois starters de la première génération, y mesurent entre 18 et 23 cm de haut, et l'ensemble totalise 6 838 pièces, ce qui en fait l'un des sets les plus imposants du catalogue LEGO. Conseillé dès 18 ans et vendu en exclusivité sur Amazon, il ne bénéficie que d'une remise de 10 %, mais les 66 € économisés comptent sur un achat de cette ampleur pour un collectionneur qui a grandi avec Pokémon Rouge et Bleu.
✅ Les points forts
- Les trois starters mythiques : Florizarre, Dracaufeu et Tortank réunis dans un seul set
- Un format monumental : 6 838 pièces et des figurines de 18 à 23 cm
- Une exclusivité Amazon : une référence de collection réservée à ce revendeur
Black Friday LEGO : quand faire ses achats de Noël cette année ?
Le Black Friday se tient le vendredi 27 novembre, mais l'événement s'étale désormais sur plusieurs jours, voire plusieurs semaines : Amazon a lancé ses offres en avance et les prolongera jusqu'au Cyber Monday du lundi 30 novembre. Pour les LEGO, la question se pose un peu différemment que pour les autres produits, car les sets les plus recherchés partent souvent en rupture bien avant la fin de l'opération, en particulier les grandes boîtes sous licence et les exclusivités. Une fois le stock épuisé, il faut parfois attendre plusieurs semaines pour le voir revenir, au risque de passer à côté de Noël.
Mieux vaut donc ne pas attendre le dernier jour quand un set figure sur votre liste, et vérifier la date de livraison affichée avant de valider la commande, puisque certaines références de grande taille sont expédiées avec un délai qui peut repousser la réception après les fêtes. Les retours prolongés jusqu'au 15 janvier permettent quant à eux d'acheter tôt sans prendre trop de risques. Pour suivre les offres sur tous les rayons, notre page dédiée au Black Friday est mise à jour en continu, et les amateurs de rétro pourront aussi jeter un œil à la Game Boy LEGO.
Quel set LEGO choisir selon l'âge et le budget ?
L'âge indiqué sur la boîte reste le premier repère, et il ne traduit pas seulement la difficulté. Les sets conseillés jusqu'à 12 ans, comme les vaisseaux Star Wars ou la fusée Pizza Planet, sont conçus pour être manipulés et résister au jeu, tandis que les gammes 18+ privilégient la finesse des détails et l'exposition, au prix d'une plus grande fragilité. Les nouveaux sets SMART Play ajoutent quant à eux une dimension interactive qui prolonge le jeu une fois le montage terminé, un argument de poids pour les plus jeunes.
Côté adultes, le choix dépend surtout de la place disponible et du temps que l'on compte consacrer au montage. Un book nook ou un casque de pilote se construit en quelques soirées et s'expose dans un espace réduit, alors qu'un set de plusieurs milliers de pièces comme le Baratie ou le trio Pokémon occupe des week-ends entiers et réclame une vraie place d'exposition. Le succès de ces grandes boîtes pour adultes n'a d'ailleurs rien d'un hasard, comme nous l'expliquions dans notre dossier sur les LEGO pour les grands.

articles.title: Attacker used 1Password employee's GitHub account to copy customer records
articles.text:
Attacker used 1Password employee’s GitHub account to copy customer records
Identity security company 1Password today disclosed a security incident in which an attacker, working through an employee’s corporate GitHub account, copied account records belonging to a subset of its customers.
According to the company, the incident came to light on Nov. 19, when 1Password began investigating signs that the GitHub account had been compromised. Using the account, the attacker is said to have pushed malicious code to 1Password’s backend services, which then downloaded what the company describes as “administrative data pertaining to our customers.”
The records taken include names and email addresses, account and user identifiers, account creation and last sign-in times, public keys, Secure Remote Password protocol parameters and other non-secret account metadata. Rounding out the list are tokens found in certain emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery.
Customer vaults, the items stored in them and the keys that protect them were not affected, according to 1Password. “At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker,” the company said in its disclosure. Account passwords and Secret Keys are not stored by the company. Also left untouched, the company says, were account recovery keys and the 1Password apps and browser extensions.
Beyond the customer records, the attacker is said to have copied source code from private repositories. Access was also gained to 1Password’s continuous integration and continuous delivery system, which contains infrastructure-related secrets needed for its product to work. According to 1Password, the source code contains no user secrets. Having triggered a rotation of all credentials that may have been exposed, the company claims there has been no impact to its services, availability or product security.
The tokens taken from emailed links cannot be used on their own to access an account, since completing an invitation or recovery also requires a sign-in through single sign-on or a six-digit code sent to the user’s registered email address. Users with provisioning invites or recovery requests pending at the time of the incident, said to be a small number, have been notified directly. As a precaution, the emailed codes have now been lengthened from six numeric digits to 10 alphanumeric characters. 1Password says it has found no internal evidence of account takeovers using the exposed tokens.
Other steps taken in response include disabling the affected GitHub account, revoking the stolen token, tightening internal controls and bringing in independent cybersecurity experts to validate its containment and remediation work.
Customers do not need to change anything in their 1Password accounts. The company is instead warning users to be cautious of phishing attempts, such as unexpected emails, texts or calls about invitations or account recovery requests they did not start. “1Password will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key,” the company noted.
1Password, which claims to serve more than 200,000 businesses, did not say how many customers had records downloaded. How the employee’s GitHub account was compromised was also left unexplained.
This is not the first intrusion 1Password has disclosed. In October 2023, the company said that an attacker had accessed its Okta tenant using session data stolen in the breach of Okta Inc.’s customer support system. No user data was found to have been compromised in that case.
Today’s disclosure comes nearly four years after rival password manager LastPass US LP revealed that a hacker had copied encrypted customer password vaults, using information taken in an earlier breach of its development environment.
1Password says it will update its post if the investigation turns up anything that changes what it has disclosed so far.

articles.title: The MacBook Neo at £619 brings Apple's laptop closer to its launch price
articles.text:
The colourful MacBook Neo at £619 brings Apple's budget laptop closer to its launch price
Remember when Apple added £100 to your MacBook Neo bill? This promotion nearly covers that entire price hike
It launched at £599 before memory prices caused Apple to have to add £100 onto your bill, but this Black Friday deal brings the base-spec MacBook Neo much closer to its initial launch price.
Buy a Silver or Citrus MacBook Neo for £619 (was £699), or a Blush model for £649 (was £699) with Joybuy's limited-run promotion.
Apple's cheapest laptop still packs a punch with an A18 Pro chip, six CPU cores, five GPU cores, 8GB memory and a 256GB SSD.
Apple's cheapest laptop is finally available for its launch price (near enough) after it quickly received a £100 price hike. Buy a Silver or Citrus MacBook Neo for £619 (or a Blush model for £649).
Why we recommend it
Apple's MacBook Neo is around half the price of a MacBook Air, its next-cheapest model, so it offers an excellent affordable entry point to the company's laptop lineup. It feels premium, delivers excellent performance from the A18 Pro chip (derived from the iPhone 16 Pro) and lasts up to 16 hours on a full charge.
Price Context & Historical Value
Apple had launched this model at £599, but sweeping price hikes added £100 to that bill thanks to ongoing supply chain constraints and rising hardware prices. You can knock up to £80 of that price hike off with this Black Friday deal.
For more Apple savings, we've found the best Black Friday MacBook deals.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the MacBook Neo if...
you're a student or casual user who need a laptop for emails, word processing, video conferencing and casual browsing – especially if you've already got other Apple products like an iPhone
❌ Skip the MacBook Neo if...
you need more performance to handle photo and video editing or you've already got one of Apple's M-series laptops

articles.title: Husband of Jensen Huang’s mistress has much more significant Chinese intelligence connections than her, report claims — US officials warn he was asset with Ministry of State Security connections
articles.text:
Husband of Jensen Huang’s mistress has much more significant Chinese intelligence connections than her, report claims — US officials warn he was asset with Ministry of State Security connections
The former Megaspeed employee's husband has ties to the Chinese intelligence service, officials have warned.
Just a day after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO, U.S. intelligence officials met to deliver a briefing to Congress about one of his love interests and her alleged ties to China's Ministry of State Security, or MSS. Alice Huang has been accused of being a Chinese spy, and her affair with Jensen Huang saw the Nvidia founder resign. But even with Jensen Huang now back in the saddle at Nvidia, attention has turned to whether she posed, or poses, a security threat to the United States as a whole, and its place in the global AI food chain. A New York Times report details the meeting for staff members of the House and Senate intelligence committees and aides to the leaders of both chambers, including its bombshell news that Alice Huang's husband has a much more significant intelligence connection.
The intelligence officials told those in attendance that they still don't fully understand what role Alice Huang played in the saga, but that there is no evidence that she initiated the affair at the behest of Chinese authorities. That being said, they also refused to dispute that she passed intelligence back to the country's top intelligence agency while the affair was underway. Further, the officials told those at the meeting that Alice Huang's husband, Kang Wei, was a more significant figure with respect to any connection to the MSS. In fact, he had at times been an MSS asset with deeper contacts within the agency than his wife. It's been reported that Alice Huang was in contact with the Chinese spy agency from the spring of 2025 until the fall of 2026, while Kang Wei was also in contact with the same agency during that time.
Alice Huang was a Megaspeed employee when it was a customer of Nvidia. The data center company was buying Nvidia's AI chips and is now under a criminal investigation over claims that it was bypassing export controls in an effort to get those advanced chips into China. The company has since been placed on a U.S. blocklist.
Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia came after days of campaigning for his reinstatement, including by U.S. President Trump. Trump later pressured Nvidia to rehire him, going so far as to call into a board meeting to do so. Despite Trump's backing, Jensen Huang must still face Congressional and Senate committees to discuss Nvidia, export controls, and any national security threats brought about by his infidelity.

articles.title: Spotify quitó a Livi, la voz del DJ con IA, y usuarios de habla hispana se quejaron del cambio
articles.text:
El 10 de noviembre, Spotify anunció en su sitio oficial una ampliación de las voces de DJ, la función Premium que mezcla canciones recomendadas con comentarios de una voz sintética. Las nuevas opciones comenzaron a desplegarse ese día en los mercados donde la función está disponible.
La actualización suma siete voces en inglés, con acentos británico, estadounidense, irlandés, australiano e indio, y dos en español: Fabi y Nico, ambas identificadas como de México. La voz en inglés original, conocida como DJ X, sigue disponible, según la compañía.
En el anuncio, Spotify describe a Fabi como una voz ingeniosa, amigable y siempre un paso adelante, y a Nico como auténtico y presente. El comunicado no menciona a Livi ni explica qué ocurrió con ella.
Lo que respondió Spotify a las quejas
Según respondió a usuarios la cuenta de soporte SpotifyCares en redes sociales, Livi ya no está disponible y el DJ utiliza ahora la voz de Fabi. En otra respuesta, la cuenta explicó que la función sigue en fase beta y que la compañía seguirá desarrollándola para sumar nuevas voces en español.
Spotify no ha aclarado si Livi volverá. Tampoco explicó por qué decidió retirarla ni si la elección de voces en español cambia según el país, ya que el anuncio solo identifica a las dos nuevas como mexicanas.
Quién era Livi y cómo llegó
Spotify presentó el DJ en español el 17 de julio de 2024, en versión beta y para usuarios Premium de España y de países de Latinoamérica como Argentina, Chile, Colombia, México y Perú, entre otros. Antes, la función solo existía en inglés.
La voz de Livi se creó a partir de Olivia Quiroz Roa, entonces editora musical sénior de Spotify con base en Ciudad de México. Según la empresa, fue elegida tras un casting internacional porque los usuarios que la evaluaron la sintieron cercana, como recibir recomendaciones de una amiga.
Entonces Spotify afirmó que tenía millones de oyentes de habla hispana y que las conversaciones en redes sociales sobre el DJ en español habían crecido más de 215% en los meses previos.
Más control para quien no quiere comentarios
La actualización de noviembre incluye otra novedad: los usuarios pueden desactivar los comentarios entre canciones para que la música suene con menos interrupciones. El DJ solo interviene con mensajes breves al iniciarse o cuando el usuario toca el botón para cambiar el ambiente.
Para elegir voz, el usuario debe abrir Spotify en el teléfono, buscar DJ y tocar el menú de tres puntos, donde también se ajustan los comentarios. Spotify sostiene que el 80% de los usuarios de DJ vuelve a usarlo semana tras semana.
Las nuevas voces y los controles comenzaron a implementarse el 10 de noviembre para los usuarios Premium de los mercados donde DJ ya está disponible.
Spotify prepara para 2027 un servicio pago de remezclas con IA
Spotify planea lanzar en el primer trimestre de 2027 un servicio pago que permitirá a sus suscriptores crear remezclas de canciones con inteligencia artificial, con un posible estreno en febrero, según el Financial Times.
El complemento costaría entre USD 4 y USD 5 adicionales sobre el plan Premium y permitiría transformar el estilo de una canción o simular que un artista interpreta el tema de otro. Las regalías y reproducciones se acreditarían a los artistas originales.
La compañía ya cerró acuerdos con Universal Music Group, Merlin y Believe, pero todavía negocia con Sony Music y Warner Music. Según Music Business Worldwide, el codirector ejecutivo Gustav Söderström afirmó que Spotify podría avanzar sin el respaldo de todas las discográficas.

articles.title: AI infrastructure stocks continue their slide, but Anthropic closes higher
articles.text:
AI infrastructure stocks continue their slide, but Anthropic closes higher
Investors continued to offload artificial intelligence infrastructure stocks today, but Anthropic PBC recouped some of its losses from earlier this week.
The AI selloff reportedly began in August. It accelerated on Nov. 17, the day Nvidia Corp. CEO Jensen Huang resigned over his affair with a former executive of Megaspeed, a cloud provider under investigation over alleged export control violations. Huang returned to the helm of the chipmaker Monday.
Nvidia closed at $173.73 the day before Huang’s resignation. It dropped as low as $125 during the executive’s two-week hiatus and surged 30% on Monday, the day he returned. Nvidia lost some of its recent gains in today’s trading session: Its share price closed 3.8% lower.
Other AI chip stocks have also taken a hit. Broadcom Inc. closed a small fraction of a percent lower than yesterday, while Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Intel Corp. fell 1.6% and 0.6%, respectively.
The semiconductor stock that logged the biggest drop today is Ambarella Inc., a relatively low-profile maker of AI image analysis chips. Its accelerators are used by edge devices to process footage from their cameras. Ambarella dropped 19.8% today after closing 19% lower yesterday.
The stock’s decline was driven not so much by the broader AI selloff, but rather the weak earnings that Ambarella posted on Tuesday. The company missed expectations across the board. Ambarella said that some customers had canceled or delayed orders to mitigate the financial impact of soaring memory prices.
Micron Inc., one of the world’s top memory chip suppliers, saw its market capitalization drop more than 4.5% today. That’s despite CEO Sanjay Mehrotra’s recent disclosure that the company has already sold out 75% of its 2027 manufacturing capacity. According to the executive, the gap between memory demand and supply is only set to increase next year.
Companies downstream from chipmakers in the AI data center supply chain fared better. Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. ended the trading session 1.8% higher after dipping into the red earlier today, while Dell Technologies Inc. gained 0.64%.
In contrast, the major cloud providers weren’t left out of today’s selloff. Amazon.com Inc., the cloud market’s largest player, closed 3% lower. Microsoft Corp. and Google LLC dropped 1.25% and 2%, respectively. Oracle Corp., which trails the three companies in market share but has emerged as an important AI infrastructure provider, took the biggest hit: It’s down 5% from yesterday.
Anthropic ended the trading session with a 1% gain. The company thereby recouped some of yesterday’s losses, which pushed its stock below its $80 debut price. Anthropic went public last week through a record-setting offering that raised more than $93 billion.
Overall, the tech-heavy Nasdaq lost 0.6% while the S&P 500 slid 0.25%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.33%.

articles.title: I tested Philips Hue Essential and White & Color Ambiance smart light bulbs side-by-side — and this is the one I'd choose for my home
articles.text:
If you're shopping for Philips Hue lights this Black Friday, you'll notice there are two main types: the classic Philips Hue series, in their distinctive black and purple boxes, and Hue Essential, which are packaged in light blue. So what's the difference, and which should you choose?
Philips Hue Essential bulbs are a more affordable version of the company's standard smart lights, and they perform incredibly well considering they're less than half the price. There are a few limitations, though. For example, Philips Hue Essential bulbs offer a maximum brightness of 806 lumens, whereas standard Philips Hue White & Color Ambiance bulbs range from 800 to 1,600 lumens.
In most other respects, the two are very similar, and considering the huge difference in price, I'd recommend the Hue Essential series in most situations. Comparing the two side-by-side, there are only a couple of differences to be aware of.
US deals
If you want to expand your Philips Hue setup into more rooms without taking out a second mortgage, this is the Black Friday deal for you. Philips Hue Essential bulbs are excellent, work with all other Huge devices, and with this offer they're less than $11 each.
Knocked down to almost half price, there's a tempting $72 saving to be had on these white and color smart lightbulbs thanks to this Black Friday deal. That's just over $25 per bulb.
UK deals
This Black Friday, there's £23 to be saved on this four-pack of E27 Hue Essential bulbs. Whether a treat for yourself or a gift for someone else, at just over £10 each, they're a smart buy.
With 30% off, this is a respectable Black Friday discount courtesy of John Lewis, and better than Amazon's current offerings, but at just a whisker over £30, each of these bulbs is three times the price of its Hue Essential counterpart.
Responsiveness
To see how the two would compare, I set up a pair of lamps – one with a Philips Hue Essential bulb, and the other with an 800-lumen Philips Hue White & Color Ambiance bulb. I added them to the same room in the Philips Hue app, which would enable me to control them simultaneously, and directly compare and contrast their output.
During most of the tests I ran, it was difficult to spot any difference between the two. Both were equally responsive, and produced colors that were identical to my naked eye when I switched between scenes. According to Signify (the company behind the Philips Hue brand), Essential bulbs use different color-matching technology to regular Hue lights; but personally, I had a hard time telling the difference.
Having said that, I did notice a dark band at the top of the Essential bulb, which wasn't present on the premium bulb. This was most apparent with purple and blue light. Note that it isn't something you'll notice if you're using the bulb in a ceiling light or table lamp, and is unlikely to be a deal-breaker unless you're exceptionally picky.
Brightness
The two were equally bright (as expected), although if I'd used a higher-output White & Color Ambiance bulb, then it would have been appreciably brighter.
However, there's one important difference that you should be aware of, particularly if you're looking for smart bulbs that will produce a natural-looking sunrise and sunset to help you wake up feeling refreshed, or to create subtle ambient lighting in your living room.
With both bulbs dialled down to their dimmest setting, the Hue Essential bulb was much brighter than the more expensive White & Color Ambiance model, as you can see in the photo below. That's because the Hue Essential bulb can only be dimmed to 2% of its maximum brightness, whereas the regular bulb can drop to just 0.2%.
Color temperature
I also found that the Essential bulb tended to show a slightly warmer cast, due to its narrower white light spectrum (2,200–6,500K compared to 1,000-20,00K for a regular Hue bulb). Depending on your preferred light temperature, the difference could be apparent if you use the two different types of bulbs in close proximity,
I wouldn't mix and match regular Hue and Hue Essential bulbs within the same room. However, they're an excellent option for those wanting to setup a Philips Hue system but have previously been intimidated by the price. They're also great if you're looking to extend your existing system to more rooms in your home, without splashing too much cash.
Price
The Philips Hue Essential range is designed to be an accessible entry point into the world of smart lighting, with the bulbs coming in at a much cheaper price than standard Philips Hue ones.
One Philips Hue Essential bulb (either screw or bayonet) costs $24.99 / £19.99 (about AU$40) at full price. If you want several, you can save money by opting for a multipack. A twin-pack costs $44.99 / £32.99 (about AU$70), and a four-pack comes in at $59.99 / £49.99 (about AU$90).
During Black Friday, those prices drop substantially, and you can get Hue Essential bulbs for around $10 / £11 each if you buy them in a multipack.
For comparison, a twin-pack of regular 800-lumen Philips Hue White & Color Ambiance bulbs costs $98.99 / £84.99 / AU$149.25, and a four-pack is $185.99 / £169.99 / AU$290.50. That's the starting price for a maximum brightness of 800 lumens; brighter bulbs cost even more.
These bulbs also get price cuts for Black Friday, and during the sale period you can expect to pay around $25 / £30 each when you pick up a multi-pack.

articles.title: Mopas triangulares, 21.000 Pa y una base que apenas necesita mantenimiento: Dyson rebaja su robot aspirador y fregona por el Black Friday
articles.text:
Si buscase ahora mismo un dispositivo para ayudarme a limpiar, iría a por un robot aspirador. Este Black Friday estamos viendo muy buenas ofertas, incluso en modelos que cuentan con sistema de fregado avanzado y bases de autovaciado que hacen que el mantenimiento que necesiten sea mínimo. Pero, ¿y cuál elegir?
Robot aspirador y fregona Dyson R2 Nurovi™ Wash+Dry
Uno de los que tenemos en el punto de mira es Dyson R2 Nurovi Wash+Dry, el robot aspirador y fregona que han estado probando nuestros compañeros de TikTok y que, además, tenemos rebajado ahora mismo de forma temporal: está disponible por 549 euros frente a los 849 euros que cuesta normalmente.
Un robot aspirador y fregona que llega a todos los rincones
Este robot aspirador y fregona de Dyson, como explican nuestros compañeros, tiene un sistema bastante particular. Sus mopas, que tienen forma triangular, se pueden extender mientras el robot circula. Eso, en la práctica, se traduce en que será capaz de llegar a esquinas y bordes, zonas que la mayoría de robots se dejan atrás sin limpiar, acumulando suciedad.
El sistema anterior se combina con hasta 21.000 Pa de potencia de succión, una cifra elevada y más que suficiente para recoger polvo y otras partículas de suciedad que haya en el suelo. Además, como tiene un cepillo antienredos, podrá recoger pelos sin que se líen o produzcan atascos en el robot. Eso mismo hace que sea una opción muy interesante si tienes mascotas en casa.
Todo eso del robot, pero su base es uno de sus puntos clave. Cuando el robot Dyson R2 Nurovi Wash+Dry termina de limpiar y regresa a la base, vaciará todos sus residuos, lavará las mopas con agua a 75 grados y las secará con aire caliente a 45 grados. Además, su depósito es capaz de almacenar suciedad durante hasta 90 días, lo que hace que sea un dispositivo que necesita muy poco mantenimiento.
Tanto si tienes una casa grande como un piso pequeño, podrás utilizar la app MyDyson para configurar el funcionamiento de este robot. Con ella podrás, entre otras cosas, organizar limpiezas, crear mapas y elegir qué zonas quieres que limpie o evite. Todo ello hace que sea un robot aspirador y fregona supercompleto que, además, tiene un descuento ahora mismo de 300 euros.

articles.title: Windows 11 : Microsoft libère plus de 860 Mo de RAM… occupés par ses propres logiciels
articles.text:
Microsoft affirme avoir récupéré plus de 860 Mo de mémoire vive sur Windows 11 en allégeant ses logiciels.
Au printemps dernier, Microsoft a reconnu que Windows 11 consommait bien trop de mémoire. Quelque mois plus tard, l’éditeur avait promis une cure d’amaigrissement pour ses PC équipés de 8 Go de RAM. Une baisse de la consommation avait été également notée en octobre avec la mise à jour 26H2 du système d’exploitation. Microsoft vient enfin d’en dire plus sur ces gains. On fait le point.
Microsoft a fait le grand ménage dans ses applications
La dernière conférence Ignite, qui s’est déroulée le 18 novembre dernier, a été l’occasion pour Microsoft de faire le point sur ses promesses concernant la consommation excessive de RAM de son OS. Ian LeGrow, Vice-président en charge du coeur des systèmes d’exploitation, a notamment expliqué que les équipes de la firme avaient réussi à libérer plus d’un demi-gigaoctet de mémoire en se penchant sur les services Defender, Purview et OneDrive, qui fonctionnent en arrière-plan. Elles ont aussi réussi à réduire de 360 Mo la consommation de la suite Microsoft 365.
Pour en arriver là, Microsoft a dû faire des ajustements conséquents. La firme a décidé de ne plus lancer systématiquement des modules jugés superflus. Certains composants qui reposent sur les mêmes briques logicielles partagent désormais la même zone mémoire. Les équipes ont aussi pris le temps d’optimiser les applications. On salue l’effort, mais on aurait quand même préféré que Microsoft conçoive des outils sobres dès le départ.
Un effort motivé par la pénurie de mémoire
Bien sûr, l’envolée du prix de la mémoire n’est pas pour rien dans la prise de conscience de Microsoft. Ian LeGrow l’a d’ailleurs reconnu lors de la conférence : « le prix de la mémoire a explosé. Par conséquent, une plus grande capacité de mémoire dans les appareils a un impact considérable sur le coût de ces appareils. ». Il a notamment expliqué que « depuis janvier dernier, (la firme avait) consacré beaucoup de temps et d’efforts à l’amélioration de la mémoire sur toute une gamme d’appareils, en (se) concentrant particulièrement sur les appareils de 16 Go et de 8 Go. »
Le résultat ? Les applications Office seraient aujourd'hui 10 % plus rapides sur des ordinateurs possédant 8 Go de RAM et les tâches peuvent être réalisées 21 % plus vite. Afin de vérifier si ces promesses étaient véritablement tenues, l’équipe de Windows Latest a fait des mesures après avoir installé la mise à jour 26H2. Sur un portable de 8 Go, la consommation passe de 5 à 3,3 Go au démarrage. Sur un PC de 16 Go datant de 3 ans, le gain atteint même 2 Go. Seul bémol, dès que les widgets sont ouverts, la consommation repart à la hausse.
Microsoft a donc bien amélioré les choses, mais la route est encore longue.

articles.title: Nintendo Switch OLED atinge 35% OFF às vésperas da Black Friday
articles.text:
Nintendo Switch OLED atinge 35% OFF às vésperas da Black Friday
Nintendo Switch com tela OLED e o game Super Mario Bros. Wonder incluso, sai 35% mais barato no Pix com cupom no Mercado Livre, em oferta da Black Week 2026
O Nintendo Switch OLED está saindo por R$ 1.766 no Pix com cupom ELETROTECHMELI no Mercado Livre. O kit com o console, o game Super Mario Bros. Wonder e três meses da Nintendo Switch Online, alcança o menor preço histórico durante a Black Week 2026, com desconto de 41% sobre o original de R$ 2.699.
Corra: pois o cupom pode acabar a qualquer momento!
O menor preço que já encontramos para o Nintendo Switch OLED foi R$ 1.679, na Black Friday de 2025 (Mercado Livre). Fora de datas promocionais, o melhor foi R$ 1.739 (Magalu, 17/11/2026), e esta oferta está R$ 27,90 acima.
O Switch OLED é a versão revisada do console mais vendido da Nintendo, cuja principal novidade é sua tela de 7″ com pontos orgânicos. Ela reproduz cores realistas e preto perfeito na resolução HD (1.280 x 720 pixels), a mesma do Switch original LCD.
A dock possui uma porta Ethernet para conexões de rede cabeadas com mais estabilidade, e o suporte traseiro está mais largo e melhor ajustável, oferecendo mais segurança ao usar o gadget no modo semiportátil.
Fora isso, o console oferece a mesma experiência do modelo padrão. Você pode usá-lo como um portátil completo, com os controles Joy-Con afixados nas laterais, apoiado sobre uma superfície ou ligado à TV pela dock com resolução Full HD, suportando até quatro jogadores locais.
O kit inclui três meses da Nintendo Switch Online, que dá acesso a partidas online e outras vantagens, e o game Super Mario Bros. Wonder, aventura que une a jogabilidade clássica da série com novas e divertidas mecânicas.
Este console é equipado com o chip Nvidia Tegra X1 e 64 GB de espaço interno, e suporta cartões microSDXC de até 2 TB. Sua bateria resiste de 4,5 a 9 horas de uso portátil, segundo a fabricante, e é alimentada pela dock no modo sistema de mesa.
O Nintendo Switch OLED (R$ 1.580 no Pix com cupom ELETROTECHMELI) vem com dois Joy-Cons com controle por movimentos e tem acesso a uma vasta biblioteca de games exclusivos da Nintendo.
A Black Friday é a principal campanha do varejo antes do Natal; a edição 2026 ocorre nesta sexta-feira (27) e lojas como o Mercado Livre oferecem cupons e promoções em gadgets com condições especiais até o fim do mês.

articles.title: iiyama Launches ProLite XCB4994DQSU-B1 49-inch Curved Dual QHD Monitor
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
iiyama Launches ProLite XCB4994DQSU-B1 49-inch Curved Dual QHD Monitor
iiyama has introduced a new 49-inch curved monitor, the ProLite XCB4994DQSU-B1. This office-oriented monitor has a 32:9 aspect ratio and a native resolution of 5120 x 1440 pixels. It is basically the equivalent of two QHD (2560 x 1440) displays placed side by side, giving users an ultrawide workspace without a central bezel. The VA panel with a matte finish has a 1000R curvature and supports refresh rates of up to 120 Hz. It features a typical brightness of 400 nits, a static contrast ratio of 3,000:1, and a 2 ms gray-to-gray response time. It covers 100% of the sRGB color space and 80% of NTSC. The monitor also supports HDR10 and Adaptive Sync, with a variable refresh rate range of 48-120 Hz over DisplayPort and 48-60 Hz over HDMI. Other display features include flicker-free operation and a blue light reducer.
Connectivity includes two HDMI 2.0 inputs and two DisplayPort 1.2 inputs. The integrated USB hub provides two USB-A 3.2 Gen 1 ports and two USB-C ports. All support data transfer speeds of up to 5 Gbps. The USB-A ports provide up to 4.5 W of power, while the USB-C ports are rated for up to 7.5 W. A headphone jack and two built-in 5 W speakers are also included. The monitor comes with a height and tilt-adjustable stand, and 100 x 100 mm VESA mounting support. iiyama lists the ProLite XCB4994DQSU-B1 on its European website for €668, including VAT.

articles.title: Siempre nos han dicho que parar 15 minutos a hacer ejercicio mejora el estudio. La ciencia dice que no es tan sencillo
articles.text:
Cuando nos ponemos a estudiar delante de un tocho de apuntes, es fácil que al rato la concentración comience a flaquear. En este caso, levantarse de la silla para hacer 15 minutos de ejercicio moderado es algo que siempre nos han dicho que puede despejarnos y mejorar el rendimiento académico. El problema es que no es tan fácil.
La base. Uno de los pilares habituales para defender los descansos activos viene de un ensayo publicado en 2014. En este un grupo de investigadores evaluó a 123 niños de entre 10 y 11 años de cuatro colegios de primaria tras hacer una hora de deberes. De este modo, cada estudiante pasó por cuatro escenarios distintos: seguir sin pausa, hacer un descanso pasivo, realizar 15 minutos de actividad física moderada o hacer 15 minutos de ejercicio vigoroso.
El resultado determinó que la mejora cognitiva más marcada se daba en el grupo de niños que habían hecho una actividad moderada. Por contra, el ejercicio vigoroso arrojó resultados similares a los que se vieron en hacer un simple descanso pasivo, seguramente por la fatiga que genera.
Tiene sentido. Para explicar cómo el movimiento puede ayudar a fijar todo lo que se ha estudiado, se suele recurrir a un estudio de 2021 donde se analizó todo lo que ocurría en el cerebro cuando se estaba haciendo bicicleta estática. Aquí los investigadores observaron que tanto el ejercicio moderado como el intenso elevaban los niveles de BDNF del cerebro y de anandamida, un endocannabinoide implicado en la plasticidad sináptica.
Tres meses después, los participantes recordaban mejor las asociaciones aprendidas tras la sesión de ejercicio moderado que tras el reposo, un efecto acompañado de cambios en los patrones de activación del hipocampo detectados mediante resonancia magnética funcional.
El deporte influye. Otro argumento habitual señala que los deportes de equipo aportan un extra cognitivo frente a actividades individuales como correr o nadar. Y esto es algo que también se ha estudiado, determinando que los deportes en lo que el entorno cambia constantemente, como el fútbol, favorecen en mayor medida el control inhibitorio y la flexibilidad cognitiva.
El rendimiento académico. Hasta aquí sabemos que el deporte puede mejorar nuestro cerebro y las conexiones que va realizando, pero cuando comprobamos si de verdad tiene un impacto en cómo rendimos en el estudio, la verdad es que hay varios matices. Estos los aporta una revisión paraguas donde se comparó el impacto de la actividad física puntual a la hecha durante vairos meses.
El resultado nos mostró que, mientras la actividad física regular y sostenida en el tiempo tiene un efecto positivo moderado en los logros académicos, el ejercicio puntual no mostró esta misma mejora de rendimiento. Esto nos hace que ver que parar de estudiar 15 minutos para hacer ejercicio no aporta beneficios al estudio, sino que es importante mantener una rutina si de verdad queremos ver sus efectos.

articles.title: China's memory giants have a record year as Huawei ships HBM without a named source
articles.text:
The state of China's memory industry in 2026 — CXMT and YMTC are booming, but HBM remains a headache
A record year for Chinese memory, while Huawei ships its own HBM without a named source.
China’s homegrown memory comes largely from two companies, CXMT for DRAM and YMTC for 3D NAND, and both are booming. CXMT’s Oct. 30 quarterly report shows a nine-month net profit of ¥132.0 billion ($19.6 billion), against a ¥5.28 billion ($785 million) loss a year earlier, on revenue more than eight times as high, at ¥269.0 billion ($40.0 billion). YMTC’s numbers, just for Q1, are at ¥47.04 billion ($7.0 billion) in revenue and ¥33.38 billion ($5.0 billion) in profit attributable to shareholders, more than double 2025.
Both are expanding and adding fabs, and each is edging into the other’s products. No Chinese manufacturer can yet produce high-bandwidth memory (HBM) in volume, though. HBM is the stacked DRAM that AI accelerators depend on, and currently the U.S. bars Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron from selling it into China. CXMT’s prospectus lists no HBM project, though its HBM3E is reportedly in risk production, an early run before the process is fully qualified. Huawei designs its own HBM but doesn’t say who makes it.
Memory is a commodity, so the story is in the wafers. We cover the companies running memory fabs in China: CXMT, YMTC, a handful of smaller Chinese fabs, and Samsung and SK hynix, which run some of their biggest plants there. Huawei makes the cut for its HBM program, though it has no memory fab. Fabless designers, module makers, and NOR flash producers are left out, except XMC for its HBM line. Fab counts, products, and financials come from filings and company statements; capacities, planned fabs, and the HBM progress that remains the big question mark rest largely on anonymous reporting. Let's dive into the current state of the Chinese DRAM industry.
CXMT: three DRAM fabs running, three more on the way
CXMT, short for ChangXin Memory Technologies, is China’s biggest homegrown DRAM maker. It operates two 12-inch fabs in Hefei and one in Beijing, each able to produce around 100,000 wafers a month. It is also building fabs in Shanghai and Hefei and is in funding talks for a second Beijing fab, which together could take it past 600,000 wafers a month. The Shanghai fab is expected to have two to three times the capacity of the Hefei base, with tools going in during the second half of 2026 and volume in 2027.
CXMT is now the fourth-largest DRAM maker worldwide, with 9.5% of DRAM revenue in Q2, according to TrendForce. CXMT says LPDDR6 is in mass production for Xiaomi, and its president says the first 4F² product, a server DDR5 RDIMM, is due by year-end. This comes after record first-half revenue of ¥150.3 billion ($22.4 billion), net profit of ¥77.6 billion ($11.5 billion), an 84.84% gross margin on its main business, and a listing on Shanghai’s STAR Market on July 27. Third-quarter profit alone was ¥54.4 billion ($8.1 billion).
The primary products are DDR5 rated up to 8,000 MT/s with 24Gb dies, and LPDDR5X rated up to 10,667 MT/s. CXMT says its fifth-generation G5 platform reaches 11.95nm active-area half-pitch with quadruple patterning for 24Gb LPDDR5X, and gets at least 50% more dies out of each wafer than G4, counted as 8Gb dies. CXMT says a DRAM product on its sixth-generation platform has also completed engineering-sample validation. Jeongdong Choe, Senior Technology Fellow at TechInsights, told Tom’s Hardware Premium that the firm measured the smallest active half-pitch on CXMT’s G4 at 14.8nm and hasn’t analyzed G5 yet.
CXMT lists no GDDR or 3D NAND among its products and is limited to nodes made without extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography as it lacks the tooling. CXMT’s second Beijing fab, however, is planned to include a 3D NAND R&D line, which could shake things up. The growth picture for now is capacity and price, with the tests of scaling without EUV lying with the RDIMM and Shanghai fab.
YMTC: going all out on NAND, DRAM in testing
YMTC, short for Yangtze Memory Technologies Co., has two fabs of its own in Wuhan, which can produce about 200,000 wafers a month together. A third fab in the Xinzhou district, registered in September last year, is expected to produce about 50,000 wafers a month by 2027 and eventually 100,000 at full capacity. While YMTC is known for its NAND flash, roughly half of Fab 3’s output is earmarked for DRAM. The company also makes enterprise SSDs and UFS and eMMC parts, and sells consumer SSDs under its ZhiTai brand. YMTC filed its own STAR Market prospectus, to match CXMT’s, on Aug. 21.
NAND flash was, until recently, the star of the show for Chinese memory, and YMTC’s Xtacking technology is one reason why. Its fifth-generation Xtacking 4.0 die, used in 1Tb TLC and 2Tb QLC parts, has 294 gates, and Choe told us 267 of them are active word lines. Most of what YMTC ships, however, is still 160- and 232-layer NAND. Samsung licensed YMTC’s Xtacking bonding patents in February 2025, so the technology could be considered both proven and valuable.
Omdia data put YMTC at 38.5% of China’s NAND market in Q2, ahead of Samsung’s 33.5%. Globally, YMTC ranked third in NAND shipments in Q2, according to Counterpoint Research, and its share of NAND revenue rose from 9% to 14% between Q1 2025 and Q1 2026. YMTC’s stated long-term targets are about 20% of global NAND supply and about 500,000 wafers a month, DRAM included.
For DRAM, YMTC’s Fab 2 is running about 5,000 wafers a month of 16Gb LPDDR5, still in R&D and testing, with no plan for mass production. However, a 9,600 MT/s part on a vertical channel transistor (VCT) 4F² cell is slated for mass production at Fab 3 if it passes qualification. XMC, YMTC’s former foundry unit, left its control in July.
The smaller fabs: Jinhua’s DDR4 and SwaySure’s unfinished line
Two smaller fabs worthy of note are Fujian Jinhua and SwaySure. The former has a 12-inch fab in Jinjiang, which produces custom DDR4 on 25nm, at 40,000–50,000 wafers a month, with about 90% going to Huawei. DDR4 prices have surged this year, by as much as 50% in the first quarter alone, as the big suppliers wind DDR4 down in favor of server and HBM parts and enterprise buyers stock up.
SwaySure, a Shenzhen company founded in March 2022 with state-owned investment, is building a 28nm 12-inch DRAM line and is reportedly backed by Huawei. Analyst Jim Handy of Objective Analysis doubts the 28nm line could make HBM. Neither company responded to our requests for additional information.
| China’s memory fabs: what each makes, and what it doesn’t |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Company | Fab (location) | Makes | Notably doesn’t make | Status | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CXMT | Hefei Phase 1 and Phase 2 (Anhui); Beijing (Yizhuang) | DRAM | GDDR, 3D NAND, HBM in volume | Producing; about 100,000 wafers a month each | 
| CXMT | Shanghai DRAM fab | DRAM for servers, PCs, and cars, plus HBM lines | — | Under construction; volume in 2027 | 
| CXMT | Shanghai HBM packaging plant | HBM stacking and packaging | — | Under construction; due by the end of 2026 | 
| CXMT | New Hefei fab; second Beijing fab | DRAM; NAND R&D line planned for Beijing | — | Hefei under construction; Beijing in funding talks | 
| YMTC | Wuhan Fab 1 and Fab 2 (Hubei) | 3D NAND, TLC and QLC, on Xtacking | DRAM in volume, HBM | Producing; about 200,000 wafers a month combined | 
| YMTC | Wuhan Fab 3 | 3D NAND; DRAM planned (9,600 MT/s LPDDR5 on a VCT 4F² cell) | — | Equipping; starts late 2026 or 2027; about 50,000 wafers a month by 2027 | 
| YMTC | Two more fabs, sites not reported | 3D NAND and some DRAM | — | Planned; 100,000 wafers a month each | 
| XMC | Wuhan, two 12-inch fabs and a reported HBM line | Specialty foundry: NOR flash, MCUs, 3D integration | HBM (a 3,000-wafer-a-month line under construction since February 2024) | Operating; out of YMTC’s control since July 2026 | 
| Fujian Jinhua (JHICC) | Jinjiang (Fujian) | Custom DDR4 on 25nm | DDR5; HBM unproven | Producing; 40,000 to 50,000 wafers a month | 
| SwaySure | Shenzhen (Guangdong) | DRAM on a 28nm line, planned | — | Under construction | 
HBM: who’s chasing, and who isn’t
Not every AI chip needs HBM. Inference hardware can get by on LPDDR5X, as Axera’s AX8860P does in Sipeed’s MaixStation, or on DRAM bonded straight onto the processor, the approach PieceMakers is betting on. Training-class accelerators like Huawei’s Ascend series still need HBM, though, and since the U.S. banned the export of HBM as of Dec. 2, 2024, China can’t buy it from the big three memory makers.
Even those who can get HBM are seeing heat and yield issues with larger memory stacks, specifically 12-high. SK hynix said on its Q3 2026 earnings call that some customers’ spec changes show “demand is indeed overwhelming supply,” and that lowering the stack is “a strategy to increase the number of cubes that can be obtained for the same capacity.” This mirrors other indicators, including potential Nvidia Rubin Ultra decisions, and it suggests that HBM is in short enough supply that even easier-to-build stacks are in high demand.
CXMT has sampled HBM with Tongfu, and HBM3 built on its 16nm-class G4 node to Huawei. Its HBM3E has now gone to several domestic AI chip designers as samples, with limited production due by the end of 2026, and an expansion expected in 2027. Yields are only about 20% to 30%, though, against about 70% at SK hynix, and in testing the chips performed closer to SK hynix’s HBM3 than to its HBM3E. An HBM packaging plant in Shanghai worth at least ¥17.1 billion ($2.5 billion) is targeted for year-end, with capacity for about 30,000 units a month.
Tongfu reportedly sampled HBM2, but its own filings mention only DRAM and flash packaging. Huawei said last year that “we will offer two proprietary HBMs.” It launched the Atlas 350 card in March, built on the Ascend 950PR, which carries 112GB of HBM. XMC has had a 3,000-wafer-a-month HBM line under construction since early 2024, but no production has been confirmed. At this time, YMTC, Jinhua, and SwaySure don’t appear to make HBM, though reports say YMTC is developing the through-silicon via (TSV) stacking it would need, and Jinhua was named in a Huawei-led HBM group in 2024.
Huawei said in 2025 that the 950PR would use HiBL 1.0, its own “low-cost HBM”; TechInsights told us it hasn’t analyzed HiBL 1.0 yet. However, Huawei’s 2025 roadmap specced out the 950PR's 128GB of HBM at 1.6TB/s. Huawei said that its 950PR is “optimized for the prefill stage of inference,” which is compute-heavy with “lower demand for memory access bandwidth,” and that using HiBL 1.0 is “more cost-effective than HBM3E and HBM4E” for that workload. The higher-end HiZQ 2.0, for the 950DT, is due in Q4 and, by Huawei’s figures, brings 144GB at 4TB/s. In both cases, Huawei’s supplier remains in doubt, and the company did not respond to our requests for comment.
| Who is chasing HBM in China |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Company | HBM effort | Stage | 
|---|---|---|
| CXMT | HBM3 and HBM3E DRAM | HBM3 samples to Huawei; HBM3E sampling, with limited production by year-end at 20–30% yields | 
| CXMT | Shanghai HBM packaging plant | Under construction; due by the end of 2026 | 
| Huawei | HiBL 1.0, in the Ascend 950PR | Shipping since March 2026 in the Atlas 350 (112GB); maker not disclosed | 
| Huawei | HiZQ 2.0, in the Ascend 950DT (144GB at 4TB/s) | Due in Q4 2026; maker not disclosed | 
| XMC | HBM packaging line, 3,000 wafers a month | Under construction since February 2024; production not confirmed | 
| Tongfu Microelectronics | HBM packaging | HBM samples with CXMT and HBM2 samples reported; filings show only DRAM and flash packaging | 
| YMTC | None in production | TSV stacking in development | 
| Fujian Jinhua | Named in a Huawei-led HBM group in 2024 | Unproven | 
| SwaySure | None known | Doubtful on a 28nm line (analyst Jim Handy) | 
| Samsung, SK hynix, Micron | Can’t sell HBM into China | Barred by the U.S. rule of Dec. 2, 2024 | 
The foreign fabs, and the restrictive rules
Of the companies from outside China, Samsung and SK hynix both run large memory fabs on Chinese soil, and both are now upgrading their NAND lines there. Samsung’s Xi’an handles about 40% of the company’s NAND, including 236-layer, or V8, in volume, with X2 converting to 286-layer, or V9, this year, slated to reach 5,000 V9 wafers a month in December and 40,000 by December 2027. A Samsung spokesperson told Tom’s Hardware Premium that the company “has been transitioning its existing manufacturing operations in Xi’an to 9th-generation V-NAND in compliance with U.S. export regulations and in close communication with the U.S. government.”
SK hynix’s Wuxi produces 30–40% of its DRAM and has moved from 1z to 1a, with the EUV layers done in Korea. Dalian turns out about 100,000 wafers a month of 192-layer floating-gate NAND and is moving to 240 layers, the most SK hynix is authorized to make there.
SK hynix, which already sells NAND with up to 321 layers elsewhere, told us it needs a U.S. license every year and declined to give product details or capacities for individual fabs. The company said that it intends for its 321-layer flash to be “over 50% of domestic (Korean) capacity in the fourth quarter,” which puts the Dalian lag into relief.
SK hynix also has “Mod B,” a second fab at its Dalian site that was completed in 2023. The company has reportedly tied a new U.S. NAND fab to Washington, letting it ship more U.S. tools there: Dalian’s 2026 license capped its equipment, no 2027 license had been issued as of mid-October, and its U.S.-based Solidigm unit has applied for an export license to buy more tools for Mod B. SK hynix told Tom’s Hardware that “no capacity expansion is being sought for the Dalian Mod B” and has been installing equipment at its Dalian factory.
Solidigm is now reportedly in talks with the U.S. Commerce Department over a $45 billion chip plant in the U.S., but wants Washington’s approval to ship equipment to upgrade the Dalian plant first, arguing that the upgrade would help finance the new site. However, SK hynix denied an earlier report of such a deal and says no specific plans have been finalized.
As for its Chongqing packaging plant, SK hynix told us it is “exploring various strategic options to enhance our packaging competitiveness,” though nothing is final. Elsewhere in China, Samsung’s Suzhou plant handles assembly and testing, and Micron’s Xi’an site handles packaging and testing.
All of this plays out inside a U.S.-China fight over chips that AI has only sped up. CXMT isn’t currently on the Commerce Department’s Entity List, which bars U.S. suppliers from shipping to listed companies without a license; YMTC, Jinhua, and SwaySure are. Jinhua has been on the list since 2018; SwaySure joined in December 2024 over its Huawei links, and YMTC was added in December 2022.
CXMT is, however, on the Pentagon’s 1260H list of Chinese military companies, which it is suing over. It’s been on the list since January 2025 and stayed on with the June update. For Samsung and SK hynix, the validated end-user status that let both firms ship in U.S. tools was revoked as of Dec. 31, 2025. Annual licenses are now required, and the Commerce Department has said it doesn’t intend to license capacity expansions or technology upgrades. Meanwhile, both companies say upgrades are under way, which sits uneasily with that policy.
China, for its part, has been weighing broader technology export controls and has now proposed adding 40 technologies, reportedly including some memory-chip design technologies, to its Catalogue of Technologies Prohibited and Restricted from Export. The draft, Announcement 48 from China’s Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology, is open for comment until Nov. 15, and anyone exporting a listed technology must register first.
| Foreign-owned memory fabs in China |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Owner | Fab (location) | Makes | Share of owner’s output | Status | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Samsung | Xi’an X1 (Shaanxi) | 3D NAND: 236-layer V8; V6 ended | About 40% of Samsung’s NAND (both Xi’an fabs) | Producing | 
| Samsung | Xi’an X2 (Shaanxi) | 3D NAND, converting to 286-layer V9 | In the Xi’an figure | Converting to V9; 5,000 V9 wafers a month in December 2026, 40,000 by December 2027 | 
| SK hynix | Wuxi (Jiangsu) | DRAM, mostly 1a; EUV layers done in Korea | 30% to 40% of SK hynix’s DRAM | Producing | 
| SK hynix (Solidigm) | Dalian Fab 1 (Liaoning) | Floating-gate 3D NAND, 192-layer, moving to 240 | About 100,000 wafers a month; 30% to 40% of SK hynix’s NAND | Producing; upgrading, authorized up to 240 layers | 
| SK hynix (Solidigm) | Dalian Mod B (Liaoning) | 3D NAND, if equipped | Not stated | Built in 2023; SK hynix says no expansion is sought; no 2027 license yet | 
Currently, China’s homegrown memory hinges on two manufacturers that are, admittedly, booming at the moment, although the memory industry worldwide has seen a massive surge since spring 2025. SK hynix said that “our DRAM and HBM volume for the next three years through 2029 are effectively sold out” with supply failing to keep up with demand as “a constraint projected to continue through 2030.” Its average selling prices rose from Q2 by mid-20% for NAND and high-20% for DRAM.
There may be some signs of at least temporary cooling in China’s consumer channel, though, as China Flash Market reports that SSD prices fell across the board this week, with most spot NAND wafers trading more than 30% below suppliers’ official prices. It looks like supply will remain a hot topic and China’s production capabilities are front and center.
CXMT and Huawei both have HBM milestones due by year-end: CXMT’s limited HBM3E production and Shanghai packaging plant, and Huawei’s 950DT with HiZQ 2.0. YMTC’s Fab 3 is due in late 2026 or 2027, and CXMT’s HBM3E expansion is expected in 2027. That leaves little time to ramp within 2027, especially at CXMT’s current yields, so we’re skeptical of volume HBM from a Chinese fab, whether measured against domestic demand or global supply, before 2028. Samsung and SK hynix, meanwhile, still need U.S. licenses for next year to keep tooling their Chinese fabs.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Take-Two toma medidas legales contra usuarios que distribuyen versiones pirata de GTA 6 para PC
articles.text:
Take-Two Interactive, empresa matriz de Rockstar Games, inició acciones legales para frenar los intentos de distribuir versiones no autorizadas de GTA 6 para computadoras. La compañía presentó una reclamación por infracción de derechos de autor ante GitHub, que provocó la eliminación de más de 3.000 repositorios relacionados con un proyecto que buscaba adaptar el videojuego para que pudiera ejecutarse de forma nativa en PC.
La iniciativa, denominada Leonida, había despertado el interés de miles de usuarios porque pretendía permitir que Grand Theft Auto VI funcionara en computadoras antes de que Rockstar Games publique una versión oficial para esta plataforma. Sin embargo, Take-Two consideró que el proyecto utilizaba material protegido de su propiedad intelectual y facilitaba la distribución de archivos obtenidos de manera no autorizada.
Según informó el medio especializado IGN, la reclamación también alcanzó a los repositorios derivados del proyecto original. Antes de su eliminación, Leonida había acumulado más de 2.900 copias o forks, creados por otros desarrolladores que buscaban continuar con la adaptación.
Por qué Take-Two pidió eliminar los repositorios de GTA 6
El proyecto Leonida fue desarrollado inicialmente por un usuario identificado como ItsNotRexed. Su objetivo era recompilar el ejecutable de la versión de Xbox de GTA 6 para conseguir que el videojuego pudiera funcionar directamente en una computadora, sin depender de una consola.
Para desarrollar esta adaptación se utilizó como referencia una filtración de archivos del juego correspondiente a Xbox Series, que comenzó a circular públicamente el 20 de noviembre de 2026. Al día siguiente se puso en marcha el repositorio de Leonida en GitHub.
Take-Two sostuvo que la iniciativa infringía sus derechos de autor porque reproducía elementos protegidos de Grand Theft Auto VI y constituía una obra derivada del videojuego original.
En su reclamación, la compañía identificó a GTA 6 como una obra audiovisual de su propiedad que incluye imágenes, material artístico, diálogos y otros elementos creativos. También argumentó que el repositorio excedía los términos de las licencias concedidas por Rockstar Games.
La solicitud no se limitó al proyecto original. La empresa pidió retirar también los miles de repositorios derivados que permitían acceder a versiones modificadas o continuar con el desarrollo de la adaptación.
La explicación de Take-Two sobre los archivos filtrados
Uno de los argumentos utilizados por los responsables de Leonida era que los usuarios debían proporcionar sus propios archivos del videojuego para ejecutar la recompilación. Es decir, el repositorio no ofrecía directamente una copia completa de GTA 6, sino una herramienta que necesitaba los archivos originales de Xbox.
Sin embargo, Take-Two cuestionó esa explicación y sostuvo que se trataba de una forma de intentar presentar el proyecto como una herramienta de uso general.
La compañía señaló que el momento en que apareció Leonida y su relación directa con la filtración demostraban que los desarrolladores conocían el origen de los archivos que necesitarían los usuarios. Según su reclamación, estos datos correspondían a material de GTA 6 que había sido obtenido y distribuido sin autorización.
La empresa considera que exigir a los usuarios que aporten sus propios archivos no elimina la responsabilidad por facilitar el uso de contenido protegido por derechos de autor.
Tras la intervención de Take-Two, el repositorio original y sus proyectos derivados dejaron de estar disponibles en GitHub. La medida representa un nuevo intento de Rockstar Games por controlar la distribución de material relacionado con su próximo lanzamiento.
Cuándo llegará GTA 6 a PC
Por ahora, quienes quieran jugar GTA 6 de manera oficial en una computadora tendrán que esperar a que Rockstar Games anuncie una versión para Windows.
El videojuego se lanzó de manera oficial el 19 de noviembre de 2026 en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S. La compañía no ha confirmado una fecha para PC, aunque existen especulaciones sobre un posible estreno durante el primer trimestre de 2027.
La ausencia de una versión para computadoras ha impulsado el interés por métodos alternativos para ejecutar el título. Sin embargo, iniciativas como Leonida se enfrentan a las medidas legales de Take-Two cuando utilizan archivos filtrados o material protegido.
Por el momento, Rockstar Games no ha anunciado oficialmente cuándo estará disponible GTA 6 para PC. Mientras tanto, la compañía continúa protegiendo los archivos del videojuego y limitando los proyectos que buscan distribuir o adaptar versiones no autorizadas antes de su lanzamiento en esa plataforma.

articles.title: T-Force Delta RGB 32GB DDR5 memory drops to $440 for a limited time
articles.text:
Double discounts on TeamGroup's T-Force Delta memory saves you $110 on 32GB DDR5 with RGB lighting for your gaming PC project, now available for $440
$550 DDR5 RAM pack discounted to $440 for a limited time only
TeamGroup's T-Force Delta RGB DDR5 6000 is a high-speed RAM kit that's perfect for high-performance PC projects, comprising two 16GB modules (totalling 32GB).
This DDR5 RAM kit is part of the Black Friday sale, where it's down to $440 (was $550) at Newegg with code BFF465.
120-degree RGB illumination adds some flair, but it's all about the T-Force Delta's integrated heat spreader and 1.35V efficiency for optimal performance. It also supports Intel XMP3.0 and AMD EXPO, allowing you to get the most out of your Intel Core or AMD Ryzen PC's gaming features.
For more RAM deals, we found 6 DDR5 kits all under $500 for Black Friday.
32GB Team T-Force Delta DDR5 RAM set (2x 16GB modules) with RGB lighting and Intel XMP3.0/AMD EXPO support for overclocking, all with a 20% saving of $110 versus full price.
Why we recommend it
32GB spread across two DDR5 16GB modules maximizes bandwidth across plentiful memory, but it's all about the Intel XMP3.0/AMD EXPO support for easy overclocking. The 120-degree RGB lighting is also very befitting of a custom PC buildout.
Price Context & Historical Value
Memory prices have surged in recent years, and while the T-Force Delta costs more than it did when Newegg first advertised it in September 2024, the seasonal $40 saving plus an extra $70 promo code offset a lot of that expense.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Team T-Force Delta RGB 32GB if...
32GB is enough for your gaming needs and you like the idea of customizable lighting
❌ Skip the Team T-Force Delta RGB 32GB if...
you're just looking to build a computer for everyday use, you have an older DDR4-compatible motherboard or you're looking to build a gaming PC on the tightest budget
