articles.title: É difícil imaginar que humanidade manterá o controle, diz Meta sobre IA
articles.text:
É difícil imaginar que humanidade manterá o controle, diz Meta sobre IA
Em post, diretor de inteligência artificial da big tech destaca a chegada iminente da chamada superinteligência.
Uma inteligência artificial mil vezes mais capaz que nós humanos dificilmente ficará sob nosso controle. É o que afirma Alexandr Wang, diretor de inteligência da Meta, em uma publicação no X. O executivo destacou a chegada iminente da chamada superinteligência, próxima fase da IA que tem gerado muitas preocupações entre desenvolvedores e líderes do setor.
Segundo Wang, além da inteligência muito maior, essa nova etapa também traria o chamado aprimoramento recursivo, ou seja, a possibilidade de realizar melhorias por conta própria, sem supervisão humana.
No post, o diretor diz ainda não concordar com uma “entrega” da sociedade à IA, mas que acredita no desenvolvimento da tecnologia pensando em um “futuro positivo” para a humanidade. Além disso, ele aponta que as ações relacionadas às IAs no próximo ano teriam “grande consequência no mundo em que vamos viver”.
Em sua publicação no X, Wang fala sobre a resolução da Hipótese de Riemann, um dos problemas matemáticos mais famosos do mundo. Em 20 de novembro, um matemático da Anthropic, Levent Alpöge, anunciou que havia resolvido a questão de 160 anos atrás utilizando o Claude, IA da companhia.
Segundo Wang, a descoberta da bomba atômica seria um mero “dever de casa” perto da resolução da hipótese de Riemann.
Ele afirma ainda que os questionamentos feitos por profissionais ao uso da inteligência artifcial no processo apontam para uma resistência da sociedade às futuras automações envolvendo desenvolvimento científico e tecnológico – algo que ele classifica como inevitável.
Após defender a ideia de que a chegada da superinteligência é iminente, o executivo da Meta falou que há um “pensamento preguiçoso” na indústria de IA.
Wang diz que o desenvolvimento com segurança não é suficiente para evitar problemas no futuro, sendo necessário também investir na construção de uma tecnologia que “entregue um futuro positivos para a humanidade”. Mas, para isso, seria necessário mudar a lógica de desenvolvimento atual.
Recentemente, outro líder de IA falou sobre a necessidade de “aceitar algumas coisas ruins” no desenvolvimento da IA, além da importância de “não se entregar” à tecnologia, o que levaria à perda de controle da situação.
Outros nomes do setor também têm se posicionado de maneira mais alarmista, como o próprio Dario Amodei, da Anthropic, que defendeu a diminuição no ritmo de desenvolvimento da tecnologia dias após um ex-funcionário falar publicamente sobre os riscos da superinteligência para a humanidade.

articles.title: Etsy clarifies AI terms after seller backlash
articles.text:
After backlash from sellers frustrated by Etsy’s new AI policies, which appeared to allow the company to train AI on user artwork, Etsy has now clarified its stance.
In a note published on Monday, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal discussed recent tweaks to the company’s terms of service and admitted that her team “should’ve given you more context on what the updates meant for your creative content.”
“Our recent terms update was meant to reflect the evolving technologies we’re using to build better tools and experiences for sellers and the Etsy community,” Goyal wrote this week. “It was not meant to enable us to train AI models for the purpose of creating copycats of your items. We do not and will not do that.”
Aaron Meshon, a longtime professional illustrator and Etsy seller, told Ars that even though the company had dialed back its AI language somewhat, the changes were mere “sugar coating.”
He said he still plans on shutting down his 15-year-old Etsy store on December 1.
“I would say I’m losing 20 percent of my yearly income,” he said. “It’s a few mortgage payments.”
He noted that Etsy’s announcement also seems to be rather tone-deaf, given that many retailers make a substantial portion of their annual revenue in the run-up to the end-of-year holiday season.

articles.title: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia's code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
articles.text:
When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired. “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO.
It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. That’s the risk Huang now faces at Nvidia.
Matt Plass, chief market strategy officer at LRN, an ethics and compliance training outfit, recently surveyed more than 2,000 workers across different industries for a study on workplace codes of conduct. As Plass sees it, the biggest risk is that employees will become ashamed of their workplace.
“People coming into the workforce now, ethics is incredibly important to them,” he told TechCrunch. “They’re really mindful of the ethical standards of their company. They’re really embarrassed and angry when senior leadership lets them down.”
The consequences of violating the rules aren’t always tangible, but they’re definitely real. Plass gave one example of a company that banned corporate travel to cut costs — only to have its CEO turn up in a VIP box at the Olympics.
“For over a decade afterwards, ‘the Olympics’ was used within that company as an example of the worst thing an employee could do. People would say, ‘Yeah, I shouldn’t have done that, but it’s not like I went to the Olympics.’”
Plass says companies that remove an executive typically do so after an investigation, then try to win back employees. “In most organizations they make a change at the top based on what’s happened,” he said, “and then they will have a hearts-and-minds initiative, to go out to their employee base and their customers and their investors and everybody else, and say, we get it. We’re sorry. We’ve changed. That’s essentially what they do.”
Of course, that playbook is harder to follow at a company like Nvidia, where Huang left without a clear succession plan, and there are serious doubts about whether the company could continue to thrive without him. In cases like that, Plass acknowledges there’s no easy answer.
“I would draw a distinction there between the kind of companies where the CEO is a kind of godhead figure … where the person and the company are almost impossible to separate,” he said. “There it’s much, much harder to deal with.”
In that context, Huang’s stutter-step over the code of conduct is easier to understand. Judging by the employee campaign for his reinstatement, Huang’s return hasn’t created a morale problem so far. But as the coming months put more pressure on Huang and his colleagues, sidestepping the code could end up costing Nvidia something harder to measure — its employees’ pride in the company.

articles.title: Why you must read Jordan Himelfarb’s New Chess book
articles.text:
Why you must read Jordan Himelfarb’s New Chess book
Discover why Jordan Himelfarb's Interregnum is a compelling read about ambition, rivalry, young chess prodigies and the battle to become world champion.
Chess is often seen as a game of strategy, patience and intellectual ability. But behind every major tournament lies a world of ambition, intense preparation, personal sacrifices and the pressure to perform.
For elite players, becoming world champion is not simply about winning matches; it is about securing a place in the history of the game.
Jordan Himelfarb's Interregnum: Inside the Grueling & Glamorous Battle to Become the Next King of Chess explores this fascinating world through the stories of grandmasters competing for one of the most prestigious titles in sport.
The book follows a defining moment in modern chess: Magnus Carlsen's decision not to defend his world championship title for a fifth time. His announcement created an opportunity for other leading players to pursue a dream that had long seemed difficult to achieve.
Combining sports journalism, character studies and behind-the-scenes storytelling, Interregnum offers a closer look at the people competing at the highest level of chess.
Here is why this book deserves a place on your reading list.
Jordan Himelfarb’s new chess book: What makes it worth reading?
1. It takes you inside the battle for the world chess championship
For years, Magnus Carlsen's dominance made the race for the world championship particularly challenging for other elite players. His decision not to defend his title changed the competitive landscape and opened the door for a new champion.
Interregnum explores what happened next, following the grandmasters who saw an opportunity to achieve their lifelong ambitions. Rather than simply documenting tournament results, Himelfarb examines the competitive environment surrounding the championship race. Readers get a sense of what it means to pursue a title that can define an entire career.
For anyone curious about professional chess, this offers an engaging perspective on the competition beyond the board.
2. It explores the personalities behind the chess pieces
One of the most interesting aspects of Interregnum is its focus on the individuals behind the game. Elite chess players are often recognised for their ratings, tournament victories and playing styles.
However, they also have personal ambitions, insecurities, unconventional personalities and different approaches to handling pressure. Himelfarb explores the lives and mindsets of these grandmasters, showing how their backgrounds and experiences influence their journeys.
The book also examines the contrast between established players whose opportunities may be running out and younger prodigies determined to make their mark.
This makes the story about much more than chess. It becomes a study of ambition, competition and human psychology.
3. It introduces readers to the changing world of chess
Chess has experienced a remarkable resurgence in recent years, attracting new audiences through online platforms, streaming and digital communities. Interregnum explores this changing landscape, including the influence of younger, internet-savvy players who are reshaping how the game is experienced and discussed.
The book captures the contrast between chess's centuries-old traditions and the modern personalities bringing fresh energy to the sport.
For readers who have followed the growing popularity of online chess, this offers an opportunity to understand the people and developments behind that transformation.
It also highlights how an ancient intellectual pursuit continues to find new audiences in a digitally connected world.
4. You don't need to be a chess expert to enjoy it
One reason people hesitate to pick up books about chess is the assumption that they need to understand complicated strategies, openings and technical terminology.
However, Interregnum is not designed as a traditional chess instruction manual. According to the book's description, it combines elements of a sports chronicle, character study and celebration of the game.
Its storytelling focuses on the personalities, ambitions and rivalries that make the championship race compelling.
The book also uses technical details without overwhelming readers with chess terminology. As highlighted in reviews by The New Yorker and Deccan Herald, its accessibility makes it appealing even to those unfamiliar with the finer details of competitive chess.
You can therefore enjoy the human stories and competitive drama without being an experienced player.
5. It shows the psychological side of competition
Competing at the highest level requires more than intelligence or technical preparation. Players must also manage expectations, anxiety, setbacks and the pressure of performing when the stakes are high.
Interregnum explores these emotional dimensions through the experiences of grandmasters pursuing the world championship.
The contrast between experienced competitors and young prodigies also raises interesting questions about timing, opportunity and ambition. Some players are racing against time, while others are only beginning their journeys.
These experiences make the book relatable beyond professional chess. Anyone pursuing a demanding personal or professional goal can recognise the tension between ambition, uncertainty and the desire to succeed.
About the Author: Jordan Himelfarb
Jordan Himelfarb is a managing editor at the Toronto Star, one of North America's major newspapers. He oversees coverage across politics, national and international affairs, and opinion.
Before becoming managing editor, he served as the newspaper's politics editor and deputy editorial page editor. He has also received three National Newspaper Award nominations, recognising his work in journalism and editing.
Interestingly, Himelfarb was previously a competitive Scrabble player before turning his attention to chess and contract bridge.
His experience in journalism and his interest in intellectually demanding games come together in Interregnum, which approaches chess through reporting, observation and character-driven storytelling.
Final thoughts
Interregnum: Inside the Grueling & Glamorous Battle to Become the Next King of Chess offers a different way to experience the world of competitive chess. Instead of focusing exclusively on moves, strategies and tournament outcomes, Jordan Himelfarb explores the people, personalities and ambitions shaping the modern game.
Whether you follow international chess, enjoy sports journalism or simply appreciate stories about individuals pursuing extraordinary goals, this book offers an engaging reading experience.
Its biggest appeal lies in showing that behind every intellectual battle is a human story filled with ambition, uncertainty, rivalry and the desire to leave a lasting legacy.

AMD's Radeon RX 9060 8GB comes to retail for a cheap, modern GPU upgrade
Cheap and good graphics cards are rare these days, but if you're trying to save every last dollar on a modern upgrade, the Radeon RX 9060 8GB (note: non-XT) has seemingly broken free of its OEM-only status and is now available at Best Buy for $429, or $10 less than even the cheapest RTX 5060 right now.
The Radeon RX 9060 8GB (note: non-XT) goes neck and neck with the RTX 5060 for less than that card currently sells for. If you need a modern budget graphics card and need to save every dollar, this is a good choice.
Read moreRead less▼
Independent testing of the RDNA 4 RX 9060 8GB shows that it runs neck and neck with the RTX 5060 in many games as a baseline, and this card offers support for the high-quality FSR 4 upscaler if you need a performance boost. A single eight-pin power connector and a modest 132W TDP won't strain older builds, either. If Nvidia is a no-go for you, check out this card instead. -- Jeff Kampman
Grab 2TB of PCIe 5.0 storage for less than $300 with the Crucial P510
PCIe 5.0 drives were already pricey, and just as prices were starting to come down, flash demand went through the roof. Still, you can score a decent deal on the Crucial P510 right now, with the drive marked down to just $294.99 at Best Buy in a 2TB capacity. In this market, that’s an excellent price. We’ve even seen several PCIe 4.0 2TB drives more expensive than the Crucial P510 is right now.
The Micron Crucial P510 is a PCIe 5.0 drive with 10,000 MB/s and 8,700 MB/s rated sequential read/write performance.
Read moreRead less▼
This is (or, I suppose, was) Crucial’s midrange PCIe 5.0 offering, sandwiched between the budget P310 and premium T710. It boasts 11,000 MB/s and 9,500 MB/s sequential read/write performance, 1,500K IOPS random read/write performance, and a 1,200 TBW endurance rating for the 2TB capacity, along with a five-year warranty.
As you can read in our Crucial P510 review, the drive offers excellent performance considering the price, especially during sustained writes where weak cache can ruin performance. — Jake Roach
Score this TP-Link tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router for just $89 — fast wireless speeds flanked by 10 GbE LAN ports
If you’re in the market for a tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router but don’t want to spend more than $100, we’ve got you covered. The TP-Link Archer BE9500 is currently available for an incredibly low $89.99 at Best Buy.
The TP-Link Archer BE9500 is a budget-friendly tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router delivering speeds up to 9.5 Gbps. It features an ultra-fast 10 Gbps WAN/LAN port, two 2.5 Gbps LAN ports, two 1 GbE LAN ports, and 320 MHz channel support on the 6 GHz band. It covers up to 2,600 sq. ft.
Read moreRead less▼
For that price, you get a tri-band router, offering 1,032 Mbps speeds on the 2.4 GHz band, up to 2,722 Mbps on the 5 GHz band, and up to 5,776 Mbps on the 6 GHz band. There are also two 2.5 GbE LAN ports, two 1 GbE LAN ports, and even a 10 GbE WAN/LAN port for connecting to a high-speed fiber internet gateway.
Other features worth mentioning on the Archer BE9500 include a USB 3.0 port for hooking up a printer or storage device, six poseable antennas, and easy configuration using the TP-Link WebGUI on a desktop or the Tether app on your smartphone. — Brandon Hill
Nab an RTX 5090 prebuilt gaming PC for the lowest price we've seen this Black Friday week
Corsair's prebuilts offer proven, high-quality components, and they're also some of the cheapest 5090 PCs we've seen during this Black Friday rush. The latest example is the Vengeance i7600 Air. This system pairs the RTX 5090 with Intel's most powerful Arrow Lake processor and 64GB of RAM for the most demanding work or play.
Get RTX 5090 and Core Ultra 9 285K power in Corsair's Vengeance i7600 Air prebuilt PC. With 64GB of RAM and 2TB of storage, this system is ready for any gaming or productivity workload you can throw at it.
Read moreRead less▼
The RTX 5090 needs no introduction as the world's most powerful gaming graphics card. It's ready to chew through ray-traced and path-traced games even with 4K monitors, and its support for DLSS 4.5 upscaling and Multi Frame Generation lets you further tune your gaming experience to taste.

With all those points in its favor, the fact that this is the cheapest RTX 5090 prebuilt gaming PC we've yet seen this Black Friday season is just whipped cream on top of the pie. Get it while the getting is good. -- Jeff Kampman
Jaw-dropping deal on RTX 5060 desktop brings the price down to just $750
Finding a good deal on a budget gaming PC is an exercise in futility amid ongoing pricing crises in RAM, storage, and graphics cards. Walmart is offering a rare glimpse of hope with an excellent deal on the ABS Cyclone M Aqua, which comes equipped with an RTX 5060, Core i5-14400F, 16GB of DDR4, and a 1TB SSD for just $750.
The ABS Cyclone M Aqua is an mATX prebuilt with an RTX 5060, Core i5-14400F, 16GB of DDR4, and a 1TB NVMe SSD.
Read moreRead less▼
With over $650 knocked off list price, this deal likely won't last long. The major downside with this machine is that it includes a single 16GB DDR4 DIMM. That cuts the speed in half, so you'll want to add another DIMM right away. Everything else here is top-notch for the price, however. Even an RTX 5060 alone is pushing up toward $500 at this point. — Jake Roach
That PlayStation 5 Pro deal didn't last too long! Lots of people looking to get lost in Leonida. It may be worth continuing to check in.
We'll keep updating you on the best deals that we find!
Get a PS5 Pro direct from Sony for $849
Look, you, like everyone else, want to play Grand Theft Auto VI. But it's not out on PC yet, so the best way to play it is on a PlayStation 5 Pro, which is often sold out and on the secondhand market for insane prices.
For Black Friday, Sony is selling a refurbished PS5 Pro for $849, which is $50 off the typical price of a new one. It comes with a controller, though instead of the standard all-white look, you'll get gray camouflage.
The PlayStation 5 Pro is the most powerful version of Sony's console. It has 2TB of storage, and this one comes with a camo controller. Best of all, it plays GTA VI.
Read moreRead less▼
We don't often recommend refurbished tech, but this PS5 Pro is coming straight from Sony, making it relatively low-risk. It still comes with a one-year warranty. 
Did I mention it can play GTA VI? — Andrew E. Freedman
Streamline your setup with a KVM switch and have easy access to multiple devices via a single screen
You may already have a KVM switch built into your monitor, as that has become a popular feature for some brands, or maybe you have three-plus monitors on your desk hooked up to your PC, laptop, or a game console. Well, this KVM deal on Amazon may help you to save some space and streamline your setup thanks to Ugreen’s 4-port KVM switch priced at only $63.99 in the Black Friday sales.
A handy KVM switch for hooking up four computers to one screen. Supports EDID emulation. All cables included except for the HDMI cables.
Read moreRead less▼
This KVM switch can hook up four computers to a single monitor and let you control all the computers with a single mouse and keyboard input. The switch can handle resolutions of up to 4K (UHD) at 60 Hz, with easy switching between inputs via the four buttons on the top of the KVM unit, or via the included desktop controller, which has the same four buttons, meaning you can hide away the KVM and cables and just have the controller on the desk, saving even more space.
There are many more configurations of devices available to set up via the KVM, and all you need is an HDMI cable and an optional USB Type-A to Type-C cable to connect to the KVM if you want to be able to control the device via the KVM switch. A KVM is a great solution if you only have room on your desk for one monitor, but want access to multiple computer devices. — Stewart Bendle
Kingston’s 2TB NV3 SSD is now $30 off when using a promo code - increases your storage capacity for just $265
Kingston’s 2TB NV3 SSD is $30 off with promo code BFF588, bringing the total down to a bearable-for-the-times $265. The PCIe 4.0 x4 drive boasts speeds of up to 6,000/5,000 (r/w) and includes Acronis cloning software for backups.
A middling Gen 4 SSD with read and write speeds of up to 6000/5000 MB/s. This M.2 NVMe drive comes in the 2280 form factor and holds enough capacity to store several AAA games, and is also great as an OS drive.
Read moreRead less▼
The NV3 has a 640TBW and 2M-hour MTBF, so you’ll likely need an upgrade before writes take down the drive. Kingston also backs this drive with a 5-year warranty. The NV3 is great for extra storage, or you can use it as your primary OS drive. I bought the 1TB model shortly after release as an extra drive for games, and I recommend it at the current price, even if it isn’t the cheapest we’ve seen. - Joe Shields
A surprise deal on an RTX Spark laptop just a month after launch — save $200 on the 24GB and 32GB Asus ProArt P14
Nvidia's RTX Spark chip launched just last month, and at least one device is already on sale: Asus' ProArt P14. Two configurations are marked down by a flat $200, including the 32GB model with the full 6,144-core GPU and 20-core CPU, and the 24GB model with a 5,120-core GPU and 18-core CPU.
The Asus ProArt P14 with RTX Spark is a 14-inch laptop with 512GB of storage. This model includes 24GB of unified memory, a 5,120-core Blackwell GPU, and an 18-core Grace CPU.
Read moreRead less▼
You'll struggle to run the AI models larger RTX Spark laptops — particularly those with 128GB of memory — are capable of running. However, this is still a premium 14-inch laptop with a competitive CPU and RTX 5060-class GPU.
Asus uses a 14-inch OLED touchscreen with a 3K resolution and 120Hz refresh rate. The chassis is constructed out of aluminum, and it weighs in just over 3.6 pounds. — Jake Roach
Logitech’s compact MX Creative Console peripheral streamlines your Adobe software usage
Seeing a decent price cut of $48 during the Black Friday sales at Amazon, the MX Creative Console from Logitech is now only $151.99. This is a much better price than its usual $199.99 listing. Similar in looks to a Steam Deck, this control console is designed to enhance your workflow when using Adobe products.
With 9 customizable LCD keys and a wireless fine-control dialpad, the MX Creative Console is designed to smooth out your graphic design workflow.
Read moreRead less▼
The MX Creative Console consists of two parts: a wired LCD display keypad with nine keys and two arrow keys for navigating between pages, plus a wireless rotary dialpad that has a central knob, a scroll wheel, and four more configurable buttons. Logitech has worked closely with Adobe to streamline software usage so that the MX Creative Console works straight out of the box with their most popular apps, such as Photoshop and Premiere Pro.
It may bear a passing resemblance to other LCD-key touchpads, but that’s where the similarities end. The MX Creative Console is designed to work with and enhance your software usage, with the aid of fine control via the dialpad. Although I’m sure you can configure this to work with a streaming setup, that’s not its intended focus. — Stewart Bendle
Brighten up your life with Olight’s tiny, magnetic, USB-charging flashlight for only $12 – great for PC building and almost anything else
Olight’s IMINI 2 mini flashlight is on sale again. It’s well-designed and costs around $20 new, but it’s on sale for under $12 during Black Friday week. It has a simple design and an integrated USB plug for charging. Simply pull the USB-A port back to turn it on. The magnet on the back is great for mounting where you need a little extra light. I bought one during Prime Day this year and use it quite often when working inside PC cases or anywhere in my office where my old eyes need additional light (50 lumens). If red isn’t your color, several other options are available at the same price.
At just 2.17 inches long, this flashlight is rated to 50 lumens, and it sports a magnetic back with a USB-A plug for charging. Pulling the back off turns on the flashlight, and the magnetic back makes it easy to mount the light on anything with ferrous metal.
Read moreRead less▼
The Olight IMINI 2 is tiny, only 55mm long, and small enough to easily fit on your keychain as intended or even in your pocket. The Imini 2 EDC includes two silicone covers for the USB port along with a carabiner clip. Note that the flashlight portion is held to the charging port via a magnet and feels like it could fall off and get lost, but so far it has not. For under $12, this portable flashlight is a steal. - Joe Shields
Grab these TP-Link and Netgear Wi-Fi 6 routers for as low as $39
After around three years on the market, Wi-Fi 7 routers have become mainstream. You can get a tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router for around $90, while a good dual-band Wi-Fi 7 router is around $75. But what if you don’t need the extra speed and capacity that Wi-Fi 7 offers, and you just want something cheap to give you decent coverage throughout your house? Well, that’s where something like the TP-Link Archer AX1450 comes into focus. Walmart is currently selling the router for $39, or 20% off its regular asking price.
The Archer AX1450 is by no means a speed demon, as it delivers up to 250 Mbps over the 2.4 GHz band and up to 1,201 Mbps on the 5 GHz band. That should be more than sufficient if you’re rocking a 1 Gbps or lower broadband connection. You get one GbE WAN port and four GbE LAN ports for connecting your wired devices. You can manage the Archer AX1450 with the usual webGUI on a desktop/laptop or use the TP-Link Tether app to control the router from your smartphone or tablet.
The TP-Link Archer AX1450 is a Wi-Fi 6 router with four GbE LAN ports and up to 1.45 Gbps aggregate wireless speeds across 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.
Read moreRead less▼
The Netgear RAX5 is a Wi-Fi 6 router with four GbE LAN ports and up to 1.6 Gbps aggregate wireless speeds across 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.
Read moreRead less▼
There’s also the Netgear RAX5, which is another Wi-Fi 6 router delivering up to 1.6 Gbps aggregate speeds. The router covers up to 1,500 square feet, and includes a GbE WAN and four GbE LAN ports. Walmart has the RAX5 on sale for $44.33, which is over $35 off its usual selling price.
They may not look pretty, and won’t win any throughput contests against their newer Wi-Fi 6E or Wi-Fi 7 competition, but those newer routers can’t touch the sub-$44 price tag. — Brandon Hill
Save $450 on a 1080p gaming rig from MSI, now on sale for less than $1,100
Best Buy has slashed an extra $160 off this MSI Codex R2 gaming PC, meaning you can save $450 right now compared to its list price. This budget-friendly gaming rig is a sure performer for 1080p gameplay, thanks to the RTX 5060, and you can pick it up for $1,099.99 right now.
A 1080p gaming PC with an RTX 5060, 16GB DDR5, 1TB SSD, and an Intel Core i5-14400F CPU.
Read moreRead less▼
The Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 is entry level but it's current gen, and it'll offer much superior performance compared to relying on your CPU's integrated GPU. It comes equipped with 3,840 CUDA cores, along with 8GB of GDDR7 VRAM. In practice, with those DLSS features enabled, this will let you run games with high graphics presets at 1080p without much bother.
Meanwhile, the Intel Core i5-14400F processor included here isn't a bad option for 1080p gaming and continues to be well-sold in many pre-built rigs. It has 10 cores, six of which are performance cores that deliver the best gaming performance. 16GB of DDR5 RAM and a 1TB SSD ensure no compromises elsewhere, too.
This is a good, solid gaming PC for a budget-conscious gamer, especially with that $450 discount on offer here. — Ben Stockton
Apple's current-gen M5 MacBook Airs are up to $300 off
If you’re in the market for a new MacBook Air, Amazon has some early Black Friday deals that are sure to put some pep in your step. You can get a 16GB/512GB M5 MacBook Air for just $1,049, representing a $250 discount over its MSRP. There’s also the same $250 discount on the 25GB/1TB SKU, bringing its price to $1,549.
But perhaps the real sweet spot in the model range is the 16GB/1TB SKU, which is discounted by $300, taking its price to a low $1,299.
This 13.6-Inch MacBook Air is complete with Apple's Liquid Retina display, 16GB of unified memory, a 512GB SSD, 12MP center stage camera, touch ID, and Wi-Fi 7 connectivity.
Read moreRead less▼
This model is the same shape and design as the one above, but you get a boost in storage. This MacBook Air comes with a 1TB SSD instead.
Read moreRead less▼
The best spec'd model on sale at Amazon right now for the MacBook Air 13 2026. This model has a 1TB SSD and 24GB of unified memory.
Read moreRead less▼
All of the MacBook Airs feature a 13.6-inch Liquid Retina display, the M5 chip from Apple using a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU, an N1 wireless chip for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity, a 12MP Center Stage camera for video calls, and Touch ID for biometric security. — Brandon Hill
A fast 4TB Samsung SSD with a 36% saving — 990 Pro 4TB back down to $699.99 right now
In a market struggling with the AI boom, the best time to buy storage was yesterday, the next best time is today. That's where a sale on this 4TB Samsung 990 Pro SSD might attract your interest, available now for $699.99.
A fast Gen 4 SSD with read and write speeds of up to 7450/6900 MB/s, almost maxing out the Gen 4 bandwidth. This M.2 NVMe drive comes in the 2280 form factor and holds enough capacity to store a large selection of your favorite games or files.
Read moreRead less▼
We found the 990 Pro to be among the best 4TB drives on the market when it was released, as our Samsung 990 Pro 4TB review will explain, and one of the best SSDs you can buy overall. This is a Gen 4 drive offering maximum sequential read and write speeds of 7,450 and 6,900 MB/s apiece, with random read and writes at 1.6 million and 1.55 million IOPS, respectively, with an endurance rating of 2,400 TBW (or terabytes written). Our testing at the time found it rivaled the competition, sitting at the top or near the top for almost all of the tests, with the lowest latency scores (a big plus for those fast load times in-game).
4TB of storage, meanwhile, means you'll have a huge capacity boost that'll give you enormous room for a big collection of games, videos and photos alongside a typical Windows installation. The $699 sale price might not be record breaking, but it's a drop from the $800-900 range it sat at just a few month's ago. — Ben Stockton.
Get a great deal on the 1TB Kingston M.2 SSD with 35% off – this PCIe 4.0 SSD is down to $139.99
Snag Kingston’s NV3 1TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD for cheap during Black Friday week. The drive offers sequential read speeds of up to 6,000 MB/s and write speeds up to 4,000 MB/s, and 895K/795K random read/write IOPS. While this drive isn't a barnstorming PCIe 5.0 model, you'll never notice during daily use, and more importantly, gaming. That makes this a solid budget upgrade for nearly any rig.
The Kingston NV3 is a PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD that sports sequential read speeds of up to 6,000 MB/s and sequential write speeds of up to 4,000 MB/s.
Read moreRead less▼
As you can see above, the NV3 is a midrange-class drive and, performance-wise, sits alongside more expensive drives. It offers a whopping 2 million hours MTBF and a solid 5-year warranty with free technical support. This drive will work well as an OS drive or simply for storing your games or other applications. - Joe Shields
Creative's compact 30W Pebble Pro speakers hit their lowest price this year
The Creative Pebble Pros are among the best PC speakers you can buy, especially on a budget, and right now, they're on sale for $59.49. That's the lowest price we've seen them this year.
These speakers are designed to be compact, with an angled design, running solely off a USB-C connection. Their price does yo-yo a bit, but this sale price means you can score it for a really good price: ideal if you're looking for a simple, good looking speaker setup with good audio quality.
These Creative USB-C speakers performed well in our testing and can hit 30W RMS/60W peak, though you'll have to bring your own 30W PD power adapter to get the loudest sound output.
Read moreRead less▼
Our Creative Pebble Pro review found these to be a decent step up in both sound and bass over the lsat-gen V3s. The duo are permanently connected, with a six-foot cable between them, which gives enough space to spread them apart. The drivers are angled towards your ears, so no need to think about stands. Connectivity, as we've mentioned, includes USB-C for data, USB-C PD for power, and a 3.5mm audio jack. You've also got a pair of 3.5mm jacks on the right speaker for a headset and mic. You'll need a 30W USB power adapter to max out the sound quality with this one, with a standard USB connection limiting you to 10W.
These are a good quality, budget friendly audio solution for your desk, so grab 'em while they're cheap. —Ben Stockton
Budget-friendly 32GB DDR5-6000 RAM kit, built for gamers
With RAM prices still high, you'll want to find a deal that can knock a few pennies off, like this Team Group set at Newegg. For $439.99 (thanks to a $70 off promo code), you can score two 16GB modules of T-Force Delta RGB RAM at Newegg, making this (almost) the cheapest kit on sale anywhere right now if you're looking for 32GB DDR5-6000 memory if the Patriot RAM below doesn't tempt you.
Get a great deal on standalone RAM from Newegg. The T-Force Delta RGB not only adds flair to your chassis, but does so with decent speeds of 6,000 MT/s.
Read moreRead less▼
This memory kit is built with gamers in mind, thanks to that frosted RGB strip at the top that'll light up your case. It has a smart RGB IC controller, meaning you can control it with most lighting software like Asus Aura or MSI Mystic Light Sync, to customize it. It also has a black heat spreader with white branding.
As far as specs go, this kit is rated for 6,000 MT/s with CAS and latency timings of 38-46-46-84 using 1.35V. It's not the fastest kit around, but you'll struggle to notice a difference unless you're running benchmarks. More importantly, though, is the price: cheap kits are selling out fast, and this is one of the cheapest. — Ben Stockton.
Nearly 50% off a powerful portable laptop charger — UGREEN Nexode 145W delivers 25,000 mAh to your devices
If you travel and have multiple devices that need charging frequently, this UGREEN Nexode Power Bank is an ideal pickup, thanks to a Black Friday discount of nearly 50%. Right now you can get $50 off the usual price of $109.99, now just $59.98.
Get a 145W power bank with 25,000 mAh and a 240W USB-C cable that can charge up to three devices simultaneously.
Read moreRead less▼
For reference, 25,000 mAh is enough to charge a smartphone more than five times, or a laptop once. UGREEN says this can charge a 16-inch MacBook Pro from 0% to 56% in just 30 minutes. UGREEN also says this is airline-approved, although if you're a frequent flyer, you should always check with your travel provider, as regulations often differ between airlines. - Stephen Warwick
Get $1,200 off an entire RTX 5090 gaming PC with a 9950X3D — liquid-cooled iBuyPower rig ships with 32GB DDR5 and a huge 4TB SSD
The only financially feasible way to get your hands on an RTX 5090 these days is to buy a prebuilt PC, and this iBuyPower number is now $1,200 off, making it one of the better 5090 prebuilts we've seen so far.
A powerhouse gaming PC with some of the best specs available. This rig has the 9950X3D fitted with the RTX 5090 to complement it, as well as 32GB DDR5 RAM and a 4TB SSD.
Grab $200 off with promo code BFMONTH at checkout.
Read moreRead less▼
The RTX 5090 needs no introduction as the fastest gaming GPU on the market, with a whopping 32GB of VRAM and 21,760 CUDA cores. This GPU is complemented by the huge AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D, a 16-core CPU with very high clock speeds and a massive 3D V-cache, which drives high gaming performance.
This is as good as it gets for a gaming PC in 2026, a true buy-it-once-and-forget-about-it option. - Stephen Warwick
Save $108 on this Asus ROG Azoth keyboard — 75% mechanical model features RGB, hot-swappable switches
This premium Asus keyboard normally sets you back $269.99, but right now you can grab this very solid keyboard at Best Buy for just $161.99, $108 off.
This 75-percent wireless keyboard features a hot-swappable PCB, up to 1,600 hours of battery life, and has a customizable OLED screen in the upper right corner.
Read moreRead less▼
This all-white keyboard has a distinctive look and features an aluminum top plate, hot-swappable PCB, and a customizable OLED display in the corner. There's also a matching wrist rest.

articles.title: Ryanair, easyJet, British Airways : 140 avions ont perdu le GPS en plein vol au-dessus de la mer du Nord
articles.text:
L’incident a duré une vingtaine de minutes, mais il a touché un nombre inhabituel d’appareils. Le 9 novembre, quelque 140 vols ont perdu leur signal GPS au-dessus du nord de l’Europe et de la mer du Nord, selon une analyse du spécialiste du renseignement aéronautique Hexbird, révélée par le quotidien britannique The i Paper. Parmi eux figuraient des avions partis d’Édimbourg, de Manchester et de Londres Heathrow, dont un Ryanair à destination de Rome, un easyJet vers Hurghada, en Égypte, et un British Airways vers Stockholm. Une quarantaine d’appareils se trouvaient dans l’espace aérien britannique ou à proximité, et sept vols ayant signalé la perte du GPS ont été guidés vers l’aéroport d’Amsterdam-Schiphol, selon le contrôle aérien néerlandais.
Une analyse de la plateforme Hexbird a fait remonter la source probable du brouillage à un unique émetteur radio situé en mer du Nord, à environ 300 kilomètres des côtes anglaises. Au même moment, trois cargos russes dont les propriétaires sont visés par des sanctions britanniques, américaines et européennes, le Lady R, le Lady D et le Maia-1, traversaient la zone sous l’escorte d’un navire de guerre russe, eux-mêmes suivis par un bâtiment français et un navire néerlandais.
Un navire militaire « presque certainement » à l’origine
Hexbird reste prudent et précise que son analyse « n’identifie pas le convoi comme la source, mais ne l’exclut pas non plus ». Ancien officier du renseignement naval, James Droxford est plus affirmatif. Selon lui, le navire de guerre russe est « presque certainement à l’origine du brouillage GPS, et non les navires marchands », peut-être pour décourager la surveillance de l’Otan.
Directeur général du Royal Institute of Navigation, Ramsey Faragher estime lui aussi que la puissance du brouillage, sur une zone très étendue, désigne plutôt une plateforme militaire dédiée. Si la piste russe se confirmait, ce serait « une intensification des perturbations que nous avons observées jusqu’à présent », juge Thomas Withington, spécialiste de la guerre électronique. « C’est la première fois, à ma connaissance, que l’on observe quelque chose d’aussi loin à l’ouest », ajoute-t-il.
Tous les acteurs ne partagent pas le même constat. Le contrôleur aérien britannique Nats assure n’avoir reçu aucun signalement de pilote faisant état d’un brouillage GPS ce jour-là, tandis que le gouvernement britannique refuse de commenter. La compagnie KLM a en revanche signalé l’incident aux autorités, qualifiant le brouillage et le leurrage de « phénomène international croissant ».
Pourquoi les avions n’ont pas été en danger
Le brouillage consiste à émettre de puissants signaux radio pour noyer ceux des satellites, très faibles une fois arrivés sur Terre. Le récepteur GPS ne parvient alors plus à calculer sa position ni l’heure exacte. Il ne faut pas le confondre avec le leurrage, ou spoofing, qui envoie de fausses positions au récepteur. Les avions de ligne ne dépendent toutefois pas du seul GPS et disposent de systèmes de navigation de secours tandis que les pilotes sont formés à voler sans signal satellite. Selon The i Paper, l’incident n’a d’ailleurs eu aucun impact opérationnel.
Les experts redoutent surtout un enchaînement de pannes. Un brouillage de cette ampleur coïncidant avec une défaillance du contrôle aérien serait un « scénario apocalyptique », estime Eric Schouten, ancien officier du renseignement néerlandais et dirigeant de la société de sûreté aérienne Dyami. Le risque dépasse aussi l’aviation, car de nombreux services s’appuient sur l’heure fournie par les satellites. « Le Royaume-Uni a eu de la chance que cela se produise aussi loin des côtes, car nous n’aurions pas voulu qu’un tel niveau de brouillage GPS inonde des choses comme nos réseaux de téléphonie mobile et nos stations de radio numérique DAB », souligne Ramsey Faragher.
Ces perturbations ont toutefois tendance à se multiplier depuis plusieurs années près des frontières russes, notamment autour de l’enclave de Kaliningrad. Elles ont d’ailleurs déjà affecté des personnalités, comme la présidente de la Commission européenne Ursula von der Leyen. En 2025, son avion avait été perturbé par un brouillage attribué à la Russie lors d’un déplacement en Bulgarie. Moscou présente de son côté ses brouilleurs comme une protection contre les attaques de drones ukrainiens. L’incident du 9 novembre se distingue par sa position, bien plus à l’ouest qu’à l’accoutumée.

articles.title: Affaire des réfrigérateurs piratés : et si le vrai coupable était l’obsolescence programmée ?
articles.text:
Affaire des réfrigérateurs piratés : et si le vrai coupable était l’obsolescence programmée ?
Menace sur la sécurité alimentaire, tensions géopolitiques et problématique de souveraineté numérique, l’affaire des frigos piratés a parfaitement illustré les problèmes graves que peut engendrer l’obsolescence programmée.
Il y a quelques semaines, la France apprenait à ses dépens l’importance de garder ses appareils numériques à jour. Dans l’affaire du piratage de frigo qui a touché plusieurs enseignes de la grande distribution et même l’Établissement français du sang, l’importance d’une vraie politique de suivi logiciel s’est faite criante.
En effet, parmi les systèmes attaqués, on retrouvait des contrôleurs Danfoss qui n’étaient plus mis à jour en raison de leur ancienneté. "La majorité des unités touchées sont des produits anciens (…) qui ont atteint leur fin de vie et ne bénéficient plus de mises à jour logicielles ou de sécurité", expliquait le fabricant danois interrogé sur la question. En octobre 2025, suite à une attaque similaire en Israël, l’entreprise conseillait d’abandonner les vieillissants contrôleurs frigorifiques AK-SM 800 (lancés au début des années 2010 et plus mis à jour depuis 2021) pour des nouveaux modèles.
"Tant que ce n’est pas encadré par la loi, cette vulnérabilité peut nous toucher à tout moment. Et on parle d’enjeu de souveraineté, de sécurité alimentaire qui peuvent avoir des répercussions très graves", analyse Lætitia Vasseur, présidente de l’association Halte à l’Obsolescence Programmée. Bien évidemment, les mises à jour ne peuvent pas tout et aucun système n’est infaillible, mais, quand il s’agit d’assurer la sécurité alimentaire à l’échelle d’un pays ou d’un continent, minimiser les risques peut faire la différence entre quelques centaines et quelques milliers de tonnes de nourriture gâchée.
Une solitude évitable
"Le problème n’a jamais été réglé : des milliers d’appareils restent dépendants d’un logiciel que leur fabricant ne met plus à jour, et que personne d’autre n’a le droit de réparer", déplore pour sa part iFixit. Si beaucoup de systèmes ont été coupés du web suite à la première attaque de mi-octobre, cela ne suffit pas. "Quand on parle d’un frigo qui a une espérance de vie de 12 ans, il est légitime de demander à ce que les mises à jour soient garanties pendant une durée très importante pour éviter tout ça", ajoute Laetitia Vasseur.
Or, la loi sur l’obsolescence programmée vise majoritairement les appareils grand public et oublie souvent le matériel professionnel souvent encadré par des relations contractuelles de qualité assez variable. "Il y a un vrai enjeu à ce que tous les sujets de durabilité et de réparabilité s’appliquent pour le grand public, mais aussi pour les professionnels où les impacts peuvent être encore plus colossaux", argue la présidente de HOP.
	
Il y a un vrai enjeu à ce que tous les sujets de durabilité et de réparabilité s’appliquent pour les professionnels où les impacts peuvent être encore plus colossaux
Dans le même esprit, la fin de la 2G/3G pourrait pousser au renouvellement de dispositifs critiques parce que le système qui les accompagne est devenu obsolète, nous explique-t-on. "Les fabricants savent très bien verrouiller nos appareils, ils savent beaucoup moins bien les protéger. Quand le fabricant garde la clé, puis s’en va, le propriétaire se retrouve seul face aux pirates", observe Sandra Auboy, responsable chez iFixit France.
Au-delà des problématiques de suivi et de garantie se pose donc la question de la durabilité du logiciel et du matériel une fois qu’il n’est plus rentable pour son constructeur d’en assurer le suivi. "Dès lors que le fabricant ne garantit plus rien, le code devrait être ouvert pour que chacun puisse s’approprier et faire perdurer ses équipements", explique-t-on chez HOP. Dans l’affaire des frigos, même un administrateur système de bonne volonté n’aurait rien pu faire face au verrouillage du système. Chez iFixit, on va plus loin en défendant le droit de s’approprier le matériel pour le réparer et le réutiliser à l’envi.
Des choix économiques
Et si la solution se trouvait finalement plus dans une désescalade technologique plutôt que dans un encadrement légal encore plus strict qui laisse le champ libre à une fuite en avant permanente ? Par définition, les frigos qui n’étaient pas connectés à Internet et dont la température était gérée par des employés présents sur place n’ont pas été exposés à ces problèmes. Poser cette question ouvre cependant des perspectives vertigineuses.
"Je ne dirais pas qu’il faut forcément toujours privilégier du low-tech, mais, avant de faire ce pas-là, il faut quand même avoir anticipé tous les impacts et tous les risques", argumente Laetitia Vasseur. "C’était probablement une solution séduisante pour gérer tout à distance avec une seule personne, mais c’est aussi une conception pécuniaire court-termiste que d’embaucher moins de monde pour gérer ces trucs-là. Et ça nous expose à ce genre de problème quand il n’y a plus de suivi".
Encore plus qu’une question d’obsolescence programmée, ce sont des choix économiques de réduction des coûts et de rationalisation des processus de gestion qui ont exposé les frigos à des cyberattaques évitables.

articles.title: Santiago, castañero riojano con 44 años de éxito y experiencia: "Antes 8 castañas costaban 100 pesetas, ahora la docena ronda los 4 euros"
articles.text:
A mediados de los 80, ocho castañas costaban 100 pesetas. Hoy la docena ronda los 4 euros y el oficio del castañero sigue creciendo. Aunque habría que definir ese “creciendo”. Santiago Palacios Cuesta, castañero autónomo y dueño de la SL Coto de Buriz, comenzó en el oficio vendiendo cucuruchos en Logroño, en 1982. Hoy la misma docena, ya decimos, supera los 4 en Cataluña, según ha contado. Y tiene las ofertas de empleo abiertas. Le disputa el puesto a otros castañeros como Mikel Álvarez Menor, de Pamplona, o Paco Pazos, en Pontevedra.
Su oficio parece la tarea de alguien de otro siglo. Y lo es: las castañeras ya eran un arquetipo popular en la Madrid de mediados del siglo XIX. No en vano, aunque la técnica ha cambiado respecto al brasero de toda la vida, asar bien una castaña exige darle muchas vueltas “tener el fuego adecuado y no despistarse”. Además, como dice su propio FAQ, no, las castañas no tienen gluten. Y la buena noticia es que el oficio no están desapareciendo, más bien al contrario.
De un puesto a 76. Santiago Palacios Cuesta tardó 16 años en dar el salto de uno a dos puestos, luego cuatro, ocho, dieciséis y treinta y dos. Hoy El Castañero suma 76 puntos de venta entre Blanes y Castro Urdiales, con paradas también en Tarragona, Cuenca y Zamora. Asa unas 100 toneladas por campaña. Las vende una a una en sus puestos y las suministra a otros castañeros y almacenistas. Lo único que hace la IA son algunos carteles.
En un reportaje de Nueve Cuatro Uno de 2024 ya contaba que parte de su producción viene de su propia parcela de 50 hectáreas. Pero es solo una parte: casi todo el fruto en cuestión llega de Extremadura, Galicia o Portugal a un almacén en Alesón, en La Rioja. Allí se clasifican por tamaño y densidad con una máquina de agua (las malas son las que flotan, porque suelen estar agujereadas por los insectos). Aunque su lema es "del árbol a tu boca", después pasan a una cámara frigorífica, porque la castaña es muy perecedera.
Los puestos, al alza. Ahora mismo, las cuatro capitales catalanas suman 169 puestos este otoño, el máximo desde antes de la pandemia, frente al centenar de 2021. Barcelona tiene al menos 64 autorizados (hay bastantes más, sin permisos); en 2013 eran apenas 29 puestos. Tarragona está batiendo su propio récord este otoño con 18. Deja el margen justo, aducen, pero es suficiente.
Porque detrás de muchos hay scouts, asociaciones vecinales y colegios que no cobran nada. Madrid ya iba por 68 puestos en 2024, según el Ayuntamiento, aunque muchos abren solo por tradición, sabiendo que no reportan pingües beneficios.
La cuenta de la vieja. 100 pesetas son 0,60 euros: unos 7,5 céntimos por castaña. Hoy salen a entre 29 y 33 céntimos, cuatro veces más caras. Pero nadie podría quejarse: los precios se multiplicaron por casi cinco desde 1982. Las ocho castañas de entonces hoy equivaldrían a unos 2,95 euros, o 4,4 euros la docena, así que, en términos reales, el cucurucho sale algo más barato que hace 44 años. Lo que sí cambió es el comprador: cada persona se lleva menos castañas.
El soto, tocado. Lo que está claro es que el problema está en el monte, no en las calles. Por volumen de producción, Galicia manda en la castaña: más de 49.000 hectáreas de castaño y unos 20 millones de kilos al año en condiciones normales. En 2025, la sequía y los incendios dejaron la cosecha gallega por debajo de los 10 millones. Aquel año los grandes incendios quemaron 105.303 hectáreas en Ourense, con sotos de Valdeorras entre los afectados. A escala nacional, la campaña 2025/26 cerró con 89.374 toneladas: un 7% menos que la anterior y un 4,5% por debajo de la media de cinco años.
2026 iba a ser el año de la recuperación. Y los castaños quemados rebrotaron, perro la sequía de septiembre y octubre lo estropeó: en Valdeorras la cosecha quedó en el 60% de lo habitual, con insectos, hongos y más castañas pequeñas de lo normal, y pocos frutos grandes. En El Bierzo, las olas de calor dejaron los erizos más pequeños y adelantaron la cosecha ya en agosto. La escasez de los últimos años ya encareció el kilo tanto en origen como en destino. Y el hongo que pudre el fruto repuntó, tras bajar del 33% al 14% de positividad media entre 2023 y 2025.
Paradoja mayorista. Que escasee no significa que el kilo se dispare a lo loco. En septiembre, primer mes de campaña, el precio medio de la castaña en Mercamadrid era de 3,54 euros el kilo. Es un 15,5% menos que los 4,18 euros de septiembre de 2025, con 275 toneladas en el mercado. Un solo mes no define ninguna tendencia, pero sí ayuda a entender por qué el cucurucho aguanta.
Palacios lo resume en tres ideas: buena castaña, fuego adecuado y muchas vueltas. Solo las dos últimas dependen de él, pero parece que les ha cogido el punto.

articles.title: Intel Core Ultra 4000 "Nova Lake-S" Preliminary Specs Leaked
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Intel Core Ultra 4000 "Nova Lake-S" Preliminary Specs Leaked
More information has surfaced about Intel's upcoming "Nova Lake-S" desktop CPU lineup. According to an Intel document obtained by Videocardz, the Core Ultra 4000 series lineup will be led by the Ultra 9 4970K BFC, with 28 cores and 144 MB of L3 cache, along with a 5.5 GHz boost clock. The document lists specs for seven Nova Lake-S desktop chips. Videocardz notes that these are C1-stepping qualification samples, so there may be some changes between these specs and the retail models, particularly the final clock speeds. We don't often see changes between qualification samples and retail processors so close to launch, but it's something to remember regardless. 
Looking at the table, the Core Ultra 9 4950K slots in just under the flagship 28-core 4970K BFC. The 4950K also has 28 cores in an 8P+16E+4LPE configuration, but it drops the BFC suffix and doesn't carry the additional L3 cache, topping out at 36 MB. The boost clock drops from 5.5 GHz on the 4970K to 5.4 GHz on the 4950K. This settles the confusion around the 4950K's core count, since the October lineup leak showed it without any LPE cores. There's also the 22-core Ultra 9 4900 BFC, an interesting non-K SKU that has fewer cores than the Ultra 7 models. This model only has a 65 W TDP, while all other leaked variants show a 125 W base power rating.After that, we get the Core Ultra 7 4870K BFC and 4850K, both of which have 24 cores (8P+12E+4LPE) and a 5.2 GHz boost, but are again split by the difference in L3 cache. Moving down the stack, the Core Ultra 5 4650K and 4650KF get 22 cores (6P+12E+4LPE), 30 MB of L3 cache, and a 5.1 GHz boost clock. Of course, the KF variant does not have an iGPU. Curiously, the 125 W 6P+12E+4LPE bLLC chip is missing from this stack, which lines up with leaker Jaykihn's claim that it was moved to Razor Lake. All Nova Lake-S CPUs support DDR5-8000 memory, up from DDR5-6400 on Arrow Lake-S. Per Videocardz, Intel is planning a next-generation desktop event in Berlin between February 22 and 25, which is now expected to be the launch event for Nova Lake-S.

articles.title: Tidal: Warum der Streaming-Dienst 27 Millionen Songs löschen will
articles.text:
Tidal verbannt vollständig KI-generierte Musik von seiner Plattform. Ab dem 9. Dezember lehnt der Streamingdienst solche Titel ab und entfernt sie aus dem Katalog. Erlaubt bleibt Musik, bei der Künstler KI „als Hilfsmittel“ einsetzen – sie darf aber nicht mehr ausschließlich von einem KI-Tool stammen.
Angekündigt hat Tidal den Schritt in einem Posting auf X und in seiner aktualisierten KI‑Richtlinie. Bislang hatte der Dienst Titel, die er als komplett von Werkzeugen wie Suno oder Lyria erzeugt einstufte, nur gekennzeichnet und von Tantiemen ausgeschlossen. „Aber das reicht nicht. Wir halten eine drastischere Änderung für nötig“, schreibt das Unternehmen. Vertriebspartner sollen solche Tracks künftig gar nicht mehr einliefern dürfen. Musik, deren Begleitdaten reine KI-Produktionen ausweisen, wird Tidal zurückweisen.
27 Millionen Titel werden verschwinden
In den vergangenen 90 Tagen entdeckte der Streamingdienst nach eigenen Angaben 43 Prozent aller angelieferten Tracks als „vollständig KI-generiert“. Am 6. November lag der Anteil mit über 60 Prozent sogar noch höher. Insgesamt sind rund 27 Millionen Titel im Katalog derzeit als KI-Musik markiert, das entspricht 6,3 Prozent des verfügbaren Angebots. Bis Anfang 2027 sollen diese Songs von der Plattform verschwinden.
Gehört wurden sie eh kaum: 96 Prozent kamen in den vergangenen drei Monaten auf null Streams. Das größere Problem sind für Tidal KI-Songs, die echte Künstler nachahmen und ihnen Streams und Tantiemen wegnehmen. Mehr als 65.000 Tracks hat der Dienst eigenen Angaben zufolge bereits entfernt, weil sie unter fremdem Namen liefen.
Die Richtlinie von Juni reicht nicht mehr
Mit dem Verbot verschärft Tidal seine erst Ende Juni vorgestellte KI-Richtlinie deutlich. Damals hatte der Dienst noch ausdrücklich erklärt, KI-generierte Musik weiter zu akzeptieren.
Komplett maschinell erzeugte Stücke bekamen ein sichtbares KI-Symbol und verdienten kein Geld mehr. Titel, die Hörer täuschen oder Künstler imitieren, wollte Tidal schon damals löschen. Doch offenbar reicht das nicht.

articles.title: Australia endurece las reglas de seguridad digital y amenaza a las grandes tecnológicas con multas millonarias
articles.text:
El parlamento australiano aprobó este miércoles la Ley de Deber Digital de Cuidado, una normativa que obliga a las grandes tecnológicas a prevenir daños en línea antes de que ocurran, bajo pena de multas que podrían alcanzar el 5% de sus ingresos globales. La cámara baja aprobó la legislación por 97 votos a 43.
Según informó la agencia AP, la norma es producto de un acuerdo entre el gobierno del Partido Laborista, de centroizquierda, y el Partido Verde, que controla el balance de poder en el Senado. La negociación derivó en siete enmiendas clave que endurecieron el texto original, incluida la posibilidad de que ciudadanos australianos demanden directamente a las plataformas por daños sufridos en línea.
Las multas pueden superar los 10.000 millones de dólares para empresas como Meta
La penalidad máxima prevista en el texto original era de 109 millones de dólares australianos (unos USD 72 millones). Las enmiendas negociadas con los Verdes reemplazaron ese techo por una multa equivalente al 5% de los ingresos globales de cada compañía. Para Meta, propietaria de Facebook e Instagram, eso podría traducirse en sanciones del orden de los USD 10.000 millones, según estimaciones publicadas por The Canberra Times.
El porcentaje ubica a Australia por encima de Canadá, donde el 3% corresponde al techo de las sanciones administrativas —las multas penales por infracciones formales pueden llegar al 5%—, aunque por debajo de la Unión Europea (UE), cuya Ley de Servicios Digitales fija el techo en el 6%. Los Verdes solicitaban inicialmente el 10%.
La ley obliga a las plataformas a evaluar riesgos y proteger a los menores
La normativa establece estándares mínimos de seguridad para redes sociales, videojuegos, aplicaciones y chatbots de inteligencia artificial (IA). Todas las plataformas deberán realizar evaluaciones de riesgo escritas cada año, conservarlas durante seis años y entregarlas a la Comisionada de eSafety —el regulador oficial de seguridad en línea del gobierno australiano— cuando sea requerido.
La ley presta especial atención a los menores de 18 años: las plataformas deberán limitar su exposición a contenido que atente contra la integridad física o mental de los menores. Los usuarios mayores de 16 años tendrán el derecho a desactivar los algoritmos de recomendación y ver únicamente el contenido de las cuentas que elijan seguir.
El régimen de responsabilidad también alcanza a los adultos: las plataformas deberán limitar la exposición a amenazas de violencia, acoso y difusión no consentida de imágenes íntimas. Los servicios que permitan que algoritmos adictivos provoquen daño serán considerados en infracción de su deber de cuidado.
Los ciudadanos podrán demandar a las tecnológicas ante tribunales australianos
Una de las enmiendas más relevantes otorga a los ciudadanos el derecho a demandar judicialmente a las plataformas por los daños sufridos. La ministra de Comunicaciones, Anika Wells, señaló que esta vía será “bastante poco frecuente”, pero reconoció que representa un cambio sustancial frente al esquema anterior, según recogió AP.
El caso del magnate minero Andrew Forrest, quien debió recurrir a tribunales de Estados Unidos para demandar a Meta por avisos fraudulentos que usaban su imagen sin permiso, ilustró la dificultad de exigir responsabilidades a empresas tecnológicas desde suelo australiano. Ese proceso aún no fue resuelto.
La ley crea además un sistema de resolución de disputas en tres etapas: primero, el mecanismo interno de cada plataforma; luego, un futuro ombudsman independiente para reclamos menores; y, por último, la acción judicial directa. Wells describió la norma como una reforma “sísmica” y advirtió que será la primera ley de seguridad en línea de Australia aprobada sin respaldo bipartidista, dado que la Coalición opositora votó en contra.
La legislación entrará en vigor tras un período de transición de 12 meses. Las empresas de noticias profesionales, el entretenimiento comercial, las pequeñas empresas y las organizaciones religiosas quedaron excluidas del alcance de la norma.

articles.title: Canadian C-band 5G is nearly twice as fast as other 5G: analysis
articles.text:
Canada’s 5G performance on C-band spectrum is improving and closing in on peer countries, according to new analysis from Opensignal showing how Canada’s 5G compares to other members of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).
To add some context, C-band is another name for midrange 5G spectrum that typically sits around 3.7 to 4.2GHz (about 3,700 to 4,200MHz) and acts as the middle option for 5G connections. It offers more capacity and higher speeds than low-band 5G, and better range than high-band 5G, also known as mmWave.
The report noted that 5G C-band usage has nearly doubled in Canada over the last three years. Opensignal noted that there was a bit of a slow start, and it is now closer to the median across its OECD peers, at 52 per cent of 5G readings now using C-band. Alongside that, 32 per cent of of 5G readings are still on the AWS spectrum that previously made up a lot of Canadian 5G readings in 2023.
Adding to this, the OECD median for 5G C-band readings has fallen from 70 per cent to 58 per cent, with countries like Austria, Finland, and Sweden shifting to lower-band spectrum for better range and indoor coverage.
Secondly, all three major Canadian operators are seeing faster 5G speeds on C-band. Users on the C-band 5G get 2.0-2.8 times faster speeds than users not on C-band 5G. Interestingly, Rogers customers saw the biggest improvement, with its C-band users getting speeds up to 2.8 times faster than non-C-band users. However, between operators, C-band speed results differ by less than 8 Mbps, ranging from 245 Mbps to 237 Mbps.
The same results are not seen for 5G Consistent Quality, which measures how often a 5G connection is good enough to use common apps. There was either no significant change or quality increased by a mere 1.3 to 1.6 per cent across tests. Rogers was the lowest, sitting at 81.2 per cent of tests. Telus jumped up to 91 per cent, and Bell was the highest at 92.1 per cent.
Interestingly, Opensignal notes that both Canada’s 5G Download Speed and its 5G Availability remain below the OECD median, with the U.K., Japan, Italy, and Germany below it. Above the median are France, the U.S., and South Korea; the latter has almost all connections using C-band, and each operator has 100MHz of contiguous spectrum. For Canadian operators, it varies depending on the carrier, and the region, with the average being between 60 to 100 MHz.

articles.title: Chefe do Instagram reafirma que app não “escuta” o que você diz
articles.text:
Chefe do Instagram reafirma que app não “escuta” o que você diz
Adam Mosseri fala mais uma vez sobre o tema e garante que aplicativo não usa microfone do celular para direcionar anúncios aos usuários.
O chefe do instagram, Adam Mosseri, falou mais uma vez sobre uma suspeita antiga de usuários do Instagram: o app da Meta usaria o microfone do celular para ouvir o que está sendo falado e direcionar anúncios. O executivo voltou a se pronunciar sobre o assunto nesta terça-feira (24/11) na própria rede social, repetindo o discurso que trouxe em outubro de 2025.
Basicamente, ele nega qualquer tipo de “escuta” pelo app no smartphone. Os argumentos utilizados são os mesmos do ano passado. Segundo ele, essa seria uma grande violação de privacidade por parte do app. Além disso, a bateria acabaria rapidamente, da mesma forma que uma luz vermelha acenderia indicando uma gravação em curso. Dessa vez, em vez de “talvez você veja algo logo depois de falar”, Mosseri reconhece que isso acontece, mas explica que isso é mais psicológico do que tech.
Ou seja: o fato de você identificar anúncios logo depois de falar teria a ver com a sua atenção ao que está na tela, e não ao conteúdo em si. A Meta sempre negou essa teoria, sugerindo que já tem tantas informações sobre os usuários que não faria sentido coletar dados a partir de gravações do tipo.
Em outubro de 2025, um vídeo bem parecido foi publicado pelo executivo. Os argumentos também são idênticos, assim como a “culpada” pelo tema ser levado a público: sua esposa, com quem Mosseri teria discussões anuais sobre. No primeiro vídeo, a legenda chama de Myth Busting, ou uma caça ao mito, em português. Dessa vez ele foi mais sucinto, mas ainda trouxe o mesmo conteúdo.
De acordo com Mosseri, são três os principais motivos para você ter a sensação de que um anúncio apareceu logo após ter falado sobre um assunto:
- Você pode ter visto esse anúncio algumas vezes antes, o que teria levado a falar sobre o tema (antes de vê-lo novamente).
- Depois de ter falado sobre, o assunto fica na sua cabeça. Ao ver o anúncio novamente, fica com a sensação de ter sido direcionado.
- Você pode ter comentado o assunto com algum amigo próximo, cujos dados são, de fato, analisados pelo instagram. Com isso, o anúncio também poderia ser interessante para você, aparecendo na sua conta.
Por esses motivos, o chefe do Instagram reconhece a situação: você comenda sobre um assunto e, logo depois, o anúncio aparece. Mas ele reforça que isso não teria absolutamente nada a ver com gravações de áudio ou vídeo.
Dessa vez, além de argumentar contra a teoria do microfone, Mosseri afirma ter noção de que não vai convencer todos os usuários de que o Instagram não grava suas conversas. Ao reconhecer que a sugestão de produtos e serviços passa, sim, essa sensação, o executivo destaca o uso de outras formas de captação de informações dos usuários.
A própria Meta fala sobre o tema desde 2016, garantindo que não há necessidade de coletar dados dessa maneira. Em um artigo sobre a teoria ainda no Facebook, a empresa destacou que o uso do microfone é exclusivo de áreas em que há algum tipo de permissão por parte do usuário, como gravações de vídeo, por exemplo.

articles.title: Ars Live recap: Don’t expect military attacks on data centers to stop
articles.text:
Amazon data centers came under military attack for the first time ever in the Middle East this year, and Russia and Ukraine exchanged an unprecedented flurry of drone strikes on each other’s data centers. To examine what such attacks on data centers mean for the future of cloud services that all modern societies depend upon, Ars hosted a live discussion.
In a conversation with Ars Technica Tech Reporter Jeremy Hsu, Joseph Jarnecki at the Royal United Services Institute first talked about why public cloud data centers have increasingly become military targets during the 2026 Iran war and the ongoing full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine:
We see an increasing acknowledgement and fact of dual use in particularly the public cloud, but also just across the board in private cloud data centers as well. The dual use that I refer to is the utilization of compute functions within these data centers—within cloud services—by militaries, for example, to run battlefield management systems, to do their HR, to do their resource management. Once a military uses a piece of civilian infrastructure, at least under international law or in terms of the principles of targeting that are taken forward by militaries, it can sometimes become a military object and is therefore of interest to an adversary, and there’s an incentive to target it.
Jarnecki also highlighted the fact that relatively cheap kamikaze drones can inflict disproportionate economic costs and create widespread cloud disruptions when striking data centers:
The second reason that we’ve seen targeting particularly in Russia’s largest data centers or some of Russia’s largest public cloud data centers like Yandex, as well as American hyperscalers that are based in the Gulf, is to impose economic cost in a way that would be disadvantageous for an adversary and would otherwise be quite difficult to impose in other ways. So it’s relatively low cost of munition to high cost of disruption. If you think about the amount of investment that’s been put forward by AWS and other companies in the Gulf to build out these data center installations relative to the cost of the amount of Shahed drones that are manufactured, produced, and utilized by Iran to target these data centers, I would put it very, very conservatively at 100X or even more. The cost ratio is really very lucrative for the adversary, and it provides the opportunity to really degrade the economic outcomes of who you are targeting.
Much of the discussion also focused on cloud resilience lessons for both governments and hyperscalers, with the latter including large cloud and data center operators such as Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Meta. articles.title: The canceled Tesla Cybertruck is the fastest-selling used truck in America
articles.text:
Tesla Cybertruck sales never reached the lofty heights CEO Elon Musk predicted when it launched. But the futuristic, steel-clad EV is finding new life in the used car market, according to analysis of sales figures by iSeeCars.com.
The automotive search engine and research platform analyzed more than 1.1 million sales of one- to five-year-old used vehicles in October 2026 and measured the average days on market by drivetrain, vehicle type, and individual model. The upshot: The Tesla Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used truck, averaging just 39.1 days on the market compared with 65.5 days for trucks overall. Used Cybertrucks sold faster than any other truck, including the Ford Maverick Hybrid, which held the No. 2 spot, and the Rivian R1T, in third place.
According to iSeeCars.com, the Cybertruck’s sales performance lines up with a broader pattern in the used vehicle market: Used battery electric vehicles are hot sellers right now, with 16 of the 25 fastest-selling used cars fully electric. EVs are even edging out hybrids in terms of average days on market. EVs average 45.6 days on market compared to 54.5 days for hybrids and 61 days for gasoline-powered vehicles. Not every EV is selling well, however. For instance, iSeeCars.com found that the Cadillac Escalade IQ was the slowest-selling vehicle in the study, averaging 134.3 days on the market, more than twice the overall industry average.
Karl Brauer, executive analyst at iSeeCars.com, told TechCrunch that high gasoline prices have changed consumer-buying habits, prompting more people to opt for an EV or hybrid over an internal combustion engine vehicle. If high prices persist, as they have since March, that trend could continue.
Keep in mind that these were October sales, the month before Musk announced Tesla would stop making the Cybertruck in 2027. Fuel prices and the relative rarity of Cybertrucks in the used car market were driving demand even before the cancellation announcement, Brauer said.
“The Cybertruck has only been out for a few years, so you have a lot of used ones coming off lease and entering the used car market for the first time,” he said, adding that used Cybertrucks are cheap relative to their MSRP.
The impending cancellation will likely fuel used Cybertruck sales, although the pace may ebb and flow over the next year.
“The canceling of the new Cybertruck is making people kind of aware — it’s like, oh wow, these things aren’t going to be coming anymore,” Brauer said. “Whatever demand is for them, supply will not be continuing to grow.”
Brauer said that once production of the Cybertruck ends — which is expected in summer 2027 — sales of used versions may pop once again.
“When the last one is being produced, that’ll probably reignite things again, and for a few months after that,” he said.

articles.text:
Firefox 161 upgrades its free built-in VPN with custom per-site rules — but only on desktop
Mozilla's Firefox latest update lets desktop users set 'Always on' or 'Always off VPN' rules for individual sites
- Firefox 161 adds automatic custom per-site VPN rules on desktop
- Firefox's built-in free VPN keeps unlimited data until January 31, 2027
- The update also brings a car app, Android audio, and quick-wipe tools
Mozilla has rolled out Firefox 161 for desktop and mobile, adding a practical automation upgrade to its free built-in VPN.
Announced in a Mozilla blog post on Tuesday, November 24, the release lets desktop users decide which websites open with the VPN active and which bypass it completely.
Flipping a privacy toggle on and off all day gets tiring. You might want an encrypted connection to check regional gift prices, while your bank refuses to load until you switch it off. Per-site rules remove that friction without pushing you straight toward one of the best VPN services.
Firefox's free VPN tool still carries real limits, though, and its unlimited data window will not last forever.
What is Firefox's free VPN, and how do per-site rules work?
Launched in Firefox 149 after an earlier beta, Firefox's free VPN is separate from the paid Mozilla VPN app. Mozilla VPN costs $4.99 a month (with an annual sub) and covers up to five full devices via Mullvad's WireGuard network, whereas the browser tool only routes Firefox traffic through an encrypted proxy.
Does it actually protect everything on your computer? No. It masks your IP address inside Firefox, but other apps stay exposed, site cookies can still identify you, and browsing history remains stored locally.
Normally capped at 50GB monthly across five server countries (aside from seasonal promos, like the one ongoing or the one active last summer), the free tool includes unlimited data on desktop and Android until January 31, 2027, with a Mozilla account in eligible regions.
To set desktop rules, click the toolbar VPN panel and select Manage VPN rules, or open Settings > Privacy & Security > VPN > Manage VPN rules. Add a site, pick Always on or Always off, and Firefox applies it automatically next time.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance.
Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
What else is new in Firefox 161?
The flame-shaped Fire button is also gradually rolling out to desktop users in Classic Window, bringing a quick data-clearing option outside Private Browsing.
From the toolbar, users can delete browsing and download history, cookies, site data, temporary files, saved form information, and website permissions and preferences.
Choosing to delete everything signs users out of websites, closes the current window, and opens a fresh one. Alternatively, users can select individual data types to clear without closing their existing window.
On Android, Reader View's Read Aloud feature is also gradually rolling out, letting users listen to webpages when their hands are busy.
Tap the Reader View icon in the address bar, then select the headphones icon to access playback controls, including play, pause, rewind, fast-forward, and playback speed. Audio continues with the screen off, and Firefox uses voices that run directly on the device, keeping page text and audio there.
Drivers with Google built-in cars can now download Firefox's new car dashboard app from Google Play to browse when parked. Mozilla says Firefox follows the principle "that not even Mozilla should know which websites you visit or what you do there," and never shares history with automakers.
According to the Firefox 161 release notes, the update also introduces an optional URL-copy shortcut and a Classic themes section featuring the older Proton look alongside a new OLED theme, while listing tab groups in the application menu.
