articles.title: Piratage de 1Password : faut-il changer son mot de passe après la fuite ?
articles.text:
Pour piéger les utilisateurs d’un gestionnaire de mots de passe, nul besoin de casser son chiffrement : il suffit de savoir exactement à qui écrire.
Un attaquant vient justement de mettre la main sur cette liste chez 1Password, il a récupéré le nom, l’adresse e-mail de connexion et la date de dernière visite d’une partie des abonnés. De quoi forger de fausses alertes bien plus convaincantes qu’un spam classique, un très mauvais timing pour l’éditeur canadien quelques mois après sa forte hausse de tarifs.
Dans son article du 25 novembre, 1Password explique que l’intrusion est partie du compte GitHub professionnel d’un employé (la plateforme où est stocké le code source). À l’aide d’un jeton d’accès volé (une sorte de badge numérique qui dispense de mot de passe), le pirate a pu lire du code privé et injecter du code malveillant vers les serveurs internes, qui lui ont ensuite renvoyé les données clients. L’enquête a débuté le 19 novembre, mais l’éditeur ne donne aucun chiffre précis et évoque simplement « un sous-ensemble » de ses millions d’utilisateurs et de ses 200 000 entreprises clientes.
    Pour aller plus loin
1Password augmente fortement le prix de ses abonnements : quelles sont les meilleures alternatives ?
            
Ce que le pirate a emporté, et ce qui a tenu
Le butin ne s’arrête pas aux noms et aux e-mails. L’attaquant a aussi copié des identifiants de compte, des dates de création, des clés publiques et des paramètres SRP (le protocole qui permet au serveur de vérifier un mot de passe sans jamais le recevoir, insuffisant pour ouvrir un compte selon l’éditeur).
Plus ennuyeux, il a récupéré les jetons de certains liens d’invitation et de récupération envoyés par e-mail, tout en accédant à la chaîne CI/CD (l’automate qui compile et déploie le logiciel), dont 1Password affirme avoir révoqué ou renouvelé tous les secrets.
Côté coffres, l’architecture a en revanche tenu bon. Chaque coffre est chiffré directement sur l’appareil grâce à deux éléments que 1Password ne stocke jamais : le mot de passe principal et la clé secrète (Secret Key) de 34 caractères générée à la création du compte.
Sans eux, les serveurs ne contiennent qu’un bloc illisible, et l’entreprise assure que les coffres n’ont été accessibles « à aucun moment ». Un scénario qui rappelle la nouvelle fuite de données chez LastPass cette année, où des coordonnées clients avaient filtré sans exposer les mots de passe.
    Pour aller plus loin
Nouvelle fuite de données chez LastPass : le gestionnaire de mot de passe encore dans la tourmente
            
Pour le moment, on ignore toujours combien de clients sont touchés, comment le jeton GitHub a été dérobé et si une rançon a été réclamée.
1Password ne dit pas non plus si tous les abonnés concernés seront avertis, seuls ceux disposant d’une invitation ou d’une récupération en attente ayant été contactés directement.
Enfin, si le code source copié ne renferme aucun secret client selon l’éditeur, il offre malgré tout une carte précieuse à quiconque voudrait y chercher de futures failles.
Que faire tout de suite ?
Vous n’avez pas besoin de changer votre mot de passe principal ni de régénérer votre clé secrète.
Le véritable danger se situe désormais dans votre boîte de réception : un faux e-mail de « récupération de compte » ou un appel du prétendu support sera d’autant plus piégeux qu’il affichera votre vrai nom et votre bonne adresse (par précaution, 1Password a d’ailleurs allongé ses codes de vérification par e-mail de six chiffres à dix caractères alphanumériques).
Le risque n’a rien de théorique, comme l’ont montré les fuites à répétition chez LastPass, et migrer vers un concurrent de notre sélection des meilleurs gestionnaires de mots de passe n’y changera rien puisque votre e-mail est déjà dans la nature. Voici les quatre réflexes à adopter immédiatement :
- Ne cliquez sur aucun lien suspect : face à un message inattendu évoquant 1Password, une invitation ou une récupération, ouvrez directement l’application ou tapez vous-même l’adresse du site.
- Ne partagez jamais vos clés : 1Password ne vous demandera jamais votre mot de passe principal ni votre clé secrète, ni par e-mail, ni par SMS, ni par téléphone.
- Signalez les tentatives : transférez tout message douteux à support@1password.com.
- Verrouillez votre compte : activez la double authentification sur votre compte 1Password si ce n’est pas déjà fait.
Un coup dur pour la confiance dans la plateforme
1Password a communiqué rapidement et son chiffrement a rempli son rôle là où c’était vital. Mais cela reste un problème de sécurité d’une entreprise qui vend de la sécurité… à vous de voir si les alternatives à 1Password valent le coup.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quels sont les meilleurs gestionnaires de mots de passe en 2026 ?

articles.title: Stockage solaire : les batteries Zendure SolarFlow AC+ en promo dès 839 €
articles.text:
Avec l’arrivée de l’hiver, le chauffage et l’éclairage font grimper la consommation au moment même où le prix de l’électricité continue d’inquiéter. Pour le Black Friday, Zendure baisse le prix de ses batteries SolarFlow AC+, capables de stocker le surplus d’une installation photovoltaïque existante ou l’électricité achetée en heures creuses, avec des offres dès 839 €.
Les journées raccourcissent, les radiateurs tournent davantage et la facture d’électricité s’alourdit d’autant, surtout pour les foyers dont les panneaux solaires ne produisent plus que quelques heures par jour à cette saison. Stocker l’électricité produite, ou achetée lorsqu’elle coûte moins cher, pour l’utiliser au bon moment devient alors une piste sérieuse pour reprendre la main sur sa consommation.
Zendure en fait le cœur de son opération Black Friday, avec des remises sur toute sa gamme SolarFlow AC+, de la SolarFlow 1600 AC+ d’entrée de gamme à la SolarFlow 4000 Mix AC+ grande capacité, en passant par le modèle phare, la SolarFlow 2400 AC+, proposée à 839 €.
Black Friday Zendure : trois batteries pour réduire sa facture d’électricité
Les trois batteries de la gamme SolarFlow AC+ de Zendure, à savoir les SolarFlow 1600 AC+, 2400 AC+ et 4000 Mix AC+, ont en commun de s’intégrer à toutes les installations solaires en toiture du marché, sans remplacer les panneaux ni l’onduleur existant. Elles savent aussi prendre le relais en cas de coupure : la SolarFlow 2400 AC+ dispose d’une alimentation de secours hors réseau, tandis que la SolarFlow 4000 Mix AC+ va plus loin avec une fonction de démarrage autonome (black start) capable d’alimenter toute la maison.
Pour ce Black Friday, Zendure propose trois offres sur sa gamme SolarFlow AC+ :
- SolarFlow 4000 Mix AC+ : 2 399 € au lieu de 2 599 €, soit - 200 € (-8 %), avec un compteur intelligent 1CT-S offert (d’une valeur de 84,99 €) et une assurance transport renforcée offerts
- SolarFlow 2400 AC+ : 839 € au lieu de 1 279 €, soit -440 € (-34 %), avec un compteur intelligent 1CT-S offert (d’une valeur de 84,99 €) offert
- SolarFlow 1600 AC+ et batterie AB2000L : 959 € au lieu de 1 678 €, soit - 719 € (-43 %), avec la possibilité d’ajouter une multiprise connectée 6-en-1 pour 1 € de plus
SolarFlow 4000 Mix AC+ : la batterie XXL capable d’alimenter toute la maison
Optimisée pour les installations photovoltaïques déjà en place sur les toits, la SolarFlow 4000 Mix AC+ est une solution de stockage couplée en AC pensée pour les foyers de trois personnes consommant environ 5 000 kWh par an, en maison mitoyenne ou en villa compacte. Sa batterie de 8 kWh, extensible jusqu’à 50 kWh avec six batteries additionnelles de 7 kWh, permet de récupérer le surplus solaire produit en journée pour le réutiliser le soir, lorsque les panneaux ne produisent plus, et d’augmenter ainsi son taux d’autoconsommation. Selon les estimations de Zendure, un tel foyer pourrait réduire sa facture d’environ 91 %, soit près de 1 250 € d’économies par an.
En réduction pour le Black Friday à 2 399 € au lieu de 2 599 €, la SolarFlow 4000 Mix AC+ s’accompagne en outre d’un compteur intelligent 1CT-S (pour piloter l’autoconsommation en temps réel) et d’une assurance transport renforcée offerts. Zendure ajoute un Powerhub monophasé pour l’achat de deux unités, ou un Powerhub triphasé pour l’achat de trois unités. Attention, ce Powerhub n’est pas expédié avec la commande : il faut en faire la demande depuis l’application Zendure, une fois la SolarFlow 4000 Mix AC+ reçue.
Elle se raccorde à l’onduleur photovoltaïque déjà installé via son port dédié PV-IN AC, qui accepte jusqu’à 5 kW et reste compatible avec les grandes marques présentes sur les toits européens, comme Huawei, SMA, Fronius, SolarEdge, Enphase ou Sungrow. Elle délivre 4 000 W de sortie AC continue sur le réseau (la configuration standard étant limitée à 800 W) et autant en charge comme en décharge de la batterie, de quoi alimenter plusieurs équipements énergivores comme un four, un lave-linge ou un lave-vaisselle. Surtout, sa fonction de démarrage autonome (black start) lui permet d’alimenter toute la maison en cas de coupure, avec une puissance hors réseau pouvant atteindre 3 680 W en entrée comme en sortie.
Pour tirer parti des heures creuses, la SolarFlow 4000 Mix AC+ s’appuie sur ZENKI, l’IA de Zendure, qui recharge la batterie lorsque l’électricité est bon marché et la décharge lorsque les prix augmentent. La plateforme de gestion énergétique HEMS permet quant à elle de piloter jusqu’à six appareils depuis un même compte.
Côté fiabilité, la batterie est protégée par le système ZenGuard et annoncée pour 10 000 cycles de charge et de décharge, avec une garantie de 10 ans et une durée de vie estimée à 15 ans. Elle se connecte en Wi-Fi, en Bluetooth, en LAN ou en RS485, une connexion filaire restant la plus stable.
Les points forts à retenir :
- Une batterie extensible jusqu’à 50 kWh, avec une capacité de base de 8 kWh
- 5 kW d’entrée AC et une puissance AC bidirectionnelle de 4 000 W
- Compatible avec les onduleurs photovoltaïques déjà installés
- Démarrage autonome (black start) en cas de coupure
SolarFlow 2400 AC+ : le modèle phare pour donner un second souffle à son installation
Pensée pour les foyers déjà équipés de panneaux en toiture, et notamment de micro-onduleurs, la SolarFlow 2400 AC+ est la solution de rénovation haut de gamme de Zendure. Elle s’adresse aux foyers dont la consommation grimpe fortement en soirée et qui souhaitent ajouter du stockage sans installer de nouveaux panneaux ni modifier leur installation, puisqu’elle fonctionne avec toutes les marques de micro-onduleurs, sans le moindre recâblage.
Pour le Black Friday, la SolarFlow 2400 AC+ passe à 839 € au lieu de 1 279 €, soit 440 € d’économie (-34 %), ce qui en fait l’offre la plus accessible de l’opération, avec en prime un compteur intelligent 1CT-S d’une valeur de 84,99 € offert.
Avec jusqu’à 2 400 W de puissance AC bidirectionnelle (800 W en configuration par défaut), elle couvre l’essentiel des pics de consommation du soir et tire le meilleur parti d’une installation solaire déjà puissante. Sa capacité de 2,4 kWh peut être portée à 16,8 kWh avec des batteries additionnelles, et elle assure une alimentation de secours hors réseau de 2 400 VA, jusqu’à 3 200 W en mode assisté par le réseau. Certifiée IP65 et dotée d’un système d’autochauffage, elle partage enfin l’écosystème de la gamme : l’IA ZENKI, la plateforme HEMS ouverte et compatible MQTT, l’intégration avec une pompe à chaleur ou une borne de recharge et la protection ZenGuard.
Les principaux atouts de la SolarFlow 2400 AC+ :
- Une capacité de 2,4 kWh, extensible jusqu’à 16,8 kWh
- Jusqu’à 2 400 W de puissance AC bidirectionnelle
- Secours hors réseau de 2 400 VA, IP65 et autochauffage
SolarFlow 1600 AC+ et AB2000L : l’entrée de gamme à 959 € (-43 %)
Vous trouvez les SolarFlow 4000 Mix AC+ et 2400 AC+ un peu trop puissantes pour vos besoins ? Zendure propose une alternative plus accessible avec la SolarFlow 1600 AC+, une solution de stockage couplée en AC pensée pour les foyers déjà équipés de panneaux en toiture dont les besoins énergétiques restent modérés.
Celle-ci embarque une batterie de 1,92 kWh, accompagnée ici d’une batterie supplémentaire AB2000L qui double la capacité de stockage pour atteindre 3,84 kWh au total. Et la très bonne nouvelle, c’est le prix de ce pack : 959 € au lieu de 1 678 €, soit 719 € d’économie (-43 %), avec en prime la possibilité d’ajouter une multiprise connectée 6-en-1 pour seulement 1 € de plus.
L’un des grands avantages de la gamme SolarFlow AC+ de Zendure, c’est son raccordement en courant alternatif. La SolarFlow 1600 AC+ s’intègre ainsi à n’importe quelle installation photovoltaïque en toiture, quelle que soit la marque du micro-onduleur, sans recâblage ni remplacement des panneaux, et s’installe en plug-and-play.
Comme ses grandes sœurs, elle profite de l’IA ZENKI, qui optimise les cycles de charge et de décharge de la batterie. C’est particulièrement intéressant avec un contrat heures pleines et heures creuses, puisque la batterie se recharge lorsque l’électricité est moins chère, puis restitue cette énergie au logement lorsque les tarifs remontent.
Côté puissance, la SolarFlow 1600 AC+ délivre jusqu’à 1 600 W en courant alternatif bidirectionnel. Limitée par défaut à 800 W, elle peut monter à 1 400 W en mode premium lorsqu’elle fonctionne seule, et jusqu’à 3 600 W une fois associée à des batteries additionnelles. Sa capacité de base de 1,92 kWh est extensible jusqu’à environ 11,5 kWh avec cinq batteries supplémentaires, et elle peut assurer une alimentation de secours jusqu’à 1 600 VA (2 200 W en mode assisté par le réseau). Certifiée IP65, elle intègre aussi un système d’autochauffage.
Les principaux atouts du pack :
- Une capacité extensible jusqu’à environ 11,5 kWh, avec un total de 3,84 kWh grâce à la batterie AB2000L
- Une puissance AC bidirectionnelle de 1 600 W
- Compatible avec tous les micro-onduleurs déjà installés
- Gestion intelligente de l’énergie avec l’IA ZENKI

articles.title: Amini wants to turn Africa’s paper archives into data for AI
articles.text:
Amini, a startup building sovereign AI infrastructure for governments in the Global South, has released Soma-1X Lite, an open-weight AI model designed to convert paper-based records into machine-readable data, targeting African countries that hold most public records in physical archives.
The company says the two-billion-parameter model can process about 15,000 pages per hour at an estimated graphics processing unit (GPU) computing cost of $0.22 per 1,000 pages. Clinton Oduor, Amini’s Head of Data Science, told TechCabal that, in an evaluation of 435 document pages across ten African languages, including Yoruba, Hausa, Swahili and Wolof, the model recorded an average character error rate of 2.9%—the lowest among the five models tested.
It can run on a GPU-equipped workstation without a dedicated data centre, or on a central processing unit (CPU), albeit slower. The model can also process documents offline, without relying on external AI services, according to Oduor.
The release comes as African governments seek to make their public records accessible, many of which remain in paper archives. Even where government information has been digitised, making it usable by digital systems remains a challenge. A 2019 Africa Open Data Index by Open Knowledge International, which assessed 420 government datasets across 30 African countries, found that only 14.5% were available in machine-readable formats.
Oduor said Soma-1X Lite could help countries bypass the conventional transition from analogue records to digital systems before adopting AI by converting paper documents directly into structured, machine-readable data. He explained that Soma-1X Lite uses vision-language models to analyse scanned documents, recognising printed text, handwriting, tables and other elements.
“Soma labels individual document elements and uses bounding boxes to link the extracted information to its location on the original page,” he said. “It also provides confidence scores to flag uncertain readings. The platform incorporates human-in-the-loop validation, enabling users to review, verify and correct information directly against the source documents.”
Amini claims Soma-1X Lite scored 84.7 on olmOCR-Bench, a public document-processing benchmark, outperforming Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT-5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5.
“Constraint has always been our superpower,” Kate Kallot, founder and CEO of Amini, said in a statement. “We did not ask how big we could build. We asked how small we could build and still stand among the best in the world.”
Founded in 2022 by Kallot, a former Nvidia executive, Amini builds sovereign AI infrastructure for the Global South, including modular, renewable-powered data centres, connectivity systems and tools for converting paper records into usable data. Over the past year, the company says it has processed millions of government records in private, sovereign environments using Soma.
In Botswana, Oduor told TechCabal that Amini is working with the Ministry of Minerals and Energy to digitise decades of geological records, including paper reports, hand-drawn maps, borehole logs and mineral resource records. The information Soma extracts feeds into Kanzi, Amini’s sovereign platform for geological and mining intelligence, which combines the digitised archives with geophysical surveys, geochemistry, drilling data, satellite imagery and mining records.
He says the platform lets government officials query national geological records and identify areas with mineral potential, with findings subject to validation by qualified geologists. The platform runs on national infrastructure, keeping the data under the government’s control. The company says the Central African Republic is expected to follow.
Amini has made Soma-1X Lite’s model weights, inference instructions and evaluation code available on Hugging Face, allowing researchers, developers, universities and government institutions to run the model privately, reproduce its results and adapt it to their needs.
The company plans to extend the model’s capabilities beyond Latin-based scripts to include the Ethiopic script used by Amharic and Arabic-based writing traditions such as Ajami. It also plans to improve its ability to process historical archives and complex documents such as maps, forms, and registries, using feedback from government deployments to improve the technology.”
Amini is joining a growing group of African technology platforms working to make public records more accessible and usable. These include Nigeria’s Minetrix AI, which aggregates government and other public records and makes them searchable through a multilingual AI platform.
For Amini, Soma is part of a broader effort to help countries build AI capabilities on infrastructure they control. The company says success would mean governments could eventually operate the systems independently, with local developers building businesses on top of the infrastructure, without depending on Amini to keep it running.
“Our goal is to enable local researchers and developers to actively contribute to the advancement of AI and build technologies that reflect the languages, knowledge, and needs of their societies,” Oduor said.

articles.title: DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 Aims to Make Robots Safer, More Dexterous, and Faster Learners
articles.text:
Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, a vision-language-action (VLA) model designed to improve robots' dexterity, reliability, and learning speed, while enabling safer operation in unstructured real-world environments.
According to DeepMind's vice president and head of robotics Carolina Parada, the model "marks a leap forward in three key areas": dexterity, reliability, and safety. She says its performance has been evaluated across more than 200 tasks, with reported improvements of 30% to 100% in success rates and 20% to 30% in task completion compared with prior versions. Demonstrated capabilities include serving food with tongs, tying a bow on a gift box, and pipetting liquids.
These tasks represent a step toward human-level dexterity by combining a number of skills, including advanced tool use, complex manipulation of deformables, and handling delicate objects with finesse.
The model is designed to work natively with different types of robots, including humanoid platforms such as Apptronik's Apollo 2 and tabletop pick & place systems such as Franka Duo platform.
Parada highlights the industrial trials conducted with Mercedes Benz, in which Apollo 2 humanoid robots were deployed on an existing industrial line, achieving a 96% success rate in tasks involving automotive kitting and sorting mixed metal brackets. In the trial, the Gemini Robotics ER embodied reasoning model enabled the robot to keep track of the workflow over multiple steps and adapt to changeing conditions, while Gemini Robotics 2.5 controlled the robot's hands and arms.
Another key aspect highlighted by Parada is Gemini Robotics 2.5's safety features, which include using reasoning guidance to identify and manage physical hazards:
Much like safety classifiers add a protective layer around Gemini’s responses, this guidance allows the robot to navigate complex environments securely. In our evaluations, this capability boosted safe task completion around obstacles by 33% and around nearby people by 43%.
DeepMind also open-sourced the new safety benchmark ASIMOV-jailbreak, containing hundreds of unsafe prompts across dozens of scenes.
Commenting on the announcement on LinkedIn, GEICO director of software Sean P. observed that "the combination of simulation, learning from mistakes, and real-world testing is what will make robots more capable and reliable in everyday tasks".
LightSpeed founder and CEO Biju Kulathakal emphasized that 96% accuracy may not be enough in real contexts involving humans:
Pausing when a person gets close is what gets robots out from behind the fence. And on a real line, customers live in the 4%. Learning from its own mistakes is how that closes.
Level principal engineer Ariel Franco Ferreira expressed his view that
Releasing an open benchmark for jailbreaks on a VLA model is the part I find most interesting, because a prompt injection that ends in a physical action is a very different failure from a bad chat answer.
He also raised the question of how to handle situations "when the robot refuses the unsafe step but leaves the task half done in a risky state".
As a final note, Gemini Robotics 2.5's development was accelerated using Gemini 4 Argon as a simulation engine, leveraging its robotics research capabilities to generate simulated environments.

articles.title: Capcom cerrará Exoprimal y dejará sin acceso al videojuego incluso a quienes compraron el disco
articles.text:
Capcom anunció que Exoprimal dejará de funcionar el 30 de septiembre de 2027, cuando la compañía apague definitivamente los servidores del videojuego de acción con dinosaurios. Desde ese momento, los jugadores perderán el acceso al título en todas las plataformas, incluso si compraron una copia física, conservan el juego instalado o intentan iniciar una partida individual.
La decisión marca el final de un proyecto que debutó en julio de 2023 y que apostó por combinar combates entre equipos de jugadores, armaduras futuristas y enfrentamientos contra enormes cantidades de dinosaurios. La compañía estableció un calendario de cierre dividido en tres etapas, que comenzó el 25 de noviembre de 2026 con la retirada de los contenidos prémium de sus pases de supervivencia.
El apagado definitivo está previsto para el 30 de septiembre de 2027. A partir de ese momento, Exoprimal ya no podrá ejecutarse porque depende de una conexión con los servidores de Capcom. Por tanto, tener el disco físico no permitirá continuar jugando cuando el servicio deje de estar disponible.
Cuándo dejará de venderse Exoprimal y qué pasará con las compras digitales
El calendario anunciado por Capcom establece que el videojuego continuará disponible en las tiendas digitales durante algunos meses. La fecha límite para comprarlo será el 31 de marzo de 2027.
Ese mismo día se retirarán de las plataformas digitales los contenidos descargables y los demás productos relacionados con el título. Quienes ya tengan una copia podrán conservarla en sus bibliotecas y descargarla nuevamente después de que desaparezca de las tiendas.
Esto significa que los jugadores no perderán inmediatamente el acceso cuando termine su comercialización. Tendrán seis meses adicionales para instalarlo, completar la historia y participar en las partidas antes del cierre definitivo de los servidores.
La primera fase de la despedida comenzó el 25 de noviembre de 2026. Desde esa fecha, los niveles prémium de los pases de supervivencia correspondientes a las cuatro temporadas dejaron de estar disponibles para su compra. Los usuarios que ya habían adquirido esos contenidos podrán utilizarlos de acuerdo con las condiciones establecidas por la compañía.
Por qué Exoprimal no funcionará ni siquiera con partidas individuales
Uno de los aspectos más importantes del anuncio es que el cierre afectará a todas las modalidades del videojuego. Aunque algunos jugadores podrían pensar que una partida individual debería seguir funcionando sin conexión, Exoprimal necesita comunicarse con los servidores para ejecutar sus actividades.
La dependencia del servicio también alcanza a los enfrentamientos en los que participan personajes controlados por inteligencia artificial. Capcom había explicado en 2024 que los bots podían ocupar los lugares de otros jugadores cuando alguien iniciaba una partida en solitario o el sistema no encontraba suficientes participantes.
Esta alternativa permitía avanzar en la historia incluso cuando había poca actividad en los servidores. Sin embargo, los personajes controlados por la inteligencia artificial tampoco podrán mantener el funcionamiento del juego cuando Capcom desconecte su infraestructura.
La medida también afecta a quienes compraron la edición física. Aunque el disco conserve los archivos necesarios para instalar el título, no será suficiente para acceder a sus funciones. En otras palabras, la compra no garantiza que el videojuego pueda utilizarse indefinidamente.
Un juego de dinosaurios que llegó en 2023
Exoprimal se lanzó el 14 de julio de 2023 para PC, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One y Xbox Series X|S. Su propuesta enfrentaba a dos equipos de cinco jugadores que utilizaban exoarmaduras para completar misiones mientras combatían contra oleadas de dinosaurios.
Las partidas también servían para descubrir una historia de ciencia ficción relacionada con la aparición de estas criaturas y los misterios detrás de los acontecimientos del juego.
En julio de 2024, después de completar el contenido previsto para sus cuatro temporadas, Capcom anunció que recuperaría los contenidos anteriores mediante un sistema de rotación. De esa manera, quienes llegaran después podrían acceder a las actividades y recompensas que se habían publicado durante el primer año.
Sin embargo, esa estrategia no modificó la dependencia de los servidores. Con el cierre anunciado para septiembre de 2027, la compañía pondrá fin a la posibilidad de jugar Exoprimal en cualquiera de sus plataformas.
El caso vuelve a poner sobre la mesa un problema de los videojuegos que requieren conexión permanente: comprar una copia física o digital no siempre significa tener acceso permanente a la experiencia. Cuando el funcionamiento depende de servidores administrados por la empresa, su cierre puede dejar sin utilidad incluso a los juegos que permanecen instalados en una consola o computadora.

articles.title: Samsung Doubles Down on V9 NAND in China
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Samsung Doubles Down on V9 NAND in China
Samsung is reportedly planning to increase its NAND production capacity in China, but it's unfortunately not the kind of NAND flash that will benefit regular consumers directly. According to Seoul Economic Daily, citing industry sources, Samsung plans to make roughly five times as much V9 NAND flash at its second fab in Xi'an, China, by the end of 2027. Sources tell SED that the X2 fab currently produces about 10,000 300 mm wafers of the 286-layer V9 NAND per month, and the plan is to raise that figure to around 50,000. This extra output is, to the surprise of no one, aimed at enterprise SSDs for AI data centers. It's interesting that this report has surfaced when NAND spot prices have already started falling.
As for the exact plans, the report says that Samsung will build an electroplating line in X2's empty cleanroom space, move equipment in around February 2027, and finish the conversion by November 2027. Additionally, 20% to 30% of the fab's existing V6 line will also be switched to V9. Overall, this looks like a plan to mostly shift to denser NAND inside an existing fab, rather than a brand-new factory expansion. Samsung has previously denied claims of expanding production capacity, so this might be more of a reshuffle. Still, the numbers suggest that a lot more NAND flash will indeed be produced according to the new plans. It looks like Samsung is doubling down on denser NAND, while TrendForce expects NAND contract prices to decline in 2027.
Sources:
				Seoul Economic Daily, 				Reuters, 				via ComputerBase.de

articles.title: Mayo Clinic to pay workers $906,000 for unpaid time spent booting up PCs and logging in
articles.text:
Cutting corners: Before anyone at a call center can take a call, they have to boot up their computer and log into every app the job needs. Mayo Clinic's appointment staff say they did it all off the clock. Now, the hospital system has agreed to pay them over $906,000 in back wages. The deal also gives them five paid minutes at the start of each day to get their machines running.
According to a court filing from Minnesota's attorney general, staff weren't paid for the minutes spent starting their computers and signing into the software they needed. That happened at the start of each shift and then again whenever they came back from a meal break. Mayo also rounded their clock times to the nearest 15 minutes. In the state's view, that cost them even more pay.
Mayo, for its part, doesn't agree with the state's take. But it still settled because it would rather see the money go to staff than spend it fighting the case. It had actually dropped rounding and started paying for that startup time back in May. The settlement now locks in those changes. If the clinic slips back, it could owe a $100,000 penalty.
As for the back pay, it covers 1,021 workers and every shift they put in between July 2024 and May 2026. Each worker gets 5.41 minutes of pay per shift at their individual hourly rate. Oddly enough, 4.41 of those minutes make up for the rounding alone. The total works out to an average of just under $890 per person before taxes.
The case itself started in 2025, when workers took their complaints to Attorney General Keith Ellison's office. While announcing the deal on Monday, Ellison warned other employers that anyone on-site or performing work-related duties is on the clock.
Bank of America faced a similar fight last year, when a former analyst sued over unpaid login time. Her suit claimed remote staff spent up to 30 minutes a day waiting on Windows, VPN tokens, and password logins before their paid shifts began. Law360 reports that the bank agreed to pay roughly $21,500 to settle, attorney fees included. A judge signed off on the deal in April.
Federal guidance has supported the workers' position since at least 2008, too. The Labor Department's call center fact sheet from that year gives starting up a computer and loading work apps as an example of when the paid workday begins.

articles.title: User passwords safe after 1Password security breach, company says
articles.text:
User data from 1Password has been compromised by hackers, but the company is assuring users that their passwords and recovery keys are safe.
The news: On Wednesday, 1Password announced it was subject to a breach on Nov. 19, when hackers gained access to the company’s backend system. That breach exposed the names, email addresses, and additional metadata of an unspecified number of users. Despite the attack, the Toronto-based cybersecurity software company said no passwords or recovery keys were exposed and said there is no need for users to update that information. 
From the source: “1Password is designed so that a breach of our systems can’t expose your vault contents,” the company wrote in a blog post on Wednesday. “Your vault secrets are encrypted with keys that only you hold, so we can’t access them, and neither can an attacker who gets into our servers.”
The context: 1Password uses a “vault system” that creates an encrypted container where users can control access to sensitive information like login details, credit card credentials, passkeys, and other documents. The company itself does not have access to the contents of user vaults, protecting them through dual-key encryption; access requires an account password and secret key that is not sent to or stored by 1Password servers.
1Password said the breach happened after an employee’s GitHub account was compromised and used by the attacker to introduce malware to the company’s source code. Aside from names and email addresses, the attacker downloaded records around account creation and sign-in times, public keys, user identifiers, and other metadata.
BetaKit reached out to 1Password for more detail on the incident and whether it reported the breach to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, but has not yet received a response.
RELATED: Why Canadian tech is standing against Bill C-22
Final thought: 1Password has since stated that the company has taken a number of remediation actions including disabling the impacted employee’s GitHub account, rotating credentials, lengthening recovery codes, and retaining independent cybersecurity experts to validate its efforts.
Still, this is another in a rash of global cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting companies from Bell to Binance, that have set many on edge. 1Password’s unique point of trust—and the sheer volume of sensitive information it stewards—makes even the appearance of insecurity particularly impactful. Greg Osuri, founder of Silicon Valley’s Akash Network, said online that his trust in the company was diminished even if no passwords had been exposed.
Feature image courtesy of 1Password.

articles.title: X’s latest update for creators focuses on vertical video
articles.text:
X announced new creation tools Wednesday, many of them focused on short-form vertical video. The updates are part of the platform’s effort to compete with social networks such as YouTube and Instagram as the format continues to grow in popularity.
The tools are designed to help creators make professional-quality vertical videos, share original content more easily, and earn more. They also give creators more ways to record, edit, and publish content directly on the platform without relying on third-party apps.
A key addition is an upgraded media editor that lets creators produce polished vertical videos without leaving X. Recording features include the ability to capture video in segments and use green-screen effects, the company said.
The editor also offers a range of postproduction tools. Creators can convert horizontal videos to vertical format, automatically generate captions, trim footage, add text overlays, choose custom thumbnails, and adjust photos before publishing.
Thanks to a recently announced update, users can now add up to 20 photos and videos to a single post, which audiences can swipe through horizontally. X says the feature is intended for sharing event recaps, behind-the-scenes moments, and product launches.
Availability of the new features varies by region, X said.
Earlier this month, the company introduced a clipping feature that lets users take snippets from longer videos, add their own commentary, and post the clips without leaving X. Clips credit and link to the original video, plus the person who creates a clip and the original poster can earn from its views.
Another feature, “React with Video,” launched earlier this year. Similar to TikTok’s “stitch” feature, this lets creators respond to posts with video commentary while displaying the original post in the background.
X has also introduced new earning opportunities and updates to its creator monetization programs in recent months. These include the “Video Kickstart Bonus,” an invitation-only pilot that rewards selected creators for publishing original vertical videos under three minutes long and without watermarks.
The platform has also launched “Subscriber-only Group Chats,” which let creators host private, real-time conversations with paying subscribers. The feature is currently open to creators with 800 or fewer subscribers, and each group chat can accommodate up to 1,000 members.

articles.title: IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes
articles.text:
IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes
- Date:
  November 23, 2026
- Source:
  IBM
- Summary:
  IBM and University of Chicago researchers have demonstrated that a quantum computer can complete an extraordinarily complex calculation in just 15 minutes, beyond the practical reach of leading classical computing methods. A novel error-detection technique also allows scientists to establish confidence in the accuracy of the results, overcoming a major hurdle in quantum computing.
- Share:
An IBM quantum computer has completed an extraordinarily complex computational task in just 15 minutes, while leading methods for simulating the calculation on conventional computers would require prohibitively long runtimes. Perhaps even more significantly, researchers were able to establish statistical confidence in the accuracy of the quantum computer's results, addressing one of the biggest obstacles in the field.
The achievement, led by IBM and researchers from the University of Chicago, satisfies the fundamental criteria for quantum advantage. This milestone occurs when a quantum computer performs a computational task beyond the practical capabilities of leading classical computing methods while producing results that can be trusted.
In their new paper, "Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity," the researchers demonstrated that both objectives could be achieved simultaneously using a novel design for encoded quantum circuits. The experiment represents one of the largest demonstrations of logical quantum computing to date. The researchers have also made their circuits and experimental results publicly available through the Quantum Advantage Tracker.
Solving Quantum Computing's Verification Problem
Unlike conventional computers, which process information using bits that represent either zero or one, quantum computers rely on quantum bits, or qubits. These can exist in combinations of both states and interact through a phenomenon known as quantum entanglement. These properties allow quantum computers to approach certain computational problems in fundamentally different ways.
For years, scientists have tested the capabilities of quantum computers using a benchmark called random circuit sampling (RCS). This technique involves running a series of randomly selected quantum operations and generating samples from a complex probability distribution. As the circuits grow larger and more complicated, reproducing their output with a classical computer becomes increasingly difficult.
However, this approach creates a fundamental dilemma. If a computation is too difficult for a classical computer to reproduce, how can researchers establish that the quantum computer performed it correctly?
As computational complexity increases, independently verifying the results becomes progressively more difficult and eventually impractical without making strong assumptions about how accurately the quantum hardware operates.
To overcome this problem, the IBM and University of Chicago team developed a more structured alternative to random circuit sampling. The researchers mathematically demonstrated that their approach preserves the same computational hardness criteria as conventional RCS while introducing a structure that allows errors to be detected during the computation.
"Verification remains one of the biggest challenges in firmly establishing experimental quantum advantage," said Bill Fefferman, Associate Professor at the University of Chicago. "This experiment develops techniques to better characterize the fidelity of hard quantum states under noise, increasing confidence that the quantum computer is solving a computationally hard problem."
Soumik Ghosh, PhD student in Fefferman's group at the University of Chicago, added, "Beyond strengthening experimental validation, advances in verification have the potential to unlock practical applications for the next generation of quantum computers."
70 Logical Qubits and Tenfold Lower Error Rates
One of the greatest challenges in building powerful quantum computers is their extraordinary sensitivity to errors. Quantum information can be disrupted by environmental disturbances, imperfections in hardware, and inaccuracies in the operations used to manipulate qubits. As computations become longer and more complex, these errors can accumulate and undermine the reliability of the results.
Quantum error correction addresses this weakness by encoding quantum information across multiple physical qubits to create more reliable units known as logical qubits. This approach allows certain errors to be identified and, depending on the technique, corrected or accounted for without destroying the underlying quantum information.
In one of the largest known demonstrations of quantum error correction, the researchers performed computations using 70 protected logical qubits. The experiment involved 2,415 logical two-qubit operations and 468 logical "T gates."
Quantum gates are the fundamental operations that manipulate quantum information, much like logic gates in conventional computers. Two-qubit gates allow qubits to interact, while T gates enable additional types of quantum operations needed for universal quantum computing. Together, these gate counts illustrate the considerable complexity of the experiment.
By encoding the quantum circuits, the researchers achieved effective logical error rates 10 times lower than the underlying physical error rates. This substantial reduction allowed the quantum computer to maintain remarkably high fidelity, a measure of how closely the actual quantum state matches the intended one, despite performing thousands of complex operations.
A New Era of Quantum Advantage
"We are now firmly in the quantum advantage era," said Jay Gambetta, Director of IBM Research and IBM Fellow. "We have demonstrated a quantum computation beyond the practical reach of classical computers that establishes, with statistical confidence, a lower bound on how faithfully it was executed. This milestone gives scientists, developers, and businesses a new foundation for trusting quantum computers as they scale to problems far beyond what we can achieve classically."
The researchers found that many leading classical simulation techniques would require impractically long periods to reproduce the computation. IBM's quantum computer, by comparison, accomplished the task in approximately 15 minutes.
Although the experiment was designed to demonstrate quantum advantage rather than solve an immediate real-world problem, it addresses two essential requirements for making large-scale quantum computing practical: controlling errors and establishing confidence in computational results.
By demonstrating both capabilities in a computation beyond the practical reach of leading classical methods, the researchers have taken a significant step toward a future in which quantum computers could reliably tackle scientific and industrial problems that are currently out of reach.
Story Source:
Materials provided by IBM. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Simon Martiel, Jay-U Chung, Alireza Seif, Soumik Ghosh, Ian Hincks, Abhinav Deshpande, Bill Fefferman, Jay M. Gambetta, Ali Javadi-Abhari. Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity. arXiv, 28 Jul 2026 DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2607.25941

articles.title: WhatsApp por fin introduce la función que más pedíamos: así son los nuevos mensajes programados
articles.text:
Los mensajes programados de WhatsApp son, por fin, una realidad. La app de mensajería de Meta ha anunciado la implementación de esta característica, que permite enviar mensajes de forma diferida de forma fácil. Una solución ideal para gestionar mejor las comunicaciones tanto personales como laborales.
Con lo nuevo de WhatsApp, ya no tendrás que poner una alarma o un recordatorio cada vez que tengas que enviar un mensaje importante, pero temas olvidarlo. Tampoco, si recuerdas algo a la mitad de la noche y quieres dejarlo listo para que se entregue de forma automática a la mañana siguiente.
Los mensajes programados representan uno de los cambios más grandes en la historia de WhatsApp. Además, son una de las funciones más reclamadas por el público. Después de todo, la entrega automática de mensajes es una herramienta que ya lleva años disponibles en otros servicios de comunicación como plataformas de correo electrónico y de comunicación empresarial.
Usar lo nuevo de WhatsApp es realmente muy sencillo. Para dejar programado un mensaje solo tienes que crearlo y mantener pulsado sobre el botón de enviar. En adelante, la app te mostrará una ventana emergente en la que podrás elegir la fecha y la hora en que quieres que se entregue. Tan simple (y tan útil) como eso.
WhatsApp introduce al fin los mensajes programados
Los mensajes programados de WhatsApp ofrecen bastante flexibilidad, pues se pueden guardar para que se entreguen desde 10 minutos y hasta 14 días después de su creación. Y si te preocupa que el destinatario sepa que no se trata de algo escrito en el acto, no te preocupes. Las personas que los reciben como si fuesen mensajes comunes y corrientes.
WhatsApp está habilitando los mensajes programados tanto en los chats individuales como en los grupos. Además, la aplicación introduce un nuevo apartado desde donde se pueden gestionar todos los envíos pendientes. Esto significa que si decides modificar o cancelar el envío de los mensajes, puedes hacerlo sin ningún inconveniente.
Es importante mencionar que los mensajes programados no funcionan solo con texto, pues WhatsApp ha confirmado que también sirven con fotos y vídeos. Sobre su implementación en los audios todavía no hay novedades, así que si sueles comunicarte con notas de voz vas a tener que esperar un poco más.
¿Y qué pasa si el móvil se queda sin batería? Todos los mensajes de WhatsApp que estén programados se envían igual, incluso aunque el teléfono desde el que se originan esté apagado. Desde la plataforma de Meta aseguran que estos mensajes están protegidos por el cifrado de extremo a extremo.
El despliegue global de los mensajes programados de WhatsApp ya está en marcha, aunque posiblemente demore algunas semanas en llegar a tu móvil. Como suele suceder, los de Mark Zuckerberg planean habilitar esta función de forma gradual en todo el mundo, así que asegúrate de revisar regularmente si ya la tienes disponible.

articles.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
articles.text:
Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that’s designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. The patent has been rejected, but unfortunately, Google might appeal or resubmit an amended version, and we could see this monstrosity come to market.
Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
Imagine an endless feed of AI slop in which you are the main character of every story.
First spotted by Patentlyze, the patent — which was filed last May and published last week — describes how My Channel would use a person’s demographic data and viewing history to create its own prompts that would then be fed into an LLM to help generate AI videos tailored to that person’s specific interests. In addition to factoring in what kinds of videos a user tends to watch, the system would capture contextual data from their device like IP addresses, GPS locations, and specific details about the user’s age. My Channel could also base its prompts on current news like sports scores and things happening on social media, and all of the video generation would take place on Google’s servers.
According to the patent, My Channel would be able to churn out entire movies of various genres. If a user watches a lot of videos about Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, the system might serve up something like Ash Koosha’s Odysseus: The Fall. The patent details how My Channel might be able to connect to other streaming services — which would give it even more information about users and, presumably, access to useful training data for video generation. It all seems like a convoluted way to whip up AI knockoffs of professionally produced art, but what’s most unsettling about the patent are its mentions of My Channel creating digital avatars of users and turning them into “the protagonist or lead character” in the content it pumps out.
Setting aside the fact that My Channel would use photos, videos, and audio clips of people to create these avatars, the system sounds like it is designed to generate a form of “entertainment” that is deeply at odds with what makes engaging with art a worthwhile, enjoyable experience. It can be fun to metaphorically project one’s self into fictional narratives to understand how characters feel, but what Google is proposing is giving people access to an endless supply of bespoke content that doesn’t at all encourage them to use their imaginations to empathize with or relate to the characters. The patent makes it seem like Google thinks that viewers would be entertained enough just by seeing themselves onscreen. That’s bleak in and of itself because My Channel sounds very much like an unholy cross between JibJab and the panoptic elements of Google.
My Channel feels like an even more depressing idea when you consider how the service would make it that much easier for its users to avoid broadening their horizons by being exposed to new things that exist outside their comfort zones. If Google were able to strike the right licensing deals with other streaming services, My Channel users could presumably gorge themselves on artless AI regurgitations of preexisting content. That might keep some people glued to the service — a goal that every streaming platform strives for — but it would also discourage them from engaging with entertainment that isn’t expressly crafted to appeal to their assumed tastes.
When people refer to AI-generated videos as “slop,” they’re talking about the fact that generative models are incapable of generating art with the same kind of creative intention that makes human-made stories compelling. Video generation models can mimic visual elements of the data (read: movies and series) they’re trained on, but they cannot truly think or feel in the way that directors, writers, and actors can. This reality is why it has been so baffling to see AI-boosting entertainment companies, streamers, and studios insisting that the technology will fundamentally revolutionize the industry for the better. It feels much more likely that gen AI is going to keep flooding the internet with garbage no one wants to watch.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (November 25, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (November 25, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here’s the roundup for Wednesday, November 25, 2026.
From Lakshmi Venu filing a suit seeking partition of Venu Srinivasan family assets to Aeravti Ventures launching a Rs 300 crore fund, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Latest news
Lakshmi Venu files suit seeking partition of Venu Srinivasan family assets
Lakshmi Venu, daughter of Venu Srinivasan, has filed a suit in the Madras High Court seeking partition of the joint-family assets of the Venu Srinivasan branch of the TVS family.
A statement from Lakshmi Venu’s counsel said she seeks her claimed share and access to family records that she says have been withheld despite repeated requests.
The suit follows a November 16 partition notice to her father, who is Chairman Emeritus of TVS Motor and Non-Executive Chairman of TVS Holdings.
Funding news
Aeravti Ventures launches Rs 300 Cr fund II
Aeravti Ventures, a Bengaluru-based early stage venture capital firm, has launched its second fund called Aeravti Ventures II, with a target corpus of Rs 300 crore.
A statement from the VC firm said, Aeravti Ventures II has secured commitments as the first close of its target corpus with the final close expected within the next six months.
Aeravti Ventures II plans to invest in 9–10 startups spanning pre-seed to pre-Series A stages, with a preference for leading pre-seed and seed rounds. The fund expects to write initial cheques of Rs 6 crore to Rs 10 crore per startup with the capacity to invest 2–3 times the initial amount in subsequent funding rounds.
Piramal Alternatives invests Rs 225 Cr in Ardee Engineering
Piramal Alternatives, the fund management arm of the Piramal Group, has announced an investment of Rs 225 crore in Ardee Engineering through Piramal India Credit Opportunities Fund II.
Ardee will use the capital to expand its manufacturing capacity and execute a growing pipeline of industrial projects.
The company designs and manufactures pre-engineered buildings and material handling systems for sectors such as manufacturing, warehousing and logistics. Its pre-engineered buildings business spans design, manufacturing and on-site installation management.
Vidyakul secures Rs 10 Cr debt funding from Michael & Susan Dell Foundation
Vernacular learning platform Vidyakul has secured Rs 10 crore in debt funding from the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation to expand its educational services across India. The funding will support courses, assessments and personalised academic assistance for students in Classes 9 to 12, alongside AI-powered tools for answering questions and delivering Hindi-language learning.
The platform currently resolves around 1.2 million student queries monthly and plans to develop learning pathways beyond Class 12. Vidyakul reported a 99.8% pass rate among its Bihar Class 12 students in the 2026 board exams, compared with the state average of 85%. More than 1.17 lakh students enrolled in its paid programmes in 2025-26.
Lakshya Aerotech raises Rs 2.5 Cr seed funding to develop indigenous physical AI tech
Lakshya Aerotech, operated by Lakshya SmartGuard Systems, has raised Rs 2.5 crore in seed funding from Santosh Kumar, promoter of Samkhyaa Group. The investment will support research and development, engineering infrastructure, product development, and domestic manufacturing capabilities. The New Delhi-based deeptech company is focused on developing indigenous physical intelligence technologies that enable machines to perceive their surroundings, make decisions and operate autonomously.
Its work centres on embedded intelligence, autonomous control and advanced engineering, with the aim of converting core technologies into commercially deployable products. Founder Lokesh Popuri said the funding would strengthen the company's research and product engineering efforts.
SUK-M raises pre-seed funding to develop indigenous thorium microreactor
Indian nuclear technology startup SUK-M has raised its first institutional pre-seed funding round, led by Speciale Invest, with participation from Navam Capital, BYT Capital and two angel investors. The funding will support the recruitment of scientists and engineers and the establishment of an experimental facility to test its compact thorium-based microreactor and assess its safety features.
The proposed reactor is designed to generate around 10 MW of electricity or 30 MW of heat per unit, with potential applications in data centres, steel plants and hydrogen production. SUK-M has completed initial computer simulations and is moving towards laboratory testing and engagement with prospective industrial customers.
Other news
Minfy and AWS expand global strategic collaboration through 2031
Minfy and Amazon Web Services (AWS) have signed a five-year global strategic collaboration agreement, extending their partnership from India and the US to worldwide markets. The new agreement, signed on November 25, 2026, is three times the target of their 2024 agreement. The companies will jointly develop and market AI and cloud solutions across manufacturing, aerospace, financial services, logistics, media, healthcare and the public sector.
Minfy will expand its industry-specific AI platforms, including mVISTA for IT-OT operations, mPRISMA for media and its financial services Customer Data Platform, built using Amazon Bedrock and AWS services. The collaboration aims to help enterprises move AI projects from pilots into scalable production systems.
Neysa launches partner programme to expand enterprise AI adoption in India
AI cloud infrastructure company Neysa has launched the Neysa Partner Program to help AI developers, system integrators, resellers and technology providers build and deliver enterprise AI solutions across India. The programme combines Neysa’s Velocis AI cloud infrastructure with partners’ applications, industry expertise and implementation capabilities. It offers four partnership categories covering solution development, integration, consulting and technology collaboration.
Support includes deal registration, technical and sales training, marketing resources, joint proposals and co-selling opportunities. The Premier Tier provides additional assistance for partners investing in joint solutions and market development. The initiative aims to help enterprises move AI projects from pilots to production without investing in their own GPU infrastructure.
Apurva.ai invites development organisations to rethink social challenges
Bengaluru-based Apurva.ai has launched an Open Call to REIMAGINE, inviting development organisations to explore new approaches to persistent social and organisational challenges. The initiative targets NGOs, social enterprises, funders, investors and accelerators working on areas such as programme implementation, impact measurement, knowledge management and organisational workflows. Participating organisations can submit one recurring challenge for examination of existing processes, underlying assumptions and potential alternative approaches, including the use of artificial intelligence.
Apurva.ai said the initiative is neither a funding opportunity nor a product demonstration and does not guarantee technology implementation. The organisation currently works with more than 50 organisations globally, while its AI-powered Apurva LENS has helped surface over half a million voices and perspectives from the development ecosystem in the Global South.
Pernod Ricard Foundation, NSRCEL launch circular innovation programme
Pernod Ricard India Foundation, in partnership with NSRCEL at IIM Bangalore, has launched the first cohort of its Circular Innovation Incubation Programme, supporting 12 early-stage startups. The initiative will focus on solutions across plastic circularity, glass circularity and climate-smart agriculture. Participating ventures are developing innovations in waste management, recycling, alternative materials, reverse logistics, precision agriculture, bioenergy and water efficiency.
The programme builds on three earlier cohorts that selected 58 startups and deployed Rs 3.2 crore in grant support. The new initiative will provide mentoring, market validation, business development, fundraising readiness and access to investors and industry partners. It will also offer milestone-based grants and structured pilot opportunities to help startups move from early-stage innovation towards commercial deployment.
Atlassian appoints Swapna Bapat as India Head of Sales
Enterprise collaboration software company Atlassian has appointed Swapna Bapat as Head of Sales for India. Based in Bengaluru, she will lead the company's sales and customer success functions, focusing on enterprise growth, customer relationships and its go-to-market strategy.
Bapat brings more than 25 years of experience across product management, presales and sales in India, the US, the Middle East and Africa. She joins Atlassian from Palo Alto Networks, where she served as Vice President and Managing Director for India and SAARC.
Boba Bhai facilitates Rs 3 Cr ESOP liquidity for employees
Korean fusion food brand Boba Bhai has facilitated an Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP) liquidity event worth Rs 3 crore for six early employees. The initiative enabled participating employees to monetise 25% of their vested ESOP holdings, making the company among the few Indian startups to offer such liquidity at the Series B stage.
The development follows its recent $18 million Series B funding round. Founded in 2023, Boba Bhai has expanded to more than 120 stores across India and serves over three lakh orders every month.
PwC India launches Future AI Experience Lab in Gurugram
PwC India has launched its Future AI Experience Lab in Gurugram to help enterprises explore AI applications and translate them into business outcomes. The facility houses more than 90 industry-specific AI solutions and assets, enabling business leaders to test technologies through hands-on experimentation.
The Lab will focus on areas including Physical AI, human-AI collaboration, customer experience, robotics, intelligent devices and enterprise functions. The initiative aims to help enterprises move beyond AI pilot projects towards measurable improvements in productivity, revenue, risk management and customer service.
Hughes Services reports 300% revenue growth in two quarters
Delhi-based logistics startup Hughes Services has reported more than 300% revenue growth over two quarters, driven by improved fleet utilisation, operational efficiency and expansion into new markets. Founded in 2025 by Rajat Singhal and Ankit Singhal, the company operates across electric vehicle logistics, trucking, heavy logistics and enterprise supply chains.
It currently manages approximately 2,200 vehicles, with electric vehicles accounting for 20% of its fleet. The company plans to transition its entire fleet to electric by 2030. Hughes Services has also expanded into 10 additional Tier II cities, including Patna, Lucknow and Bhubaneswar, to tap growing demand from quick-commerce and consumer businesses.
FatakPay partners UGRO Capital for co-lending
Mumbai-based fintech platform FatakPay has partnered with UGRO Capital to expand access to formal credit through a co-lending arrangement. Under the partnership, FatakPay's NBFC subsidiary, FDPL Finance, and UGRO Capital will jointly extend instant personal loans to eligible salaried and self-employed individuals.
FatakPay will manage customer sourcing, digital onboarding and loan servicing, while UGRO Capital will provide credit underwriting, risk assessment and lending expertise. Both companies will jointly fund and manage the loan portfolio.
SquadStack, Bizom deploy Voice AI for FMCG retailers
SquadStack.ai and Bizom have deployed a Voice AI agent to capture orders from kirana and medical stores missed by field sales representatives. The solution contacts retailers, communicates product targets and ongoing trade schemes, builds confirmed orders and integrates them directly into Bizom's distribution platform.
The solution currently communicates in Hinglish and understands retailers' references to products through prices, packaging colours and local terminology. The companies said the technology recovers missed sales without replacing human sales representatives or increasing field headcount.
Usha Financial Services reports 120% growth in Q2 profit
Usha Financial Services Limited reported a 119.54% year-on-year increase in standalone profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 8.73 crore for the second quarter of FY27. Total income rose 50.81% to Rs 25.60 crore, while profit before tax increased 114.50% to Rs 11.41 crore. The company's gross loan book stood at Rs 502.76 crore as of September 30, 2026, registering 27.72% annual growth.
Its net worth increased 13.83% to Rs 246.45 crore. Asset quality remained stable, with gross non-performing assets at 2.70% and net NPAs at 2.08%. For the first half of FY27, PAT grew 79.84% to ₹16.76 crore, while total income increased 33.51% to ₹45.91 crore.
Pine Labs launches AI agents for merchant operations
Pine Labs has introduced two AI agents, Guide and Marketer Agent, under its Agentic Org platform to help small businesses manage operations and digital marketing. Integrated into the Pine Labs One merchant application, Guide enables merchants to access sales, payments, settlements, refunds and transaction information through conversational queries.
Marketer Agent helps businesses create advertising campaigns by handling keyword research, creative generation, audience targeting and campaign setup, initially across Google platforms. Merchants can review and approve campaigns before advertising expenditure is committed.
Fynd wins UK retail technology deal with N Brown
Mumbai-based retail technology company Fynd has partnered with UK retailer N Brown, which has selected its Boltic platform for integration and workflow automation. The partnership marks Fynd's first major retail customer acquisition in the UK since entering the market.
The platform will connect different business systems and automate workflows involving orders, customers, dispatches, returns, products and inventory. The integration is expected to improve operational visibility, reduce delays and enable faster customer service. Fynd, backed by Reliance Retail Ventures, serves around 20,000 stores and more than 2,600 brands and retailers globally.
INERA unveils new agricultural biosolutions for farmers
INERA, the agricultural biotechnology arm of Absolute, has unveiled a new range of crop solutions under its NAVODAYA 2026 launch programme. The portfolio includes BioMorphX, a patented enzyme-driven biostimulant designed to strengthen root development, Leiro Biostamin, a plant-based protein hydrolysate that helps crops withstand environmental stress, and XOVIO Milvaura, a biological fungicide targeting powdery and downy mildew.
The launches come amid challenging agricultural conditions, with India's southwest monsoon recording a 13% deficit. INERA currently reaches over two million farmers through 10,000 channel partners across 17 states.
Biz2X partners SIDBI to strengthen digital lending operations
Digital lending platform Biz2X has partnered with the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) to strengthen its lending operations through technology. Under the agreement, Biz2X will provide its lending CRM platform to streamline lead management, improve operational efficiency and enhance credit delivery to MSMEs.
The platform will integrate leads generated through WhatsApp, direct selling agents, OEM partners and marketing campaigns into a unified system. It will also provide AI-powered BizBot insights, management dashboards and mobile application capabilities for field teams.
Devnagri AI launches multilingual speech recognition solution
Enterprise language infrastructure company Devnagri AI has launched Blackbird, an automatic speech recognition solution designed to convert spoken conversations into text across Indian languages. The platform targets enterprise applications such as contact centres and AI-powered voice agents, with capabilities to handle regional accents, pronunciation variations and everyday speech patterns.
According to the company, Blackbird recorded word error rates of 10.8%-12.4% for Hindi, 10.1% for Punjabi and 11.8% for Bengali in tests using publicly available datasets. Its speech recognition latency is below 50 milliseconds, supporting real-time applications.

articles.title: 9 startups picked for 1st Africa Ignite climate adaptation cohort
articles.text:
The United Nations Industrial Development Organisation (UNIDO) and BFA Global have selected nine climate adaptation startups from eight African countries for the first cohort of the Africa Ignite programme.
Funded by the Adaptation Fund Climate Innovation Accelerator (AFCIA) and run under the Adaptation SME Innovation Facility (ASIF), Ignite targets early-stage startups that have built a working prototype but are yet to validate it with users. The nine were chosen from 453 applications.
Over eight weeks, founders will test their solutions with farmers, cooperatives and agribusinesses. Weekly live sessions, specialist office hours, AI training and real-world user testing will help them gather evidence of demand and impact, sharpen their business models, and prepare to land customers and raise investment.
“Every founder in this cohort has a working prototype. The next step is often the hardest: putting it in front of a cassava farmer, a coffee cooperative or a poultry producer and learning what they will use and pay for,” said Rasima Swarup, ASIF lead at BFA Global.
The cohort includes Benin’s ALLO VETO, which helps poultry farmers formulate affordable feed from local ingredients when drought disrupts supply; Angolan biodigester maker EcoBioGás; and Tanzania’s GeoVLUP Adaptation Services, which turns farm and climate data into practical guidance for coffee farmers.
Also selected are Ugandan circular savings platform Ghala Circular Solutions; Zimbabwe’s Global Vision Impact, which captures and stores runoff water for households during dry spells; and Kenyan agritech Kilimora, whose AgriKonnekt platform delivers localised climate intelligence to cooperatives.
Rounding out the cohort are Zambia’s LinkBridge, which builds shared solar-powered irrigation for clusters of smallholder farmers; Malawian food traceability startup MTENGO wa Mizu; and Kenya’s North Coast Innovators, which cuts post-harvest losses for cassava farmers through solar drying and milling.
More than half of the startups are founded or co-founded by women, and seven of the nine have a woman in a leadership position.
The programme kicked off on November 11, pauses in December and resumes in January, with the startups set to present their results at a Founder Showcase and Feedback Forum in late February 2027.

articles.title: « La plus grande collection d’identifiants que j’ai découverte » : 2 milliards de mots de passe Gmail, Facebook et Netflix ont été exposés sur Internet
articles.text:
Jeremiah Fowler, un chercheur en cybersécurité réputé, vient de mettre la main sur une base de données exposée sur Internet. Celle-ci n’était « ni protégée par un mot de passe, ni chiffrée ». Autrement dit, n’importe qui pouvait la consulter sans avoir besoin d’un mot de passe ou d’un identifiant. Dans ce répertoire, il a découvert environ 2 milliards d’identifiants, à savoir des adresses e-mail, des noms d’utilisateur et des mots de passe.
 I discovered 2 Billion Usernames, Logins, and Passwords exposed in a suspected data breach of a criminal marketplace. Millions of individuals, businesses, organizations, and government account credentials exposed. Read my full report here: https://t.co/9uf3S4w6ns https://t.co/VAEI3yx6IE
— Jeremiah Fowler Security Researcher (@yoda69) November 24, 2026
« Par son volume et son ampleur, c’est la plus grande collection d’identifiants que j’ai découverte en toutes mes années de chercheur en sécurité », souligne le chercheur dans son rapport, publié par ExpressVPN ce 24 novembre 2026.
C’est plus de 13 fois la base de 149 millions de mots de passe, dénichée en janvier par le même expert. Jeremiah Fowler n’en est en effet pas à son coup d’essai. En 2025, le chercheur avait déjà mis au jour 2,7 milliards de mots de passe Wi-Fi et d’adresses IP. Quelques mois plus tard, il avait aussi repéré 184 millions de mots de passe piratés.
Gmail, Netflix, Facebook… Quels services sont touchés ?
Presque tous les services en ligne sont répertoriés dans la base de données. Le chercheur a comptabilisé environ 608 millions d’identifiants Gmail, 114 millions liés à d’autres services Google, 88 millions d’identifiants Facebook, 41,7 millions liés à des comptes Roblox, 36,6 millions pour Amazon, 32,9 millions pour X et 31 millions pour Instagram.
Près de 20 millions d’identifiants Netflix, plus de 15 millions d’identifiants PayPal et près de deux millions d’identifiants Binance ont aussi été recensés. Enfin, plus de 61 millions d’identifiants sont associés à des adresses gouvernementales en .gov. Notez que des internautes français sont concernés. En effet, certains dossiers sont classés par pays, avec des abréviations comme US, UK, DE ou encore FR.
Le chercheur précise bien que les chiffres avancés par ses soins ne sont que des estimations. En effet, un même compte peut apparaître plusieurs fois, ce qui tend à gonfler le nombre de victimes potentielles. Par ailleurs, le répertoire contient sans doute des mots de passe périmés.
« La présence d’environ 2 milliards d’enregistrements d’identifiants ne doit pas être interprétée comme représentant 2 milliards de victimes individuelles », précise le chercheur à la suite de ses investigations.
Bien plus que des mots de passe
La base de données ne contient pas que des identifiants et des mots de passe. Le chercheur a aussi découvert des cookies et des jetons de session, des petits fichiers qui permettent de rester connecté à un site sans devoir retaper son mot de passe à chaque fois. Ces fichiers sont déposés par un site sur votre navigateur. Un pirate qui le récupère peut s’en servir pour se connecter à votre place, sans connaître votre mot de passe et sans passer par la double authentification. Entre de mauvaises mains, ils peuvent offrir aux pirates « plus de moyens d’entrer qu’un simple mot de passe », rappelle le chercheur.
Dans 400 000 documents, l’expert a repéré des listes d’applications installées, des mots de passe enregistrés, le contenu du presse-papiers ou encore des informations techniques sur l’ordinateur de la victime. Ces données permettent de dresser un « profil détaillé de chaque victime ». Le chercheur a aussi trouvé des milliers de comptes associés à des sites du dark web. Dans les documents, il a en effet déniché des milliers d’adresses en « .onion », accompagnées de noms d’utilisateur et de mots de passe.
« C’est la première fois que je vois un grand nombre de comptes du dark web dans des identifiants piratés », s’étonne Jeremiah Fowler.
À lire aussi : Cyberattaques en cours dans le « monde entier » – le FBI alerte sur une vague d’intrusions menées par ARTEX, une redoutable IA
Des virus voleurs de données
Selon Jeremiah Fowler, ces identifiants ont vraisemblablement été dérobés par des « infostealers », des logiciels malveillants spécialisés dans le vol de données. Une fois installés sur un appareil, ils aspirent tout ce qui est enregistré dans le navigateur et les applications installées, ou enregistrent ce que vous tapez sur le clavier. C’est pourquoi on trouve énormément de données différentes dans le répertoire. Selon les estimations les plus récentes de Flashpoint, les infostealers infectent chaque année plus de 10 millions d’appareils.
Pour le moment, on ignore qui est à l’origine de la base de données. Celle-ci pourrait bien appartenir à une plateforme criminelle qui revend des identifiants volés, ou à un revendeur, théorise Jeremiah Fowler. Le chercheur a alerté l’hébergeur de la base, qui a coupé l’accès quelques jours plus tard par mesure de sécurité.
Si votre appareil est infecté par un infostealer, le fait de changer vos mots de passe ne suffira pas à vous protéger. Si « le logiciel malveillant reste actif », il pourra revenir à la charge et s’emparer de vos nouveaux mots de passe, prévient le chercheur. Il vaut mieux analyser votre appareil avec un antivirus pour tenter de débusquer un éventuel virus. Ce n’est qu’une fois que vous êtes certain que votre PC n’a pas été infecté que vous pouvez créer un nouveau mot de passe. Dans la foulée, prenez la peine d’activer la double authentification, de préférence avec une application dédiée ou une clé de sécurité.
