articles.title: La tecnología más original que hemos probado en 2026 no es un móvil. Es un carrito de bebé
articles.text:
En la gala de los Premios Xataka Verisure 2026 hubo trofeo para el iPhone 18 Pro Max, el Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra o un televisor de LG de nueve milímetros. Y en una de las categorías que estrenábamos, la de lo más original que hemos probado, ha ganado un carrito de bebé: el Cybex e-Gazelle S. Lo he usado desde que nació mi hija.
CYBEX Cochecito dorado e-GAZELLE S, máx. 22 kg (modo individual) / 2x 22 kg (modo dúo), sistema todo en 1 con accionamiento eléctrico y 20+ configuraciones, Stormy Blue
Casi todos los ganadores son una versión mejorada de algo que ya existía. El e-Gazelle S no lleva nada especialmente sofisticado: un motor en las ruedas traseras, una batería extraíble y dos botones en el manillar.
La electrónica más simple del mundo mundial. Lo que sorprende es meter eso en un objeto que lleva tanto tiempo siendo analógico y sin grandes cambios. Cybex lo anunció en 2024 por 1.099,95 euros. Dos años después ya se lo podemos juzgar por el uso, no por la promesa.
Hace dos cosas:
- Ayuda en las cuestas, empujando al subir y frenando al bajar.
- Y se mece solo: bloqueas las ruedas, pulsas un botón y va adelante y atrás, con tres intensidades.
De las cuestas puedo decir poco, porque en Valencia tenemos pocas. El escaso desnivel por el que he ido ha demostrado algo, pero ya digo: no vivo en Santander ni en Vigo, sino en el casco urbano de Torrent.
A la mecedora sí he podido sacarle más partido. Las primeras semanas mi hija prefería los brazos. Una tarde, en una terraza, lloraba sin motivo aparente; probé el mecido sin mucha fe y se calmó durante un buen rato. La batería aguanta más de una hora meciendo.
Protege tu hogar frente a robos y ocupaciones con las cerraduras inteligentes de Verisure, disponibles como parte del sistema de alarma Verisure. Al margen de permitir abrir la puerta usando las llaves o desde el móvil, alertan ante cualquier intento de manipulación y transmiten la información a la unidad central de la compañía para generar un salto de alarma. Descubre la solución que mejor se ajusta a las necesidades de tu vivienda o negocio.
También tiene pegas, claro. Es un carro que prioriza la estabilidad, la capacidad de carga y la comodidad, así que las ruedas traseras sobresalen del chasis y en ascensores y pasillos acabas golpeando algo y teniendo que mirar por dónde irá la rueda, que no es lo mismo que por dónde irá el chasis del carrito.
Un carrito que "hace de niñera" es la crítica fácil, y la primera que me hice yo. Pero lo que importa es cuánto se usa. Nadie deja al bebé en la hamaca toda la tarde, y nadie se escandaliza por diez minutos con el bebé ahí para poder ducharse sin que ocurra una tragedia. Esto es igual: no sirve para desentenderse, sirve para el rato concreto en que hace falta.
El precio: solo con la silla, 1.100 euros; con capazo, 1.340. Mucho. Pero el Bugaboo Donkey 6, su rival más directo, ronda los 1.400 sin ninguna asistencia eléctrica. Para quien viva entre cuestas, creo que las cuentas salen.
Y creo que por eso ha ganado: es lo único de la lista que ha hecho que desconocidos me paren por la calle para preguntar qué es.

articles.title: Macarena Arnás, grafóloga, analiza la firma de Pedro Sánchez: "Es una persona con capacidad de resistencia, terquedad y mucho apego a la familia"
articles.text:
La firma de Pedro Sánchez ha acabado sobre la mesa de un programa de televisión en plena carrera hacia las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre de 2026. Ha sucedido en “La Comedia Nacional”, el programa de Héctor de Miguél en La Séptima, donde contactaron con la grafóloga Macarena Arnás para que explicara qué podría esconder la rúbrica del presidente del Gobierno, en la que dice ver desde capacidad de resistencia hasta terquedad. Es la misma que el candidato socialista deja, por ejemplo, en las cartas de propaganda electoral.
Una letra que se inclina. Arnás, que además de grafóloga es perito calígrafa y autora de un libro sobre firmas célebres, empezó destacando la inclinación de una de las letras hacia la izquierda, algo que, según ella, se puede ver a simple vista. Y es que en grafología, explicó, hay que tener en cuenta la izquierda y la derecha, y en este caso esa inclinación indicaría que Sánchez “puede tener muy buena memoria, capacidad de resistencia también por esos ángulos pronunciados y fortaleza tanto mental como física”.
Pero la misma inclinación tendría, siempre según la grafóloga, una segunda lectura, porque también apuntaría a alguien con “dificultad para olvidar el pasado y mucho apego a la familia”.
Todo en mayúsculas. La firma, según la describe el diario, se compone de una “P”, un punto y un “Sánchez”, todo en mayúsculas. Cuando le preguntaron si eso no le llamaba la atención, Arnás respondió que ese rasgo admite dos interpretaciones: “Una es que quiere dar claridad y legibilidad al escrito y otra podría ser que intenta mostrar a veces una imagen de mayor fortaleza de la que realmente posee”. En ese segundo caso, añadió, podría ser alguien que aparenta más fortaleza en la primera impresión, pero que luego tiene mayor sensibilidad, “porque hay algunas formas curvas también presentes en la firma”.
El subrayado y la P. También le preguntaron por la línea que subraya la firma y por una “P” que se parece más a una “D”. Sobre el subrayado, la grafóloga explicó que es muy habitual, ya que el apellido “está muy vinculado con la parte profesional, entonces puede indicar mayor necesidad de reconocimiento en la esfera profesional”. Y sobre esa “P” con poco “palito”, su lectura fue que “hay mayor ángulo que curva en ese caso”, lo que, en sus palabras, “sí podría indicar un exceso a veces de racionalidad y también de terquedad”.
Lo que dice la evidencia. Eso sí, todas estas interpretaciones son las de Arnás, y la grafología no ha conseguido demostrar que la letra sirva para medir la personalidad. La British Psychological Society (Sociedad Británica de Psicología) la sitúa al mismo nivel que la astrología, el más bajo de su escala de validez, según explica Maldita Ciencia. De hecho, un metaanálisis publicado en 1989 en ‘Personality and Individual Differences’ sobre su uso en la selección de personal concluyó que, con textos de contenido neutro, la validez de los grafólogos era prácticamente nula, y que psicólogos sin formación en grafología los superaban en todas las medidas. Vamos, que la evidencia no respalda que una firma revele cómo es quien la estampa.
El análisis encaja en una campaña en la que, según plantea el propio diario, además del programa electoral cuentan muchos otros recursos centrados en la figura de cada candidato, desde un gesto en un debate hasta una publicación en redes sociales, y en la que hay quien se fija en detalles que a muchos les pasan desapercibidos, como la forma de firmar.

articles.title: Voitures électriques : l'Union européenne pourrait inclure le Royaume-Uni dans son futur label « Made in Europe
articles.text:
Plus de 282 000 Nissan Leaf sont sorties de l’usine de Sunderland, dans le nord-est de l’Angleterre, et la troisième génération y est assemblée avec une batterie produite juste en face, chez AESC. Difficile de faire plus européen pour une marque japonaise. Pourtant, sur le papier du règlement que prépare Bruxelles, cette Leaf pèse administrativement le même poids qu’un SUV importé de Shenzhen : le Brexit a tracé une frontière invisible entre Sunderland et les aides du continent, que les Vingt-Sept envisagent désormais d’effacer.
Selon des diplomates européens cités par Reuters, les États membres penchent en effet pour intégrer les voitures électriques britanniques au futur dispositif « Made in Europe ». L’Irlande, qui préside le Conseil de l’UE jusqu’à fin décembre, a présenté lundi un compromis élargissant la zone d’assemblage éligible de l’Union au Royaume-Uni, en passant par la Norvège, l’Islande, le Liechtenstein et la Suisse.
Ce cadre découle de l’Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA), un projet de règlement présenté par la Commission le 4 mars 2026. Il conditionne les achats publics et les aides d’État à un contenu local minimum : dans la copie initiale, au moins 70 % de la valeur des composants (hors batterie) doit provenir de l’Union, avec des exigences distinctes pour la batterie et la motorisation, servant de socle au bonus réservé aux voitures « Made in EU » en préparation.
Votre production solaire dépasse votre consommation ? Stockez le surplus au lieu de le revendre à bas prix. Le SolarFlow 2400 AC+ se branche sur votre installation existante, 100 % plug-and-play, et s’amortit plus vite grâce au Black Friday.
    Pour aller plus loin
Voiture électrique : l’Europe prépare un bonus réservé au « Made in EU »
            
Ce que la Nissan Leaf a à gagner
En France, la Leaf profite déjà de la prime CEE (l’ex-bonus écologique financé par les fournisseurs d’énergie), à hauteur d’au moins 3 181 euros selon Nissan. Elle passe toutefois à côté du complément réservé aux véhicules assemblés dans l’Espace économique européen avec une batterie européenne, dont le Royaume-Uni ne fait pas partie. Or l’IAA généraliserait cette logique aux aides nationales des Vingt-Sept : sans le compromis irlandais, la Leaf découverte lors de notre essai de la Nissan Leaf 3 perdrait un argument décisif face aux Volkswagen ID.3 et Renault Mégane E-Tech assemblées dans l’UE (à 35 300 euros en entrée de gamme, quelques milliers d’euros font toute la différence).
L’assemblage ne règle pourtant pas tout. Le bloc trois-en-un de la Leaf, qui réunit le moteur, l’onduleur (chargé de convertir le courant continu de la batterie pour alimenter le moteur) et le réducteur, est fabriqué au Japon, une pièce qui pèse dans le calcul du contenu local. Là encore, la présidence irlandaise envisagerait d’ouvrir le volet composants à des partenaires comme le Japon et la Corée du Sud, une bouffée d’air bienvenue pour le crossover électrique de Nissan.
    Pour aller plus loin
On a essayé la nouvelle Nissan Leaf : la pionnière des voitures électriques fait sa révolution, et c’est une bonne surprise
            
Un compromis qui n’est pas encore une loi
Le texte irlandais doit encore être validé par les gouvernements, qui visent une position commune début décembre avant d’entamer les négociations avec le Parlement européen au plus tôt en janvier. La clause de réciprocité reste notamment à boucler : Londres ne serait intégré au dispositif qu’à condition d’ouvrir à son tour ses aides et ses marchés publics aux produits européens.
Selon le Financial Times, le Royaume-Uni n’aurait en revanche plus à aligner ses droits de douane sur les voitures électriques chinoises, un point qui bloquait côté britannique. Une autre échéance menace toutefois l’usine de Sunderland : sans nouvel accord, les règles d’origine du traité post-Brexit se durcissent dès le 1er janvier 2027, imposant 55 % de valeur européenne ou britannique par voiture sous peine de 10 % de droits de douane.
Acheter une Leaf maintenant ou attendre ?
Si la Nissan Leaf vous intéresse, inutile de repousser votre achat en attendant une nouvelle prime venue de Bruxelles. L’IAA ne crée pas de chèque européen : il encadre simplement les futures aides nationales, et son entrée en vigueur n’est pas attendue avant 2027.
En attendant, la prime CEE s’applique déjà selon les règles actuelles (il suffit de vérifier la liste des modèles éligibles sur le site de l’Ademe avant de signer). Le véritable suspense portera ensuite sur la manière dont la France ajustera sa propre aide une fois le critère « Made in Europe » européen définitivement adopté.

articles.title: Verschwörungstheorien widerlegen: Warum das der KI-Chatbot DebunkBot besser kann als du
articles.text:
Entlarvt in 8 Minuten: KI-Chatbot überzeugt im Gespräch mit Verschwörungstheoretikern
Es ist mittlerweile eine weit verbreitete Auffassung, dass Fakten allein Meinungen nicht ändern. Nirgendwo wird dies deutlicher als bei Verschwörungstheorien: Viele Menschen sind überzeugt, dass man Verschwörungstheoretiker:innen durch Gespräche nicht von ihren Überzeugungen abbringen kann. Das ist jedoch nur bedingt wahr. articles.title: How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
articles.text:
How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
Rising electricity demand is locking in fossil-fuel generation.
In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote a feature story describing how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I’ve lost count of how many times he’s already been proved right.
Sure, it’s technically possible to meet the world’s rising electricity demand with other power sources, including renewables like wind and solar supported by batteries. But the reality in the US so far is that the data center boom is helping to fuel a massive natural-gas resurgence.
Just one example: Plans for the Meta data center in Louisiana that David focused on in his story have expanded, and its power needs have too. The local utility went from three planned natural-gas plants to 10. And as I wrote in a new story this week, data center developers are now looking beyond the grid and planning to build their own off-grid gas power plants. How did we get here?
If you want to understand the future of the grid, one way to do it is by looking at interconnection queues—lists of power plants that have requested a connection to the system. In recent years these queues have been dominated by renewables like wind and solar power, which are generally the cheapest way to build new energy capacity today.
But there’s been a shift in some places, particularly for PJM, the country’s largest power grid operator, which covers parts of 13 states in an area stretching from Illinois to Washington, DC. PJM has seen a major uptick in natural-gas proposals. In August, the operator announced that it had accepted proposals for 715 total projects with a capacity of over 200 gigawatts to join its queue. Nearly half that total capacity represented natural-gas plants.
If all the projects in the queue were built, it would increase the fossil-fuel share on PJM’s grid from 61% to 67%, according to an analysis by Kevin Kircher, an energy modeler and assistant professor of mechanical engineering at Purdue.
PJM’s queue is reflective of a bigger trend across the US. Natural gas is already the single biggest source of electricity in the country, and it has basically become the default to meet exploding power demand.
This AI-driven rush is already affecting greenhouse-gas emissions for tech companies. Meta’s emissions are up 45% over last year’s, according to the company’s recently released 2026 Sustainability Report. That’s even higher than the jumps from fellow hyperscalers Google (18%), Amazon (16%), and Microsoft (25%). The company is also “reevaluating” its 2030 goal to reach net-zero emissions, according to the report, though there aren’t details about how or when it might reach a decision there.
And there’s another tidbit in that Meta report worth noting: The company said that when the grid can’t deliver power “on the necessary timeline,” it will look to other methods, including building its own on-site power generation.
This fits into a related and growing trend that I’ve been tracking recently: Data center developers are looking to bypass long wait times to hook up to the grid by building their own power plants instead.
It’s not new for large industrial facilities to supply their own power. Chemical plants often have natural-gas infrastructure on-site to generate electricity and heat, for example (though they’re generally connected to the grid as well). Mining operations are often remote, requiring an off-grid power source.
But the desire to come online quickly means there could be a massive boom in off-grid power plants for data centers. Over 100 such facilities have been proposed in the US, with a total capacity of 115 gigawatts (that’s more than double the entire peak power demand of California). The vast majority of these sites have been proposed since the beginning of 2025.
There are alternative ways to help meet growing electricity demand: Wind and solar are inexpensive options, and pairing them with batteries could improve their reliability, for example. I’ve also written before about demand flexibility—efforts to limit power drawn from the grid when demand is high.
Right now, though, the evidence continues to stack up that the AI boom in the US is basically synonymous with a natural-gas boom.

articles.title: Palo Alto Networks warns of Fragnesia flaw exploited in PAN-OS attacks
articles.text:
Threat actors are chaining exploits for the PHP2Shell and Fragnesia vulnerabilities to target Palo Alto Networks devices with management interfaces exposed to the internet.
PHP2Shell is the name for two critical PHP vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which allow unauthenticated attackers to run code remotely with the privileges of the PHP web worker.
The Fragnesia vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-46300, is a Linux kernel vulnerability in the XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem that lets a local attacker with low-privileges to escalate permissions to root level.
An alert from CISA on October 28 warned that both security issues were being chained in attacks to deploy PHP webshells on vulnerable systems and execute commands as root.
Around the same time, Dream Security researchers reported observing a campaign using the same chain, targeting servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, including a U.S. government affiliate.
Palo Alto Networks has confirmed in an advisory today that such attacks also target firewalls running PAN-OS.
“Exploitation of CVE-2026-46300 has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet,” reads the security bulletin.
The networking company says that all exploitation activity it observed involved PAN-OS devices that exposed their management interface to the public internet, which goes against its recommended ‘best practices.’
Palo Alto Networks did not provide any technical details about the chaining of the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, but noted that this is the only known way to exploit Fragnesia, and they are not aware of another exploitation pathway for the flaw.
The company has released fixes for Fragnesia for PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 12.2, with the exact patch-carrying build varying by release.
Given that the two flaws are exploited together, administrators who applied updates that addressed the PHP2Shell flaw should be safe from these attacks.
In addition to applying the security updates, Palo Alto Networks also recommends that those who need to keep a remote management interface available restrict access to trusted internal IP addresses.

articles.title: Wave’s 25 million-user blueprint: How low fees disrupted Francophone West Africa’s mobile money ‘cartels’
articles.text:
As mobile money platform Wave crosses the 25 million active account mark, its Public Policy Lead, Awa Gueye, tells GODFREY GEORGE how the company forced down prices across the WAEMU region—and details the structural and regulatory hurdles that still prevent millions of informal businesses and women from participating fully in the digital economy.
A decade ago, digital payments in Francophone West Africa were still at an early stage, with adoption and the services available gradually expanding. Wave Mobile Money accelerated this development when it launched in the region by introducing a radically lower, flat-fee pricing structure.
The resulting price war forced established telecom-backed operators to slash their own commissions, fundamentally altering the digital payments landscape across the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). MTN MoMo eliminated withdrawal fees in Côte d’Ivoire in 2025, and Orange cut transfer fees to zero ahead of Wave’s launch in Cameroon.
For Awa Gueye, Wave’s Public Policy Lead, the true disruption is not merely in the pricing, but in the shift in consumer psychology.
“The biggest change is in what people expect,” Gueye says. “When someone sends small amounts several times a week, fees decide whether digital payments are part of daily life or reserved for emergencies. Once customers experience a low-cost, simple and reliable service, they expect that standard everywhere.”
That shift in expectation is borne out by the numbers. Wave now boasts 25 million active accounts, a figure Gueye uses to illustrate how rapidly unbanked populations will adopt digital financial services when the friction of cost and complexity is removed. This consumer demand has compelled the broader WAEMU market to pivot toward lower prices and improved product offerings.
For policymakers, however, the challenge is ensuring this new, competitive equilibrium is maintained. According to Gueye, regulatory frameworks must proactively protect the conditions that enabled this disruption, fostering a market where “providers compete on the value they deliver, and where the customer is the one who benefits.”
The Illusion of account ownership
While rising mobile money registration figures are frequently celebrated by governments and development agencies, Gueye cautions that mere account ownership is a flawed metric for evaluating financial inclusion.
“Opening an account is only the first step,” Gueye notes. “Inclusion is real when someone can use that account to receive income, pay a supplier, save a little, or deal with an unexpected expense, and when they trust it enough to do so every week.”
Genuine inclusion requires digital wallets to serve as gateways to savings, credit, and insurance—the financial instruments necessary for households and small enterprises to plan for the future and absorb economic shocks. However, several structural barriers continue to block this transition from basic access to active usage.
Cost remains a primary deterrent; for users making frequent, low-value transactions, even modest percentage-based fees rapidly erode capital, driving them back to the informal cash economy. Furthermore, stringent Know-Your-Customer (KYC) requirements disproportionately exclude rural populations and women, who frequently lack formal identification documents.
To overcome these hurdles, Gueye advocates for a shift in how regulators measure success, urging them to track user activity and economic outcomes rather than raw account numbers.
She also calls for the widespread adoption of tiered, risk-based KYC protocols that allow low-value accounts to be opened with simplified documentation. Governments, she suggests, could accelerate adoption by digitising the payment of civil service salaries, social welfare transfers, and supplier invoices.
Crucially, Gueye points to the potential of leveraging digital transaction histories to build alternative credit profiles, allowing individuals and small businesses without formal financial records to finally access responsible credit and insurance products.
Navigating the WAEMU regulatory labyrinth
Operating across multiple jurisdictions in Francophone West Africa presents a complex regulatory puzzle. While the WAEMU region benefits from a shared central bank (the BCEAO) and a unified framework for electronic money, friction arises when national regulations intersect with this regional base.
Rules governing taxation, telecommunications, data protection, and consumer rights often diverge from one country to the next. For a pan-African provider like Wave, a single product can be subjected to disparate compliance requirements across different borders, slowing the rollout of beneficial services.
Despite these bottlenecks, Gueye believes a balance between rapid innovation, consumer protection, and systemic stability is achievable, provided regulators engage in early, structured dialogue with industry players. She points to the BCEAO’s financial inclusion lab as a successful model, allowing regulators and providers to collaboratively test new concepts under controlled supervision.
Gueye argues that regulations should remain technology-neutral and risk-based, with clear implementation timelines and extensive industry consultation. “Regional coordination should keep a service built for one market usable in the next,” she says. “For any innovation, the same questions apply: who is accountable, how are customers protected, and what happens when something goes wrong?”
A cautious case for stablecoins
At recent industry gatherings, such as the Africa Financial Industry Summit (AFIS) and Moonshot by TechCabal, stablecoins have dominated discussions, particularly regarding their potential to streamline cross-border payments. While mobile money has successfully digitised domestic transfers, moving capital across African borders—especially between different currency zones—remains slow, expensive, and reliant on cumbersome correspondent banking networks.
Gueye acknowledges that stablecoins warrant serious attention, identifying cross-border settlement as their most credible use case.
“That gap is where stablecoins could help, for example in supporting SMEs to pay for their suppliers across borders or in faster settlement between regulated institutions to ensure business continuity for the end user,” she explains.
However, Wave’s approach remains pragmatic and compliance-driven. Gueye stresses that any integration of stablecoins would strictly require a clear regulatory framework and the explicit approval of relevant authorities in each operating market.
Designing for women’s economic agency
Perhaps the most persistent failure of Africa’s digital financial revolution is the continued marginalisation of women, both as consumers and as industry leaders.
For a digital financial product to truly serve a woman, Gueye argues, several prerequisites must be met: she must possess her own mobile device, hold her own identification, and retain sole control over her account. Beyond affordability, female users require stringent privacy protections, physical safety, and customer support accessible in their preferred language.
To close the gender gap, Gueye proposes targeted policy interventions. Chief among them is the implementation of simpler, tiered KYC requirements to address the identification deficit that disproportionately affects women.
She also urges regulators and providers to disaggregate their data by gender, providing a clearer picture of actual usage patterns rather than aggregate account ownership.
The digitisation of wages, social transfers, and market fees would also ensure capital is deposited directly into accounts controlled by women. Furthermore, the industry must design products tailored to the realities of female-led enterprises, offering affordable merchant payment solutions, savings tools, and digital transaction records capable of unlocking credit access. Increasing the number of female agents and frontline staff, who often establish trust more effectively with female customers, is also crucial.
Within the industry itself, female representation remains a priority for Wave, where women comprise 51% of the workforce.
“We believe diverse teams build better products for a wider range of customers,” Gueye says. “Women should help design products and shape the rules that govern them, as regulators, policy leads, engineers and founders. That means mentoring and sponsorship, transparent promotion paths, and making sure women have a seat at the table in consultations and industry forums.”
Ultimately, Gueye concludes, the success of these platforms should be judged by a single metric: economic agency—the tangible ability of users to receive income, make autonomous financial decisions, and grow their businesses.

articles.title: The Witcher 4 Should Improve on Witcher 3 as Much as GTA 6 Did on GTA 5, Says CDPR
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
The Witcher 4 Should Improve on Witcher 3 as Much as GTA 6 Did on GTA 5, Says CDPR
CD Projekt RED is not exactly shy when it comes to hyping up The Witcher 4. As much as critics and audiences alike loved The Witcher 3, its successor is already setting some pretty high expectations for itself. According to CDPR's Joint CEO Michał Nowakowski, the company expects The Witcher 4 to be as big a step up from The Witcher 3 as GTA 6 is from GTA 5. Nowakowski made the comments during the company's Q3 earnings call, after Erste analyst Krzysztof Tkocz asked whether a leap like the one Rockstar just delivered is possible for CDPR's next Witcher game. Nowakowski said the studio has indeed looked at "the game" and saw the differences, but he wasn't going to do a full GTA 5 versus GTA 6 breakdown. Here's what he did say, however:
Michał Nowakowski, Joint CEO CD Projekt RedDo we believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4? I think so, yes. I mean, it's been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game so yes, you can expect us to make a much bigger jump between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4.
That comparison is a huge one, and it might be extremely optimistic for CDPR to compare The Witcher 4 to GTA 6, given the reception Rockstar's game has already gotten. Nowakowski said during the call that GTA 6's release hasn't changed how CDPR approaches development, also noting that their games are ambition-driven rather than budget-driven. Still, given the records GTA 6 has already broken and what its trajectory looks like, CDPR seems to have set an extremely high bar for itself. The Witcher 4 is currently targeting a 2028 release window, so we will have to wait and see if CDPR can deliver on that promise.
Sources:
				CD Projekt Red Q3 Earnings, 				via GamesRadar+

articles.title: BepiColombo has finally reached Mercury after an eight-year trip
articles.text:
The big picture: BepiColombo has entered orbit around Mercury after an eight-year flight that used solar-powered electric engines and repeated planetary flybys to slow the spacecraft down. The European Space Agency said BepiColombo entered Mercury's orbit with both probes still attached. The probes will separate and take up different orbits, putting one close to the surface and sending the other much farther out to measure how Mercury's magnetic field interacts with the solar wind.
Getting to Mercury meant shedding speed, not just covering distance. After its launch in October 2018, BepiColombo had to move closer to the Sun without picking up so much speed that it overshot the planet. "Energetically, it takes more energy to go to Mercury than to go to the outer Solar System," Emma Bunce, a University of Leicester plasma physicist and one of the mission's lead scientists, told Nature.
To limit the amount of propellant it needed to carry, BepiColombo relied mainly on solar-powered electric propulsion rather than conventional thrusters. The electric propulsion system did not work entirely as planned, delaying the mission by 11 months.
The spacecraft also used gravity assists from Earth, the Moon, Venus, and Mercury over nine circuits around the Sun. Mercury itself helped slow the spacecraft before it entered orbit: BepiColombo flew past the planet six times, capturing its first close-up images of Mercury during the initial flyby in 2021.
BepiColombo is only the second mission to orbit Mercury, after NASA's MESSENGER, which circled the planet from 2011 to 2015. This time, the two probes will stay together until early December, when they are scheduled to reach the orbit assigned to Mio, the spacecraft built by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency.
Mio will follow an ellipse that takes it from 500 kilometers (311 miles) above the surface to 11,000 kilometers (6,835 miles) out, letting it sample the magnetic field and its interaction with the solar wind across a wide range of altitudes.
ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter will then gradually descend, with its final orbit scheduled for March 2027. It will fly between 400 and 1,500 kilometers (248 and 932 miles) above the planet, keeping it close enough for its instruments to continuously study the surface. Among those instruments is the Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer, or MIXS, which Bunce says is the first X-ray imaging device sent on an interplanetary mission.
The team did not have to wait until the spacecraft entered Mercury's orbit to test MIXS. During the cruise, mission scientists pointed it at the Crab Nebula, the remnant of a supernova observed from Earth in 1054. The instrument's next assignment is much closer: imaging Mercury's surface in X-rays while Mio makes its own set of measurements thousands of kilometers farther out during each orbit.

articles.title: China acusa EUA de perseguir empresas do país após condenação da Huawei
articles.text:
A China acusou os Estados Unidos de impor obstáculos às empresas chinesas após um júri de Nova York considerar a Huawei culpada de roubo de segredos industriais e de crimes relacionados às atividades da companhia no Irã. Pequim criticou a decisão e afirmou que apoiará a fabricante na defesa de seus direitos e interesses.
O grupo de telecomunicações foi considerado culpado na terça-feira (24) de roubar segredos comerciais, cometer fraude bancária e ajudar o governo iraniano a monitorar e censurar o acesso de usuários à internet. A empresa também foi acusada de mentir às autoridades estadunidenses sobre suas atividades no país do Oriente Médio.
Apesar das condenações, a Huawei foi absolvida da acusação considerada mais grave no processo: associação ilícita para obter propriedade intelectual.
A decisão provocou reação do governo chinês nesta quarta-feira (25). Durante entrevista coletiva, Guo Jiakun, porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores da China, afirmou que Pequim se opõe veementemente às restrições impostas por Washington.
“O governo chinês se opõe de modo veemente aos obstáculos e limitações impostos pelos Estados Unidos às empresas chinesas e apoia firmemente estas companhias na defesa de seus direitos e interesses legítimos”, declarou.
A Huawei também contestou o resultado do julgamento. Em comunicado, a companhia afirmou que as acusações não têm fundamento jurídico nem factual e que vai analisar as decisões para adotar as medidas legais necessárias.

EUA acusam Huawei de roubar segredos industriais por 20 anos
- A Promotoria do Brooklyn, responsável pelo processo, acusou a Huawei e três de suas subsidiárias de conduzir negócios nos Estados Unidos com base em mentiras e roubos. Segundo os promotores, as subsidiárias da fabricante teriam obtido segredos industriais de empresas americanas de telecomunicações entre 2000 e 2020;
- A acusação afirma que a Huawei tentou recrutar funcionários dessas companhias para conseguir informações confidenciais sobre o setor de tecnologia. Com os dados, a empresa teria desenvolvido produtos semelhantes aos dos concorrentes e os comercializado por preços menores;
- Os promotores também apontaram a existência de programa interno de recompensas criado em 2013. A iniciativa oferecia bônus a funcionários que conseguissem acesso a segredos industriais de empresas concorrentes;
- O Departamento de Justiça dos Estados Unidos também declarou que a Huawei ajudou o regime iraniano a monitorar e censurar o acesso de usuários à internet. A fabricante ainda teria mentido sobre suas atividades no país;
- Em comunicado, o procurador-geral adjunto dos Estados Unidos, A. Tysen Duva, afirmou que o veredicto envia uma mensagem de que Washington defenderá suas empresas, trabalhadores e segurança nacional diante de companhias estrangeiras que recorram a práticas ilegais para obter vantagens.
Huawei já era alvo de desconfiança no Ocidente
A fabricante chinesa está há vários anos sob escrutínio em diferentes países ocidentais, que a acusam de espionagem em favor de Pequim. As suspeitas contribuíram para tensões entre governos ocidentais e a empresa, que contesta as acusações.
A pena da Huawei no processo estadunidense deverá ser definida em setembro de 2027.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages in group and individual chats
articles.text:
WhatsApp on Wednesday started rolling out a much-sought-after feature: the ability to schedule messages in both individual and group chats.
The feature is rolling out globally to all users across iOS and Android. Once it becomes available, you can type a message and long-press the send button to schedule it. You can choose to send a message anywhere between 10 minutes and 14 days later.
Users will be able to see all their scheduled messages and delete them if needed. It’s not clear if there is a way to edit the schedule of a message.
Notably, scheduled messages will be sent even if your phone is off or outside network coverage. You can schedule messages containing text, photos, and videos.
The feature could prove useful for wishing someone a happy birthday on time or chatting with people across time zones. Businesses may also find it easier to schedule texts and updates to their customers, and people who use the app to coordinate work will likely find themselves using scheduled texts to update their teams.
WhatsApp rivals like Telegram and Signal have had the ability to schedule messages for a while now, so the Meta-owned chat app is late in rolling it out.

articles.title: Diversity is increasing within BDC portfolio companies but remains stubbornly low among leadership
articles.text:
A majority of companies backed by the Business Development Bank of Canada’s venture capital arm are practising diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI), but those efforts aren’t translating into leadership positions.
The news: BDC Capital released its fifth annual report on DEI and environmental, social, and governance practices on Tuesday. On the DEI side, the report looks at how BDC portfolio companies and supported venture capital general partners (GPs) are engaging with and implementing DEI policies.
From the source: Between 2021 and 2025, BDC surveyed 82 GPs, including 70 BDC-backed GPs and 12 internal teams, and surveyed a sample of its 1,399 eligible portfolio companies. Notably, participation from GPs was spotty, with a non-response rate of 30 percent. Reporting shows more than half of participating GPs have a DEI strategy, and 63 percent have introduced efforts to reduce bias in hiring. 
The context: Among the VC ecosystem, the overall impact of adopting DEI policies and practices is viewed favourably, with 38 percent of respondents saying its impact was positive or very positive; just 1 percent said it had negative impacts. Respondents also cited improved decision-making and innovation (26 percent) and stakeholder expectations (17 percent) as their primary reasons for implementing DEI practices. Both of those metrics were overshadowed, however, by larger percentages of non-responses (30 and 33 percent, respectively).
Among portfolio companies, talent attraction was the highest motivator for DEI adoption (42 percent). A majority of portfolio companies reported that adopting DEI practices had a neutral impact (51 percent), while just 15 percent said it was very positive. Despite a majority of GPs and companies practicing DEI, as employees move up the rungs of leadership, that representation narrows. While 95 percent of portfolio companies report having women and visible minorities on staff, only 24 percent of companies reported women making up half or more of their management team, and 43 percent reported that visible minorities make up 25 percent or more.
Final thought: For GPs in particular, rates of inclusion have risen among all groups by between two and nine percent, except for Indigenous representation, which shrank by two percent. April Hicke, the founder of equity-based recruitment platform Toast, said those increases were akin to standing still and condemned low levels of representation in leadership, telling BetaKit, “ignoring half the talent pool is a business problem.”
“Women work at 95 percent of Canada’s VC-backed companies, but a quarter of those companies still have zero women in management, so this isn’t a pipeline problem. Obviously, something is still stopping women from moving up,” she said.
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.
Feature image courtesy BDC.

articles.title: Take-Two se lanza contra los ports pirata de ‘GTA 6’ para PC
articles.text:
GTA 6 está batiendo récords a diestra y siniestra, pero Take-Two Interactive no se está dejando encandilar por las luces de su lanzamiento. La casa matriz de Rockstar Games está decidida a frenar cualquier intento no autorizado de llevar el nuevo juego a PC, y ha sacado a relucir todo su músculo legal para conseguirlo.
Según recoge IGN, Take-Two Interactive envió un reclamo por violación de sus derechos de autor a GitHub que llevó a la eliminación de una red conformada por más de 3.000 repositorios. El principal apuntado es Leonida, un proyecto que apuntaba a recompilar la versión de Xbox de GTA 6 para que se pueda ejecutar de forma nativa en PC.
La iniciativa original de ItsNotRexed se basaba en el ejecutable de GTA 6 para Xbox que filtró Cyberleek la semana pasada. El repositorio original había capturado la atención de una gran cantidad de entusiastas, llevando a la creación de más de 2.900 forks hasta el momento en que T2 decidió tomar cartas en el asunto.
Así lo indica la reclamación que presentó la compañía que lidera Strauss Zelnick:
"Somos el equipo de protección de la propiedad intelectual de Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., empresa matriz de Rockstar Games. Nos ponemos en contacto con ustedes para solicitar la retirada del repositorio de GitHub de ItsNotRexed, así como de los más de 2900 forks asociados al mismo, ya que infringen los derechos de autor de las obras de Take-Two y facilitan la infracción de los derechos de autor sobre el título de Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI.
Nuestra obra protegida por derechos de autor es GRAND THEFT AUTO VI, una obra audiovisual exclusiva propiedad de Take-Two Interactive, que incluye (sin carácter limitativo) contenido audiovisual, material artístico, imágenes, diálogos y otros elementos creativos protegidos por derechos de autor.
El repositorio se describe como Leonida: una recompilación nativa para PC de la versión de Xbox de Grand Theft Auto 6. Dicho repositorio reproduce elementos protegidos por derechos de autor presentes en GRAND THEFT AUTO VI y constituye una obra derivada de GRAND THEFT AUTO VI.
Asimismo, el repositorio excede los términos de la licencia que Rockstar Games concede a los usuarios, lo que constituye una infracción de los derechos de autor".
Take-Two acaba con los intentos pirata de llevar GTA 6 a PC
El repositorio de Leonida que pertenecía a ItsNotRexed ya no se encuentra disponible en GitHub, y lo mismo sucede con todos proyectos derivados para llevar GTA 6 a PC. Desde Take-Two Interactive sostienen que, si bien la iniciativa en cuestión requería que cada usuario consiguiera "sus propios archivos" del juego, no era más que un argumento endeble para tratar de enmascarar su naturaleza pirata.
"El 20 de noviembre de 2026, se distribuyeron públicamente archivos de juego sustraídos de una versión de Grand Theft Auto VI para Xbox Series. Al día siguiente, se puso en marcha el repositorio Leonida, con el objetivo de ejecutar la versión de GTA VI para Xbox Series en un PC. El archivo README de dicho repositorio exige, como requisito previo, contar con los archivos del juego para Xbox Series; es decir, la misma plataforma a la que hacía referencia la filtración.
La indicación de 'aportar tus propios archivos' pretende trasladar al usuario la responsabilidad de suministrarlos, tratando de dar la impresión de que se trata de un proyecto de carácter general. Se trata de una maniobra deliberadamente engañosa: tanto el momento en que surge el proyecto como su enfoque explícito en Grand Theft Auto dejan claro que los 'archivos' que el usuario debe proporcionar son, en realidad, los archivos no autorizados de GTA VI (propiedad intelectual de Take-Two) que circulan públicamente, y que los desarrolladores del proyecto son plenamente conscientes de ello".
Sea como sea, quienes quieran jugar GTA 6 de forma legítima desde el PC no tendrán más opción que seguir esperando. Existen rumores de que Rockstar Games podría lanzar la versión par Windows en el primer trimestre de 2027, aunque todavía no hay novedades oficiales. Recordemos que hoy Grand Theft Auto VI está disponible en PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X|S y Xbox Cloud Gaming, aunque esta última opción está limitada a consolas.

articles.title: Why Y Combinator is backing fewer African startups
articles.text:
Four years after African founders made up roughly one in 17 companies in a Y Combinator batch, the continent has become a footnote at Demo Day. The reasons say as much about how YC has changed as about African tech.
In early-2022, Y Combinator’s Winter batch included 24 African startups, 18 of them from Nigeria. For the first time, an African country ranked third in a YC cohort, behind only the United States (US) and India. Lagos founders talked about the accelerator as a rite of passage, and the Paystack exit to Stripe made the path look repeatable.
Indeed, Disrupt Africa wrote articles around that time about the “cult of Y Combinator”, and the rave reviews the programme received from founders that participated in it.
That moment did not last. By Winter 2023 the African count had fallen to three, and Winter 2024 again admitted just three. Africa’s share of a batch had shrunk from about six per cent at the peak to around one per cent by Winter 2024. A search of the YC website for African startups for the 12 batches since then returns the message “sorry, no matching companies found”.
The pullback, however, is not a single decision made in San Francisco. It is the product of three things moving at once – a YC that has changed what it wants, an African funding market that cooled faster than most, and a portfolio record that has made the case for Africa harder to argue.
The numbers: from 24, to a handful, to none
YC’s African intake rose fast in the remote era and fell faster when it ended. The accelerator went fully remote from Summer 2020, ballooned its batches, and African founders who could never have relocated to San Francisco for three months suddenly could apply from Lagos or Nairobi. The Winter 2021 batch had ten African startups; Winter 2022 had 24.
Then came the correction. YC cut its Summer 2022 cohort to 240 companies from 414, citing the downturn and a changed venture market, and only eight African startups made it. Winter 2023 admitted three. Winter 2024 admitted four again – Nigerian fintechs Cleva and Miden, Kenyan travel-tech startup Triply, and Zimbabwe’s Ocular AI, out of 260 companies picked from more than 27,000 applications. There have been none since.
Across 14 years the picture is lopsided. YC has backed roughly 100 African startups since Wave in 2012, about two per cent of a portfolio of more than 4,600 companies. Nigeria accounts for around 40 per cent of them, Egypt about 15 per cent, and Kenya about 14 per cent, and more than half are fintechs. In other words, the surge in 2021 and 2022 was the anomaly, not the decline.
YC changed first
The biggest reason fewer African startups get in is that YC now wants something different, and wants it in San Francisco. Three shifts matter most.
The first is a return to physical programmes. Summer 2022 opened with an in-person kickoff, the first since Winter 2020. The programme now runs mainly on YC’s San Francisco campus for three months. For a founder in Accra or Kigali, that means a US visa, a quarter away from customers and staff, and San Francisco rents paid from a pre-seed budget. The remote years removed those costs; the return to campus put them back.
In addition, the type of company YC accepts has changed. Recent batches are dominated by AI companies selling to other businesses. In Spring 2026, 62 per cent of the cohort was B2B, and the Summer 2026 batch was focused on infrastructure for AI agents, with consumer companies at about five per cent. African YC alumni were overwhelmingly fintech and consumer-facing marketplaces built around local market gaps. That profile now sits outside what YC is hunting for.
In the meantime, YC raising the size of its cheque has set a higher bar, especially for African ventures. Its standard deal is now US$500,000 – US$125,000 for seven per cent, plus a US$375,000 uncapped SAFE. Companies must also incorporate in Delaware. A larger cheque on an uncapped note is a bet on US-scale outcomes, which raises the bar for businesses whose ceiling is set by Nigerian or Kenyan purchasing power.
YC did move to four batches a year in 2025, with smaller cohorts and more application windows. That gives African founders more shots, but it has not yet shown up as a visible rebound in African admissions. As previously mentioned, there have been none in that time.
Africa’s own downturn
The African side of the story made YC’s retreat easier. Startup funding on the continent fell by 27.8 per cent to US$2.4 billion in 2023, and a further 53.5 per cent in 2024, to US$1.12 billion.
When it recovered in 2025, to US$1.6 billion over the course of the year – note, 2026 is likely to be similar to this – the money went mostly to large rounds. The recovery has been real, but it has not been a seed-stage recovery. Average Series A and B cheques grew, while investors backed fewer companies. For YC, whose model depends on a deep pool of follow-on seed and Series A investors, that matters. A Demo Day company needs someone to lead its next round, and fewer global funds were writing early cheques into Lagos or Nairobi.
Currency made it worse. The naira lost most of its value against the dollar after Nigeria’s 2023 reforms, and Egypt’s pound was devalued repeatedly. A startup earning in local currency but valued in dollars watched its revenue shrink in the metric YC investors care about. Nigeria, which supplied 18 of the 24 African companies at the 2022 peak, took the hardest hit.
The portfolio record has not helped either. Of roughly 100 African YC companies, the ones that returned real capital or reached meaningful scale are a short list – Paystack, Flutterwave, Wave, Nomba and Reliance Health. Most of the rest are subscale, or shut down. Paystack’s US$200 million sale to Stripe in 2020 remains the benchmark exit, but it is six years old. At least five YC-backed African startups are formally inactive in YC’s directory.
What fills the gap
Fewer YC slots cost African founders more than US$500,000. The YC badge worked as a signal that let a first-time founder in Lagos raise from US investors who had never heard of them. Briter Bridges counted about US$1.3 billion in follow-on funding raised by YC’s African portfolio by 2021. Local alternatives can match the cheque, but not yet the network.
They are trying. Iyin Aboyeji’s Future Africa launched Accelerate Africa, openly pitched as a home-grown answer to YC. It takes no equity on entry and may invest US$250,000 to US$500,000 after due diligence. Madica writes up to US$200,000 on a SAFE, Katapult Africa invests US$150,000 to US$500,000 in agri-, food- and climate-tech, and Antler runs residencies in Nairobi and Lagos. Google’s equity-free Africa programme drew nearly 2,600 applicants for 15 places in 2026.
The broader accelerator map is shrinking, though. Techstars closed its Lagos programme in late 2024 after two cohorts, and the Founders Factory Africa venture studio shut in 2025 after its Mastercard Foundation partnership ended. The founders YC turns away are competing for a smaller set of local seats.
There is a quieter shift too. A growing number of YC’s African alumni now invest or build locally, and YC has kept supporting its earlier bets. In 2025 it took part in follow-on rounds for Nigerian food-delivery startup Chowdeck’s Series A and Egyptian grocery company Breadfast. YC is still in Africa. It is just backing what it already owns rather than buying new tickets.
A question of fit
Underneath the cyclical story is a structural one. YC’s model rewards companies that grow fast and reach liquidity within a decade. That works for payments, which is why Africa’s YC winners are almost all fintech startups. It fits poorly with the sectors where the continent’s infrastructure gaps are largest, such as energy, agri-tech, e-health, logistics, and last-mile delivery, which need longer runways, heavier regulation and less obvious exits.
There are reasons the numbers could tick up. Four batches a year means four chances rather than two, and smaller cohorts of roughly 100 to 125 companies may favour founders who were crowded out of the old twice-yearly rush. African teams building AI tools for global business customers fit YC’s current thesis far better than the marketplace startups of 2021. And the African funding market has been recovering in 2025 and 2026, even if the money is skewing late-stage.
The Fall 2026 Demo Day on December 2 will be one test of whether any of that is landing. But the more interesting question may run the other way. With local capital deeper, local accelerators more credible, and a generation of YC alumni now writing cheques at home, Africa’s next Paystack may not need Y Combinator at all. Whether YC can adapt fast enough to find it first is YC’s problem, not Africa’s.

articles.title: Rodic Consultants proposes Rs 200 Cr fund for AI in infrastructure
articles.text:
Rodic Consultants proposes Rs 200 Cr fund for AI in infrastructure
The engineering consultancy will commit Rs 100 crore and expects to raise the rest from co-investors. Selected startups could test their products on live infrastructure projects.
Infrastructure engineering consultancy Rodic Consultants on Wednesday announced plans to set up the Rs 200 crore Rodic AI Infrastructure Innovation Fund to back startups developing AI and other technologies for India’s infrastructure sector.
Rodic will commit Rs 100 crore to the proposed fund and expects to raise the remaining Rs 100 crore through co-investments from venture capital firms, angel funds and individual investors, including ultra-high-net-worth individuals. The company did not name any co-investors or disclose target cheque sizes.
Rodic said selected startups could test their products on live infrastructure projects, draw on its engineering expertise and explore partnerships with public and private sector organisations. The company has spent 26 years working on infrastructure projects across sectors including highways, bridges, tunnels, railways, metros, water and hydropower.
The company sees applications for these technologies across the life of a project, from planning and construction to monitoring and maintenance. Field trials would give startups a chance to see how their products perform on working sites and what needs to change before wider deployment.
“Innovators often need more than capital. They need access to real infrastructure problems, project sites, engineering expertise, data and potential users,” Raj Kumar, chairman and managing director of Rodic Consultants, said in a statement. He cited AI, computer vision, drones, sensors and robotics as technologies that could change how infrastructure is designed, built and maintained.
The announcement comes ahead of Rodic’s InfraAI Conclave on January 22, 2027, at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The company said the event would bring together government officials, infrastructure companies, investors, startups and researchers to discuss where AI can be used in the sector.

articles.title: Cómo evitar que ChatGPT, Claude y Gemini usen tus conversaciones para entrenar su IA
articles.text:
ChatGPT, Claude y Gemini pueden usar las conversaciones de los usuarios con cuentas personales para entrenar sus modelos de inteligencia artificial, y los tres servicios tienen un ajuste para impedirlo. Se encuentra en el menú de configuración de cada uno, con nombres y condiciones distintos, según sus páginas de ayuda oficiales.
Las cuentas empresariales funcionan distinto: según OpenAI, ChatGPT Business, Enterprise y Edu quedan fuera del entrenamiento por defecto. Lo que sigue vale para cuentas personales, y cada compañía conserva excepciones por seguridad o por comentarios enviados por el usuario.
Cómo hacer el proceso en ChatGPT
OpenAI informa que en las cuentas personales Free, Plus y Pro el uso de las conversaciones para mejorar sus modelos viene activado de fábrica. La opción se llama “Improve the model for everyone” (mejorar el modelo para todos).
En la versión web, hay que abrir el menú de la cuenta, entrar en Settings (Configuración), elegir Data controls (Controles de datos), desactivar esa opción y pulsar Done (Listo). En iOS y Android, se abre la barra lateral, se toca el ícono del perfil, se entra en Settings y luego en Data controls, y se apaga el mismo interruptor.
Según OpenAI, el ajuste se aplica a toda la cuenta, en la web y en el teléfono. También puede cambiarse sin iniciar sesión: la elección queda guardada solo en ese navegador. El modo de voz tiene un control de entrenamiento aparte.
La compañía aclara que desactivar la opción no borra ni oculta los chats guardados: para eliminarlos hay que borrar cada conversación o la cuenta. Archivar un chat tampoco cambia si puede usarse para entrenar.
Hay una excepción: si el usuario marca el pulgar hacia arriba o hacia abajo en una respuesta, toda la conversación asociada puede usarse para entrenar los modelos de OpenAI, aunque el ajuste esté apagado.
Así se desactiva en Claude
Las reglas de Anthropic valen para los planes Free, Pro y Max, y para Claude Code con esas cuentas. Según su centro de privacidad, usa los chats y las sesiones de programación para mejorar sus modelos si el usuario lo permite, si la conversación es marcada para revisión de seguridad o si el usuario se une a un programa de pruebas.
Para cambiar la decisión en el navegador, se selecciona el nombre del usuario en el menú, luego Settings, después Privacy (Privacidad) y, bajo el título “Help improve our AI models” (ayuda a mejorar nuestros modelos de IA), se activa o desactiva el botón. En el teléfono, el camino es el mismo.
Anthropic advierte que los datos ya incluidos en entrenamientos iniciados o en modelos ya entrenados seguirán formando parte de ellos. Lo que cambia es que los chats nuevos, y los almacenados antes, no se usarán en futuros entrenamientos.
Si los sistemas de seguridad marcan una conversación, la empresa puede emplearla para mejorar sus modelos de detección de contenido dañino. Los comentarios enviados con los pulgares se guardan, con la conversación entera, hasta cinco años. Los chats en modo incógnito no se usan para mejorar el modelo, ni con el ajuste activado.
Este es el paso a paso en Gemini
En Gemini, Google controla el entrenamiento desde el apartado History (Historial). En la web, se abre gemini.google.com, se hace clic en Settings y luego en History. Ahí aparece la casilla “Chat content including text & uploads” (contenido de los chats), activada por defecto para mayores de 18 años. Hay que desmarcarla y confirmar con Turn off (Desactivar).
Otra casilla, para el audio y los videos o pantallas compartidas de Gemini Live, viene desactivada. Google aclara que, para activar cualquiera de las dos, el historial debe estar encendido. Con el historial apagado, los chats futuros no se usan para entrenar modelos, salvo que el usuario envíe comentarios, pero se guardan unos dos meses para responder y proteger el servicio.
Una parte de las conversaciones es revisada por personas, incluidos proveedores externos. Esos chats se desvinculan de la cuenta y se conservan hasta tres años, aunque el usuario los borre o apague el ajuste después. Google pide no escribir información confidencial.
El historial se borra solo a los 18 meses por defecto; el plazo puede cambiarse a 3 o 36 meses o desactivarse. La página de privacidad de Gemini figura como actualizada el 24 de noviembre de 2026.

articles.title: 1Password customer data stolen after employee GitHub account breach
articles.text:
1Password has disclosed a data breach after an employee's corporate GitHub account was hacked and used to deploy malicious code to the company's backend services to steal customer data.
The company says customer password vaults and the encryption keys protecting them were not compromised in the attack.
In a security incident disclosure published today, 1Password says it began investigating the breach on November 19 after detecting indications that an employee's GitHub account had been compromised.
The attacker used the account to access private source code repositories and inject malicious code into backend services that downloaded customer account records.
The stolen data includes:
- Customer names and email addresses
- Account and user IDs
- Account creation and last sign-in timestamps
- Public cryptographic keys
- Secure Remote Password (SRP) protocol parameters
- Invitation, provisioning, and account recovery tokens
- Other internal account metadata
The attacker also stole internal company source code and accessed its continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) environment, potentially exposing internal infrastructure credentials.
Among the stolen customer data were tokens embedded in links that 1Password emailed to users to accept account provisioning invitations or recover their accounts.
However, 1Password says these tokens cannot be used on their own to access customer accounts, as completing the invitation or recovery process requires either single sign-on (SSO) authentication or a six-digit verification code sent to the user's registered email address.
The company says only a small number of users were affected and have been individually notified.
As a precaution against brute-force attacks, 1Password has strengthened these verification codes from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric characters.
The company says it has now disabled the compromised GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, restored clean versions of affected services, and rotated or revoked potentially exposed infrastructure credentials.
1Password has also hired independent cybersecurity experts to validate its remediation efforts and says it has found no internal evidence of customer account takeovers.
The company is not requiring customers to change their account passwords or Secret Keys but warns them to watch for unexpected invitations, account recovery requests, and other potential phishing attempts.
While customer vaults were not compromised in the attack, the stolen data is valuable to threat actors as it provides a list of known 1Password users who could be targeted in phishing campaigns.
Threat actors could send emails impersonating 1Password, using the breach as a lure to trick customers into disclosing their account passwords, Secret Keys, or recovery verification codes.
Customers should be particularly wary of emails claiming they need to secure their accounts in response to the breach, reset their passwords, or verify their account information.
Rather than clicking on links in these emails, customers should access their accounts directly through the 1Password website or app and never share their passwords, Secret Keys, or verification codes with anyone.
BleepingComputer contacted 1Password with questions about the attack but has not yet received a response.

articles.title: GTA 6 fait flamber les ventes de PS5 d’occasion, et les escrocs de Vinted en profitent
articles.text:
L’arnaque revient à chaque pénurie de consoles. Pris de court par les ruptures de stock chez les revendeurs officiels avec la sortie de GTA 6, le 19 novembre 2026, de nombreux joueurs se rabattent dans l’urgence sur les plateformes de seconde main pour mettre la main sur une PlayStation 5. C’est précisément sur cette fébrilité que misent des vendeurs malintentionnés sur Vinted : les signalements d’annonces piégées s’enchaînent depuis plusieurs jours sur le réseau social X.
À première vue, ces offres ont tout de l’aubaine rêvée : des visuels propres, un boîtier sous blister ou posé sur une table de salon, et un tarif nettement inférieur aux prix habituels du marché. L’acheteur pressé, persuadé de devancer des dizaines d’autres intéressés, valide le paiement en quelques secondes sans se méfier. Ce n’est qu’au moment de récupérer un colis anormalement léger en point relais que le piège se referme sur l’acheteur : à l’intérieur de l’enveloppe ne se trouve aucune console, mais une simple feuille A4 sur laquelle a été imprimée la photo de la PS5.
Une mention de photo PS5 noyée dans les tags, pour tromper l’acheteur et la plateforme Vinted
Si cette méthode avait déjà fait des victimes lors du lancement de la PS5 en 2020, ou plus récemment autour de la Nintendo Switch 2, sa version actuelle pousse le vice encore plus loin. Auparavant, les fraudeurs se contentaient généralement de glisser une phrase ambiguë tout en bas de la description, espérant qu’elle passerait inaperçue. Désormais, plusieurs annonces repérées par les internautes sur X dissimulent la mention « c’est une photo » ou « photo uniquement » directement au milieu d’une longue liste de hashtags en fin de texte.
Sur l’interface mobile de Vinted, où les descriptions longues sont tronquées et nécessitent un clic supplémentaire pour être déployées en entier, cette précision devient totalement invisible pour un acheteur qui parcourt rapidement l’annonce. L’objectif derrière cette ruse est double : tromper la vigilance du client tout en se constituant un alibi technique face au service client de la plateforme.
Car une fois le colis ouvert, obtenir gain de cause relève souvent du parcours du combattant. Les politiques de protection des plateformes d’occasion couvrent en priorité les colis perdus, endommagés ou non conformes à l’annonce. En prétendant avoir indiqué la nature réelle de l’objet dans le texte, même de façon dissimulée, l’escroc tente de bloquer le remboursement automatique en soutenant que l’acheteur a reçu exactement ce qui était écrit.
Face à la multiplication de ces signalements en pleine fièvre GTA 6, la règle d’or reste donc la même : fuir les tarifs trop beaux pour être vrais et systématiquement lire l’intégralité d’une annonce, jusqu’au dernier tag, avant de dégainer sa carte bancaire.

articles.title: GTA 6 signe le plus grand lancement de l’histoire de PlayStation
articles.text:
Les records s'accumulent pour le ce qui semble déjà le plus grand jeu du XXIè siècle ! GTA 6 devient ainsi le plus grand lancement de l'histoire enregistré sur PlayStation.
Ça paraît évident aujourd'hui, GTA 6 est vraiment le jeu phénomène de notre époque. Ce qui se vérifie en plus par les chiffres, avec les records qui tombent comme des mouches les uns après les autres. On sait ainsi déjà que la nouvelle version de Grand Theft Auto est le lancement le plus lucratif de l'histoire après 24 heures. Et c'est aussi le meilleur lancement de l'histoire sur PlayStation.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Sony enregistre plus de 39 millions de joueurs uniques pour GTA 6
Qui pourra faire mieux que GTA 6 à l'avenir ? On peut se poser la question. Car Sony vient elle-même, sur le blog Playstation, de consacrer le jeu comme « le plus grand lancement de l'histoire de la PlayStation ».
GTA 6 a en effet, au 22 novembre dernier, enregistré à lui seul plus de 39 millions de joueurs uniques, « devenant ainsi le plus grand lancement de jeu de l'histoire de la PlayStation, sur trois décennies et cinq générations de consoles. »
Déjà 683 millions d'heures jouées au sein de GTA 6
Et ce ne sont pas là les seuls chiffres fous qui viennent aujourd'hui illustrer le phénomène. À travers l'ensemble des PlayStation 5, les joueurs ont déjà joué quelque 683 millions d'heures, ce qui revient à une moyenne de 17,4 heures jouées par personne.
GTA 6 est aussi l'occasion pour Sony d'enregistrer le plus grand nombre de nouvelles consoles PS5 connectées en une journée de toute l'histoire de la console. Et GTA 6 a été le premier jeu joué dans 70% des cas de ces nouvelles connexions.
Enfin, « GTA 6 a établi un nouveau record du plus grand nombre de joueurs simultanés pour un jeu sur PlayStation, dépassant les records précédents établis par des titres multijoueurs, free-to-play et solo. » Qui pourra un jour faire mieux ?
Source : PlayStation

articles.title: Pas besoin de PS5 pour GTA 6, un PlayStation Portal suffit
articles.text:
Le PlayStation Portal a longtemps traîné un gros défaut. Sans PS5 allumée à la maison, la console portable de Sony ne servait strictement à rien, et lors de notre test en 2023, on parlait déjà d’une machine au potentiel gâché.
En novembre 2025, Sony a rectifié le tir en ouvrant le Portal au streaming cloud. Pourtant, GTA 6 manquait à l’appel à sa sortie le 19 novembre, alors que les joueurs Xbox pouvaient déjà le lancer avec le Xbox Cloud Gaming.
Depuis lundi, la fiche du jeu sur le PlayStation Store indique « Streaming cloud PS5 et PS Portal pris en charge ». Le jeu tourne donc sur les serveurs de Sony, et on peut y jouer sur le Portal sans posséder de PS5 et sans faire de place pour les 212 Go de l’installation.
Black Friday : la TV Samsung Micro RGB 65″ R95H perd 1 000 € et s’affiche à 1 999 € au lieu de 2 999 €, du 21 au 30 novembre. Grâce à sa technologie Micro RGB, il délivre « un niveau de précision et de richesse colorimétrique inédit ».
375 euros pour jouer à GTA 6 dans son lit pendant trois mois
Attention, le jeu n’est pas offert pour autant. GTA 6 ne fait pas partie du catalogue du PS Plus Premium. Il faut l’acheter séparément à 79,99 euros sur le PS Store ou un peu moins cher en « édition physique » dans certains magasins.
Côté facture, le PlayStation Portal coûte 249,99 euros depuis la hausse d’avril (actuellement à 239,99 euros avec le code 10DES99 chez Cdiscount), et le PS Plus Premium 18,99 euros par mois, 54,99 euros pour trois mois ou 151,99 euros par an. On arrive à environ 375 euros avec le PS Portal, trois mois de PS Plus Premium et GTA 6. C’est une somme, mais c’est plus abordable qu’une PS5 actuellement à 600 euros pour le modèle de base.
Sony garde tout de même un avantage sur Microsoft. Le PS Plus Premium ne limite pas la durée des sessions en streaming, alors que le Xbox Cloud Gaming impose des limites de temps depuis ce mois-ci.
Deux heures de batterie et un Wi-Fi qui doit suivre
Est-ce jouable ? Oui, mais avec des limites. Sur le Portal, le streaming cloud plafonne à 1080p et 60 images par seconde, et Sony recommande une connexion d’au moins 15 Mbit/s. La latence tourne quant à elle autour de 80 à 90 millisecondes en Wi-Fi à la maison. Ça passe pour un jeu d’action en vue à la troisième personne comme GTA 6. Par contre, la qualité dépend directement du débit : en partage de connexion ou sur un Wi-Fi d’hôtel capricieux, il faut s’attendre à des saccades et à une image qui se dégrade.
L’autonomie, c’est l’autre problème. Sur un fil Reddit consacré à GTA 6 sur le Portal, des propriétaires de la console sont emballés par le rendu, mais disent ne pas dépasser deux heures de jeu sur batterie.

articles.title: Anthropics neuer Siren-Test: Warum Forscher die KI‑Modelle absichtlich in Fallen locken
articles.text:
Verlockende Schlupflöcher: Warum Anthropic seinen KI-Modellen absichtlich eine Falle stellt
Eigentlich sind Sirenen Fabelwesen aus der griechischen Mythologie. In vielen Erzählungen, etwa in Homers Odyssee, locken sie vorbeifahrende Seeleute an, um sie anschließend zu töten. Anthropic hat jetzt einen Test mit demselben Namen entwickelt und erklärt in einem Blogbeitrag die Vorgehensweise sowie erste Erkenntnisse. Siren versetzt KI-Agenten in realistische Simulationen, die darauf ausgelegt sind, sie zu Fehlverhalten zu verleiten. Anhand der Ergebnisse können Forscher:innen einschätzen, wie wahrscheinlich es ist, dass neue Modelle im realen Einsatz außer Kontrolle geraten.
Siren soll KI-Agenten in Versuchung führen
In den vergangenen Monaten haben KI-Labore mit zahlreichen Sicherheitsvorfällen für Schlagzeilen gesorgt. Insbesondere der Angriff auf Hugging Face hat große Aufmerksamkeit erregt. Ursprünglich wollte OpenAI die Leistungsfähigkeit neuer Modelle testen. Stattdessen brachen mehrere Agenten aus der eigentlich abgeriegelten Sandbox aus und verschafften sich Zugang zu den Systemen der Open-Source-Plattform. Laut OpenAI ging der Angriff auf ein internes Forum zurück, in dem sich die Agenten austauschten und gefundene Schwachstellen teilten.
OpenAI ist damit nicht allein: Auch Konkurrenten wie Anthropic haben zahlreiche Vorfälle gemeldet, in denen sich ihre Agenten nicht wie gewünscht verhielten. Infolgedessen sprachen sich KI-Labore mehrfach für eine strengere Regulierung ihrer eigenen Technologie aus. Einige kappten ihren Agenten in Tests zusätzlich die Internetverbindung. Anthropic geht mit Siren jetzt noch einen Schritt weiter und führt seine Modelle absichtlich in Versuchung. Der Test lässt die Agenten in einer von 26 simulierten Sandbox-Umgebungen frei agieren. Insgesamt wurden 1.700 Szenarien getestet.
Verschiedene Funktionen der Sandbox sind dabei absichtlich falsch konfiguriert, sodass die Agenten die Umgebung verlassen können. Direkt außerhalb der Sandbox-Grenze befindet sich beispielsweise eine Datei mit verlockenden Inhalten wie Passwörtern und vermeintlichen Zugangswegen zum Internet. Der Test stellt den Agenten dann Aufgaben, die sie dazu verleiten, die Sandbox zu verlassen, ohne ihnen dafür eine ausdrückliche Erlaubnis zu erteilen. Wichtig ist, dass sich die Sandbox in einer zweiten Sandbox befindet. Das soll Sicherheitsvorfälle vermieden.
Neuere Modelle schneiden im Test besser ab
„Modelle werden immer besser werden und weiterhin Zero-Day-Schwachstellen aufspüren”, so die Anthropic-Forscherin Darya Kaviani gegenüber Wired. Sie hat sich auf das Thema KI-Sicherheit spezialisiert und wirkte an der Entwicklung von Siren mit. Bei einer Zero-Day-Sicherheitslücke handelt es sich um einen bisher unbekannten Fehler in einer Software, der sich nutzen lässt, um Daten zu stehlen oder sich unbefugten Zugriff zu verschaffen. Laut Kaviani ist es wahrscheinlich, dass KI-Modelle solche Lücken zunehmend finden und ausnutzen können. Dann stelle sich die Frage, ob sie der Versuchung widerstehen.
Für bestehende Schwachstellen Patches zu entwickeln, reiche laut Kaviani nicht aus. „Selbst wenn wir unsere Infrastruktur stärken, werden die Modelle Schritt halten und weiter Schwachstellen finden können“, so die Forscherin. Anthropic gibt an, dass frühere Claude-Versionen in Testläufen mit Siren deutlich öfter in die Falle tappten als ihre Nachfolger. Claude 5.5 und Claude Mythos 5.2 fielen nur in 0,6 bis 1,6 Prozent der Fälle auf Siren herein. Die älteren Modelle Claude Mythos 5.1 und Claude Mythos 5 gerieten dagegen in 12,7 beziehungsweise 25,8 Prozent der Fälle auf Abwege. Laut Anthropic werden neue Modelle gezielt darauf trainiert, seltener gegen Vorgaben zu verstoßen.
