articles.title: Como editar um story do Instagram depois de postado
articles.text:
Como editar um story do Instagram depois de postado
Editar stories já postados no Instagram permite corrigir textos e ajustar stickers em até 15 minutos sem perder visualizações, curtidas ou a ordem da publicação original
Você sabia que é possível editar um story do Instagram mesmo após publicá-lo, corrigindo textos e ajustando figurinhas? A função está disponível diretamente nos aplicativos para Android e iPhone por meio do menu “Mais” na própria publicação.
Para editar um story já publicado, a alteração precisa ser feita no limite de 15 minutos após o envio original na rede social. O ajuste mantém todas as visualizações e curtidas intactas, exibindo apenas um discreto aviso de que o conteúdo foi modificado.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te ensina o passo a passo para editar stories já publicados no Instagram.
Você pode editar um story depois de postado diretamente pelo aplicativo do Instagram para celular Android ou iPhone. Veja o passo a passo para alterar um conteúdo que já foi postado na rede social:
Abra o aplicativo do Instagram no seu celular e toque na sua foto de perfil, no canto superior esquerdo, para visualizar os seus stories recentes.
Com a publicação aberta na tela, toque no botão “Mais”, ícone de três pontos no canto inferior direito, para abrir a aba com as opções e ferramentas disponíveis para o conteúdo.
Toque em “Editar story” e, caso seja sua primeira vez usando a ferramenta, confirme tocando no botão “Entendi” para avançar.
Use as ferramentas de edição para corrigir textos, reposicionar figurinhas ou modificar elementos visuais do story, lembrando que a mídia original (foto ou vídeo de fundo) não pode ser substituída.
Após revisar todas as modificações feitas na tela, toque em “Salvar alterações” no canto inferior direito e aguarde alguns instantes até que o aplicativo atualize o story publicado para seus seguidores.
Ao editar stories já publicados no Instagram, a rede social aplica ajustes visuais e técnicos para sinalizar a atualização sem prejudicar o alcance da postagem. Confira os principais efeitos que ocorrem ao alterar um story:
- Selo de alteração: o Instagram exibe uma etiqueta “Editado” acompanhada de um ícone de lápis logo abaixo do seu nome de usuário, sinalizando para os seguidores que o conteúdo passou por modificações;
- Preservação do engajamento: todas as métricas de interação acumuladas antes da mudança, como a lista de visualizações, curtidas e respostas enviadas por mensagem direta (DM), permanecem intactas na publicação;
- Posição e público intocados: o story não é republicado como novo nem volta para o final da fila, mantendo a ordem na sequência e respeitando as configurações de privacidade definidas inicialmente;
- Remoção de republicações: caso outros perfis tenham compartilhado o seu story antes da alteração, esses recompartilhamentos feitos a partir do original são automaticamente removidos do ar pelo Instagram.
Não, você não perde suas visualizações ao editar stories no Instagram dentro da janela de 15 minutos após a postagem. Todo o engajamento original, incluindo curtidas e respostas, permanece intacto na publicação, que passa apenas a exibir o selo “Editado” para informar a atualização aos seguidores.
Não, o story editado não é atualizado automaticamente nos compartilhamentos feitos pelos seus seguidores. Para evitar inconsistências de exibição, o Instagram remove do ar todas as cópias ligadas à versão original, exigindo que outros perfis voltem a compartilhar stories a partir da publicação corrigida.
O Instagram não estabelece um limite fixo de alterações ao editar story depois de postado, restringindo o recurso apenas ao prazo de 15 minutos após a publicação. Durante essa janela de tempo, você pode reabrir a interface de edição e salvar ajustes nos textos ou figurinhas quantas vezes precisar no mesmo arquivo.
A opção para editar um story depois de postado fica disponível apenas quando a publicação atende a regras técnicas e prazos definidos pelo Instagram. Veja os motivos mais comuns que fazem o botão de edição sumir do seu menu:
- Prazo expirado: a janela de edição dura apenas 15 minutos após o envio. Passado esse limite de tempo, o recurso é bloqueado e você precisará apagar e publicar o conteúdo novamente;
- Liberação gradual: o Instagram distribui novas ferramentas em lotes pelo servidor, o que significa que a função ainda pode não ter sido ativada para a sua conta;
- Aplicativo desatualizado: versões antigas do Instagram não suportam os recursos mais recentes do sistema, exigindo a atualização manual do aplicativo na App Store ou Play Store;
- Recursos incompatíveis: a inclusão de stickers interativos específicos, como a figurinha “Sua Vez”, bloqueia o modo de edição devido às limitações técnicas de sincronização;
- Integração com o Facebook: stories configurados para compartilhamento cruzado com o Facebook têm a edição bloqueada para evitar falhas de exibição entre as duas redes sociais.
Se você perdeu a janela de 15 minutos para editar a publicação, a saída prática é apagar o story no Instagram e subir o conteúdo corrigido do zero. Antes de excluir a postagem, salve o arquivo na galeria do celular para reaproveitar a foto ou o vídeo original sem perder o arquivo.
Na hora de republicar, aproveite para montar stories criativos, adicionando textos, trilhas sonoras ou enquetes que ficaram de fora da primeira versão. Vale lembrar que, se você usar stickers interativos ou ativar o envio simultâneo para o Facebook, o sistema bloqueará novas edições posteriores.

articles.title: Stickers con audio en WhatsApp: cómo crear imágenes con voz y sonidos de hasta 10 segundos
articles.text:
WhatsApp comenzó a habilitar una nueva función que permitirá a sus usuarios enviar stickers acompañados de grabaciones de voz, frases y efectos sonoros. La herramienta, que empezó a implementarse el martes 24 de noviembre de 2026, amplía las posibilidades de personalización de los mensajes y permite convertir imágenes estáticas o animadas en contenidos que también transmiten sonidos.
Los nuevos stickers con audio pueden incluir grabaciones de hasta 10 segundos, una característica que busca hacer más expresivas las conversaciones dentro de la aplicación. A diferencia de los stickers tradicionales, que solo transmiten una imagen, este formato incorpora un componente sonoro que el destinatario puede reproducir cuando lo desee.
La función ya está disponible para algunos usuarios y su distribución será gradual. Esto significa que no todas las cuentas tendrán acceso inmediato, incluso si utilizan la versión más reciente de WhatsApp.
Cómo funcionan los nuevos stickers con audio de WhatsApp
La principal diferencia frente a los stickers convencionales es que las imágenes ahora pueden incorporar un sonido asociado. Para identificar cuáles tienen esta característica, WhatsApp muestra un pequeño ícono de volumen sobre el sticker.
Cuando una persona recibe uno de estos contenidos, debe pulsar sobre la imagen para escuchar el audio. La reproducción no comienza automáticamente al abrir una conversación, una decisión que permite evitar sonidos inesperados cuando alguien revisa sus mensajes.
Esta característica también respeta el modo silencioso del teléfono y las preferencias de reproducción de cada usuario. De esta manera, quienes no quieran escuchar los sonidos pueden mantener sus dispositivos en silencio sin que los stickers interrumpan otras actividades.
Otro aspecto importante es la privacidad. Según el portal especializado WABetaInfo, tanto las imágenes como los archivos de sonido asociados están protegidos mediante el cifrado de extremo a extremo de WhatsApp. Este sistema impide que terceros puedan acceder al contenido de los mensajes durante su transmisión.
La novedad permite utilizar grabaciones personales, frases breves y efectos de sonido para acompañar imágenes que normalmente se comparten como reacciones dentro de los chats.
Paso a paso para crear stickers con audio en WhatsApp
Los usuarios que ya tengan habilitada la herramienta pueden crear sus propios stickers sonoros desde el editor integrado de la aplicación. No necesitan instalar programas externos ni recurrir a otras plataformas para combinar imágenes y grabaciones.
El procedimiento comienza desde cualquier conversación y utiliza las opciones disponibles en el apartado de stickers.
Para crear uno, se deben seguir estos pasos:
- Abrir WhatsApp e ingresar a una conversación individual o grupal.
- Acceder al apartado de stickers desde el teclado de mensajes.
- Seleccionar la opción para crear un sticker nuevo y elegir una fotografía.
- Presionar el ícono de ondas sonoras que aparece dentro del editor.
- Grabar un mensaje de voz o seleccionar un archivo de audio almacenado en el celular.
- Recortar el fragmento de sonido que se desea utilizar.
- Guardar el resultado y enviarlo al contacto o grupo.
Una vez enviado, el destinatario podrá identificar que se trata de un sticker con sonido gracias al ícono de volumen. Para reproducirlo, únicamente tendrá que pulsar sobre la imagen.
Cuánto puede durar el audio de los stickers
Una de las limitaciones de esta herramienta es la duración de los archivos sonoros. De acuerdo con las pruebas realizadas en versiones de desarrollo, los stickers estáticos admiten grabaciones de hasta 10 segundos.
En el caso de los stickers creados a partir de videos, el límite es diferente: pueden conservar hasta cinco segundos del sonido original. Esto permite aprovechar fragmentos de imágenes animadas para generar reacciones con audio sin necesidad de elaborar una grabación independiente.
La duración reducida responde al propósito de estos contenidos, que están pensados para complementar conversaciones rápidas y no para compartir mensajes de voz extensos.
Cuándo estará disponible la nueva función para todos
WhatsApp comenzó a distribuir los stickers con audio el 24 de noviembre de 2026, pero su llegada será progresiva. Por ello, algunos usuarios podrán encontrar la herramienta en el editor de stickers mientras que otros todavía tendrán que esperar.
La disponibilidad depende de la activación de la función en cada cuenta, por lo que actualizar la aplicación no garantiza que aparezca inmediatamente.
Con esta incorporación, WhatsApp amplía las opciones para personalizar las conversaciones y añade una alternativa a los mensajes de voz tradicionales. La novedad permite combinar imágenes, expresiones y sonidos en un mismo contenido, una forma distinta de comunicarse sin necesidad de escribir o enviar una grabación por separado.

articles.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Automating Spark Upgrades with Codex Agents at OpenAI
articles.text:
At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mouli Mukherjee, Engineering Manager for Data Infrastructure at OpenAI, argued that AI agents are most useful not for rebuilding a data platform, but for the open-ended operational work that is hard to turn into fixed playbooks. OpenAI’s platform runs at exabyte scale, with hundreds of thousands of datasets and a Spark fleet on millions of cores, and Mukherjee showed how Codex-driven agents can take on that kind of work when the right systems sit underneath them.
Mukherjee clearly distinguished between deterministic systems and agents. She stated that anything requiring consistent outputs for the same inputs, such as access control, configuration resolution, and data correctness guarantees, should remain within the realm of proper systems. Agents utilize these systems as tools and do not attempt to reimplement them. As she expressed:
We should definitely build the systems where we want guarantees and guardrails.
Agents earn their place where failure modes and remediations cannot be fully enumerated in advance, such as debugging: follow the evidence, decide what to try next, and stay inside the tools’ guarantees.
The Spark upgrade outlines steps taken to ensure safety. The team first built a shadow-run service for testing, which reused production inputs and operated on a low-priority queue to avoid impacting live operations. They also implemented a configuration override service to prevent experiments from changing global settings and developed a validation skill to compare production and shadow runs. After these safeguards were in place, agents claimed jobs, launched shadow runs, reviewed validation reports, classified errors, and transitioned jobs to the new Spark version.
Mukherjee reported that the same primitives now cover more of routine platform operations. Agents can tune job efficiency continuously by inspecting query plans, trying a config change, comparing runs, and iterating. For lower-risk incremental library releases, the team sometimes skips the shadow step and promotes directly, trading capacity for higher rollback risk. Jobs that pass shadow validation but later fail in production can auto-roll back to the previous Spark version so pipelines keep running without manual intervention. On the support side, agents can search past incident reports, suggest runbook updates, trace why a table is stale through orchestrator and scheduler logs, and help users understand access-control denials, while permissions still enforce the user’s own credentials.
Mukherjee recommended starting with the repetitive, open-ended tasks where judgment matters and failure modes are too numerous to hard-code, building the safety mechanisms first, and only then letting agents operate inside those bounds so experimentation stays repeatable, observable, and reversible.

articles.title: Planeta com até o dobro da massa da Terra pode estar escondido após Netuno
articles.text:
Um planeta ainda não identificado pode estar escondido nos confins do Sistema Solar, além da órbita de Netuno. Batizado provisoriamente de Planeta X2, o corpo celeste teria entre 1,5 e 2 vezes a massa da Terra e poderia ajudar a explicar alterações observadas nas trajetórias de objetos gelados daquela região.
A hipótese foi apresentada em estudo publicado na revista científica Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society. A pesquisa reúne astrônomos do Japão, do Brasil e da Austrália e propõe a existência de uma super-Terra rochosa entre 200 e 500 unidades astronômicas do Sol.
Isso significa que o objeto estaria muito mais distante da estrela do que Netuno. Uma unidade astronômica corresponde à distância média entre a Terra e o Sol.
O que os cientistas encontraram?
- O Planeta X2 não foi fotografado nem observado diretamente. Sua possível existência surgiu de simulações computacionais que analisaram perturbações gravitacionais em corpos distantes do Cinturão de Kuiper, região que abriga objetos gelados além de Netuno;
- Entre os exemplos considerados pelos pesquisadores está Sedna, planeta anão que apresenta órbita bastante distante do Sol;
- Segundo o estudo, a influência gravitacional de um planeta ainda desconhecido poderia ajudar a explicar o comportamento desses objetos;
- A pesquisa foi liderada por Patryk Sofia Lykawka, da Universidade Kindai (Japão). Também participaram Pedro Bernardinelli, da Universidade de São Paulo (USP), e Jonathan Horner, da Universidade de Southern Queensland (Austrália);
- O nome X2 foi escolhido para diferenciar a hipótese de outras propostas sobre a existência de um planeta desconhecido nos limites do Sistema Solar, como o chamado Planeta Nove.
Leia mais:
- Astrônomos descobrem planeta de lava que pode se parecer com a Terra primitiva
- Planeta coberto de lava desafia cientistas ao manter atmosfera contra todas as expectativas
- Cientistas simulam como seria a Terra sem nenhuma forma de vida
Como confirmar a existência do Planeta X2?
A próxima etapa depende de observações astronômicas. Os pesquisadores esperam que o Observatório Vera C. Rubin, no Chile, ajude a testar as previsões dos modelos e a procurar sinais do movimento do possível planeta.
A distância é um dos principais obstáculos para a identificação. Como receberia pouca luz solar, o objeto teria brilho muito fraco, o que dificulta sua detecção por telescópios convencionais.
Se a hipótese for confirmada, a descoberta poderá alterar a compreensão sobre a formação do Sistema Solar, especialmente sobre a migração dos planetas gigantes nos primeiros bilhões de anos de sua história.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Vom Tiefpunkt zum Neuanfang: Björn Keune weiß, warum Gründer auf ihre Mental Health aufpassen sollten
articles.text:
Trotz Millionen auf dem Konto unglücklich: Wie dieser Gründer neuen Mut fasst – und anderen hilft
Björn Keune weiß, wie schnell wirtschaftlicher Erfolg zur persönlichen Belastung werden kann. Mit Marken wie HelloBody und Banana Beauty baute er Invincible Brands zu einem der erfolgreichsten deutschen Direct-to-Consumer-Unternehmen mit 100 Millionen Euro Umsatz auf. 2020 verkauften die Gründer die Berliner Firma an Henkel, das einen Millionenbetrag zahlte. Doch Keune kämpfte damals mit Stress, Drogen und depressiven Phasen. Heute geht er einen anderen Weg: Gemeinsam mit seiner Partnerin Sophie Pineker betreibt er Onoera. Mit ihrer Arbeit wollen sie Menschen beim Umgang mit psychischer Belastung helfen. Sie bieten Atemarbeit an, die Menschen helfen soll, mit Stress umzugehen und wieder Zugang zu ihren Gefühlen zu finden.
Im Interview spricht er über seinen persönlichen Tiefpunkt, seinen Neuanfang und darüber, warum Gründer besser auf ihre mentale Gesundheit achten sollten. Das Gespräch führte Alexander Hüsing von deutsche-startups.de.
2020 habt Ihr Invincible Brands für eine Millionensumme an Henkel verkauft. Wie hast Du diesen Moment persönlich erlebt?
Ich habe überhaupt nicht gefeiert. Nicht einmal mit meinem Team. Als das Geld auf meinem Konto landete, habe ich nichts gefühlt. Ich war völlig abgestumpft. Jahrelang hatte ich geglaubt, finanzieller Erfolg würde mir Freiheit bringen. Und dann war dieser Moment da – aber die Freude blieb aus.
Wie konnte es trotz des wirtschaftlichen Erfolgs so weit kommen?
Wir hatten Invincible Brands in kurzer Zeit von null auf 100 Millionen Umsatz aufgebaut und beschäftigten mehrere Hundert Menschen. Ich arbeitete damals 16 bis 18 Stunden am Tag. Dazu kam, dass ich zwar gut darin war, Unternehmen aufzubauen, Mitarbeiter einzustellen und Wachstum zu organisieren, mich diese Arbeit aber nie wirklich erfüllte. Ich stand unter doppeltem Druck: dem Stress als Gründer und dem Gefühl, etwas zu tun, das nicht wirklich zu mir passte.
Wie bist du damit umgegangen?
Ich wusste nicht, wie ich diesen Stress bewältigen sollte. Also habe ich versucht, ihn mit Alkohol, Drogen, Pornografie und Sex zu betäuben. Ich wollte für einen Moment nichts mehr fühlen. Auf gewisse Weise hat das sogar funktioniert. Ohne diese Ventile hätte ich die Jahre als Unternehmer vielleicht gar nicht durchgehalten. Aber es war nicht gesund. Ich wurde immer abgestumpfter und geriet in einen Teufelskreis. Weil niemand davon erfahren sollte, entstand zusätzlicher Stress, den ich auf dieselbe Weise verdrängte.
Wann hast du gemerkt, dass etwas schiefläuft?
Lange Zeit gar nicht. Ich war so sehr mit dem Unternehmen beschäftigt, dass ich kaum wahrnahm, was mit mir passierte. Irgendwann fühlte ich fast nichts mehr, hatte depressive Phasen und mein Umgang mit Drogen wurde zunehmend problematisch. Da wusste ich: Ich brauche Hilfe.
Warum hast du so lange weitergemacht?
Schon als Teenager glaubte ich, Unternehmertum und finanzieller Erfolg würden automatisch Freiheit bedeuten. Ich wollte unabhängig sein, keinen Chef haben. Also konzentrierte ich mich darauf, ein erfolgreicher Unternehmer zu werden. Erst viel später verstand ich, dass ich zwar die Fähigkeiten dafür hatte, mich diese Arbeit aber nicht erfüllte. Ich hatte nie wirklich hinterfragt, was ich eigentlich wollte.
    „Irgendwann fühlte ich fast nichts mehr, hatte depressive Phasen und mein Umgang mit Drogen wurde zunehmend problematisch.“
Du hattest vier Jahre lang einen Coach. Warum hast du ihm deine Probleme verschwiegen?
Ich habe ihm nie die ganze Wahrheit erzählt. Ich konnte meine Probleme so gut verstecken, dass selbst er nicht wusste, wie es mir ging. Ich versuchte, alles mit dem Kopf zu lösen. Dabei musste ich erst lernen, meine Gefühle wieder wahrzunehmen und anders mit Stress umzugehen.
Was hat dir schließlich geholfen?
Ich hatte bereits meditiert und einiges ausprobiert. Der Wendepunkt war für mich eine Form der Atemarbeit, das sogenannte Conscious Connected Breathwork. Dabei begleitet einen eine erfahrene Person über längere Zeit. In diesen Sitzungen konnte ich erstmals wieder Gefühle zulassen, die ich jahrelang unterdrückt hatte. Ich spürte, wie viel Stress sich angestaut hatte. Danach fühlte ich mich wieder lebendig und innerlich ruhig.
Und dein Umgang mit Alkohol und Drogen?
Der hat sich grundlegend verändert. Nach einem fünftägigen Retreat habe ich diese Mittel nicht mehr angerührt. Stress gibt es natürlich auch heute noch. Aber inzwischen weiß ich besser, wie ich damit umgehen kann. Insgesamt habe ich rund 100 solcher Sitzungen erlebt und mich intensiv mit meinen Problemen beschäftigt.
Du beschreibst das fünftägige Retreat als Wendepunkt. War das tatsächlich eine Veränderung von heute auf morgen, oder gab es danach auch Rückschläge?
Die Veränderung kam tatsächlich sofort. Gleichzeitig habe ich anfangs noch in alten Mustern gelebt. Die Integration war dann ein Prozess über mehrere Jahre – vor allem, dranzubleiben und die Praxis beizubehalten. Ich hatte schon vorher immer mal wieder Breathwork und Meditation gemacht; nach dem Retreat bin ich aber nicht wirklich in die alten Muster zurückgefallen und habe das Alte wirklich losgelassen. Natürlich ist es trotzdem Teil meiner Geschichte geblieben. Breathwork und Meditation haben mir geholfen, auf dem neuen Weg zu bleiben.
    „Wenn ich heute noch einmal gründen würde, würde ich das Unternehmen nicht verkaufen.“
Heute arbeitest du mit deiner Partnerin Sophie selbst in diesem Bereich. Warum?
Ich habe etwas gefunden, das mich wirklich erfüllt: Menschen in schwierigen Situationen zu begleiten. Mit unserer Firma Onoera bieten wir selbst solche Atemsitzungen an. Früher konnte ich Unternehmen aufbauen und Wachstum organisieren. Aber diese Arbeit gab mir nie die innere Zufriedenheit, die ich heute empfinde. Erfolg bedeutet für mich inzwischen, ein erfülltes und friedliches Leben zu führen – statt möglichst viel Geld zu verdienen.
Wenn du heute noch einmal Invincible Brands gründen würdest: Was würdest du anders machen?
Wenn ich heute noch einmal gründen würde, würde ich das Unternehmen nicht verkaufen. Ich würde es als Ort und Arbeitsplatz behalten, um die Dinge, die mir heute wichtig sind – Breathwork, Meditation und eine ehrliche, authentische Entwicklung von Menschen – vielen Menschen zugänglich zu machen. Der Verkauf von Produkten wäre dabei eher Mittel zum Zweck; das Unternehmen und seine Kultur würden sich um das drehen, was ich gelernt habe.
Die Startup-Szene feiert Finanzierungsrunden, Wachstum und Exits. Ist das Teil des Problems?
Für mich persönlich war das nicht entscheidend. Ich stand trotz unseres wirtschaftlichen Erfolgs nie besonders in der Öffentlichkeit. Und ich finde es auch nicht falsch, große Finanzierungsrunden oder Exits zu feiern. Aber wir sollten genauer hinschauen, wie es den Menschen dabei geht. Was bringt eine erfolgreiche Finanzierungsrunde, wenn man innerlich völlig am Ende ist?
    „Heute ermutige ich junge Gründer, in die ich investiert habe, sich Zeit für Coaching, Meditation und andere Unterstützung zu nehmen.“
Welche Verantwortung tragen Investoren?
Investoren sollten Gründer ermutigen, sich Zeit für ihre mentale Gesundheit zu nehmen. Ich glaubte damals, rund um die Uhr arbeiten zu müssen, um von meinen Investoren respektiert zu werden. Rückblickend war das wohl vor allem eine Geschichte, die ich mir selbst erzählt habe. Schließlich hatten sie viel Geld auf mich gesetzt. Wenn ich in einen Burnout oder eine Depression gerate, gewinnt niemand. Heute ermutige ich junge Gründer, in die ich investiert habe, sich Zeit für Coaching, Meditation und andere Unterstützung zu nehmen.
Was rätst Du Gründern, die selbst in eine solche Abwärtsspirale geraten?
Sucht Euch Unterstützung. Versucht nicht, alles allein zu lösen. Als Gründer trägt man viel Verantwortung – für Mitarbeiter, Investoren, das Unternehmen und die Familie. Mir hat es enorm geholfen, diese Last einmal abgeben zu können. Entscheidend ist, einen Weg zu finden, mit Stress umzugehen, statt ihn ständig zu verdrängen. Unternehmertum muss nicht zwangsläufig bedeuten, dass man darunter leidet.

articles.title: How NVIDIA Connects Startups to Build an AI Ecosystem
articles.text:
For AI startups, the real challenge is often not building AI itself, but getting it to work reliably in the real world.
From the hands-on expertise of veteran workers on manufacturing floors and robots operating autonomously around the clock to the unstructured environments of construction sites and the vast amounts of data and complex workflows inside enterprises, AI must overcome more than technical barriers. It must also address challenges involving data, deployment, customers and commercialization. For AI startups, overcoming these “last-mile” challenges is key to moving technology into real-world industrial applications.
NVIDIA’s Inception Program is designed around these needs. By leveraging NVIDIA’s computing platforms and software tools, startups can bring their innovations into vertical markets such as manufacturing, robotics, construction and enterprise software, contributing to the broader industrial ecosystem. At the same time, the problems and requirements startups encounter in real-world applications can feed back into NVIDIA’s development tools and ecosystem.
The Inception Program aims to serve as the first point of entry for startups seeking to work with NVIDIA. It provides a gateway into the NVIDIA ecosystem, allowing startups to learn about available resources while giving NVIDIA visibility into the startups using its technologies.
NVIDIA Inception Extends from Technology Resources to Market Access
Unlike traditional accelerators with fixed curricula, application cycles and graduation processes, NVIDIA Inception is more like an open startup ecosystem and a key resource partner, helping members move from technology development to products and markets.
“NVIDIA Inception is not a conventional accelerator program.” Its biggest difference is that it does not have fixed application cycles, training curriculum or single development path. Instead, it first identifies a startup’s “most pressing needs” and then provides the appropriate development tools, hardware and software benefits, technical training and support, while connecting startups with investors, partners and international market resources.
Startups that are already using AI tools to develop applications, or that expect to need AI technologies as they develop their products, may be suitable for the program.
Early-stage teams may need GPUs, software development kits (SDKs), and hardware and software benefits. As they move into the productization stage, their needs shift toward technology, funding, talent and customers. Inception members can access NVIDIA SDKs, pretrained models, development platforms and training courses from the Deep Learning Institute (DLI), while NVIDIA GTC, the Inception pavilion at InnoVEX, and the NVIDIA Venture Capital Alliance can help startups connect with partners and overseas markets.
As AI applications continue to expand rapidly, the types of startups covered by the Inception Program have also evolved. Early members included companies working in gaming, data science and 3D simulation. Generative AI became mainstream after 2023, while Agentic AI, biomedical technologies and Physical AI have recently attracted continued attention. However, the number of members is not the only measure of the program’s success. NVIDIA places greater emphasis on whether startups use these resources to secure actual funding, commercial contracts and key customers, as well as achieve product-market fit (PMF).
From technology resources to market connections, the role of the Inception Program also changes as startups progress through different stages of development. The experiences of Holon Robotics, Nexuni, ROSO and Profet AI reflect the different challenges AI startups face as they move from technology development to industrial deployment. How platform resources connect with those needs is also critical to the continued expansion of the AI ecosystem.
Holon Robotics: Turning Veteran Know-How Into Robot Capabilities
In traditional manufacturing environments, the challenge of adopting AI is not simply model accuracy, but how to digitize and continuously preserve hard-to-quantify “domain knowledge.” Holon Robotics has developed its own robot operating system, HolonOS, as its core platform, integrating robotic arms from multiple brands, sensors and AI technologies, with a focus on processes such as grinding, polishing, welding and surface treatment.
Holon Robotics founder and CEO Yuan-Chieh Lo said these tasks rely heavily on the experience and intuitive “feel” that veteran workers develop over years of practice, making them among the most difficult aspects of traditional manufacturing automation to standardize. At the same time, workpiece conditions vary across grinding and polishing processes, making real-world data difficult to obtain and turning manufacturing data itself into an important asset.
To model and predict how material removal changes over time during metal surface processing, Holon has adopted Real-to-Sim and Sim-to-Real technologies and architectures. The company combines real-world physical sensing data with the NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and Newton physics engine for simulation, then deploys the resulting training outcomes to physical robots, creating a cycle of “data → AI training → virtual simulation → robot execution → data feedback.” Even workers without programming backgrounds can complete deployment within minutes, substantially lowering the barrier to robot adoption while allowing manufacturers to focus more on production and preserving accumulated expertise.
NVIDIA’s GPU computing platform, 3D vision and simulation capabilities enable Holon to expand its training scenarios while reducing the cost of physical testing. Lo said Taiwan’s diverse and densely connected manufacturing environment serves as an important “training ground,” while the accumulated workpiece and process data can also provide a foundation for entering overseas markets.
Nexuni: Building a Robot AI Brain for Around-the-Clock Autonomous Operation
While Holon focuses on digitizing manufacturing knowledge, Nexuni is addressing a different challenge: how to turn AI-powered robots into productive tools capable of working for extended periods. Nexuni believes that labor shortages are making automation not merely a means of improving efficiency, but increasingly a necessity for maintaining industrial operations. The company therefore focuses on welding as well as inspections of critical facilities that require 24-hour shifts or around-the-clock operation.
Nexuni has developed a general-purpose robot brain, Nexuni Intelligent Robot Orchestration (NIRO), which uses an Agentic AI architecture and vision-language-action (VLA) models to allow on-site personnel to issue complex task commands in natural language. Combined with sensing technologies such as LiDAR and 3D vision, the system adjusts its actions based on environmental perception, localization, planning and control results, and is applied in areas including intelligent inspection and intelligent welding.
Nexuni said that when it first joined the NVIDIA Inception Program, it valued NVIDIA’s resources and hardware benefits. As product development progressed, however, NVIDIA’s technical support and software tools became increasingly important. The team uses edge computing platforms including the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin and NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor for robot deployment, and uses software such as NVIDIA Omniverse and NVIDIA Isaac Sim to build 3D digital-twin environments. It reproduces varying conditions such as lighting, ground materials and object placement in simulation for reinforcement-learning training, then transfers the trained policies to physical robots through Sim-to-Real, significantly shortening on-site tuning and deployment time.
Nexuni General Manager Chiang-Chuan Chen said, “A proof of concept (POC) may take only 10 minutes, but actual deployment is a 24-hour, nonstop test.” A robot completing a task once in a demonstration environment does not mean it can operate continuously in a factory. It must also rely on NIRO to handle sensor anomalies, environmental changes, localization errors and long-duration operation. NVIDIA’s role has therefore expanded from hardware resources to software tools and technical support, helping bring robots’ AI capabilities into real-world environments.
ROSO: Physical AI Takes on Unstructured Construction Environments
As AI moves from standardized production lines into construction sites, environmental uncertainty increases significantly, raising the demands on perception, decision-making and control. Founded by teams from Feng Chia University (FCU) and National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (NYCU), ROSO combines computational architectural design, spatial computing and robot control to develop large-scale customized 3D printing of architectural and artistic structures, as well as robots for spraying, putty application and sanding on indoor walls and ceilings.
Shih-Yuan Wang, associate professor at the Graduate Institute of Architecture at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University and co-founder of ROSO, said that construction sites are constantly changing in terms of work locations, materials and personnel. Robots therefore cannot rely solely on fixed paths, but must also be able to perceive their surroundings, make decisions and adjust their movements. This is at the core of Physical AI: AI must do more than process text or images; it must perceive, make decisions and precisely control machines in the real physical world.
In terms of hardware architecture, ROSO integrates an autonomous mobile robot (AMR) base with a multi-axis robotic arm, using the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin as its edge computing core. It also incorporates NVIDIA cuMotion and vision AI sensors to handle dynamic obstacle avoidance and path replanning, while using Isaac Sim software for simulation and testing.
ROSO also brings its robots directly onto actual construction sites to validate the technology, accumulating data from dynamic environments through real-world projects. The company is currently planning to establish joint laboratories with international academic research institutions and is actively expanding into overseas markets. Technically, ROSO is targeting an automation rate of more than 80% and moving toward autonomous collaboration among multiple robots.
Profet AI: From Enterprise Knowledge to Process Execution for Governable Manufacturing AI
On the enterprise software side, AI adoption faces another challenge: how to bring existing data, models and enterprise knowledge into actual workflows. High-tech manufacturers, particularly in semiconductors, semiconductor packaging and testing, and PCBs, face pressure to shorten new product introduction (NPI) and failure analysis (FA) timelines, as well as knowledge-transfer and collaboration bottlenecks caused by the turnover of experienced engineers.
Profet AI has long focused on AI for manufacturing. The company initially entered the market through automated machine learning (AutoML) and has in recent years expanded into an enterprise AI Agent operations platform, Domain Twin. Hsing-Kuang Chen, special assistant to the CEO of Profet AI, said, “Enterprises actually do not lack algorithms or models. What they really lack is a way to connect domain knowledge, business processes, data and access controls to create a secure and controllable execution environment.”
Profet AI therefore focuses on Domain, Governance and Execution. It converts the experience of senior engineers, engineering documents, process data and decision logic into enterprise knowledge that can be used, managed and reused by AI. Through access controls, human verification and operation logs, Agents can connect to manufacturing execution systems (MES), enterprise resource planning (ERP), product lifecycle management (PLM) and other IT/OT systems within clearly defined boundaries, participating in cross-department workflows and task execution.
For applications involving semiconductor equipment, Profet AI is also deploying AI Agents on the engineering and equipment side to support knowledge retrieval, anomaly analysis and equipment troubleshooting. The company has also introduced the concept of an “AI Factory,” enabling multiple Agents to work collaboratively within existing systems and workflows. Through Domain Twin’s access-control and governance mechanisms, Agents can participate in task execution and cross-department collaboration within clearly defined boundaries. Profet AI says it now has more than 400 enterprise customers and 5,500 successful deployment cases, and continues to help manufacturers expand AI from point applications to deployment across workflows, production lines and factories.
Crossing the AI Ecosystem’s Last Mile: A Two-Way Platform-to-Application Loop
The innovation journeys of these four AI startups, despite spanning different vertical markets, point to a common challenge at the heart of AI commercialization: as foundation models and general-purpose computing become increasingly accessible, differentiation in AI deployment depends more heavily on industry knowledge, deployment experience and real-world data.
Holon converts the tacit know-how of veteran workers into structured data that robots can understand; Nexuni focuses on long-duration autonomous robot operation; ROSO brings Physical AI into highly dynamic, unstructured construction environments; and Profet AI brings enterprise knowledge and workflows into AI Agent governance and execution.
Throughout this process, NVIDIA provides development tools, simulation, technical support and international market connections, while startups bring these capabilities into different industries, accumulate data and experience through real-world deployment, and then feed their requirements and feedback back to the platform. This is not simply a one-way technology supply relationship. Instead, it creates a continuous two-way loop between the platform and applications.
The core value of the NVIDIA Inception Program lies not in how many events it organizes or how many matchmaking opportunities it facilitates, but in whether it can help startups “shorten the time to success.” As AI competition increasingly expands from cloud-based models and general-purpose computing to the front lines of industry, this two-way platform-to-application loop will be key to helping AI cross the last mile and continue to bring AI into real-world industrial applications.

articles.title: The loneliest peptide party in New York
articles.text:
This is Optimizer, a weekly newsletter sent from Verge senior reviewer Victoria Song that dissects and discusses the latest gizmos and potions that swear they’re going to change your life. Opt in for Optimizer here.
The loneliest peptide party in New York
The peptide curious are looking for answers, and finding dubious products instead.
On a rainy fall evening, an experimental art venue in Chelsea Market had a small line out the door. There are always lines in New York City. Viral food trends, gallery exhibitions, pop-ups, and parties. The folks in line looked like your average joe, ready for a Friday night on the town. You wouldn’t look twice — except, perhaps, for a man with a wizard beard and a laser sword strapped to his back.
Inside, the man with a laser sword stood in the middle of the cavernous bottom floor of a two-story warehouse strewn with large bean bags. On the wall were psychedelic projections of jellyfish, shrimp, and other sea creatures. A bizarre choice, considering peptides won’t induce any trippy vision quests, and not a single person was getting groovy. The industrial beams had posters with QR codes that you could scan to get samples of Afterglow, a new type of peptide product. According to seemingly discarded pamphlets around the venue, Afterglow isn’t a standard injectable or oral peptide. The company makes strips that dissolve under the tongue. The “Afterglow Peptide Field Guide” also described what each sample does, dosing recommendations, and potential side effects. At the upstairs bar, bartenders mixed custom cocktails called Afterburn — complete with bioluminescent veggie nectar — and Margatrutide. (For the record, a bioluminescent veggie nectar cocktail tastes as awful as you think.)
Welcome to a peptide launch party.
Peptide parties are old news in San Francisco, but they’re somewhat more novel in New York City. Milling around the edges of the venue were various reporters and photographers. We were all trying to get a sense of why anyone had bothered to come out. Not that many did. Despite the venue’s size, the main floor had plenty of empty space.
One person I spoke to was a fencer with sore joints. They’d heard that one of the peptides might help with recovery. Another had a father in the wellness industry and had heard vague things about how effective peptides could be. One woman, staring at a projected jellyfish, merely shrugged. Her friend was more into “wellness stuff” and she had no plans, so, why not check out a party? A man, staring into his bag of Afterglow samples, was mostly interested in weight loss but scared about the safety of gray market products. A few feet away, another man was furiously reading the Afterglow pamphlet. “I like to know what I put in my body,” he said.
The only problem was he didn’t remember which sample he had tried.
A common refrain: Well, this beats doing research online. This, at least, was a social event where you could theoretically connect with other people. And there were clusters of strangers speaking to each other. Mostly, near the bar. Everywhere else, people stared awkwardly on their phones, their eyes occasionally roaming the room without meeting anyone else’s gaze for more than a second or two. After a while, they’d disappear into the back room and reappear with a goody bag full of peptide samples.
After 90 minutes, I decided to leave. For the umpteenth time that evening, I’d walked up to someone, asked about peptides, and got a noncommittal “I really don’t know anything — I just came to learn more.” (When asked if they had, they invariably shrugged and pointed to the goody bag.) It was clear that the only peptide evangelists here were likely associated with the launch. The whole thing, to me, seemed as if someone had tried to draw a cool party from memory. The last thing I saw was a person draped in a ghost sheet sitting alone in the corner.
As it turned out, the man with the laser sword was a performance artist who’d been invited to attend. Out of journalistic integrity, I asked if he had ever tried peptides. He told me he was more interested in the unifying energy of the universe. When I got up to leave, he waved and said, “Giggles.”
If I were peptide curious, the Afterglow launch party was a pretty awful way to learn anything about these substances. To be fair, Afterglow’s Partiful invitation mostly described this event as “an environment great for aura farming” and the “hard launch of [its] first of many experiments in culture.” Nevertheless, as part of the press, I did walk away with a smattering of Afterglow’s products. In total, I got packets of what Afterglow calls Charge (NAD+), Rejuvenate (glutathione), Wolverine Blend (BPC-157 / TB-500), Strength Blend (CJC-1295 / Ipamorelin), Glow Blend (GHK-Cu / BPC-157 / TB-500), Connect (PT-141), GLP-2 (tirzepatide), and GLP-3 (retatrutide). Or at least that’s what the packaging says. There’s no way to truly verify gray market peptides for safety or efficacy because they’re unregulated products.
First of all, last I checked, GLP-1 medications do not upgrade like iPhone models. Afterglow’s pamphlet correctly lists that your body has “three hormone switches”: GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon. The accompanying descriptors of what each does are broadly correct, though lacking in nuance. For example, there is a hormone called glucagon-like peptide 2, but it’s not tirzepatide. The “real” GLP-2 is a hormone related to intestinal health. Tirzepatide is still considered a GLP-1 medication that’s a dual agonist because it works on two hormones (GLP-1 and GIP.) The GLP-2 moniker is a misnomer popularized by ill-informed influencers. The same goes for retatrutide, which, as of this writing, is still an unapproved GLP-1 medication that works on three hormones (GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon) and is therefore a triple agonist. There is no such thing as GLP-3.
For all the samples, there were no instructions regarding dosing on the packaging — just another QR code leading to Afterglow’s product page. Those pages happen to contain instructions for how to use the strips, and the amount of product within the strips. There are disclaimers about how little studied the compounds are, but nothing about interactions, side effects, or what to expect while taking. Just a throwaway line to talk to your doctor.
All that information, you’d have to find on the pamphlet given at the party. (Ironically, some “important cautions” on the pamphlet state to avoid taking samples with alcohol, at a party where the booze was flowing.) Provided you didn’t throw it out. One would hope that information is on a box if you were to buy directly from the seller. But for all intents and purposes, what I just described is what a clueless partygoer would have to go on.
If everything in that pamphlet were 100 percent factual, perhaps a conscientious partygoer could feel reassured. On that front, I have bad news. The pamphlet calls PT-141 an “FDA-approved peptide that boosts sexual desire for both men and women.”
PT-141, also known as bremelanotide or Vyleesi, is FDA approved. But only for premenopausal women suffering from hypoactive sexual desire disorder. It is not approved for post-menopausal women, men, or for general sexual performance enhancement.
Another concern: How does one evaluate a sublingual peptide strip? Specifically, is this delivery method even scientifically proven effective in humans? Spoiler: It’s not! A collapsible FAQ menu on Afterglow’s site states, “We don’t know yet. Nobody has published how much of most peptides reaches the blood from a strip compared with an injection. We’re funding studies to measure exactly that, and we’ll share what we find.”
As for why you’d want to even try a sublingual strip? Afterglow’s website suggests it’s more convenient than injections or pills. No refrigeration, no needles, and no need for learning how to reconstitute a drug. Just pop a strip under the tongue and go.
And good luck trying to find reputable sources of information on your own. Afterglow says it’s funding its own research, but its site has no reviewable documentation just yet. A Google search brings up a questionable AI overview, a handful of links from dubious med spas, a couple of dead links, and one PubMed study in mice. Most of the links also primarily discuss the difference between oral peptides in pill form and injectables — so not terribly relevant here.
I’d consider it fair game if I were confident that anyone at the party I went to did their due diligence. As it stands, I talked with over a dozen people who were mostly there for vibes, booze, and freebies.
Not all peptide parties are created equal. Some happen on WWII cargo ships, complete with panel discussions about peptide supply chains. Another “peptide 101” talk I attended in New York happened at the back of a bitcoin bar. There, most attendees also knew very little about peptides, but at least they got treated to a PowerPoint presentation about the basics. There was a dubious demonstration of how to inject oneself that would’ve probably made any pharmacist or doctor scream. But at the very least, peptides were defined and attendees could ask questions. (The answers to those questions were on the right track with regard to the dangers of the gray market. They were less reliable about scientific rigor and why “anecdotal evidence” is not the same as clinical evidence of safety.)
But a striking, recurring theme is just how much is unknown. These substances aren’t well-studied in humans, so there’s not much evidence as to long-term benefits or side effects. The peptide curious know shocking little about the substances they’re supposedly interested in. Likewise, it’s incredibly difficult to get reliable, unbiased data on gray market interest or usage, though there have been attempts to quantify this surging demand in recent months. Case in point, telehealth provider Hims & Hers just conducted a consumer survey of roughly 2,000 American adults. Of those surveyed, 68 percent said they had little to no knowledge about peptides. Less than 18 percent were even able to identify that peptides are chains of amino acids. Even so, 40 percent said they were interested or very interested in trying injectable prescription treatments — including peptides — if offered by a telehealth service.
Even so, peptides are everywhere. The word appears in copious ads for skincare creams, weight loss drugs, and supplements. Looksmaxxers, influencers, and celebrities like Gwyneth Paltrow and Joe Rogan talk about them in podcasts, documentaries, and social media as if they’re miracle shortcuts. Hims & Hers has even announced it’s launching a service called Peptide Plus — nevermind that the vast majority of what it’ll offer are not actual peptides.
In this kind of environment, of course more people will become peptide curious. Which makes it even more concerning that the most readily available information sources are not medical or scientific experts well-versed on the topic at hand. There are dubious links online summarized into less-than-critical AI overviews. There are pamphlets handed out at weird parties, where there’s more booze and schmooze than education. Influencers branding themselves as experts as they flash crudely summarized studies in a bar back room. Industry panels that are inaccessible to the average consumer, full of jargon and assumed knowledge of the science at hand.
It’s clear something needs to be done until general knowledge improves. Until then, the parties will continue.

articles.title: El Gobierno aprueba en Consejo de Ministros la prohibición de los váper de sabores. La razón es su repunte en adolescentes
articles.text:
Este martes el Consejo de Ministros llegó cargado de cambios de gran relevancia en el ámbito social y también fiscal, pero a otros cambios legislativos no se les dio tanta publicidad. Uno de ellos es la modificación del Real Decreto 579/2017 para prohibir los sabores en los cigarrillos electrónicos y regular por primera vez las bolsas de nicotina con el objetivo de evitar que los adolescentes caigan en este producto nocivo.
Bajo la espera. En este momento solo tenemos en las notas de este Consejo de Ministros este cambio legislativo, pero en el BOE no ha aparecido reflejado. En este caso, las fuentes del Ministerio de Sanidad citadas por Europa Press apuntan a que la norma aparecerá publicada en el BOE el próximo lunes.
Lo que cambia. A falta de leer el articulado final en el BOE, el decreto se enmarca dentro del Plan Integral de Prevención y Control del Tabaquismo 2024-2027 y rescata parte de la ofensiva antitabaco después de que la reforma integral de la Ley del Tabaco, que se tramitaba en paralelo, decayera tras el adelanto electoral.
De esta manera, si nos ceñimos a los documentos publicados previamente, esta norma llegaría a prohibir los aromas y sabores artificiales o dulces en los cigarrillos electrónicos. Solo se permitirá el aroma a tabaco con el objetivo explícito de restar atractivo a estos dispositivos entre los menores. Pero además, se incorporan como nueva categoría legal las bolsas de nicotina con el objetivo de que pasen un control sanitario que antes no existía, además de limitar su concentración de nicotina.
Los datos. El argumento del Ministerio de Sanidad para blindar estas medidas antes del cierre de la legislatura está en la encuesta ESTUDES 2025 del Plan Nacional sobre Drogas, elaborada a partir de 35.256 entrevistas a estudiantes de Secundaria de entre 14 y 18 años. En esta se apuntaba a que el 40,8 % de los estudiantes afirma haber vapeado en los últimos 12 meses, lo que supone un descenso de 5,1 puntos porcentuales respecto a 2023.
Además, el consumo en los últimos 30 días, que es el referente para conocer el uso regular, repuntó del 26,3% al 27,1%. Es por ello que, para Sanidad, esa resistencia del consumo mensual demuestra que los sabores frutales y dulces siguen actuando como puerta de entrada y fidelización entre los menores.
La patronal. En el plano económico, la industria también ha puesto cifras sobre la mesa para oponerse a la medida. La Unión de Promotores y Empresarios del Vapeo (UPEV) asegura que el veto a los sabores pone en riesgo 4.650 empleos y a más de 450 pymes especializadas, apoyándose en una estimación de la consultora Afi que cifra el impacto potencial en hasta 328 millones de euros en valor añadido. Es por ello que afean que no se haya contado con ellos antes de aplicar una medida que afecta económicamente de una manera tan importante.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Unpatched Flaw in Defunct Idunno AntiCsrf Library
articles.text:
Threat actors are exploiting an unpatched vulnerability in the open source anti-CSRF library Idunno AntiCsrf for remote code execution (RCE), security researchers warn.
AntiCsrf is a legacy ASP.NET module for WebForms applications that has no active maintainer and is no longer actively supported. The most recent version, 0.9.1 Beta, was released in December 2008.
Tracked as CVE-2026-131914 (CVSS score of 9.3), the exploited security defect is described as an insecure deserialization bug in the processing of HTTP POST requests to ASP.NET WebForms endpoints.
“Exploitation requires only a single HTTP POST request with no prior authentication or valid CSRF token. Active exploitation in the wild has been observed,” Google Cloud’s Mandiant warned on November 18.
The flaw allows an attacker to supply any non-empty value in the CSRF cookie along with a Base64-encoded gadget chain to gain RCE in the context of the IIS worker process, Mandiant notes.
According to preemptive cybersecurity firm WatchTowr, the issue exists because AntiCsrf does not perform sufficient checks on data from incoming form submissions before reconstructing it into program objects.
“The vulnerable check runs before the application’s own page logic, so it can affect many pages on an affected site, not just ones that use a login form. A successful attack gives the attacker control over the process that runs the website, which can lead to full compromise of the server,” WatchTowr says.
On Tuesday, the US cybersecurity agency CISA added CVE-2026-131914 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list, urging federal agencies to address it within three days.
As no official patch is available for the vulnerability, all organizations relying on the 18-year-old AntiCsrf to validate anti-CSRF tokens on form submissions should immediately discontinue the module and transition to an actively supported solution.
“WatchTowr Intel detected exploit probes across our honeypots that used creative .NET compiled gadget payloads to confirm if a given system is vulnerable. We validated the exploit and confirmed that, if the host was vulnerable, the server would be tricked into redirecting to a unique URL that would discreetly confirm control of the web server to the attacker,” WatchTowr principal threat intelligence specialist Yordan Ganchev told SecurityWeek.
“There is no patch, and likely there won’t be one. Defenders should audit ASP.NET products to identify ones packaging the Idunno.AntiCSRF library and review their audit logs for signs of exploitation. Where possible, the library should be replaced in affected applications. Where that’s not possible, apply WAF rules until alternative workarounds are identified,” Ganchev added.

articles.title: Real Ventures returns with sixth fund and a refreshed accelerator program
articles.text:
Annual general meetings for venture funds don’t typically feature a musical performance.
“We’re looking to help you build the conditions for commercial success, but not at the expense of the purpose that you’re about.”
John Stokes, Real Ventures
But Montréal’s Real Ventures has never played by the rules. At the firm’s AGM in September, partner Katy Yam serenaded attendees (including portfolio companies and limited partners) with a karaoke rendition of the Broadway hit Defying Gravity. The moment felt significant; after a fundraising hiatus, Defying Gravity was the theme of Real’s AGM, highlighting a unique, against-the-grain vision the firm was putting forward for its first new fundraise since 2017.
Real Ventures announced the first close of its sixth pre-seed fund on Wednesday, along with the relaunch of its flagship accelerator program, FounderFuel. The fund, officially called Antifragile Fund I, has announced a first close of $45 million, anchored by the Government of Québec and several returning LPs, like Desjardins Capital, Fonds de solidarité FTQ, Teralys Capital (through the La Caisse-backed Fonds québécois d’amorçage Teralys), and BDC Capital (through its Black Entrepreneurs Fund). Targeting a $60-million total, the fund represents a remarkable comeback for a firm that paused fundraising in 2022 following a number of key departures, and whose future was uncertain amid a venture market downturn.
The comeback accompanies an evolution of the fund’s ethos and approach, according to managing partner John Stokes. The partners are looking to find and nurture founders “daring to question the systems we all depend on,” from sectors like energy and healthcare to civic infrastructure, he said in an interview.
Part of that means resisting the pull toward maximizing shareholder value over all else, including company values and mission. Some principles come from the book Incorruptible: Why Good Companies Go Bad and How Great Companies Stay Great, by American entrepreneur and author Eric Ries, which Real handed out to attendees at its AGM. In an era where corporate profits often seem to trump all other considerations, Real is making a bet on alternative ways of building startups where purpose and profit can stay on the same track.
“We’re looking to help you build the conditions for commercial success, but not at the expense of the purpose that you’re about,” Stokes said.
RELATED: Real Ventures launches revamped fellowship program for founder well-being
The first eight companies Real selects for FounderFuel, its Montréal-based, five-month accelerator program, will get to try out this approach. Though Real had run the program for years up until 2023, backing startups like BenchSci and Transit, this is the first time that it will make FounderFuel core to its fund thesis.
The idea is to invest $500,000 CAD into each cohort company at the pre-seed stage, reserving follow-on capital as well. In some cases, Real will consider investment opportunities outside of the accelerator cohort. Stokes and Montréal-based partners Sam Haffar and Katy Yam will all act as investment partners and be “hands-on” in the FounderFuel program. Stokes said Real is open to backing companies across Canada but expects FounderFuel participants to be in Montréal for the program’s duration.
“If you look at the fast pace of technological evolution…it has become even more difficult to be an entrepreneur,” Beatrice Couture, principal at Teralys Capital, said in an interview. “What Real figured out over the years is that founders who don’t have the resilience and capacity to grow with their company might break.”
Resilience is a familiar notion for today’s Real Ventures team. Co-founded in 2007 by Stokes, JS Cournoyer, and Alan MacIntosh before Canada’s venture capital (VC) industry took off, it notched some early successes. Real went on to back notable startups like League, Mejuri, and Sonder, establishing itself as one of Canada’s top pre-seed investors.
In 2022, following the 2021 VC boom and subsequent bust, as well as leadership shake-ups, Real paused raising its sixth fund. Toronto-based managing partner Janet Bannister stepped back from her role and later left to launch her own founder-focused early-stage firm, Staircase Ventures. BetaKit reported at the time that investors weren’t pleased with Real’s fund performance, and that having leadership outside Québec hadn’t helped.
Stokes said the major market headwinds coincided with a shift among LPs about the right balance between a fund’s value and how much capital it returned—a fine line that he acknowledged Real didn’t walk that well. “We were clearly going through a transition as we moved from the founding team of Real to those that would take it on to the next level, and we were doing that at a time when there were a lot of challenges,” Stokes said. Since then, he added, Real has had “amazing support” from its LPs.
Indeed, several of its investors have now returned. The AI boom has wrought returns in the intervening years, from portfolio companies like AI chipmaker Tenstorrent and physical AI scaleup Vention, which, respectively, have returned the entire value and half the value of Real’s third $89-million fund. Real has also earned industry honours for top deals, such as its support of live event commerce platform atVenu.
RELATED: Real Ventures partners with Panache, Inovia to relaunch FounderFuel accelerator
And despite a recent change in provincial government, the Québec government is participating as a key investor through Investissement Québec. Its support of Real Ventures (up to $30 million) was part of a broader announcement to back three local funds, including AQC Capital’s third fund, which is receiving up to $50 million, and ACET Capital’s fourth fund at up to $25 million.
Stéphane Paquet, Québec’s Minister of Economic Development, Innovation and Energy, said in a French statement that the investment will help local entrepreneurs “transform their innovations into commercial successes” and share Québec’s expertise with the world.
Having Real and FounderFuel back in the ecosystem is an exciting prospect, according to Couture. “They have shown over the years that they are able to find these outlier companies before anyone else,” she said. “I hope that they will do it again this time.”
Feature image courtesy Real Ventures.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.text:
AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
- Date:
  November 14, 2026
- Source:
  University of California - Berkeley
- Summary:
  Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.
- Share:
More than 300,000 people in the United States die from sudden cardiac arrest each year. This deadly emergency occurs when the heart's electrical system suddenly fails, causing the heart to stop pumping blood. It can strike older adults with known heart conditions as well as seemingly healthy young athletes. Although implanted defibrillators can prevent some of these deaths, doctors have long struggled to determine which patients need them most.
Now, researchers at UC Berkeley have identified a previously overlooked warning signal in routine heart scans that could make it easier to recognize people at risk before a fatal event occurs.
The discovery was made using artificial intelligence trained on more than 440,000 electrocardiograms, or EKGs, collected in Sweden. By comparing the electrical patterns recorded in these scans with information from death certificates, the researchers taught an AI system to recognize subtle differences between healthy individuals, patients with known heart risks, and people who eventually died from sudden cardiac causes.
The team then evaluated the technology using thousands of additional patient records from the United States and Taiwan, testing whether the patterns could reliably identify people at heightened risk in different populations.
AI Detects Hidden Heart Risks That Standard Tests Miss
The results suggest that AI can identify vulnerable patients more effectively than the conventional tests doctors typically rely on. Current screening methods largely focus on how much blood the heart pumps with each contraction, a measurement used to assess whether someone might benefit from an implanted defibrillator.
Using these traditional measurements, doctors can identify a group of patients with an annual sudden cardiac death rate of 4.6%. The AI system, however, identified a group with an annual death rate of 7%, demonstrating a greater ability to distinguish patients facing serious danger.
Importantly, the algorithm also recognized a broader population of people at elevated risk, including thousands who would not normally raise concerns under existing medical guidelines. Most of these individuals would have been classified as relatively low risk using conventional methods.
Another major advantage is that the AI system works with ordinary EKG images, which are already routinely collected in hospitals and medical centers around the world. This means the technology could potentially improve screening without requiring an entirely new type of medical test.
The findings, published in Nature, could eventually help physicians make more informed decisions about who should receive an implanted defibrillator. They also raise an intriguing scientific question about what changes inside the heart produce the electrical patterns that AI has learned to recognize.
"Medical decisions are really hard, and I think that's why AI is so exciting for me," said Ziad Obermeyer, an associate professor at UC Berkeley's School of Public Health and the study's lead author. "We can not only make better decisions, but also start to understand what's actually going on with these patients before their heart stops."
Why Sudden Cardiac Death Is So Difficult to Predict
Sudden cardiac arrest is different from a heart attack. A heart attack happens when blood flow to part of the heart becomes blocked or severely restricted. Cardiac arrest, by contrast, results from a failure of the electrical signals that coordinate the heartbeat.
Immediate CPR and an electrical shock from an automated external defibrillator can sometimes restore the heart's rhythm. However, roughly 90% of people who experience sudden cardiac arrest outside a hospital die within minutes, making early recognition of those at risk especially important.
For Obermeyer, an emergency physician whose research combines artificial intelligence, medicine, and health policy, sudden cardiac death remains one of medicine's most frustrating unsolved problems.
Because victims often die without warning, researchers have limited opportunities to observe what happens inside the heart immediately before it stops. An autopsy may uncover blocked blood vessels, hardened tissue, or other structural abnormalities, but it cannot fully reveal how the heart was functioning in the moments leading up to death.
"One thing that makes the problem very tragic, but also very well suited for AI, is that we have the cure for this problem," Obermeyer said. "If you knew you were one of the people who was going to drop dead, you would go to a cardiologist and you'd get a defibrillator implanted. The problem is that doctors can't figure out who needs one before it's too late."
The Problem With Current Heart Risk Screening
Doctors currently rely heavily on a measurement of how effectively the heart pushes blood out with each beat. Patients whose hearts pump below a specified threshold may be considered candidates for an implantable cardioverter defibrillator, a device that can deliver an electrical shock when a dangerous heart rhythm develops.
But obtaining this measurement generally requires a more extensive medical evaluation. Many people who eventually experience sudden cardiac arrest never receive such testing because they have no obvious reason to suspect they are in danger.
The approach also has limitations for patients who are identified as high risk. About two-thirds of implanted defibrillators in these patients never need to deliver a shock. As a result, many individuals undergo expensive, invasive procedures for potentially fatal emergencies that may never occur.
At the same time, thousands of people who are not recognized as being at risk die unexpectedly each year.
"In some fraction of those people, we could have prevented those deaths if we had just known it in time," Obermeyer said. "There are a lot of lives being lost from people who are dropping dead of sudden cardiac death that are preventable if we just had better AI tools to find these things."
The researchers hope that identifying more accurate warning signs could help doctors direct preventive treatments toward the patients most likely to benefit.
How Researchers Trained AI to Recognize Deadly Heart Patterns
Developing the algorithm required three independent collections of medical data gathered from different parts of the world.
The researchers began with six years of EKG recordings from Sweden's unified healthcare system. By linking these scans to death certificates, they could examine the electrical patterns of patients who later experienced sudden cardiac death and compare them with those of other patients.
The AI learned to identify combinations of spikes, waves, and other characteristics in the recordings that appeared to be associated with increased risk. Once the system had been trained, the team tested it against two additional datasets: two years of anonymized EKG records from a San Diego hospital system and a separate collection of patient data from Taipei.
This international testing helped researchers evaluate whether the algorithm's predictive abilities extended beyond the Swedish population used to develop it.
"Good AI starts with good data," said Obermeyer, who is also part of the joint UCSF-UC Berkeley Computational Precision Health program. "Unfortunately, data like the ones we used for this study are incredibly hard to access. It's a big part of why there's so little clinical AI in use today."
Obtaining and organizing the information was itself a massive undertaking. According to Obermeyer, assembling the datasets took approximately 10 years and involved contributions from two organizations he helped establish, Dandelion Health and Nightingale Open Science. Both organizations work to advance medical research through better access to data and artificial intelligence.
"It's one of the tremendous luxuries of being at Berkeley," Obermeyer said. "You can pursue these projects that just are a slow burn and then have -- hopefully -- a big return when they get over the finish line."
From Hidden Heart Signals to Lifesaving Treatments
The researchers have already begun exploring how the system might be used in actual healthcare settings.
Obermeyer is collaborating with medical systems in Sweden, Taiwan, and the United States to introduce the algorithm into hospital EKG databases. The goal is to examine existing heart scans for signs of elevated risk and identify patients who may benefit from additional monitoring.
Under the proposed approach, physicians would contact patients whose EKGs receive a high-risk assessment and offer them the opportunity to wear a patch that continuously records their heart's electrical activity.
These longer recordings could provide valuable clues about the biological processes responsible for the warning signals detected by the AI. Understanding those processes could help researchers explain why certain hearts are more vulnerable to suddenly developing fatal electrical disturbances.
For some patients, the additional information might ultimately support a recommendation to receive an implanted defibrillator, potentially preventing a sudden and otherwise unexpected death.
Obermeyer has also created a website where people interested in learning about their own risk can provide basic personal information and an email address. The research team can then contact them about EKG analysis when the technology becomes more widely available.
Could AI Reveal New Secrets About the Human Heart?
Beyond its potential to improve the prevention of sudden cardiac death, the discovery highlights how artificial intelligence could help scientists investigate medical mysteries that have resisted conventional approaches.
Rather than simply identifying patients who might need treatment, the algorithm has uncovered patterns in heart activity that researchers do not yet fully understand. Studying those signals could lead to new insights into the electrical disturbances responsible for sudden cardiac death and potentially reveal additional opportunities for prevention.
Obermeyer believes this ability to uncover previously unrecognized biological patterns could become one of AI's most important contributions to medicine, opening new directions for research while helping physicians make better decisions.
"There is also going to be a new way of doing science that comes out of these tools," Obermeyer said, "and it's fun to think about how that starts happening."
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of California - Berkeley. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Ziad Obermeyer, Alexander Schubert, James Ross, Sendhil Mullainathan, Markus Lingman. An ECG biomarker for sudden cardiac death discovered with deep learning. Nature, 2026; 655 (8121): 210 DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-10674-6

articles.title: Dans combien de bâtiments de GTA 6 peut-on vraiment entrer ?
articles.text:
Rockstar Games a pris son temps pour développer GTA 6, qui place son intrigue à Leonida, un État fictif inspiré de la Floride. En résulte une carte immense, dont la taille n’est pas que de la poudre aux yeux. Il y a beaucoup à faire dans Leonida et, surtout, beaucoup d’endroits à visiter. On en prend pour preuve cette statistique ahurissante partagée sur Reddit par un joueur, Aileos, ce mardi 24 novembre.
D’après le décompte d’Aileos, qui n’est pas officiel, bien sûr, il y aurait 5 588 bâtiments dans GTA 6. On pourrait entrer dans 1 563 d’entre eux, soit quasiment 28 %. Pour savoir si un bâtiment est accessible, il faut prêter attention à la carte du jeu : en bleu foncé, on peut entrer ; grisé, la porte reste close.
Plus de 1 500 bâtiments accessibles, mais pas tous en entier
Combien d’heures faudrait-il pour visiter ces 1 563 bâtiments, quand bien même certains ne seraient que des garages dont on fait le tour en quelques minutes ? C’est par exemple le cas de la maison de Belville, aperçue dès 2021 sur une photo accrochée dans un bar du remaster de GTA San Andreas : impossible d’entrer dans la maison elle-même, mais on peut forcer la porte de son garage.
« Tu te souviens quand la fuite annonçait 700 et que tout le monde trouvait ça abusé. 1 500, c’est irréel », s’emballe UnknownApoc. poonslyr69 nuance : « J’imagine que c’est quelque chose comme 700 bâtiments entièrement explorables, et environ 800 bâtiments partiellement accessibles. Des trucs comme des garages ou des sous-sols. » Même dans cette hypothèse basse, les seuls intérieurs complets atteindraient les 700 de la fuite, un chiffre que beaucoup jugeaient déjà irréaliste.
Pour aider à s’y retrouver dans GTA 6, on rappelle qu’IGN propose un guide officiel et gratuit, réalisé en partenariat avec Rockstar Games, qui comprend une carte interactive de Leonida. On attend maintenant celle ou celui qui osera se lancer dans la visite complète des 1 563 intérieurs, chronomètre en main, pour connaître sa durée. Il y aura bien quelqu’un pour se porter volontaire.
